It was disclosed that the feasibility study will be conducted in July while the RDA has already surveyed the area and finalised the initial plan.
According to the initial plan, underpasses will be constructed on the Mall in front of Pearl Continental Hotel, General Headquarters (GHQ) Chowk, General Post Office Chowk and the Military Hospital Chowk. Besides this, a flyover will be developed at Ammar Chowk and Qasim Market.
Currently, the travelling time to Peshawar Road from Kutchery Chowk and Nur Khan Airbase is more than one hour. With completion of this signal-free corridor, it will reduce it to 20 minutes. The news source also mentioned that the cantonment authorities plan to run public transport on the route from Saddar to Motorway and the IIA, work on which will start after the completion of the signal free corridor project in Pindi.
Read:
‘Ammar Chowk project completes, Kutchery Chowk up next’
RDA Director General Anwar Jappa stated that the authority has plans to make Liaquat Bagh Chowk signal-free for which an underpass will be constructed on Murree Road in front of Liaquat Bagh. The RDA has prepared the initial plan, which has been forwarded to the Punjab government for final approval.

title: LDA approves revised plan for Akbar Chowk Flyover
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) approved the revised Akbar Chowk Flyover plan in a meeting chaired by Punjab Caretaker Chief Minister Mohsin Naqvi, a news source reported on May 25.
Read:
Construction work recommences on LHR’s Akbar Chowk Flyover
The meeting was attended by the Planning and Development Chairman, Chief Secretary, LDA Director General and Additional, Secretaries of Housing, Finance, Local Government, representatives from NESPAK, Line Departments, and members of the governing body.
In the meeting, besides the Akbar Chowk Flyover plan, different decisions regarding the LDA were approved along with reviewing proposed amendments to the building and zone regulations. The minister highlighted the need to compensate landowners according to the market rate for the acquired lands.
Read:
Foundation stone laid for Akbar Chowk Underpass project
The meeting authorised LDA’s auction committee to conduct an auction for shops at Park and Ride Plaza in Liberty Market. Moreover, the meeting approved a comprehensive review of the four-lane Ravi Bridge project. The meeting also conducting an assessment for allocating land for the establishment of petrol pumps at transportation terminal sites.

title: CDA to construct 11th Avenue to avoid traffic congestion in E-11
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has decided to commence the construction of 11th Avenue to prevent possible traffic congestion at Sector E-11 and Khayaban-i-Iqbal after the completion of under-construction road linking newly constructed
Margalla Avenue
with Sector E-11, a news source reported on May 24.
Read:
CDA issues reminder of upcoming commercial plots’ auction
The news source mentioned that after the completion of work on the 5.5-kilometre-long road from Sector D-12 (where Margalla Avenue ends) to E-11 in July, the traffic of Margalla Avenue will move towards Khayaban-i-Iqbal and E-11 Sector, which will result in a traffic mess.
Read:
CDA hands over possession of plots in Park Enclave Phase II, III
CDA Chairman Noorul Amin Mengal disclosed that the authority has decided to construct 11th Avenue, which will provide a direct link to E-11 with Srinagar Highway. A survey for the 11th Avenue Islamabad construction has also been started, he added. It was mentioned that the survey will be completed within a month. The traffic load will be divided once the 11th Avenue gets completed as it will be linked with Srinagar Highway and IJP road.

title: CDWP gives nod to development projects across Pakistan
full_text:
Islamabad: The Central Development Working Party (CDWP) has given approval for 15 development projects in Pakistan, worth PKR 249.21 billion, according to news published on May 24.
Read:
CDWP okays development projects of various sectors
A meeting was held with Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal. As per the details, the approved development projects were related to the Ministry of Housing and Works, Ministry of Communication, Power Division, Ministry of Railways, and Ministry of National Health Services Regulations and Coordination.
As per the details, the CDWP has referred Umbrella PC-1 of the Flood Protection Sector Project-III (updated) worth PKR 194.6 billion to the Economic Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) for approval. The meeting also referred the revised Sehat Sahulat Programme at the cost of PKR 31.93 billion to the ECNEC for final approval.
The following are the details of the other approved development projects in Pakistan:
Construction of an Interchange on Hazara Motorway, connecting Abbottabad and Sherwan Road right after the first Tunnel (Shimla Hill Tunnel), at the cost of PKR 1.82 billion
Rehabilitation and upgradation of Kundal Interchange (M-14) to Chashma-DI Khan Road (revised) under DI Khan Road Development Package, at the cost of PKR 2.80 billion
Read:
NHA Board refers PC-1 of Chakdara–Chitral Road project to CDWP
PC-1 for rehabilitation and upgradation of Pezu Tank Road, at the cost of PKR 4.87 billion
Construction of Railway Underpass Gojra, District Toba Tek Singh, at the total cost of PKR 1.44 billion
Renovation and construction of offices, women’s barracks, and multi-purpose training rooms at the office of the superintendent of Railway Police, Rawalpindi (revised), at the cost of PKR 310.375 million
Establishment of capacity building and institutional strengthening in the Planning Commission, at the cost of PKR 2.02 billion
Electrification of villages at Dera Bugti–Package, at the total cost of PKR 960.093 million
Re-commissioning of 5 no Accidental Diesel Electric Locomotives (revised), at the cost of PKR 2.48 billion
Rehabilitation of the firefighting system at KMC, at the total cost of PKR 1.83 billion
Provision of missing facilities at Swabi University, at the cost of PKR 2.03 billion
Read:
CDWP gives nod to Karachi Circular Railway project
Establishment of the Photar Campus of Punjab at Gujar Khan, at the cost of PKR 638.45 million
Construction of academic blocks of Shaheed Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Medical University, at the cost of PKR 2.89 billion

title: ICCI asked to finalise site for industrial estate in Islamabad
developer: Punjab Industrial Estate Management and Development
full_text:
Islamabad: Islamabad Chamber of Commerce and Industry (ICCI) has been asked to finalise one of the proposed sites for establishment of an industrial estate in the capital city, a news source reported on May 18.
Read:
ICCI suggests starting development work in ISB’s markets
Punjab Industry and Commerce Minister S.M Tanveer, while addressing the business community at ICCI, stated that the Punjab Industrial Estate Management and Development Company has identified four sites for setting up the industrial estate by ICCI. However, it will be finalised by the ICCI.
In the same meeting, Punjab Excise and Communications Minister Bilal Afzal informed the attendees that funds have been released for the rehabilitation of
Kahuta Road
. It was also mentioned that roads, covering 2,600 kilometres, leading to various industrial estates will be repaired. He asked the business community to send their concerns related to the excise and communication department through their chambers and every effort will be made to resolve them.
Read:
ICCI to have representation in CDA Board meetings
The meeting discussed the establishment of an industrial area around Islamabad including the Kahuta area. The Punjab Cabinet members opined out that industrialisation should be promoted by the private sector for increasing exports and improving foreign exchange earnings. ICCI President Ahsan Zafar Bakhtawari recommended formulating 10-year economic policies for better promotion of business and investment.

title: CDA to launch mega road development projects in ISB’s rural areas
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has decided to launch mega development projects, worth PKR 10 billion, in rural areas of the capital city, according to a news published in the leading newspaper on May 9.
Read:
CDA mulls setting up City Business District along Margalla Avenue
The news source mentioned that the CDA Engineering Wing has invited tenders from the construction companies in order to award contracts for 17 projects, worth PKR 2.8 billion, in the first phase. CDA Director Work Tahir Mahmood stated that ICT’s local department’s help was sought to identify the roads, towns, and areas that required work. He went on to say that the PC-1 of the projects have been prepared and now tenders have been called. It was mentioned that the 17 projects will be completed in a period of three months.
The following are the details of the road development projects:
Rehabilitation and upgradation of
Shah Allah Ditta Road
up to Alexander Well, at the estimated cost of PKR 380 million
Rehabilitation of Main Golra Road, at the cost of PKR 144 million
Upgradation and rehabilitation of Jodh and Sarai Kharboza Road, at an estimated cost of PKR 135 million
Rehabilitation of roads in Golra, Sangjani, and other areas, at a total cost of PKR 130 million
Rehabilitation of Simly Dam Road, Sewer, and Jandghand Roads, at the cost of PKR 120 million
Rehabilitation of roads in Mandla, Bari Imam, Banigala, Gokina, and Sanjalian, at the estimated cost of PKR 141 million
Read:
CDA proposes to construct a road in Margalla Hills
Rehabilitation of Phulgran, Sakreela, and Member Roads, for the cost of PKR 160 million
Construction of a road from Naiabadi to Huzaifa Town and internal roads of Malpur and Bhara Kahu, at the cost of PKR 151 million
Rehabilitation of Sihala Japan Road and other schemes for Golra Mast, Khana, and other rural areas.

title: PC-1 preparations start for Leh Expressway, Flood Channel project
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA)’s governing body approved the plan to prepare a new PC-1 for
Leh Expressway
and Flood Channel project with a focus on the flood mitigation plan in the Nullah Leh, a news source reported on May 6.
Read:
Leh Expressway Flood Channel project: New PC-1 to be submitted next week
The 62nd meeting of the governing body was held in which the new plan of the said project was approved. According to a senior RDA official, the Punjab government wants to reduce the cost of the project and wants to focus on mitigating flood in monsoon season by separating the stormwater coming from Margalla Hills and sewage from the twin cities of Islamabad and Rawalpindi.
Read:
RDA to develop Nullah Leh Expressway project with government funding
The news source mentioned that the authority will hire a consultant to make a new plan. The government agency will be hired for this purpose. The chief engineer went on to say that the plan will be prepared soon so that the work could be started in the next fiscal year. He further added that roads will be constructed on both sides of the nullah.

title: Govt commits to collaborate with WB for sustainable development
full_text:
Islamabad: Finance Minister (FM) Ishaq Dar stated that the incumbent government is committed to working in collaboration with the World Bank (WB) in a bid to achieve the goal of sustainable development in Pakistan, according to news published in the leading newspaper on May 4.
Read:
WB team visits PLRA, reviews land record computerisation
Dar met with a WB delegation, headed by WB Vice President (VP) for Human Development Mamta Murthi, to discuss collaboration for
sustainable development
. During the meeting, the FM appreciated the role of the WB and lauded the efforts made by Pakistan. He expressed gratitude for the financial and technical assistance provided by the WB.
Moreover, the VP highlighted the significance of investing in human capital, especially in social protection, women’s development, and population control etc. She emphasised the importance of community participation in executing development projects.
Read:
KP to sell ‘Carbon Credits’ through WB
The meeting was attended by Special Adviser to Prime Minister (SAPM) on Revenue Tariq Pasha, Special Adviser to Prime Minister (SAPM) on Finance Tariq Bajwa, Special Secretary Finance, Secretary Finance, and other senior officers from Finance Division.

title: CDA proposes to construct a road in Margalla Hills
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) is considering a proposal to construct a 5-kilometre long road from a popular restaurant to Bari Imam in
Margalla Hills
, a news source reported on May 5.
Read:
CDA to hold plot auction in May end
As per the details, the CDA Planning and Engineering Wings will review the proposal before submitting it to the higher authorities. Once it is approved, the Engineering Wing will prepare PC-1 for the new road and forward it to CDA Development Working Party (DWP) for approval.
Read:
CDA to restore Shah Allah Dittas’s trail, construct sports complex
According to a CDA official, the proposal will utilise an off-track road between the restaurant and Bari Imam in order to manage the traffic congestion. The official mentioned that authorities will thoroughly review the proposal before taking the final decision.

title: RDA takes up stalled underpass project to make Murree Road signal free
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) has decided to resume a stalled underpass project to make
Murree Road
signal free, according to news published on April 26.
Read:
Authorities directed to renovate RWP’s historic Liaquat Bagh
An RDA senior official mentioned that the authority spent over PKR 11 million in 2017 on the feasibility study to determine whether to build an underpass or a flyover at Liaquat Bagh Square. The project was shelved in 2018.
Read:
Massive drive against encroachments in Rawalpindi starts next week
The RDA has once again forwarded the project to the Punjab government for its inclusion in the Annual Development Programme (ADP)’s budget for the coming fiscal year. According to the new plan, the RDA will construct an underpass on the road from Saddar to Faizabad and a provide a road link for Liaquat Road towards Fawara Chowk.

title: CDA approves imp road infrastructure projects
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has approved the PC-1 of Margalla Avenue Extension, Lehtrar Road, and hiring of a consulting firm for the mixed-use Kuri Enclave housing project, according to a news published in national dailies on April 20.
Read:
CDA to develop mixed-use housing project in Zone-IV
The approvals were granted in CDA Development Working Party (CDADWP) meeting, which was chaired by the authority chairman Noor-ul-Amin Mengal. As per the details, the
Margalla Avenue Extension
project will connect Rawalpindi-Kohat Road (N-5) with Islamabad Peshawar Motorway (M-1), while the Lehtrar Road will link Khanna Pull with PINSTECH.
Read:
CDA to restore old Murree Road for Eid-ul-Fitr
The CDADWP meeting members also approved the consultancy services for Orchard Heights. The same meeting approved PC-II of project consultancy services for conducting road safety audit in the capital city. The consultancy firm will formulate recommendations for smooth and safe traffic flow on roads. Reportedly, the audit will also help reduce road accidents and improve road safety in planning and design.

title: CDA to restore old Murree Road for Eid-ul-Fitr
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has decided to repair the old Murree Road under the flyover portion of the
Bhara Kahu bypass
in order to ensure smooth traffic movement for Eid-ul-Fitr, according to news published on April 17.
Read:
CDA to develop new parks in Islamabad
CDA Chairman Noorul Amin Mengal has directed the engineering wing to repair the dilapidated and uneven 1-kilometre-long section of the old Murree Road (beneath the flyover portion of the bypass). He has revealed that transom work has been completed. While visiting the project site, he ordered the relevant authorities to remove shuttering and other material on the road to ensure smooth traffic flow.
Read:
CDA officials directed to handover possession in developed parts of Park Enclave
The news source mentioned that the portion of the road linking Malpur with Jhugi Stop has been completed but the city managers have yet to decide if the road will open to traffic by Eid. The news source mentioned that the flyover portion of the project will be completed within the next two months.

title: CDA to develop new parks in Islamabad
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has decided to establish several new and modern parks in the capital city in a bid to provide better recreational facilities to the residents, a news source reported on April 14.
Read:
CDA approves formation of new Building Control Wing
Sources mentioned that the authority has already developed around 37 public parks in the last 10 years and is planning to increase this number in the coming years. According to a CDA official, the civic agency needs three to four months to develop a new park once all the codal formalities are completed. Currently, there are six amusement parks in the plan, which are sufficient to cater to the recreational needs of residents of Islamabad.
Read:
CDA invites tender for Simly Dam Road Rehabilitation Project
Reportedly, a new policy was adopted that whenever a new sector is developed, an amusement park will be established with it. As per the detail, the CDA has been developing several new sectors including I-11, I-12, I-14, I-15, I-16, D-12, and
Park Enclave
along with model villages, and parks are being developed in these areas.

title: CDA invites tender for Simly Dam Road Rehabilitation Project
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has invited tenders from approved contractors for the rehabilitation of Simly Dam Road, a news source reported on April 10.
Read:
CDA to approve commercial buildings’ plans within one month
CDA Chairman Noorul Amin Mengal, on his Twitter handle, shared that the rehabilitation of
Simly Dam Road
has been tendered. Sources mentioned that sealed tenders were invited from contractors on a percentage basis from Category C-4 or above, with the project code CE-01 for the year 2022-2023.
As per the details, the estimated cost for rehabilitation and maintenance work of the damaged section of Simly Dam approach road in Islamabad is PKR 74.954836 million and requires a money deposit of PKR 1.499097 million. The news source mentioned that more information on the terms and conditions can be found on the CDA and PPRA websites. The interested contractors can obtain tender documents from the Deputy Director Road Division-III Office, on making a payment of PKR 5,000 per set during office hours.
Read:
CDA opens online possession for plots in Sector I-15
Moreover, the last date for submission of the application for issuance of tender documents is April 25 and the tender documents will be issued on April 26. It revealed that the opening of the sealed tenders will happen on April 28. The successful bidder must provide relevant attested documents according to the laid down requirements. The bidder must also provide an authorization letter and CNIC for the person deputed to submit the application and collect the tender form.

title: Launch of DHA-Lahore’s signal-free corridor, Bedian Road underpass projects expected soon
developer: Lahore Muhammad Ali Randhawa, who is also Lahore Development
full_text:
Lahore: The launch of construction work at DHA-Lahore’s signal-free corridor (connecting Firdous Market underpass with DHA Main Boulevard) and Bedian Road underpass near DHA Phase 5 roundabout is expected soon, according to a news story published in leading newspapers on March 19. The news source has confirmed that the work for legal procedures related to cost estimation, approval bidding, and award of the project has been initiated.
Read:
CM approves signal-free corridor from Center Point to Defence in Lahore
As per the details, the
signal-free corridor
will start from Firdous Market Underpass (Gulberg), pass through the Cavalry intersection and Ghora Chowk in Cantt and be linked with the DHA Main Boulevard at Defence Mor. Under this project, a four-lane underpass at Cavalry Chowk and a four-land flyover at Ghora Chowk will be constructed. The project also includes remodeling of the Defence Mor intersection.
The underpass at Bedian Road near DHA Phase-5 roundabout will be a four-lane wide dual carriageway; it will also feature protected U-turns. Commissioner Lahore Muhammad Ali Randhawa, who is also Lahore Development Authority (LDA) Director General, said that once completed, these projects will benefit a large number of citizens by smoothening traffic flow, improving environment, reducing travel time and saving fuel cost. He shared these views while visiting the project sites.
Randhawa directed the officials to expedite the work related to approvals and bidding so work could be launched on these projects. According to the PC-1 of the signal-free corridor, the cost approved by the government was PKR 3.2 billion; this has now been increased to PKR 4.2 billion. The estimated cost of Bedian Road underpass project has now escalated to PKR 2.8 billion.
Read:
EPA invites public hearing on MB Gulberg to Defence Mor signal-free corridor
Bedian Road underpass will take six months to complete while the signal-free corridor will be completed in eight months. The news source also revealed that the traffic management plan to be followed during the construction period has already been finalised. As per the proposed plan, Masood Anwari Road will remain open for traffic by a two-lane service road on both sides, while the traffic coming from Cantt, Shami Road will be diverted to Khursheed Alam Road towards Ghora Chowk and onwards. Traffic at Khalif Butt Chowk and Ghora Chowek will be managed by utilizing the existing spaces.
It is important to note that both projects are approved by the government, but weren’t executed due to the non-availability of funds.

title: WAPDA to double power supply to national grid by 2030
full_text:
Islamabad: The electricity supply to the national grid by the year 2030 will be achieved through low-cost and environmentally friendly hydroelectric power projects, news sources quoted a spokesperson of the Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA) on March 12.
Read:
Mohmand Dam to be completed by 2026: Chairman WAPDA
In a recent statement issued by WAPDA, the hydroelectric power plants currently generate 9,500 megawatts of electricity, while the authority plans to double that amount to 20,000 within the next seven years. This increase in electricity generation capacity will be achieved through the completion of several hydroelectric dam projects, including the Diamir Bhasha Dam,
Dasu Hydropower Project
, Mohmand Dam, Tarbela Fifth Expansion Project, Naygaj Dam, Karam Tangi Dam, Kachhi Canal, and K4 Project.
Read:
WAPDA shares details of compensation to Dasu Power Project’s affectees
In addition to boosting electricity production, these dams will increase the country’s water storage capacity by 12 million acre-feet annually. It is worth mentioning that the WAPDA has initiated several hydroelectric projects with support from international organisations and development banks, including the
World Bank (WB)
and Asian Development Bank (ADB). Recently, WAPDA signed an agreement with the World Bank for a floating solar power project with an installed capacity of 300 megawatts (MW).

title: CDA to impose fines on residents for wasting water
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has decided to fine residents for wasting water during the upcoming summer season, the news sources reported on March 7.
Read:
CDA to install 20 tube wells to improve water supply in Islamabad
The authority has formed special inspection teams to monitor and fine residents for violations of water use including washing vehicles and wasteful conduct. The authority has also raised the previous limit of PKR 5,000 to upwards of PKR 25,000 for repeating the offence. In this regard, the authority has allowed the inspection teams to send challans of repeated offenders to the CDA magistrate to revise the penalty. In a statement by the authority, it was stated that the decision for the increased fine was taken in view of the repeat of water-wasting-related offences in posh areas where residents can pay fines.
Read:
FGEHA shares details on allotment of plots in Park Road Housing Scheme
It is important to note that Islamabad is facing the worst water shortage since it lacks a reliable groundwater source. The authority has recently allowed the Federal Government Employee Housing Authority (FGEHA) to construct a missing link of the 1.2-kilometre water line from
Shah Allah Ditta to Sector G.
the project will provide 1.2 million gallons of water (MGWD) to the residents of the surrounding areas.

title: Balochistan PHE proposes dams to address water shortage in Quetta
full_text:
Quetta: The Balochistan Public Health Engineer (PHE) department has submitted a proposal for the construction of three dams in Quetta to address the water shortage issue, news sources reported on March 8.
Read:
PKR 400 mn released for Gwadar water projects
The feasibility report and PC-1 for the Babar Kach,
Burj Aziz Khan, and Halak dams
have been completed by the Balochistan Public Health Engineering (PHE) agency. The decision was made, citing the depleting subsurface water levels in the provincial capital and the looming danger of the spread of waterborne diseases in the city.
The total cost for the three dams is estimated to be PKR 143 billion, with the Babar Kach Dam being the most expensive at PKR 73 billion. The Balochistan government has requested the federal government include these projects in the Public Sector Development Program (PSDP) for the fiscal year 2023–24. Balochistan Chief Minister Mir Abdul Quddus Bizenjo is expected to approach the prime minister to consider these projects to alleviate the water shortage in the region.
Read:
ADB approves funds for emergency assistance in Balochistan’s flood-affected areas
There has been a persistent water shortage in Quetta, the province’s largest city. The government has announced several water development projects for the city under federal government’s patronage. However, the problem has not been addressed so far.

title: RDA seeks EOI for digital survey of under-construction buildings
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) has invited Expressions of interest (EOI)s from qualified town planning consulting firms to conduct digital field survey of under-construction, unapproved buildings within its jurisdiction, the news sources reported on March 7.
Read:
RDA to devise economic strategy to self-fund development projects
The RDA hired surveyor firm will be responsible for developing an Android application and conducting digital survey of buildings in the residential, commercial, industrial, and institutional sectors. The authority has asked the interested firms to submit their EOIs, fulfilling all the statutory regulations in compliance with the Punjab Procurement Rules 2014 (PPRA), along with the necessary documents. As per the EOI published, the authority seeks the following from the qualified firms to participate:
Interested firms must provide a certified true copy of the Memorandum/article of Association, partnership deed, or joint venture agreement, and a certificate of registration with the Pakistan Council of Architects and Town Planners (PCATP) along with the valid renewal letter until 2022 in the relevant project profile category.
The firms must submit a list of permanent professional staff along with CVs of relevant core staff showing relevant project-wise experience with the exact time duration for each project, and an undertaking that they have not been blacklisted/defaulted by any government agency/department/organisation.
Read:
RDA urged to complete Rawalpindi’s master plan 2050 at earliest
The EOI must reach the office of the Director (LU&BC) RDA by March 22, 2023. The RDA reserves the right to disqualify any application if it contains false, fabricated, or materially incorrect information.
Interested bidders can purchase the prequalification document by submitting a written application and paying a non-refundable fee of PKR 2,000 in favour of the Director (LU&BC), RDA. The bidding documents containing specifications can be downloaded from the RDA website.
International firms must make a JV/consortium with a local firm/firms, and only a maximum of three firms are allowed to make a JV/consortium.
Read:
RDA launches awareness campaign regarding Peri-Urban Structure Plan
It is important to note that RDA has launched multiple operations against illegal buildings and construction in the city.

title: Punjab LG to digitise bidding and tendering system
developer: The Punjab Local Government and Community Development
full_text:
Lahore: The Punjab Local Government and Community Development (LGCD) department has decided to digitise the bidding and tendering system throughout the province, the news sources reported on March 7.
Read:
Punjab Excise department offers discount on e-payment of property tax
The system will be implemented in collaboration with the Bank of Punjab (BOP) for smart E-governance solutions. The decision was announced by Punjab Minister for Local Government and Community Development (LGCD) Minister, Ibrahim Hassan Murad during a meeting. The minister said that the
e-solutions
will transform the department into a model system. Under the system, the Punjab government will also digitise bidding and tendering systems, and services and payments will be computerised to maintain transparency.
Moreover, the paper trail and manual system will be replaced with a computerised system for better record management and prevention of fraud.
Read:
UAE company to invest in Punjab E-governance project
It is pertinent to mention that the Punjab Land Record Authority (PLRA) in association with the World Bank (WB) has launched the digital land record system. The system is part of the government’s push for digital and innovative governance to expedite service delivery and reduce bureaucratic hindrances in public sector organisations.

title: Govt to hire consultant for ML-1 project soon
full_text:
Islamabad: The federal government has decided to hire an international consultant for the Karachi to Peshawar Main Line-1 (ML-1) project, news sources reported on March 6.
Read:
Govt to focus on KCR, ML-1 projects for early completion
The Central Development Working Party (CDWP) has approved the final decision to allocate PKR 909.285 million for the project. Out of this amount, PKR 450 million has been assigned for hiring an consultant while the remaining amount will be utilized for paying salaries and other expenses of the project.
Additionally, the project also includes the establishment of a
Project Management Unit (PMU)
and a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) in Lahore and the Ministry of Railways, respectively, to efficiently monitor and supervise project activities such as cost estimation, tender processing, and execution. The project will also include the hiring of human resources to carry out these activities.
Read:
ADB offers to finance ML-1 project
It is important to note that the ML-1 project starts from Karachi and travels through four provinces before concluding in Peshawar. There have been some disagreements between the two countries regarding the finance and cost estimates of the project. Recently, Pakistan decided to decline Asian Development Bank’s (ADB) offer to start the project citing a mutual agreement with China for the project.

title: RUDA attracts USD 600 mn investment pledges
full_text:
Lahore: The Ravi Urban Development Authority (RUDA) has received investment pledges of over USD 600 million in investments in its various development projects, news sources reported on March 5.
Read:
RUDA to construct 100,000 low-cost houses near River Ravi
The investments were pledged by international organisations and under government-to-government agreements during the three-day Dubai International Property Show (IPS)-2023. The RUDA signed seven Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) and held 15 meetings with various parties during the event, leading to successful collaborations generating foreign direct investment (FDI).
Read:
RUDA, CBD sign seven MoUs at International Property Show
Previously, RUDA and
Punjab Central Business Development Authority (PCBDA)
signed agreements worth USD 500 million with leading international companies during the first session of the Dubai property show last month. The authority visited Dubai to explore best practices of government-to-government and public-private partnership projects and to build on the success of their participation in IPS.

title: ECC approves grants for Ministry of Housing & Works
full_text:
Islamabad: The Economic Coordination Committee (ECC) has approved various technical supplemental grants for the execution of development schemes related to housing and works in different parts of the country, news sources reported on March 2.
Read:
ECC approves PKR 5 bn Ramzan Relief Package
The ECC has mandated the Ministry of Housing and Works to oversee the execution of these schemes and ensure that they are completed within the stipulated timelines and budgets. The grants for the following projects are approved for completion:
PKR 200 million has been allocated to the
Ministry of Housing and Works
for the development of the road from Lalmosa to Noona Wali Bhago and Malwana, with link infrastructure Tehsil Kharian
PKR 429.436 million has been approved for development schemes in district Kasur, under the Ministry of Housing and Works
PKR 702.9 million has been granted for the execution of schemes in Punjab province under the sustainable development goals achievement program by the Ministry of Planning, Development and Special Initiatives
Read:
ECC gives nod to Credit Guarantee Scheme to supplement low-income housing initiative
PKR 12 million has been granted to the Ministry of Interior for the National Program for Improvement of Watercourses Phase-II in Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT).
PKR 20 million has been granted to the Ministry of Interior for the National Program for enhancement command areas in Barani areas of ICT
The Ministry of Interior has been granted PKR 1112.04 million for the project implementation letter of HQ FC (South) & HQ FC (North) KP fund

title: CDA to approve rural area development project
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has proposed a Rural Area Development project worth PKR 10 billion to develop suburban areas of the federal capital, according to news sources.
Read:
Commercial building owners required to share structural stability certificates with CDA
Project Concept 1 (PC-1) of the project will be presented before the Development Working Party (DWP), which is set to review and consider the project on March 3 (today) for final approval. CDA Chairman Noorul Amin Mengal, in his first media briefing, shared his plans, including the rural development projects, which aim to ‘end the urban-rural divide’.
As per the sources, the proposed
PC-I outlines development
works for necessary infrastructure facilities such as roads, clean drinking water, and street pavement in rural areas. The project will provide sanitation, communication, drinking water, and basic facilities to almost 700,000 inhabitants.
Read:
CDA to add 13 new routes in orange, red line BRT
However, the project’s approval is still subject to the DWP’s review. The CDA chairman also shared updates on sector development, stating that it is one of his top priorities and that work in Sector E-12 and I-12 is being expedited. The chairman also announced that Sector I-15 is almost finished, and over 5,000 allottees will be given possession letters on March 10.

title: Japan to donate USD 5 mn for flood relief efforts in Pakistan
full_text:
Islamabad: Japan will donate USD 5 million to Pakistan for the Emergency Flood Assistance Project, the news sources reported on March 1.
Read:
Japan donates USD 38.9 million to flood victims
The funds will be used by the government to expand the scope of the original project, particularly to support:
Urgent provision of climate-resilient seeds for staple crop cultivation
Women-led livelihoods to meet basic household needs
In this regard, an agreement was signed between the Asian Development Bank (ADB) Country Director Yong Ye and the Ministry of Economic Affairs. As per the press release, the grant is offered under the Japan Fund for
Prosperous and Resilient Asia and the Pacific (JFPRAP),
which is administered by ADB under the  Emergency Flood Assistance Project (Additional Financing). The grant is in addition to the funds allocated by Japan for immediate assistance for flood affectees in Sindh and Balochistan and will be used through third-party organisations and United Nations (UN)-associated relief funds.
Read:
Japan releases USD 7 mn for flood relief activities in Pakistan
It is important to note that a devastating flood in August last year displaced nearly 30 million people. As per the government account, this has resulted in an economic loss to the tune of USD 30 billion.

title: Construction of commercial buildings allowed on Srinagar Highway’s unacquired ROW
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) Planning Wing has allowed the construction of commercial buildings on the unacquired right of way (ROW) of Srinagar Highway, a news source reported on February 25.
Read:
CDA to expand Srinagar Highway, Jinnah Avenue
As per the details, the
Srinagar Highway
, according to the Master Plan of 1960, was supposed to have a Right of Way (ROW) expanding to 1,200 feet. Due to this, the civic agency has acquired land in major areas. However, it was decided that the remaining unacquired area of ROW in Zone II, will be used for commercial projects. The news source disclosed that the authority will not acquire the ROW in G-16 and G-17 because it has been allotted for commercial buildings.
Read:
CDA approves construction of flyover at Srinagar Highway
Moreover, the authority has fixed PKR 7,500 as per square yard commercialisation charge on the area of commercial plots. Previously, the city managers decided to charge a conversion fee on the entire plot area.

title: KP-EZDMC issues LOI to solarise economic zones
developer: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Economic Zones Development
full_text:
Peshawar: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Economic Zones Development and Management Company (KP-EZDMC) has issued a Letter of Intent (LOI) to InfraCo Asia for completing a feasibility study to solarise the economic zones in the province, according to news published on February 24.
Read:
Industrialists briefed on facilities available at Mohmand SEZ
The news source mentioned that the issuance of an LOI indicates the commitment of InfraCo Asia and KP to collaborate for exploring the potential of solar energy and increasing its usage in the economic zones. As per the details, the solarisation of the
economic zones
includes the integration of solar power into the energy mix of the zones in a bid to provide a cost-effective and quick source of energy.
Read:
CM Mehmood briefed on existing, upcoming economic zones in KP
Moreover, the solarisation of economic zones will help in reducing the overall business cost since the cost of energy has a vital role to play in the cost of production. The event was attended by KP Chief Secretary Imdadullah Bosal, KP-EZDMC Chief Commercial Officer (CCO), British High Commission Pakistan Development Director, and team lead of Sustainable Employment and Economic Development (SEED).

title: CDA to construct underpass near Serena Chowk
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has decided to widen Srinagar Highway, near Serena Chowk and construct a single-barrel underpass, a news source reported on February 22.
Read:
CDA launches affordable apartment project for overseas Pakistanis
As per the details, a consultant will prepare a feasibility report and design the widening of Srinagar Highway, starting from the
7th Avenue Interchange
to Serena Chowk. It was revealed that the underpass is being constructed for the smooth flow of traffic.
Read:
CDA to issue transfer deed for auctioned plots in Islamabad
Reportedly, the CDA has approved the hiring of a consultant for conducting a feasibility study for the Sector I-11 National Bus Terminal. The news source also mentioned that the authority has plans to complete six parking plazas by June to provide modern parking facilities in the busiest commercial areas of the city. It was disclosed that each parking plaza will feature a shopping area, cinema, and food court. The parking capacity of the parking plaza will be 5 to 8 floors.

title: Gulberg Elevated Expressway to be funded by ADB: LDA
full_text:
Lahore: Lahore Development Authority (LDA) Director General (DG) Amir Ahmad Khan has said that the Gulberg Elevated Expressway project will be funded by the Asian Development Bank (ADB), the news sources reported on February 15.
Read:
Gulberg Elevated Expressway made part of Lahore Master plan 2050
The director general revealed this following a meeting with a four-member delegation of ADB, which met to discuss the funding options and the project’s scope. On the occasion, DG Amir said that the Gulberg Elevated Expressway will be a flagship project for the city.
According to LDA DG Amir, the project’s goals are to
improve traffic flow
in a busy area of Lahore and link traffic to the city’s entrance and exit points. The participants were also briefed by LDA Chief Engineer-I Israr Saeed Khan on the project’s design elements and potential environmental effects.
Read:
CM Elahi greenlights Lahore Elevated Expressway project
It is important to note that the Gulberg Elevated Expressway project’s Project Concept 1 (PC-1) was approved in 2020. The 10.5-kilometre-long track will cost PKR 85 billion and will connect Gulberg Main Boulevard with the Lahore-Islamabad Motorway (M-2), bypassing Shadman, Samanabad, Ferozepur Road, and Gulshan Ravi.

title: NHA approves Sialkot-Narowal link road project
full_text:
Sialkot: The National Highway Authority (NHA) Executive Board has approved the revised Project Concept-1 (PC-1) of the Sialkot-Narowal link road project, news sources reported on February 20.
Read:
Minister directs early submission
of PC-1 for Narowal Sports City
The 73-kilometre-long, 4-lane Sialkot-Narowal road will connect the Narrowal and Narang Mandi with the Sialkot-Lahore Motorway (M-11). As per the sources, the project would cost PKR 74 billion and would be an extension of the M-11, reducing commute times for vehicles coming from the border region. The NHA has sent the revised PC-1 to the
Ministry of Planning and Development (P&D)
and the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) for final approval.
Read:
Reconstruction of Narowal-Zafarwal Road begins
In addition to this, the NHA Board also approved the following projects:
PKR 10.95 billion for the construction of 48-kilometre-long Section III of the Chakdara-Chitral Road Project (N-45) from 4 Kalkatak-Chitral
PKR 2.60 billion for the 18-kilometre-long Paharpur-BandKorai-Rodikhel-Sidra Morr (N-55) project
Installation of Intelligent Traffic System (ITS) on the rest of motorways as per Concession Agreements and Regular Agreements/Rules/etc
Read:
Narowal gets PKR 5.12 bn for upgradation of roads, drain infrastructure
Release of ‘Position Paper’ of the 221.95 kilometre-long Indus Highway (N-55) Additional Carriageway Project from Shikarpur-Rajanpur Section

title: FGEHA to construct missing water supply line for G-13,14
full_text:
Islamabad: The Federal Government Employees Housing Authority (FGEHA) has decided to construct a water supply line for the residents of Sectors G-13 and G-14, the news sources reported on February 20.
Read:
Missing link of water supply line taken up by FGEHA
As part of the project, the FGEHA would construct a 2-kilometre-long missing link from Shah Allah Dita’s water reservoir to provide the residents of the aforementioned sectors with a reliable water supply. Once completed, the project would provide
2.5 million gallons of water per day (MGD).
The authority has already approved Project Concept-1 (PC-1) of the project, and the tender for the said project will be issued soon. As per the sources, the project will be completed in a year on a priority basis. Once completed, the sectors will be integrated with the Capital Development Authority (CDA)’s water supply network.
Read:
FGEHA approves water supply system for sectors G13, G-14
It is important to note that Sectors G-13 and 14 were supposed to receive a water supply line, but the CDA could only construct a 12-kilometre portion of the 14-kilometre water supply line from the Shah Allah Dita reservoir.

title: FDA orders expedited development work in city
developer: Ali Annan Qamar has ordered the Faisalabad Development
full_text:
Faisalabad: Faisalabad Deputy Commissioner (DC) Ali Annan Qamar has ordered the Faisalabad Development Authority (FDA) to expedite work on the ongoing development work and beautification drive in the city, news sources reported on February 17.
Read:
FDA to issue smart cards to property owners
The DC ordered the administration to take the necessary actions to build roads, overhead bridges, and underpasses. He also ordered the preparation of a comprehensive plan for the beautification drive and a timeline for the completion of the ongoing development projects. The FDA officials also gave a detailed presentation of the road infrastructure development work and regularisation of the city roads and housing societies.
Read:
Owners of properties in FDA-controlled areas to get smart cards
It is pertinent to mention that Faisalabad is the third largest city in the country and is managed by the FDA. The authority oversees
17 commercial marketplaces,
18 residential colonies, and FDA City, a large housing development with seven orchards planted according to a specific theme, in addition to the creation of public parks.

title: AJK gives nod to 11 development projects
developer: A meeting of the Cabinet Development
full_text:
Islamabad: The Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) government has approved 11
development projects
, amounting to PKR 6 billion, in different districts of the state, according to news published on February 14.
Read:
AJK to launch housing scheme for journalists in 45 days
A meeting of the Cabinet Development Committee (CDC) was held, which was chaired by Prime Minister of AJK Sardar Tanveer Ilyas Khan. The meeting approved five projects for physical planning and housing, worth PKR 3 billion, four projects for public works and one project each for health and education.  The physical planning and housing sector projects include:
Completion of remaining facilities in the reconstruction of the Supreme Court and High Court
Upgradation of the water supply scheme in Palindri of District Sidhnuti for PKR 7,404 million
Greater Water Supply Scheme Hattian Bala, at the total cost of PKR 437.1 million
Installation of an elevator in the High Court Building Muzaffarabad, worth PKR 426.65 million  Water Supply Scheme Tehsil Headquarters of Hospital Chachoi in District Kotli for PKR 663.3 million
Completion of remaining work on Water Supply Scheme Phase-I at Rawlaot for the outstanding work of Darek Dam, at the cost of PKR 866.8 million
Read:
AJK PM lays foundation stone of free-of-cost housing project for poor
In communication and Works, the approved projects include:
Remodelling of city squares in the capital city Muzaffarabad
Construction of RCC Bridge on Salar Nala and Panji, Kalri Kasgma Road in District Bhimber, worth PKR 531.07 million
Upgradation of Jandala Pir Gili Road Phase-I in Bhimbar district
Reconditioning of the remaining part of Kotli Nikyal Road in Kotli district, at the cost of PKR 488.7 million

title: New wastewater treatment system inaugurated in KP
developer: Minister for Local Government Election & Rural Development
full_text:
Peshawar: Caretaker Minister for Local Government Election & Rural Development Department (LGE&RDD) Advocate Sawal Nazir launched the first-of-its-kind Decentralized Wastewater Treatment System (Dewats) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), according to news published on February 15.
Read:
KP to sell ‘Carbon Credits’ through WB
Reportedly, the newly-inaugurated wastewater treatment systems have been developed at Wazirbagh Park in Peshawar by the Water and Sanitation Services Peshawar (WSSP) with financial and technical assistance from UNICEF. The system will treat sewerage water from the surrounding locales and repurpose it for
the irrigation of the park.
During the inauguration ceremony, Minister Nazir was briefed on the project’s overall aspects, including environmental benefits, community benefits and overall cost.
Read:
KP CM directs to start construction work on Dir Motorway
The minister lauded the development and termed it the right step for converting potable water and curbing water pollution. He also thanked UNICEF fit its assistance.

title: CDA to conduct survey for structural stability of all high-rise, commercial buildings
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has directed Building Control to conduct a survey of all commercial and high-rise buildings in the federal city to check structural stability, according to news published on February 15.
Read:
CDA to expand Srinagar Highway, Jinnah Avenue
As per the details, Deputy Director General Mohammad Shahbaz Hussain directed all the wings of the building control to carry out a survey of all commercial and high-rise buildings within ICT limits as the federal city falls in Zone-2B of seismic zones.
CDA
Chairman Captain (retired) Noor-ul-Amin Mengal has asked all the developers, occupants, and owners are requested to get the buildings vetted for structural stability from reputable third-party consultants in order to avoid any untoward event.
Read:
CDA to review ‘Kurri Road’ expansion proposal
A CDA official (whose name was not disclosed) mentioned that this exercise is being done to check the structural stability of buildings so that the faulty ones could be pointed out. Moreover, it was shared that Islamabad lies in Zone 2-B, keeping this in mind, awareness should be created among the stakeholders regarding the importance of structural stability of buildings.

title: Stakeholders briefed on Rawalpindi’s peri-urban structure plans
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) on Saturday (February 11) briefed stakeholders of the Taxila and Kahuta regarding the ongoing development of peri-urban structure plans and site development zones, the news sources reported.
Read:
RDA launches awareness campaign regarding Peri-Urban Structure Plan
In this regard, a briefing on the ongoing zoning developments was given to residents, municipal officials, and architects at meetings held in the offices of assistant commissioner Taxila and tehsil officer Kahuta. The city administration and
Mott Macdonald Pakistan (MMP),
the zoning consultant, provided a briefing to the meeting on the proposed data and the division of the Rawalpindi region into three zones.
It was stated that under the peri-urban plans, the area will be divided into distinct zones, with housing societies and industries not being permitted outside the proposed areas, in order to better manage the population and restrict land use. Moreover, areas outside of a particular zone will only be used for farming and cultivation.
Read:
FWO shares progress status of peri-urban housing project
On the occasion, RDA Director General Mohammad Saif Anwar Jappa said that the authority is working in collaboration with the local government and the civic agency to prepare a
25-year master plan
for the city.
It is also important to mention that the RDA has been preparing a zone development plan for the next 25 years and has hired a consultant to demarcate land for the various sections. Under the plan, Rawalpindi city will be divided into separate residential, industrial, and green zones for better land management.

title: Rashakai SEZ to be made operational next month
full_text:
Peshawar: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Economic Zones Development & Management Company (KP-EZDMC) Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Javed Iqbal Khattak shared that the Rashakai – a prioritised Special Economic Zone (SEZ) – will be made operational in March, a news source reported on February 13.
Read:
PM Shehbaz briefed on progress of Rashakai SEZ
CEO Khattak shared that 98% of the infrastructure development in the Rashakai SEZ is completed and it will be the first of the four prioritised SEZs to become operational. It is a flagship project of the KP government, developed under the industrial cooperation of the China-Pakistan-Economic-Corridor (
CPEC
) framework that spreads over an area of 1000 acres.
Sharing details about the SEZ, the power transmission and transformation are near completion, which are vital parts of the project. The main purpose of this project is to set up export-oriented industrial units in the zone. The SEZ is expected to generate 250,000 to 300,000 employment opportunities.
Read:
SEZA announces plans to boost exports under CPEC
Reportedly, so far, 18 Pakistani and Chinese companies have signed joint venture agreements. The CEO highlighted that many investors have started construction work on the industrial units.

title: Resolution of G-9 Markaz’s issues top priority: President ICCI
full_text:
Islamabad: Islamabad Chamber of Commerce and Industry (ICCI) President Ahsan Zafar Bakhtawari has said that the completion of development work of Sector G-9 Markaz is his top priority task, and he will raise the issue with the Capital Development Authority (CDA), news sources reported on February 7.
Read:
CDA to allow skyscrapers of up to 1,000 ft in Blue Area
Bakhtawari made the remarks during the swearing-in ceremony for the newly elected office bearers of the G-9 Markaz Traders Welfare Association. He stated that he has brought the
tax-related issues
to the attention of the CDA and the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) in order to resolve them as soon as possible. The president emphasized that he recently met with CDA representatives and discussed issues pertaining to road rehabilitation, parking plaza construction, footpath repairs, filtration plant installation, and streetlight restoration. He added that the land for the parking plaza is already identified and that work on the project will start soon.
Read:
Construction work paces up on parking plaza in Blue Area-Islamabad
It is important to note that the G-9 market is one of the biggest markets after the Blue Area. Recently, CDA announced a comprehensive zoning plan for the city, regularising land in the city and designating specific residential and commercial areas.

title: ADB offers to finance ML-1 project
full_text:
Islamabad: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has offered to finance the USD 10 billion Karachi-Peshawar railway Main Line-1 (ML-1) project, news sources reported on February 9.
Read:
PR to upgrade ML-1’s infrastructure
The international lending agency offered to execute the project in the absence of an agreement with China. As per the sources, Pakistan has refused to take up the offer, citing the ongoing negotiations with China under the
government-to-government (G2G)
agreement. Speaking to the media, Planning Secretary Syed Zafar Ali Shah said that the federal government is interested in carrying out the multibillion-dollar project with China at the insistence of the latter. He said that the government would accommodate and take up the ADB’s offer in some other project.
Read:
Directives issued to expedite work on KCR, ML-1
It is important to note that the
ADB previously offered
to execute the ML-1 project but was declined at that time as well. At that time, Minister for Planning and Development Ahsan Iqbal had said that the government would utilise the ADB’s offer in other development projects, such as the Central Asian Regional Economic Cooperation Programme.

title: LDA begins a citywide anti-encroachment campaign
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) on Monday (February 6) launched a massive city-wide anti-encroachment drive to clear roads of unauthorized structures, news sources reported.
Read:
LHC prohibits LDA from starting multiple road development projects
The preliminary operation was carried out on Abdul Haq Road (Johar Town’s G-1 Market Road), where several buildings, including seven commercial bank branches, were sealed. In an official statement issued by the authority, it was highlighted that LDA teams also sealed four restaurants and 20 food points. Additionally, 60 establishments, including stores and buildings, were sealed for encroaching on violation of
Right of Way (RoW) rules
and for hampering traffic flow.
The operation was started in response to the Lahore High Court’s (LHC) orders to address market traffic issues that are causing smog and deteriorating air quality. The court ordered the authority to remove encroachments and convert the city’s nine roads into model roads with zero encroachments.
Read:
Gulberg Elevated Expressway made part of Lahore Master plan 2050
Here is a list of the
nine roads
where LDA intends to conduct an anti-encroachment drive:
LDA include Johar Town (Doctors Hospital to Expo Centre)
Main Boulevard, Allama Iqbal Town (Wahdat Road to Scheme Mor via Dubai Chowk)
Gulberg (Zahoor Elahi Road, Hali Road, MM Alam Road)
Mustafa Town (main road starting from Wahdat Road)
Jubilee Town (main road starting from Link Canal Road)
LDA Avenue-1 (main road starting from Jail Road)
Garden Town (from Kalma Chowk and to Faisal Town)
Township (Khokhar Chowk to Hamdard Chowk).

title: CDWP okays development projects of various sectors
full_text:
Islamabad: The Central Development Working Party (CDWP) has approved 10 development projects, worth PKR 87.17 billion, according to news published in the leading newspaper on February 7.
Read:
CDWP approves projects, refers 6 projects to ECNEC for approval
A meeting was held in which CDWP members met Federal Minister for Planning and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal. The meeting approved 10 uplift projects related to the Ministry of Housing and Works, the Ministry of Communication, the Ministry of National Health Services Regulations and Coordination, the Higher Education Commission (HEC), and the Ministry of Science and Technology.
The following are the details of the projects approved by
CDWP
:
Reconstruction of Turbat-Mand Road, from Ratodero-Gwadar Motorway (M-8) to Radeeq (Iranian border), at the total cost of PKR 20,992.875 million
Construction of Pun Panjgur-Gichak-Awaran Road, District Awaran, at the cost of PKR 29,638.353 million
Completion of Niheng Bridge at Rodbun, District Kech, at the cost of 673.688 million
Strengthening Institution for Refugee’s Administration (SIRA), at the cost of PKR 2,043 million
Establishment of a Cancer Hospital in Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT), at a total cost of PKR 3,406.169 million
Reconstruction of Mangopir, at the cost of PKR 3190.432 million
Read:
CDWP approves USD 9.1 bn railway ML-1 project
Construction of 26-megawatt Shagharthang Hydropower Project, at the cost of PKR 17,972.902 million
Gwadar Safe City Project (Phase-1), at the cost of PKR 4,966.905 million
Development of Ziarat Town at the cost of PKR 5,558.545 million
Establishment of the National Forensic Science Laboratory at the cost of PKR 1978.422 million
In the meeting, the forum forwarded the reconstruction of the Turbat-Mand Road, the construction of the Pun Panjgur-Gichak-Awaran Road, and the Shagharthang Hydropower project to the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC).

title: Kalma Chowk Remodelling project: Underpass’s one side likely to open soon
full_text:
Lahore: Punjab Central Business District Development Authority (PCBDDA) Executive Director (Technical) and Project Director Engineer Riaz Hussain shared that one side of the Kalma Chowk Remodelling project might open to traffic by February 15, a news source reported on February 5.
Read:
Kalma Chowk Underpass remodelling enters next phase; traffic plan shared
As per the details, one side of the underpass, from Barkat Market/Garden Town to Gulberg Main Boulevard and Liberty Chowk Roundabout, will become operational by February 15. To meet this deadline, construction has been geared up as additional labour has been deployed to continue work round-the-clock. Taking notice of the traffic hurdles and congestion, the government wants to completely make the said road operational ahead of the Pakistan Super League (PSL)’s cricket matches starting in Lahore on February 26.
Moreover, the project director mentioned that the caretaker Minister for Communication & Works Bilal Afzal has been assigned to monitor the progress of the project daily. An official of
PCBDDA
(whose name was not disclosed) mentioned that the work is underway related to piles, and excavation of the underpass – from the existing Kalma Chowk underpass entering the old Walton Airport area and terminating at the CBD project site.
Read:
Kalma Chowk Underpass progress to be reviewed regularly: Minister
The news source mentioned that 60% of the work on the first lintel of the tunnel has been completed. It was disclosed that work on the rigid pavement and laying of the base, sub-base, and asphalt will be completed by February 15. The official stated that once this is completed, the construction work will be shifted to lintel-related works for the remaining portion along with the starting work at the Centre Point, where the second underpass is planned. These points are expected to be opened to traffic by the end of next month.

title: CDA to operate Silver Line Bus service on IJP Road
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has decided to operate the Silver Line Metro Bus service on IJP Road to accommodate commuters, news sources reported on February 3.
Read:
CDA planning to expand metro bus service routes
The authority, in a board meeting, decided to develop bus bays and stations for Silver Line Bus service at every kilometre, with the inclusion of service areas, tuck shops, and lavatories, to provide better commuter services to passengers across Rawalpindi and Islamabad. The ongoing development work,
as per the PC-I
, includes the construction of a road, two flyovers, two bridges, and seven culverts, all of which are aimed at widening and overhauling IJP Road. Also, the CDA chairman had directed the completion of the project by March 23.
Read:
Plan in final stage to tap iron reserves in Chiniot, Kalabagh: PM
It is pertinent to mention that the IJP Road is one of the major arteries of the capital. It links Islamabad and Rawalpindi besides connecting G.T. Road and Islamabad Expressway.

title: RUDA, NRTC sign MoU for smart communication infrastructure
full_text:
Lahore: The Ravi Urban Development Authority (RUDA) on Wednesday (February 1) signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the National Radio & Telecommunication Corporation (NRTC), news sources reported.
Read:
RUDA to construct 100,000 low-cost houses near River Ravi
As per the MoU signed, the NRTC will provide infrastructural support by installing smart communication equipment in the existing as well as upcoming RUDA projects. Additionally, it will offer support for radio transmission, satellite, IT & Electronic Technological towers in RUDA’s smart city, safe city projects. On the occasion, NRTC Managing Director (MD) Brigadier Muhammad Asim Ishaque expressed that the department will deploy the latest and most modern solutions for public realms design, urban development, town planning, afforestation,
water treatment,
energy conservation and other related areas.
Read:
Govt shares land-use specifications for RUDA Industrial Estate project
It is important to note that RUDA is one of the first smart city projects in Pakistan that calls for the development of technology-rich cities. The project has also attracted Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) from KSA and the United Kingdom in its smart economic and industrial zone as well as highrise projects.

title: IJP Road to open to traffic by month end
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) Chairman Captain (retired) Muhammad Usman Younis on Tuesday (January 24) announced the construction of the IJP Road will be completed by the end of this month, news sources reported.
Read:
Landscaping work started on IJP Road
Sharing the news of the opening of the IJP Road via his Twitter account, the chairman said that the IJP road will be complete and fully functional by the end of this month. He further revealed that the Agha Shahi (9th) Avenue flyover will be completed later and open to traffic once all the piling work is complete.
Read:
IJP Road to open to traffic ahead of its deadline
It is important to note that
IJP Road
is one of the busiest roads in the city that connects Rawalpindi with Islamabad and is used by heavy and public transport frequently. The IJP Road construction project was launched in October 2021, with the initial date of completion set for April 2023. The project was awarded to the National Logistics Cell (NLC).

title: CDA shares construction update on Bhara Kahu Bypass project
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has initiated asphalt work on the Bhara Kahu bypass project with the aim to complete the work completed by the next month, according to news published in the leading newspaper on January 23.
Read:
CDA to release PKR 500mn for Bhara Kahu Bypass project
The news source mentioned that the asphalt work of Malpur Interchange and starting point of the road has been initiated. The CDA officials (whose names were not disclosed) mentioned that the said road project will be completed by the end of next month.
Read:
Construction update shared on Bhara Kahu Bypass project
Reportedly, the work on the elevated portion of the
Bhara Kahu Bypass
project is also in progress. The authority is working on the project round the clock and every effort is being made to complete the project as soon as possible. The officials mentioned that the elevated portion of the project will take more time due to the engineering requirements. The said portion is expected to be completed by mid-March.

title: LDA extends tender opening date of Babu Sabu Interchange project
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) has extended the tender opening of the Babu Sabu Interchange project, according to news published on January 24.
Read:
LDA floats three design options for Babu Sabu-Band Road rehabilitation
As per the details, the former Chief Minister (CM) Chaudhry Pervaiz Elahi laid the foundation stone for the
Babu Sabu Interchange project
. A spokesperson of LDA Engineering Wing (whose name was not disclosed) mentioned that the tender opening date for the said project was January 13, which was later extended to January 20. Now, the authority has once again extended the opening date to January 30.
Moreover, the authority issued letters of invitation to many construction companies for the Babu Sabu Interchange project. The news source reported that the construction work will start on Band Road from Babu Sabu Interchange to Ring Road. title: CDA urged to develop G-9 Markaz on priority

CDA to acquire 30 new metro buses, bidding results announced

CDA board approves layout plan of 1-14 Markaz

Blue Area

Deadline shared for completion of Islamabad’s signal-free IJP Road

by March 23, so work on the green belt must be completed before it.

title: LDA’s plan in place to remove encroachments on several roads, improve traffic flow

Govt to allocate Cholistan land to farmers for temporary cultivation for 5 yrs

title: CDA proposes changes to Zone III’s regulations
full_text:

title: FDA governing body approves Faisalabad Master plan 2040

Faisalabad: The Faisalabad Development Authority’s (FDA) governing body on Wednesday (December 28) approved the first draft of the Faisalabad Master Plan (2022-42), news sources reported.

title: CM Elahi chairs LDA governing body meeting, approves master plan

sustainable policy measures

title: PM announces PKR 5 bn to rehabilitate flood affectees in Sindh
full_text:
Karachi: Prime Minister (PM) Shebaz Sharif on Wednesday (December 21) announced a PKR 5 billion package for flood victims in Sindh, whose houses have been damaged in the flood, news sources reported.
Read:
World Bank approved USD 1.6 bn for flood relief efforts in Sindh
The prime minister visited the flood-ravaged areas of interior Sindh and announced a package to help with rehabilitation efforts. PM Shehbaz Sharif promised to do everything possible to minimize damage and provide compensation to individuals who had lost their livelihoods.
Additionally,
Minister of Planning and Development Ahsan Iqbal
presented the Prime Minister with a ‘Resilient, Recovery, Rehabilitation, and Reconstruction Framework/4RF’ plan. This plan outlines short, medium, and long-term strategies to help the survivors. The minister briefed the premier on the government’s ongoing efforts and their plan to participate in the Geneva Flood Donor Conference taking place in January 2023.
Read:
Sindh govt to build track for Yellow line near Jam Sadiq Bridge
It is important to mention that Pakistan has been devastated by some of the worst floods in decades. It is estimated that 40 million people have been displaced, and millions more have lost their livelihoods. With winter approaching, many are left without shelter.

title: Lahore Master Plan 2050 to ensure urban facilities for citizens: DG LDA
full_text:
Lahore: Lahore Development Authority (LDA) Director General (DG) Aamir Ahmed Khan has said that the Master Plan 2050 will ensure improved urban facilities for citizens of the Lahore Division over the next three decades, news sources reported on December 19.

EPA Punjab issues public interest notice for Lahore Master Plan 2050 assessment

title: German firm to set up waste-to-energy project in Lahore
