title: LDA to reclassify housing schemes for revenue generation
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) has decided to reclassify land in various housing schemes across the city to increase revenue generation, news sources reported on September 20.
Read:
LDA Land Use Rules 2020 finalised for promotion of construction activity
The final decision for the approval of the new policy will be taken by the LDA governing body. As per the new plan, after the reclassification, LDA will generate PKR 50 billion from the sales of plots. Moreover, societies will be required to build civic centres and commercial marketplaces to boost business prospects and increase income generation. Meanwhile, the LDA will welcome traders and investors to participate in the initiatives.
Furthermore, the housing complexes of
Gulberg and Garden T
own will be reclassified in the first phase, followed by Allama Iqbal Town, Quaid-e-Azam Town, and Faisal Town in the second phase.
Read:
Punjab to officially inaugurate Central Business District next month
It is vital to note that the LDA has requested
significant funding
from the government in order to satisfy financial demands and fund ongoing development initiatives. The organisation has also opted to diversify its own resources in order to develop solid and long-term revenue streams. One of the ways the LDA has decided to proceed with their strategy is to reclassify land in various regions of the city.

title: Punjab approves funds for Kamoke under Punjab Cities Program
developer: Punjab Minister for Local Government and Community Development
full_text:
Lahore: The Punjab government on Saturday (September 17) approved PKR 2.7 billion for the development of Kamoke city, news sources reported.
Read:
Punjab Cities Programme Phase-2’s launch up next
The funds have been approved by the government under the
Punjab Cities Program (PCP)
, which is supported by the World Bank (WB). Under the project, Kamoke will be provided with machinery, manpower, and funds for its welfare and development. Giving a briefing to the media, Punjab Minister for Local Government and Community Development (LGCD)
Mian Mahmood-ur-Rasheed
said that Kamoke is one of the 16 tehsils that would be developed under PCP and will be given the resources to make it a beautiful city. He stated that the funds will be utilised to improve water supply, sewerage, roads, street lighting, park maintenance, and solid waste management. Furthermore, 22,000 empty local government seats will be filled for improved administration.
Read:
Punjab to officially inaugurate Central Business District next month
It is worth noting that Kamoke is a nearby city to Lahore with a growing population. However, the city is also one of Punjab’s underdeveloped cities. The government has decided to grant funding to smaller cities in order to prevent people from migrating to larger urban regions.

title: WASA, JICA to install surface water treatment plant in Faisalabad
full_text:
Faisalabad: The Water and Sanitation Agency (WASA) Faisalabad and the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) have inked an agreement to construct a surface water treatment plant in the industrial city’s eastern sector, news sources reported on September 16.
Read:
JICA, WASA to join efforts to control urban flooding in Rawalpindi
The surface water treatment facility will be completed by 2025, with a PKR 7.25 billion grant-in-aid from JICA. According to the feasibility assessment, the 3.5 million gallons per day (MGD) capacity project will provide potable water to 0.2 million people, with the capacity later increasing to 10 MGD under the
Master Plan 2018-2038.
According to Project Concept-1 (PC-1), the capacity of the water treatment plant will be upgraded and expanded to 5 million MGD in the first phase and will also involve the construction of a 4.1-kilometre transmission line. Along with this, two ground reservoirs and two overhead reservoirs will be built, as well as primary, secondary, and
tertiary distribution systems
. In addition to this, water meters will be installed to manage water supply usage.
Read:
Punjab to establish WASA in Sialkot, Sahiwal under PICIIP
It is important to mention that the project was part of the Japan assistance programme that helps built water and sanitation projects in developing countries. This project was approved by the
Central Development Working Party (CDWP)
in 2020 and was scheduled to be completed in three years.

title: LDA to operationalise Manawan-Harbanspura-Ring Road project soon
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) has shared that the Manawan-Harbanspura-Ring Road project will be made operational by the end of next month, according to news published in the leading newspaper on September 9.
Read:
LDA directed to address matters of overseas Pakistanis on fast track basis
The PKR 182.219 million Manawan-Harbanspura Ring Road project has been pending for a long time, which causes traffic congestion and pollution. LDA Vice Chairman Naeemul Haq stated that the project is in the best interest of the public.  The vice chairman inaugurated the Nayal Pul-Fateh Garh Road rehabilitation project. During the inauguration, he mentioned that the authorities concerned should focus on completing sports complex projects in the city including Tajpura and Manawan sports complexes.
Read:
LDA asks funds for Kharak to Arfa Kareem Tower signal-free corridor
Moreover, the LDA officials (whose names were not disclosed) briefed the LDA Vice Chairman on the progress of work on the
Shahkam Chowk flyover
, Saggian and other road infrastructure improvement projects, and sports complex projects.

title: PC-1 approved for construction of link Margalla Road, Park Road, Bhara Kahu Bypass
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has approved PC-1s for major development projects – worth an accumulative PKR 12 billion – including the construction of Bhara Kahu Bypass, a road to link Margalla Road with Sector E-11, and the expansion and overhauling of Park Road, according to news published on September 7.
Read:
CDA Chairman confident of early completion of development projects
CDA Chairman (retired) Captain Mohammad Usman informed that the Development Working Party (DWP) approved all three projects. As per the details, a 5-kilometre-long road will be constructed to link
Margalla Road
with E-11. The road will start from GT Road and will end near Sector D-12 at Khayaban-i-Iqbal near E-11, where an interchange will be constructed. The project is expected to be completed within a year. Moreover, the city administrators revealed that the Margalla Road from GT Road to D-12 is near completion and will be completed by December.
Another PC-1 approved during the meeting was for the expansion and overhauling of Park Road. Under this project, Park Road will be expanded and widened from Rawal Chow to Tramari Chowk. It was mentioned that an additional lane will also be added to each side. According to sources, DWP has also instructed CDA to build a metro bus station on Park Road.
Read:
Bhara Kahu Bypass project: CDA making all-out efforts for on-time completion
Additionally, the Bhara Kahu Bypass project will include a 1.5-kilometre flyover, starting from Murree Road near Quaid-i-Azam University Stop and will end at Murree Road, near Jugi Stop. The project is expected to be completed within four months.

title: NLC to launch Karachi-Lahore shuttle cargo service
full_text:
Islamabad: Federal Minister for Planning & Development Ahsan Iqbal has ordered the National Logistic Cell (NLC) to launch a shuttle cargo service between Karachi and Lahore, news sources reported on September 6. The service will provide affordable cargo services to merchants and businesses in both metropolises.
Read:
NLC to construct bus stops for Green, Blue Line Metro in ISB
Reportedly, the minister issued the instruction during the  66th meeting of the National Logistics Board (NLB) on Friday (September 1). The minister asked the NLC to prepare a feasibility report on the project and the intended timeline for the proposed initiative. The minister said that the shuttle service will serve as an economical alternative to the private cargo services, which are driving the prices of commodities up.
Read:
Railways to improve cargo services to facilitate businesses
On this occasion, the minister was informed by the NLC management that at present, the total fleet of the NLC stands at 900 cargo vehicles, while the organization is planning to add 200 more to bring the total to 1,100 vehicles by the end of the fiscal year (FY) 2022-23.
Read:
NLC to complete 7th Avenue Interchange project before deadline
It is important to mention that NLC is one of the largest state-owned cargo and transportation services in the country that offers services across the spectrum.

title: Planning minister directs early completion of Gwadar Safe City project
developer: Federal Minister for Planning and Development
full_text:
Gwadar: Federal Minister for Planning and Development Ahsan Iqbal on Tuesday (August 30) directed the provincial government of Balochistan to complete the Gwadar Safe City Project (GSCP) in the next six months, news sources reported.
Read:
Omani firm to invest in Jacobabad-Gwadar rail connectivity project
The minister directed for Project Concept-1 (PC-1) of the GSCP to be revised before the next
Central Working Development Party (CDWP)
meeting in September. The minister also instructed that a technical consultation meeting be held with the
Punjab Safe City Authority (PSCA)
in the first week of September. The minister was informed that the provincial government has already signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the PSCA for technical support and project implementation. The minister said the project is extremely important for Gwadar as the city is a gateway to the China-Pakistan-Economic-Corridor (CPEC) project.
Read:
KP govt to set up Safe City project in Peshawar
According to the PC-1, the provincial administration plans to deploy 675 closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras in Gwadar. The provincial government has also purchased cameras for Quetta, which will be operated by the Quetta Safe City Authority (QSCA).

title: Bhara Kahu Bypass project: CDA making all-out efforts for on-time completion
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has launched all-out efforts for early completion of the Bhara Kahu Bypass project, news sources reported on August 29. CDA Chairman (retired) Capt Mohammad Usman has formed special teams for the monitoring and early completion of the project.
Read:
Development work starts in Bhara Kahu Housing Scheme Green Enclave-II
According to reports, the chairman met with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who directed the CDA administration to make every effort to complete the project within the next four months. The chairman informed the premier that the authorities had begun a topographic survey of the route, which would be complete in the coming days. After completing the survey, the CDA will complete the bypass engineering design before finalizing
Project Concept-I (PC-I)
.
A CDA spokesperson told the media that PM Shehbaz Sharif is personally supervising the project. The authority has already partnered with Frontier Work Organisation (FWO), and formal construction work is scheduled to begin in the second week of September.
Read:
Bhara Kahu Bypass: CDA seeks FWO’s PC-I draft to avoid further delays
It is important to note that the PKR 5 billion project is one of the city’s main road infrastructure development projects. According to its PC-I, the bypass would be five kilometres long, including a one-kilometre-long elevated road (flyover), with two interchanges, one at the beginning and one at the end.
The route will begin from Murree Road at the Quaid-i-Azam University stop, travel along Kayani Road, and return to Murree Road near the Jugi stop. Thereafter, it will feature a one-kilometre-long flyover that will end at the end of Bhara Kahu.

title: Punjab to start Heritage and Urban Regeneration project for walled city Lahore
full_text:
Lahore: Punjab Local Government & Community Development (LG&CD) Department has decided to start an urban regeneration project for the walled city of Lahore, news sources reported on August 26. The PKR 4 billion project will help restore old structures and monuments of the walled city.
Read:
Rehabilitation projects for Lahore’s Walled City approved
Reportedly, Municipal Secretary Syed Mubasher Hussain said that the areas around the
Shahi Qila, Badshahi Masjid,
and other neighbouring sites will be rebuilt in the project’s first phase. Once completed, the project is planned to boost tourism and recreational activities in the city. Moreover, it was announced that the government would seek external aid to restore buildings.
Read:
JICA, WASA to join efforts to control urban flooding in Rawalpindi
It is worth noting that the French government has recently agreed to fund the repair and renovation of the walled city. The French government will provide funds, technical experience, and consultancy services as part of the endeavour to restore Lahore’s historical mystique.

title: ADB starts loan disbursement for KP Cities Improvement Project
full_text:
Peshawar: The Asia Development Bank (ADB) has started rolling out the loan amount to the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) government under the Cities Improvement Project, news sources reported on August 24. The loan will be used to provide clean drinking water, sanitation services, and basic facilities in major cities across the province.
Read:
Peshawar declared capital Metropolitan government
According to reports, the KP government has disbursed PKR 240 million for the project after receiving funds from ADB. As part of the deal, ADB will offer a USD 1 billion loan, the largest in the province’s history, for the two-phase
city enhancement project.
In the first phase, funds will be used to provide basic services in five major cities: Peshawar, Mardan, Abbottabad, Swat, and Kohat. These services would be upgraded further in the second phase in Bannu, Dera Ismail Khan, and Peshawar BRT services.
Read:
Kuwaiti firm to invest in energy projects in KP
Furthermore, the ADB will provide funds to make the cities livable according to international standards by providing clean drinking water, improving drainage systems, building water treatment plants to make drainage water reusable, establishing dumping sites for waste disposal, and constructing public parks.

title: PKR 1.5 bn released to repair roads falling in Peoples Bus Service routes
full_text:
Karachi: City Administrator Barrister Murtaza Wahab announced that the Sindh government has released PRK 1.5 billion for the repair of roads in the route of Peoples Bus Service, according to news published in the national dailies on August 21.
Read:
Sindh govt inaugurates ‘Peoples Bus Service’ for Karachi’s seven routes
As per the details, the seven routes where Peoples Bus Service operate will be repaired in the first phase. After the repair of those roads, the rehabilitation of other roads will be started. The city administrator mentioned that the tendering process for awarding the contracts for road repairs will be initiated soon.
The administrator mentioned that under the development scheme, the construction and repair of Miran Shah Road, Chakiwara Road, Sher Shah Road, and 31 other roads in the Sindh Industrial Trading Estate (SITE) area, a road in Federal B Area, Shahrah-i-Noor Jahan in district central, the roads around Jinnah and Civil hospitals, and the main road of Orangi Town will be included.
Moreover, Administrator Wahab mentioned that a flyover in Gulistan-e-Johar will be developed at the cost of PKR 2 billion. Under the said project, a six-lane bridge will be constructed to resolve the traffic woes of the people of Korangi.
Read:
Directives issued to complete work on Karachi’s Peoples Bus Service route
He revealed that 157 development schemes for Karachi have been approved at the accumulated cost of PKR 18 billion. Out of the total, 146 schemes will be executed under the
Annual Development Programme
(ADP). So far, PKR 12 billion has been released for these schemes.

title: New Peshawar Valley Project: Intimation letters to be issued under land sharing formula
full_text:
Peshawar: The Peshawar Development Authority’s Board of Directors (BoD) on Monday (August 15) decided to issue Letters of Intimation (LOI) to the proposed New Peshawar Valley Project landowners, news sources reported. The LOI will be issued to the owners under the newly proposed land sharing formula devised by the authority and approved by the provincial cabinet.
Read:
New Peshawar Valley Project: KP CM orders establishment of site office
Reportedly, the decision was made during the civic body’s 9th Board of Directors meeting, which was chaired by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Chief Minister (CM) Mehmood Khan. On the occasion, CM Mehmood asked the authority’s members and development team to complete the construction of the various ongoing development works in the New Peshawar Valley Project. He said that the project is of extreme importance to the citizens and aims to provide a modern housing scheme for the citizens. During the meeting, the following decisions were made:
The board constituted a committee under the supervision of the Minister for Finance to make necessary amendments to
Peshawar Development Authority
’s Auction Regulations 2021. The said committee will submit its proposal to the board for final approval.
The board approved regularising 22 remaining contract employees of the authority recruited under the deceased-son quota.
The BoD has also approved the
land record Management Information System (MIS)
for the New Peshawar Valley Housing Scheme to digitise all matters related to the land records of the housing scheme.
Read:
Peshawar’s Warsak Road to get 2 high-rise buildings; groundbreaking held
On this occasion, the chief minister directed the relevant authorities to expedite progress on building an access road to the New Peshawar Valley. He also directed the concerned departments to make meaningful efforts for the urgent settlement of Regi Model Town’s Zone I, Zone II, and Zone V concerns.

title: WB to fund hydropower projects in Swat
full_text:
Islamabad:  The World Bank (WB) will fund the construction of two hydroelectric power projects in the Swat district this year, news sources reported. The projects include Maiden Hydropower Project (with a power generation capacity of 157 megawatts (MW)) and Gabral Kalam Hydropower Project (with a power generation capacity of 88 MW).
Read:
World Bank to offer USD 85 mn for low-cost housing finance
Reportedly, the announcement was made by WB Senior Energy Specialist Muhammad Saqib during a meeting with the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Energy Development Organization. It was announced that WB will offer USD 450 million to the provincial government, which will be used for the construction and operations of the hydroelectric projects. In addition, once completed in 2027, the project will earn a net income of PKR 13 billion annually for the provincial government of KP.
Read:
World Bank suggests building new port in Balochistan to address demand
It is also worth noting that the World Bank is supporting a
floating solar energy project
in partnership with the Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA). The initiative will be the country’s first of its kind to address energy-related issues.

title: Punjab to establish WASA in Sialkot, Sahiwal under PICIIP
developer: Punjab Local Government and Community Development
full_text:
Lahore: The Punjab government will establish the Water and Sanitation Agency (WASA) in the divisions of Sialkot and Sahiwal, news sources reported on August 5. The water management authority will be established under the Punjab Intermediate Cities Improvement Investment Programme (PICIIP).
Read:
Local Government reps discuss waste removal strategies for Karachi
According to reports, the decision was made during a meeting between Punjab Local Government and Community Development (LGCD) Secretary Imran Sikander Baloch and representatives from the
Asian Development Bank (ADB).
On the occasion, the secretary stated that work on development projects in both cities will be expedited following the monsoon. He also stated that the government would start new projects in
Sialkot and Sahiwal f
rom November this year.
Read:
China to build Sialkot’s first waste water treatment plant
Furthermore, he stated that the government has already completed several initiatives, including developing three public parks in Sialkot as part of the Punjab Intermediate Project (PIP) and providing modern solid waste management technology. He also mentioned that the government is interested in expanding the scope of the PICIIP initiative to seven more cities to enhance infrastructure and modernise it.

title: Sector I-12: CDA opens bids; development work to start soon
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has opened bids for the development of the stalled Sector I-12, news sources reported on July 31. Bids were received for the development work of the Sub-sector I-12/1 and I-12/4.
Read:
CDA shares updates on development work underway in Sector I-12
According to the source, the authority received the bids under sector 42 (F) of the Public Procurement Regulatory Authority(PPRA) rules. According to project
Concept-1 (PC-1)
, development work in subsectors I-12/1 and I-12/4 involves the construction of drainage systems, sewage networks, streets, culverts, and other development work.
As per the news, the CDA received the lowest bid of PKR 1.830 billion from a private enterprise, which is estimated to be 25% higher than the proposed price. The development work will commence soon after the firm is issued a work permit.
Read:
CDA to hire consultant for development of zoning plan
In another development, the CDA has announced its intentions to hire a private firm to
relocate the dumping site
from Sector I-12 to a new location. The dumping site has been one of the key causes behind the delayed development operations in the aforementioned sector. The authorities have already concluded development work in Sub-sectors I-12/2 and I-12/3, and owners have already received possession letters.

title: CDA to hire consultant for new landfill site
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has decided to appoint a third-party consultant to assist in identifying and surveying a new landfill site in the city to shift the existing dumping site in
Sector I-12
– as the development work kicks off in the sector, news sources reported on July 25. The consultant will prepare a feasibility report after choosing one of the four potential sites: Bhara Kahu, Sangjani, near Old Airport and another near Mandra.
Read:
CDA streamlines property transfer process
According to CDA Director General (DG) Shahjahan Khan, the new landfill site would be built in compliance with modern scientific and technological requirements. He went on to say that the current location in Sector I-12 is a dump site, not a landfill. Moreover, it was also revealed that the decision to shift the dump site from I-12 was made due to the recent resumption of construction activities in the said sector.
Read:
CDA hands over land for 5 dumping stations to MCI
It is worth noting that the CDA and the
Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA)
met last year to discuss the possibility of utilising Mandra near Chakwal as a combined dump site. The city generates around 6,000 tonnes of garbage, which is now dumped on I-12 because no adequate disposal site has been constructed yet.

title: CDA to acquire more buses for Blue, Green line service
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Saturday (July 23) decided to acquire 20 more buses for its Blue and Green Line Metro Bus Service within a week, news sources reported. The decision was made following an overwhelming response to the bus service in the federal capital.
Read:
CDA reviews progress of under-construction Blue, Green Line metro bus stations
The decision was reportedly made during a visit to the bus service by CDA Chairman Amer Ali Ahmed, who reviewed the city’s development work. The chairman was informed that a total of 5,800 and 6,000 people travel daily on the Blue and Green lines, respectively, while only eight buses run on each route, which is less than the required number.
Furthermore, it was informed that work on developing bus stations for both routes is ongoing and will be completed by August 14. Furthermore, the CDA has already granted a contract to the
Frontier Works Organization (FWO)
to build separate routes for the Blue and Green lines to keep them separate from regular traffic.
Read:
CDA shares updates on development work in E-12
It is worth noting that Prime Minister (PM) Shehbaz Sharif inaugurated the Blue and Green lines earlier this month to provide affordable public transportation for the capital city. The
Blue Line bus service
operates from Koral to PIMS, while the Green Line runs from Bhara Kahu to the PIMS stop.

title: KP bans construction on tourist sites till approval of master plans
full_text:
Peshawar: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Chief Minister (CM) Mehmood Khan on Saturday (July 23) banned all sorts of construction activities on tourist sites across the province until their master plans are approved, news sources reported. The ban was placed to prevent haphazard construction activities on provincial tourist sites.
Read:
300 vacancies approved for KP Tourism Police force
Reportedly, CM Mehmood made this decision while chairing a review meeting. He asked the provincial authorities to expedite work on fully functionalising the special purpose development authorities set up for tourist areas to enable the implementation of the
master plans
. Moreover, orders were issued for the strategy to be finalized within one week for the outsourcing of feasible rest houses along with the revenue generation plan.
Read:
Pakistan’s ranking on Intl’ Travel & Tourism Development Index increases
Additionally, the meeting also reviewed progress on the road infrastructure projects in tourist sites, including the 22-kilometre-long Mankial-Baddha Serai Road and the 24-kilometre-long Thandiani Road. The meeting was informed that the work orders for both road projects have been issued, and the construction work will start soon.

title: New Peshawar Valley Project: KP CM orders establishment of site office
full_text:
Peshawar: Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Chief Minister (CM) Mehmood Khan on Thursday (July 21) directed concerned authorities to establish a temporary site office for the New Peshawar Valley Project, news sources reported. The office will be used for the deployment of security staff for the project site.
Read:
Final approval granted to ‘New Peshawar Valley’ mega-city master plan
The directives were issued during a high-power meeting convened to review the project’s progress. During the meeting, Khan directed that a permanent site office be built as soon as possible to ensure that the project is completed on time. The meeting was informed that the concerned authority would identify land for setting up a permanent site office in the coming days. Sources also confirmed that the Project Concept-1 (PC-1) of the New Peshawar Valley Project has already been prepared.
Read:
New Peshawar Valley’s master plan to be approved in next meeting
CM Mehmood also asked concerned departments to send intimation letters to landowners by July 25 to complete the project on time. In response, the authorities’ representatives informed that the intimation letters to the landowners would be sent soon as per the decided land sharing formula. Reportedly, the government has already confirmed the acquisition of 13,898 kanal land for the project.
Read:
Peshawar BRT wins int’l award on using innovative solution
Furthermore, the meeting reviewed the sanitation, plantation, and security of the Hayatabad Phase V project. The minister instructed the
Peshawar Development Authority (PDA)
to complete the preliminary work of installing fences and gates to ensure the residents’ safety.

title: NTDC to build 500KV transmission line in Chakwal for industrial sector
developer: According to reports, the Germany-based KfW Development
full_text:
Chakwal: The National Transmission and Despatch Company Limited (NTDC) has acquired land to construct a 500-kilo volt (KV) power station for the Chakwal industrial sector, news sources reported on July 17. The PKR 8.926 billion projects have been sponsored by the Pakistani government and a German bank.
Read:
NTDC acquires soft loan for development of Jhimpir wind corridor
According to reports, the Germany-based KfW Development Bank will fund the project with EUR 43.76 million, which would be used to purchase land and equipment. The project comprises the construction of two
500 KV transmission lines
between Ghazi Brotha and Gatti, as well as Gakkar and Rawat. The project will strengthen the power supply situation in the
Islamabad Electric Supply Company (IESCO)
and Electric Supply Company (FESCO) territories. It will also enhance the voltage profile in Chakwal, Choa Saidan Shah, Gujjar Khan, Dandot, Pinanwal, Talagang, Padshahan, Chakri, and other FESCO-served districts.
Read:
Cement industry expected to expand by 50%
It is worth noting that the Chawal region is a well-known core of the country’s cement sector, with several leading cement manufacturers having manufacturing plants there. Improving power supply is anticipated to boost cement production and supply, which is critical for the construction industry.

title: France to finance Lahore Fort, buffer zone renovation project
full_text:
Lahore: The Punjab government, in collaboration with the French government, will carry out the Lahore Fort and buffer zone renovation project, news sources reported on July 13. The two projects of an accumulative worth of PKR 4.2 billion will be completed under the Heritage & Urban Regeneration in Lahore (HURL).
Read:
France provides soft loan for Chitral, Dargai hydropower projects’ restoration
Reportedly, an agreement was signed between the Walled City Lahore Authority (WCLA) and the Agence Française de Développement (French Development Agency). The French bank will provide assistance of EUR 22 million over a period of five years under HURL. The project includes the renovation of
Lahore Fort
and its buffer zone, which also includes the old food street behind the fort, Taxali, and adjacent parks.
Moreover, explaining the aims and objectives of the project, the French Ambassador to Pakistan Nicolas Galey said that the project will restore the
UNESCO heritage site
to its former glory and will also attract more tourists. He also added that the French government is proud to be part of the restoration project.
Read:
WCLA discovers 400-year-old tunnel at Lahore Fort
It is worth noting that the Lahore Fort is an internationally recognised heritage monument, having been classified as a site of cultural significance by UNESCO in 1984. The WCLA was founded in 2012 to oversee the walled city’s issues, including restoration, managing the Fort and other monuments erected during the Mughal and British eras.

title: LDA opens Shahkam Chowk Flyover to ease traffic
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) has opened the Shahkam Chowk Flyover to assist motorists over the holiday, news sources reported on July 10. The two-lane flyover project, worth PKR 4.233 billion, connects New Defence Road, Kahna/Ferozepur Road, and Multan Road at Mohlanwal, as well as many housing developments, villages, and minor settlements.
Read:
Shahkam Chowk flyover project: NLC to widen Defence Road, Lahore
Reportedly, the flyover has been opened to ease traffic flow during the Eid holidays. However, the finishing work of the project will continue 30 days after the opening of the flyover. This also includes moving electrical poles, beautification, and traffic line markings on the flyover.
At a press conference, LDA Chief Engineer (II) Mazhar Hussain Khan stated that the project was completed on schedule, which is a huge relief for inhabitants of Multan Road, Defence Road, and Bahria Town. He also stated that, in addition to improving traffic flow, the initiative will help improve the area’s environmental condition. In addition, he briefed the media on the PKR 4.3 billion
Saggian Road Rehabilitation
Project and the PKR 5 billion
Sheranwala Gate Project.
Read:
Punjab govt announces ‘Naya Lahore Development Package’
He added that both the projects are on schedule and would be completed within the next three to four months, subject to the settlement of any land acquisition concerns. He stated that the LDA has completed all outstanding initiatives targeted at enhancing the city’s traffic flow. It is vital to note that the government has set aside a
significant sum
for different road infrastructure improvements in the city, particularly at entry and exit points.

title: ADB proposes underground gas storage to improve supply
full_text:
Islamabad: To meet the increased energy demand and improve supply, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) has recommended the development of an Underground Gas Storage (UGS) in Sindh, news sources reported on July 10. The bank has prepared a feasibility study to build the storage at the now-depleted gas field of Khorewah-1 in Sindh’s Badin District.
Read:
Pakistan to develop underground strategic gas reserve for long term supply
Reportedly, the feasibility report prepared by the Danish consulting firm estimates the total cost of the project to be around USD 1.388 billion, with a storage capacity of 70 billion cubic feet (BCF) of gas. The field, once completed, will be filled with gas coming from various streams, including the
Turkmenistan–Afghanistan–Pakistan–India (TAPI)
Pipeline, the
Offshore Gas Pipeline Project (OGPP)
, and the Iran-Pakistan (IP) Gas Pipeline. The stored gas will be supplied to the areas of high demand using the existing gas distribution infrastructure of the Sui Gas supply company.
Furthermore, the strategic gas reserves will deliver gas to the southern region of Pakistan during the winter, whilst the UGS storage would largely offer natural gas to Pakistan’s northern region. This has the benefit of supplying gas straight from the LNG storage facility rather than re-gasifying the LNG, moving it to the northeast to the UGS plant, and then delivering it back to the south at peak demand.
Read:
GHQ proposes strategic oil reserves in Gwadar
It is vital to note that Pakistan is on the verge of a gas shortage as local supplies have decreased and international gas prices have skyrocketed. The government has already planned the construction of strategic underground gas reserves in various places of the country, including Gwadar, to address the situation.

title: NHA invites bids for linking North Waziristan with CPEC’s M-14
full_text:
Waziristan: The National Highway Authority (NHA) on Monday (July 05) invited requests for proposal (RFP)s of consultancy services for the feasibility study and detailed design for a project aimed to connect Waziristan with Motorway-14 (M-14) – which is part of the western alignment route of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), news sources reported.
Read:
Pakistan welcomes Afghanistan’s interest in CPEC
Under the project, the federal government will allocate funds for the 184-kilometre-long road project connecting Ghulam Khan in
North Waziristan
with the said motorway section under the Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP) 2022-23 through a separate head/allocation. The authority has set August 10 as the deadline for submitting proposals, while a pre-proposal meeting will be convened on July 19 at the
NHA headquarters in Islamabad.
The procurement will be conducted using the single-stage-two-envelopes process.  The project, when completed, will connect the Waziristan and CPEC Motorway 14 routes with the Pakistan-Afghanistan border.
Read:
FBR to abolish 12 checkpoints set along Iran, Afghanistan borders
Moreover, Ghulam Khan is the third most significant border crossing between Pakistan and Afghanistan, after Torkham and Chaman. The Esa Khel Interchange is located on M-14 in the Punjab district of Mianwali, near the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) district of Lakki Marwat. The Bannu district of KP is located between Mianwali and Ghulam Khan.

title: KMC to get PKR 32 bn development budget for FY2022-23
full_text:
Karachi: The Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) will get a PKR 32.21 billion development budget for the fiscal year (FY) 2022-23, news sources reported on June 30. The total receipts are estimated at PKR 32.21 billion, whereas the total expenditure is PKR 32.19 billion.
Read:
KMC moves high court regarding Frere Hall’s beautification campaign
Reportedly, the budget was presented by Karachi Administrator Murtaza Wahab at a press briefing here at Khaliq Dina Hall. According to budget documents, the KMC would get PKR 32.21 billion, which includes current revenue of PKR 26.61 billion and capital receipts of PKR 0.5 billion, as well as PKR 5 billion in the District
Annual Development Programme (ADP)
sections.
Similarly, the Sindh government would transfer PKR 18.6 billion under the ‘OZD share’ and PKR 200 million under the entertainment tax, with liabilities of PKR 1.85 billion on KMC also scheduled to be remitted to KMC. Reportedly, the corporation is expecting to get PKR 1.477 billion in revenue from land enforcement, estate, Katchi Abadi regulation, PD Orangi, and parking taxes.
Expenditure
On the spending side, the KMC will spend PKR 32.195 billion on different city development projects:
PKR 8.67 billion will be spent on non-development budget items such as pensions and miscellaneous expenses, including bail-out packages for subordinate departments
PKR 5.756 billion has been allocated for medical and healthcare services
PKR 3.943 billion has been allocated for municipal services
PKR 2.72 billion will be spent on development projects
PKR 2.079 billion has been allocated for the engineering department of KMC
PKR 1.422 billion has been earmarked for land enforcement and
Katchi Abadi welfare
, including PD Orangi and parking
Read:
Sindh govt inaugurates ‘Peoples Bus Service’ for Karachi’s seven routes
PKR 1.184 billion has been allocated for parks and horticulture activities
PKR 973 million has been allocated for culture, sports and recreation activities
PKR 898 million has been allocated for the Finance and Accounts department
PKR 888 million will be spent on the
Competitive and Livable City of Karachi (CLI
CK
)
PKR 500 million has been allocated for the development of roads, sidewalks, sewerage lines, bridges, and intersections across the city
PKR 271.38 million will be spent on road repair and rehabilitation
PKR 250 million will be spent on the management of street lights on major roads
PKR 184.23 million has been allocated for the law department
PKR 172 million has been earmarked for the improvement of general infrastructure
PKR 115 million has been set aside for the purchase of ventilators and medical equipment for KMC-managed hospitals
PKR 85 million will be spent on the improvement of Karachi Zoo, and Safari Park, and the purchase of new animals

title: CDA, NADRA sign agreement for digital property management
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) signed an agreement with the National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) to develop a biometric property verification system, news sources reported on June 30. The system will use biometrics to prevent forgery, fraud and illegal transfer of properties in the capital city.
Read:
NADRA to provide support for Sehat Sahulat Programme in Punjab
The agreement was signed in the presence of NADRA Chairman Tariq Malik and CDA Chairman Amir Ali Ahmed at the former’s headquarters. According to the terms of the agreement, NADRA will design and implement a Biometric Verification Solution (BVS) for the sale, purchase, and transfer of all assets in the
Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT)
.
Read:
CDA invites bids for maintenance services in monsoon season
This new system will benefit a total of 20,000 property sales, purchases, and transfers that occur in the CDA each year.  Speaking on the occasion, NADRA Chairman Tariq Malik stated that the digital solution provided by NADRA has the capacity to biometrically verify citizens and their family members to meet the challenges faced by any organization. This, in addition to the current affidavit system, provides an additional layer of protection against fraud, while also improving the internal workings of the CDA.
Read:
NADRA facilitation centre to be set up along Islamabad Expressway
According to CDA Chairman Amir Ali, the BVS system will also increase the organization’s transparency, provide accurate identification, and minimize the risk of unwanted breaches within the CDA.

title: Monsoon Rain: CDA setup flood emergency response teams
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has decided to create a resource allocation plan to coordinate flood relief preparations and emergency response in the event of approaching pre-monsoon rainfall, news sources reported on June 21. A total of PKR 50 million has been set aside for the purchase of flood management and water pumping equipment.
Read:
PMD forecasts heavy pre-monsoon rains in June
Reportedly, to monitor and manage the impending rainy season, the CDA has also established the
District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA)
, with Deputy Commissioner (DC) Arif Nawaz as convenor. Furthermore, to minimise urban floods, the committee will use data from the Survey of Pakistan to map nullahs and manage the resources required for effective coordination. The CDA has asked that the DDMA focus on sensitive and critical locations, such as Katchi Abadis, to avoid any loss of human lives.
Furthermore, in order to coordinate flood relief activities, associated departments such as IESCO, food, and livestock are placed on alert with instructions to assure the availability of all essential measures and supplies, as well as human resources.
Read:
CDA prepared for monsoon emergencies
It is crucial to note that the
urban flood in E-11
caused significant damage during the 2021 monsoon season. It was caused by debris and encroachment clogging the flood channel.

title: Govt approves rehabilitation of 10 roads in Gujrat
full_text:
Gujrat: The Punjab government has approved the rehabilitation of 10 main roads in the rural areas of
Gujrat
, according to a news story published on June 20.  As per the details, the 6-kilometre-long portion of Gujrat-Jalapur Jattan Road up to the University of Gujrat’s (UoG) Hafiz Hayat Campus Road will be restored at the total cost of PKR 312 million. Here are the details of the road rehabilitation projects:
Read:
Construction work starts on PKR 74 mn cricket stadium in Gujrat
22-kilometre-long portion of Mungowal-Dina Road will be restored at the total cost of PKR 879 million
19-kilometre portion from Head Ali Beig to Sara-i-Alamgir city, at the accumulative cost of PKR 636 million
18-kilometre-long portion from Shaheen Chowk to Mungowal of Gujrat-Sargodha Road, at the total cost of PKR 475 million
18-kilometre-long area of Kunjah-Dinga Road, at the accumulative cost of PKR 390 million
14-kilometre-long portion from Sadoke to Matwanwala of Gujrat-Dinga Road, at the total cost of PKR 582 million
11-kilometre-long part of Tarikha to Khanki headworks road, at the cost of PKR 264 million
10-kilometre-long portion of Kolta to Dilawarpur Road, at the cost of PKR 444 million
8.25-kilometre-long part from Bhelesar Morr to Daulatnagar of Gujrat-Bhimber Road, at the estimated cost of PKR 300 million
7.5-kilometre portion from Gujrat city to Sahdiwal Town of Gujrat-Shadiwal Road, at the cost of PKR 180 million
Read:
Restoration work kicks off at old GT road, Gujrat
Previously, the 5-kilometre road section from Jalapur Jattan city to UoG Road was dualized and reconstructed with the funds provided by the federal government. However, no more road infrastructure structure projects could be part of the Annual Development Program (ADP) due to several reasons. According to officials (whose names were not disclosed), the schemes are expected to become part of the ADP as a supplementary grant.

title: CDA approves slight realignment of Margalla Road
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) board has approved a slight realignment of Margalla Road near Shah Allah Ditta in order to preserve the century-old graveyard, according to news published in the leading newspaper on June 18.
Read:
Margalla Road project: first phase likely to complete in July
The board meeting was held with Chairman Amer Ali Ahmed in the chair to approve the realignment of the road. As per the details, the CDA board has approved the shifting of the roads towards the southern side and Sectors C-13, D-12 to save the graveyard. The chairman also ordered the relevant authorities to initiate the compensation process for the affectees of the new alignment.
Read:
CDA to realign Margalla Road to save old graveyard
Moreover, the said road project starts from GT Road and will end at D-12. Once the interchange will be constructed, the small portion of 11th Avenue will be
connected to Khayaban-i-Iqbal
. The attendees were informed that the construction work on Margalla Road Phase-I (from GT Road to D-12) is 70% completed. The Frontier Work Organisation (FWO) was facing a problem completing the project because of the graveyard. Previously, the authority was planning of constructing a flyover or a tunnel to save the graveyard.

title: KDA DG shares update on ‘Karachi Master Plan 2047’
full_text:
Karachi: Karachi Development Authority (KDA) Director General Syed Muhammad Ali Shah stated that work on ‘Karachi Master Plan 2047’ is underway, according to a news story published on June 16.
Read:
KDA to launch affordable housing schemes, development projects soon
During a meeting held at the Karachi Chamber of Commerce & Industry (KCCI), KDA DG Shah revealed that the feasibility of the plan has been approved under which the city’s infrastructure will be revamped to state-of-the-art infrastructure as per international standards.
In the meeting, the KDA DG revealed that the authority is working on the K-IV project and infrastructure development projects related to it. The authority is undertaking projects where the water supply network under K-IV was unavailable.
Sharing details about Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) project, KDA DG Shah disclosed that several buses were operating under Green Line BRT and some buses have arrived for Orange Line BRT – which will be completed soon. Also, work on Red Line Project will be initiated soon. He added that the said projects will be completed within the shortest possible time.
Moreover, the director general mentioned that due to a lack of coordination between Sindh Building Control Authority (SBCA), KDA, and Water Board several problems were created during development work. Fortunately, this issue has been addressed and coordination among departments has been improved.
Read:
Sindh to form separate body for Karachi master plan development
Reportedly, the biggest issues faced by Karachi were illegal constructions, rising activities of the land-grabbing mafia, encroachments, unlawful parking, and misuse of public parks. To resolve these problems, KDA DG has decided to take strict actions against
encroachment
and illegal construction.

title: PKR 16 bn approved for development of 33 roads in AJK
full_text:
Muzaffarabad: The Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Cabinet Development Committee (CDC) has approved 33 projects worth PKR 16.32 billion road projects, according to a news story published in the leading newspapers on June 12.
Read:
AJK to set up tourism authority
A meeting, chaired by Prime Minister (PM) Sardar Tanveer Ilyas, was held to review the ongoing projects of a 620-kilometre-long road network by Communications and Works (C&W) developed under the ‘Kashmir Development Package’. As per the details, 220-kilometres were approved for the southern district of Bhimber, Mirpur, and Kotli while 400-kilometres were approved for the northern districts of Neelum Valley, Sudhnoti, Haveli,
Muzaffarabad
, Jhelum Valley, Poonch, and Bagh.
Read:
PM AJK directs formulation of strategy for industries’ growth
Moreover, the meeting also approved reconditioning/construction of 30-kilometres long roads in constituencies LA-4, and LA-3 of Mirpur district and an 18-kilometre long road from Chattar Klass to Danna in district Muzaffarabad. It was also informed that the stability of land on either side of the roads will be ensured to prevent landslides. The trees will be planted on the sides of the roads as well. PM Ilyas mentioned that weighing scales will be installed on the main highways so that the overloaded vehicles will not damage the roads.

title: CDA retrieves 350 kanals in grand anti-encroachment drive in E-12
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Wednesday (June 08) conducted a grand anti-encroachment drive in Sector E-12 to retrieve government land, news sources reported. The authorities successfully retrieved 350 kanals of state land from illegal encroachers.
Read:
Margalla Hills Road: CDA gives six-month extension to FWO for completion
Reportedly, the operation was conducted in the presence of a heavy police contingent and the city district administration. It was revealed that the authorities had demolished illegal streets, boundary walls and other constructed structures on state land. The land was later transferred to the concerned departments.
Read:
CDA open bids for awarding Bhara Kahu bypass project
It is pertinent to mention that the
CDA is now developing Sector E-12
. The authority has allocated 289.805 million for the development of water supply, construction of connecting roads, including main highways, drainage system, installation of street lights, sewerage network, and other uplift works. The authority also handed over 120 plots to the owners in March this year.

title: President reconstitutes National Economic Council under Article 156
developer: PM Shehbaz has nominated Minister for Planning and Development
full_text:
Islamabad: President Dr Arif Alvi has reconstituted the 13-member National Economic Council (NEC), an economic advisory body to manage overall economic conditions and formulate plans, news sources reported on June 08. The body has been revived under article 156 of the constitution of Pakistan.
Read:
‘Value of land in Rawalpindi Ring Road’s economic zones inching up’
Reportedly, the president approved the formation of the body with the
Prime Minister (PM) Shehbaz Sharif
as its head, and the four chief ministers of provinces as their permanent members. The body is composed of members of the federal and provincial governments, as well as members nominated by the premier and chief ministers, respectively. It was also revealed that PM Shehbaz has nominated Minister for Planning and Development Ahsan Iqbal, Finance Minister Miftah Ismail, Commerce Minister Syed Naveed Qamar and Communications Minister Asad Mehmood from the federal government to become part of the NEC.
The provincial governments have nominated Sardar Awais Ahmed Khan Leghari from Punjab, Senator Nisar Khoro from Sindh, Taimur Saleem Jhagra from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) and Noor Muhammad Damar from Balochistan.
Read:
Gwadar International Airport gets ECNEC’s nod
As per the constitution, the committee is bound to meet twice per year to deliberate on matters of mutual interest and economic distribution between the provinces and the federal government.

title: Rawal Dam Interchange to open ahead of its committed timeline
full_text:
Islamabad: The Frontier Works Organisation (FWO) is working on the construction of the Rawal Dam Interchange and will complete the project one month ahead of its committed timeline, which was October 2022, according to news published on June 4.
Read:
Directives issued to expedite work on Rawal Dam Interchange project
Capital Development Authority (CDA) Member Engineering Syed Munawar Shah revealed that Prime Minister (PM) Shehbaz Sharif has directed the civic agency to
complete the project
by September 2022. The member engineering stated that the project was awarded to the joint venture of Calson and Maqbool Associates in June 2020. However, the work was stalled because of the price hike.
Read:
Rawal Dam Interchange, 7th Avenue ordered to complete ahead of October deadline
PM Shehbaz handed over the project to FWO and asked to complete the project without any increase in the cost of the contract. As per the details, the project features one underpass, an overhead bridge, several slip roads, and an underpass connecting Margalla Town. The said project is being constructed at the junction of Park Road, Murree Road, and Club Road.

title: Development work begins on alternate road in Tatapani, Chilas
full_text:
Gilgit: Gilgit-Baltistan (GB) Chief Minister (CM) Khalid Khurshid Khan inaugurated development work on the alternate road in the Tatapani area of Chilas so that travellers can avoid the landslide-prone section of the Karakoram Highway, according to news published on June 7.
Read:
CPEC: Pakistan to include three road infrastructure projects in JCC
CM Khurshid stated that the alternative road should be constructed on an emergency basis. As per the details, the PKR 55 million worth project is expected to be completed by December 1. Moreover, CM Khurshid informed that the special
economic zone
was being established in Diamer for the development of the area. He also disclosed that power and sewerage projects have been started in Chilas. Additionally, Chilas Development Authority is being set up. It was revealed that work on the Daral-Tangir road will start soon and medical, dental, and nursing colleges will be established in Chilas.
Read:
NLC starts work on 76-km Gilgit-Shandur Road
The ceremony was attended by Minister for Excise Haji Shah Baig, Diamer Deputy Commissioner Fayyaz Ahmed, GB Assembly Member Maulana Fazal Rahim, and Minister for Health Haji Gulbar Khan.

title: Committee approves development projects for Kohat
full_text:
Kohat: District Development Advisory Committee (DDAC) Chairman Ziaullah Bangash has approved PKR 60 million development projects for Kohat, according to news published in the leading newspaper on June 2.
Read:
Kohat property dealers’ association urges to lift ban on land transfer
DDAC Bangash chaired a review meeting at the office of Deputy Commissioner Roshan Mehsud. During the meeting, the head of departments briefed the DDAC on the ongoing development projects. The DDAC directed the relevant authorities to speed up the work on the projects for timely completion. Moreover, the DDAC Bangash mentioned that after the completion of Kacahi Road, work on Khawaja Abad, Chargbagh, Ambar Banda, Marai, Hospital, and Junglekhel roads will be started.
Read:
KPRA launches registration campaign for businesses in DI Khan, Kohat
Earlier, the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) government approved PKR 200 million funds for the rehabilitation and
construction of new roads
in the PK-82 constituency. The Provincial Minister of Irrigation Arshad Ayub Khan Orakzai announced that a cadet college will be established in the Orakzai district in order to provide quality education to locals.

title: China-Pak launches Green CPEC Alliance
full_text:
Islamabad: The Pakistan-China Institute (PCI), in collaboration with the Sustainable Development Policy Institute (SDPI), has launched Pakistan’s first ‘Green China Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) Alliance’, news sources reported. The program has been launched for the decarbonisation of the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) and to make it more sustainable.
Read:
CPEC: Pakistan to include three road infrastructure projects in JCC
According to reports, the programme was unveiled during a conference on
Pakistan’s sustainable development
and the BRI. It was said that the major goal of the initiative would be to bring governments from both sides, as well as ministries and businesses, together to create eco-friendly projects. The primary goal would be to encourage and steer Chinese infrastructure expenditures away from carbon-intensive investments and toward green infrastructure projects, such as transitioning from coal to renewable energy sources such as wind, solar, and hydropower.
On the occasion, Acting Ambassador of the People’s Republic of China in Pakistan Pang Chunxue stated that the green initiatives under the BRI will assist the people of Pakistan while also helping to combat
global climate change.
She stated that Pakistan and China’s relations have improved in a variety of sectors, including sustainable development, contemporary food security, and energy infrastructure.
Read:
All economic zones in KP to run on solar energy
It is vital to note that under BRI, China and Pakistan are implementing some of the world’s largest man-made infrastructure projects, with a combined value of USD 62 billion. The development of the Gwadar seaport is one of the major projects, which also includes smart cities.

title: Govt to allocate PKR 700 bn for PSDP in FY23: Ahsan Iqbal
full_text:
Islamabad: Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal said on Thursday (June 2) that the government will allocate PKR 700 billion for the Public Sector Development Program (PSDP) in the fiscal year 2022–23 (FY23), news sources reported. He said that, in total, 44% of PSDP projects are provincial projects and the remaining 46% are federal projects.
Read:
Federal govt completes 27 small dams in Balochistan under PSDP
The minister stated that the government’s major PSDP  priorities of FY23 will be to increase spending on youth, developing infrastructure, and water scarcity. Furthermore, he stated that the government will generate an additional PKR 200 billion for PSDP through
public-private partnerships (PPP)
in order to fund further development projects.
In addition to the nine economic zones under CPEC, he said that the government will include the Hattar Special Economic Zone project in the CPEC project once again.
Read:
CPEC JWG: Pak, China review progress of SEZs
It is important to mention here that the government has reduced the development budget amid economic stress and increasing inflation and the global market changes.

title: Govt to spend PKR 130 mn on Sagian Road
developer: The work order for the project was issued by Lahore Development
full_text:
Lahore: The Punjab government will spend PKR 130.73 million on the beautification and rehabilitation of Sagian Road bypass and Phool Mandi, news sources reported on May 28. Under the project, the entrance and exit points of the interchange will be beautified.
Read:
LDA asks for PKR 202 bn development budget for FY-23
Reportedly, the government has issued a work order to the lowest bidder for the project. HRD Construction won the bid at PKR 130.75 million. The project is slated to be completed within a period of three months. As per the detailed order, the contractors will beautify the entrance and exit points with artwork, painting of roadside fences, and plantation on both sides of the road.

LDA Chief Muhammad Ali Randhawa
visited the Sagain Road interchange project construction site and examined the ongoing development work. The chief was informed that 55 % of the development work worth PKR 3.40 billion had been accomplished.
Read:
Sagian Road Project: Punjab govt approves PKR 4.45 bn extended PC-1
The contractor will construct a 4.4-kilometre road on both sides from Ravi Bridge to Phool Mandi Chowk, a 1.2-kilometre road from Phool Mandi Chowk to Lahore Shiekhupura road, and a 3.1-kilometre road from Phool Mandi Chowk to the Faizpur Interchange. In addition, sewerage work in the area will also be completed to resolve the long-standing water problem. Moreover, the completion of the project would benefit 100,000 vehicles every day.

title: ADB to allocate USD 2 bn for development projects in Pak
full_text:
Islamabad: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) on Thursday (May 26) announced a proposal of USD 2 billion in funding for development projects in Pakistan during the coming months, news sources reported. The funding will be released following consultation with public and private organisations.
Read:
ADB disburses over USD 1 bn in loans, aid
According to reports, the ADB would support initiatives related to food security, water, irrigation, and education. The announcement was made by ADB Deputy Country Director Asad Aleem during a consultation meeting with the
Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI)
in Lahore. He stated that consultative sessions had also been held with the governments of Sindh and Punjab in order to ensure the proper execution of vital programmes for Pakistan’s development.
Read:
World Bank shares estimates on Punjab real estate sectors’ tax potential
LCCI Senior Vice President Mian Rehman Aziz Chan said on the occasion that ADB has funded approximately USD 37 billion for the country’s socio-economic development since 1996. This excellent collaboration has resulted in the development of society’s lowest segments

title: LDA DG visits LDA Avenue-1 office, directs safety measures
full_text:
Lahore: Lahore Development Authority (LDA) Director General (DG) Chaudhry Muhammad Ali Randhawa on Thursday (May 26) visited the offices of LDA Avenue-1, news sources reported. He directed the officers to maintain effective safety measures for the scheme’s data security.
Read:
LDA City’s Jinnah Sector land acquisition to be completed soon
According to reports, on his first visit to the LDA Avenue-1 office, the newly-appointed DG visited several departments of the projects and examined current development activity. The LDA officers informed the DG of the project’s operations. Randhawa directed the officers to maintain effective fire safety procedures in order to preserve the residents’ files and data.
He also urged the concerned departments to maintain the maximum degree of security for the residents and to renovate the schemes’ parks and roads. He also instructed the officers to create a committee to address concerns related to the development of the schemes on a priority basis. It is worth noting that LDA Avenue-1 is one of the LDA’s own initiatives.
Read:
LDA Avenue 1 affectees compensated, details uploaded on website
The LDA management has acquired land in the adjoining
Chiniot Housing Scheme
to accommodate file holders.

title: CDA shares details on 1st phase of Bhara Kahu bypass construction
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has shared details of the construction of the first phase of the Bhara Kahu bypass, according to the news reports published on May 25.
Read:
CDA to swap 327-acre land with Islamabad Wildlife Management Board
The CDA officials informed that the said project will be divided into two phases. The first phase starts from GT Road Sangjani to D-12 and the second phase is
Bhara Kahu bypass
. According to the CDA officials, the work on the first phase of the project is in full swing with 70% of the work completed. It was mentioned that the work on the Bhara Kahu bypass will be started soon. The CDA engineering wing officials mentioned that the engineering design and alignment of the bypass have already been finalised by Army’s E&C branch. The city managers are waiting for the draft of PC-1, which is being reviewed b the Frontier Works Organisation (FWO).
Read:
CDA plans to boost water supply to 50 MGD by month’s end
After receiving the PC-1 from FWO, the CDA will send it for final approval to the Development Working Party (DWP). Once the PC-1 gets approved, work will start on the construction of the bypass. The Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) draft report has been submitted to the Pakistan Environment Protection Agency (EPA). Reportedly, the 7.8-kilometre long bypass was designed to provide an alternative route for people travelling to Galyat, Kashmir, and Murree. As per the details, the proposed bypass will start from the Malpur area and end near Satra Meel on Murree Road.

title: PR prepares PC-1 for rehabilitation of Lahore-Chak Amru rail line
full_text:
Lahore: The Pakistan Railway (PR) has prepared PC-1 for the rehabilitation of the Lahore-Chak Amru rail line and will submit it to the federal government to be included in the Public Sector Development Programme in the next fiscal year, according to news published in the national dailies on May 23.
Read:
Pakistan Railways launches first cold chain freight service
Chairman Evacuee Trust Property Board (ETPB) Chairman Dr Habib Ur Rehman Gilani revealed that a meeting was held at Narowal in which attendees were informed that PC-1 worth PKR 14 billion of Lahore-Chak Amru through
Narowal and Kartarpur rail section
was prepared for funds allocation. As per the details, the PR will replace critical stretches of the existing track and maintain the existing engines, coaches, and relay interlocking/signalling system.
Moreover, the said rail line can be of international significance since Sikhs can use it to reach Kartarpur and other temples within the shortest time. Keeping this in mind, the PR has been asked to complete it as a top priority. Reportedly, the train is operational from Lahore to Narowal; however, due to the dilapidated condition of the track, the train’s speed is limited to 60 km per hour.
Read:
Pakistan Railways plans to connect KCR with BRT lines
Chairman Gilani has asked the PR officials to rehabilitate the rail track from Narowal to Kartarpur and start operating two trains daily. If the train is restored completely, the train speed can be increased to 120 km per hour and travel time from Lahore to Kartarpur will be reduced to one hour. PR Additional General Manager Amir Baloch mentioned that the PC-1 of the project will be submitted to the government for approval.

title: KCR to be executed on LHR’s orange line metro model: Minister
full_text:
Karachi: Minister of Planning Development and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal stated that Karachi Circular Railway (KCR) project will be implemented on the same model as Lahore’s Orange Line Metro Train, according to a news story published on May 21.
Read:
Centre to assist in completion of HYD-SKR Motorway, KCR projects
A preparatory meeting of the joint working group on transport infrastructure was held recently and was chaired by Planning Development and Special Initiatives Minister Ahsan Iqbal. The meeting was attended by officials of the National Highway Authority (NHA), the China Pakistan Economic Corridor Authority, Gwadar Port Authority, and the Ministry of Planning and Railways.
As per the details, the Minister has directed the railway authorities to evaluate the cost of the 250 km/hour track for the future viability of the project. During the meeting, Planning Development and Special Initiatives Minister Ahsan Iqbal discussed the Karachi-Peshawar Railway Line (
ML-1
) project and expressed concerns over the delay. He asked the relevant authorities to expedite the pace of the said project.
Read:
PM Sharif promises funds for K-4 project, KCR’s inclusion in CPEC
Moreover, the KCR project will construct a 43-kilometre long world-class mass transit system using environmentally-friendly electric trains. Additionally, the project includes the development of underpasses and flyover along the KCR route and the elimination of 22-level crossings.

title: RDA to kick start Kutcherry Chowk remodelling project soon
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) will start working on the PKR 5 billion Kutcherry Chowk remodelling project soon, news sources reported on May 23. The Project Concept-1 (PC-1) and the feasibility report of the project have already been approved.
Read:
Expansion of road connecting Kohat’s Kutcheri Chowk with PAF Square in works
In a media briefing regarding the project, RDA spokesperson Hafiz Irfan stated that the authorities will work on the relocation of telephone lines, gas pipelines, and other municipal utilities in the first phase of the project. After the first phase is completed, the development of the
signal-free corridor will begin
. Furthermore, he stated that the project will entail the building of a flyover and three underpasses to accommodate a larger volume of traffic.
Read:
RDA shares development plan, seeks PKR 1.18 tr for infrastructure
It is worth noting here that the Kutcherry Chowk project is one of the three mega projects launched by RDA for the traffic management of the city. The other two projects include the construction of
Ammar Chowk
and the Defence Road project.

title: WAPDA to double hydroelectric power by year 2028-29
full_text:
Islamabad: The Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA) has devised a strategy to double hydroelectric power’s proportion of the country’s electric supply by 2028-29, news sources reported. The plan will increase the share of hydroelectric power from the current level of 9,406 megawatts to 20,591 megawatts.
Read:
WAPDA to boost water storage capacity to 24 MAF
According to reports,
WAPDA would add electricity in two phases
to raise the clean energy share of the total. The first phase will be completed by 2025, adding 2,960 megawatts to secure a total generation capacity of 12,366 megawatts. Another 8,225 megawatts will be added to the national power lines in the second phase, bringing the total to 20,591. The second phase will conclude in 2029.
In terms of total units generated, WAPDA presently generates 37 billion units of low-cost hydroelectric electricity. This figure will be increased to 54 billion by 2025 with the addition of 17 billion units of sustainable energy. Similarly, 27 billion hydropower units will be added between 2025 and 2029, totaling 81 billion units.
Read:
WAPDA proposes country’s first floating solar plant
At present hydroelectric power makes up roughly 31 % of the overall energy produced in the country.

title: CDA plans to boost water supply to 50 MGD by month’s end
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) plans to increase the water supply to residents of the capital city to 50 million gallons per day (MGD) by the end of May, news sources reported on May 18. Currently, the overall water supply is standing at 45 MGD after the repair of several water supply channels.
Read:
CDA’s water wing to float PKR 4 mn tender for supply tankers’ repair
The decision to increase the water supply was made during a meeting chaired by Chairman CDA Amir Ali Ahmad. He directed all concerned departments and officials to take all necessary steps required to improve the water supply by repairing leaks and making
water tube wells operationa
l. The meeting was briefed that the authority has added a total of 15 MGD of water to the existing capacity by repairing 1,000 leakages, functionalising 14 old tube wells, and operationalising another 18 new tube wells. It was also revealed that the capital city’s water requirements are met through the following sources:
20 MGD of water from
Simly Dam
9 MGD from Khanpur Dam
2 MGD from Rawal Dam with the addition of another 2 MGD in the coming days
Read:
CDA, UNDP introduce new waste management system in Islamabad
Moreover, the meeting was told that the total water supply will increase to 50 MGD of water with the addition of 4 MGD from other sources as well.

title: CDA restarts development work in E-12 sector
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has finally restarted the development work in the E-12 sector after carrying out a state land retrieval operation, according to a news story published on May 9.
Read:
CDA launches civil work in Sector E-12/4
Reportedly, last year, the capital city administration awarded the contracts for the development work in two sub-sectors of E-12 for the construction of streets, sewerage, roads, water supply network, and drainage. However, the civic agency failed to complete the work in one year due to the resistance from the locals.
As per the details, 11% of work is completed in sub-sector 2 whereas 17% of work is finished in sub-sector 3. According to a CDA engineer, the authority has ordered to complete the development as soon as possible. Moreover, the tendering process of awarding work in sub-sector 4 is in the final stages. The engineer stated that development work will start soon. It was disclosed that the same will be done for sub-sector 1.
Read:
CDA to start uplift work in Sector E-12/4
It is pertinent to mention that over 4,000 people have been waiting for possession of plots in the E-12 sector; unfortunately, the dispute between villagers and CDA has prevented it. The CDA’s Land and Estate Wing has so far
allotted 282 plots
through National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA). The allotment letters will be issued soon to get the possession of the whole sector.

title: CDA shares timeline for completion of I.J. Principal Road
full_text:

NLC to complete PKR 4.9 bn IJP Road in 18 months
In a meeting, the National Logistic Cell (NLC) and Capital Development Authority (CDA) briefed CDA Chairman Amer Ali Ahmed on the progress of the renovation of I.J. Principal Road. He was informed that 41% of
work on the road
has been completed. The chairman directed the civic agency to clear routes along I.J. Principal Road in order to divert traffic there. Also, a control room has been established to help motorists in case of emergency.
Moreover, the CDA Chairman Ahmed has directed the contractor to speed up the work, especially the 4-kilometre area from Pirwadahi Adda to Pirwadahi Mor. He has asked the engineering wing to complete this area of the road by August.
Read:
CDA creates wing for Faisal Mosque, plans renovation
It is pertinent to note that under the PKR 4.9 billion project, seven culverts, 2 flyovers, and 2 bridges will be constructed besides overhauling the road. title: Construction work to start on Balakot Power project soon
full_text:
Mansehra: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Chief Minister (CM) Mahmood Khan is expected to inaugurate work on the 300 megawatts Balakot Hydropower project in the coming weeks, according to media reports published on May 7.

Land acquisition process begins for Balakot Hydropower project
As per the details, the district administration has acquired 8,000 kanals of land at Paras, Ghanool, Sangar, and Bala Schain patwar circles for the development of the said energy project with financial assistance from the Asian Development Bank.
Reportedly, the executive committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) has already approved USD 750 million for
Balakot Hydropower Project
. It was disclosed that the Pakhtunkhwa Energy Department Organisation is seeking applications for the appointments of assistant directors, engineers, and other cadres. It was disclosed that the bidding and selection process of contractors have already been completed. A consortium of companies has been finalised to work on the project.
Read:
District administration imposes Section 4 for Balakot Hydropower project land acquisition
It is pertinent to note that the project is being executed by Pakhtunkhwa Energy Development Organisation at Kunar River in the Kaghan Valley.

title: Malir Expressway project to be completed in 30 months: SEPA

A meeting was held where the director general presented the detailed analysis of the approval process of the 39-kilometre long Malir Expressway to the Sindh Minister for Environment, Climate Change and Coastal Development Muhammad Ismail Rahu. Deadline issued for construction of Malir Expressway up to Quaidabad

SEPA
