title: NHA recommends Mansehra-Muzaffarabad Link Road for CDWP’s approval
developer: Link Road project for the approval of the Central Development
full_text:
Islamabad: The National Highway Authority (NHA) Board has recommended Project Concept-1 (PC-1) for the Mansehra-Muzaffarabad Link Road project for the approval of the Central Development Working Party (CDWP), news sources reported on April 28.
Read:
Mansehra-Naran-Jalkhad Road opens to traffic
The 26-kilometre-long project, worth PKR 44.72 billion, is part of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).  After the approval from CDWP, the project will be sent to the
Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC)
for final approval. The proposed project will be constructed as per the design proposed by NHA in 2013. Sardar Mohammad Yusuf, a Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) assembly member, stated at a gathering that the project would benefit the local economy by increasing tourism in the region.
Read:
Muzaffarabad-Mansehra CPEC Link Road: NHA approves PC-1 of PKR 44 bn
He further stated that if the Mansehra-Muzaffarabad Motorway is linked with the
Hazara Motorway
through Pano Dehri and Gujjar Galli, it will pass through verdant alpine forests, providing a scenic journey for tourists. He stated that this would also bring tourists to the Kaghan valley and other parts of the Hazara division and Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK).

title: WAPDA proposes country’s first floating solar plant
full_text:
Islamabad: The Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA) has sought financing from the World Bank (WB) to establish Pakistan’s first 300-megawatt (MW) floating solar power project, news sources reported on April 20. The Floating Solar Project (FSP) is proposed to be installed at the Ghazi Brotha Hydroelectric Power Plant.
Read:
WAPDA to convert water supply schemes to solar power in KP
It was reported that the WB team of experts will visit Pakistan and will remain here for 10 days for extensive consultations with all stakeholders, such as the
Ministry of Water Resources, WAPDA
, and the Economic Affairs Division. Following the visit, the World Bank team would provide a feasibility report on the project, detailing the proposed financing structure as well as the estimated Return on Investment (ROI) in the following term.
According to the information published, a 150-MW floating solar subproject would be installed in the Ghazi Barrage headpond, while another of comparable capacity will be installed in the forebay of the current Ghazi Brotha Hydropower plant. The project has been offered as an alternate energy source to traditional coal-based and furnace oil-based power projects.
Read:
Solar-powered grids inaugurated in Swabi
It is critical to remember that the country’s energy consumption is increasing, with more electricity supply required by 2030. The overall energy required to support industrialisation is estimated to be roughly 54 Gigawatts (GWH). However, renewable energy accounts for only a modest portion of total energy use. According to the research, Pakistan’s installed capacity by the end of 2020 was 39-GWH, which originated from 36% gas resources, 25% hydropower plants, and 18% oil reserves.

title: Pakistan to develop underground strategic gas reserve for long term supply
full_text:
Islamabad: The government intends to build the country’s first Strategic Underground Gas Storage (SUGS) to deal with supply disruptions and gaps in demand, news sources reported on April 21. The project would cost PKR 127 billion.
Read:
GHQ proposes strategic oil reserves in Gwadar
According to reports, the government has chosen to pursue long-term strategic needs to develop energy resilience and improve energy security in the face of chronic gas supply deficits. The bankable feasibility study for the development of SUGS will cost about PKR 1.848 billion, with the objective of building a framework for the construction of strategic natural gas storage facilities. The Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) will also be included in the feasibility study.
Furthermore, the investigation found that the
Asian Development Bank (ADB)
gave project feasibility funds of USD 575,000 in 2021. The government had designated locations for the SUGS throughout Sindh. The bank analysed the competitive bidding process, short-listed the consultants, and recently hired Ramboll as a consultant for the underground gas storage study on the parameters agreed upon with the ADB.  It is vital to note that Pakistan is rapidly becoming an energy-deficient country, owing to the country’s declining natural gas reserves and high reliance on imported Liquid Natural Gas (LNG).
Read:
Qatar Investment Authority keen to invest in RLNG power plants
Pakistan is also constructing gas pipelines such as Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India (TAPI), Iran-Pakistan-India (IPI), and LNG imports from Qatar and other countries to bridge the demand-supply gap.

title: Centre to assist in completion of HYD-SKR Motorway, KCR projects
full_text:
Islamabad: The federal government has decided to assist the Sindh government in the completion of major infrastructure projects being constructed under the Public Sector Development Program (PSDP) including; the Hyderabad-Sukkur Motorway (M-6) and Karachi Circular Railway (KCR), according to media reports on April 22.
Read:
PPPA, NHA to sign agreement for Sukkur-Hyderabad Motorway project
The said announcement was made during a meeting held between Sindh Chief Minister (CM) Murad Ali Shah and Federal Minister for Planning and Development Ahsan Iqbal. During the meeting, the federal minister assured maximum support for the completion of projects including Hyderabad-Sukkur Motorway, KCR, and Greater Karachi Water Supply Project (K-4).
Read:
PM Sharif promises funds for K-4 project, KCR’s inclusion in CPEC
Moreover, Federal Minister Iqbal stated that the work on
Hyderabad-Sukkur Motorway
(M-6) should be expedited to resolve the travel problems. He went on to say that the nine industrial zones were supposed to be made operational in 2020; however, due to unforeseen delays, the first industrial zone is expected to start in 2024, the second in 2025, and the third one in 2027. The federal minister maintained that the projects will be completed within the stipulated time through interdepartmental cooperation.

title: Authorities directed to connect Islamabad’s Orange Line, Metro Bus routes
full_text:
Islamabad: Prime Minister (PM) Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday (April 21) has directed authorities to connect the routes of Rawalpindi Metro Bus and the newly launched Orange Line Metro Bus, news sources reported. For this purpose, a junction will be set up at Faiz Ahmed Faiz Station – near the Higher Education Commission Building in Islamabad. The construction work on this bay in already under progress and will become operational from Monday (April 25)
Read:
Islamabad metro bus service becomes operational
The premier has directed
Capital Development Authority (CDA)
Chairman Amir Ali Ahmad to oversee the required improvements to the route. Following the new adjustments, the Rawalpindi Metro Bus route between Saddar-Rawalpindi and Islamabad Secretariat will be linked to the Orange Line Bus Service, which transports people from Peshawar Mor to Islamabad International Airport. The suggested approach will minimise road traffic while simultaneously improving local transportation infrastructure.
Read:
NADRA facilitation centre to be set up along Islamabad Expressway
It is important to recall that the Orange Line Bus service was launched a few days back to facilitate the long commute between the Peshawar Mor and Islamabad International Airport. The government has subsidised the route fare for Ramzan. As a temporary measure, buses from metro buses have been used to run the route while 30 buses have already been procured from China as a permanent solution to the public transport problem of the capital city.

title: KP shares updates on road projects leading to tourist sites
full_text:
Peshawar: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) tourism department has shared the progress status of the rehabilitation and construction of roads leading to tourist sites launched under the Integrated Tourism Development project, according to news published on April 15.
Read:
KP govt released PKR 740 mn for tehsil financial stability, infrastructure
A review meeting was held by the KP tourism department to check the progress of rehabilitation and construction of 11 access roads underway in the Malakand division and 6 roads in the Hazara division. The meeting was attended by Chief Minister (CM) Mahmood Khan, Secretary Environment and Forestry Abid Majeed, Secretary Communications and Works Ijaz Ansari, Secretary Tourism Aamir Tareen, and other relevant senior officials. Rural Roads Development Project
, and Integrated Tourism Development Project.

The attendees were also informed that the financial opening of 22-kilometre Mankiyal road and 24-kilometre Thandiyani will be completed by the end of April.  Moreover, the 34-kilometre Kalam to Mataltan and Mahodand roads have been included in the provincial road projects. Read:
Unilever Pakistan to provide utilities at popular tourist sites in KP
Furthermore, the attendees were informed that 1,337-kilometre district roads will be carried out along with the constriction of 62 bridges, under the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Rural Roads Development project. The CM Khan directed to complete the projects on time without compromising quality.

title: Orders issued for completion of Rawal Dam flyover by September
developer: Shehbaz Sharif has directed the Capital Development
full_text:
Islamabad: Prime Minister (PM) Shehbaz Sharif has directed the Capital Development Authority (CDA) to complete the Rawal Dam Chowk Flyover project by September, according to a news story published on April 17.

Authorities asked to open Rawal Dam flyover in 2 months

pace must be expedited
and completed by September this year. Many political leaders including Muhammad Hanif Abbasi, Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry, Ahsan Iqbal, and others were also present on the occasion.

Orders issued for early completion of Rawal Dam Chowk Flyover
During the visit, the prime minister ordered an inquiry into the delay of the project. title: Construction of RRR project formally kicks off
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The construction of Rawalpindi Ring Road (RRR) has been formally inaugurated and is expected to be complete in one and a half years to resolve the traffic congestion issue on priority, according to media reports published in the national dailies on April 17.

PM Khan lays foundation stone of RRR project

RDA gets go-ahead to launch work on ring road, Leh Expressway projects

title: CDA’s water wing launches 80 water filtration plants for Islamabad
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has made 80 water filtration plants operational in the capital city, news sources reported on April 16. The project was completed by the water supply wing of the CDA to provide residents with clean, potable water.

CDA to install 20 tube wells to improve water supply in Islamabad

Installation of water filtration plants in

to facilitate the residents

CDA restore water supply to G-7/3 other areas

Details shared on 700 ongoing development projects in Sindh

title: MDA issues tender for Eidgah to Rasheedabad Flyover dualisation
full_text:
Multan: The Multan Development Authority (MDA) has released a tender for the dualisation of the road from Eidgah Chowk to Rasheedabad Flyover, news sources reported on April 4. A total of PKR 90 million will be spent on the construction work, while a total of 1 billion has been set aside for the land acquisition.
Read:
Multan Development Authority posts 75% increase in annual revenue
According to reports, the authority published a tender barely three months before the conclusion of the fiscal year (FY) 2021-22. It was also revealed that the
Multan Development Authority (MDA)
intends to rehabilitate and expand the road from Eidgah Chowk to Chowk Kumharanwala. The project’s cost was expected to be PKR 1.15 billion. However, the Punjab government only provided PKR 120 million, which was inadequate to begin the land purchase process.
Read:
MDA devises amnesty scheme for regularisation of educational institutes
Meanwhile, the administration has issued a PKR 90.12 million tender for the dualisation of Eidgah Chowk to Rasheedabad Flyover. The project’s tender will be opened on April 20. The authority has asked qualified organizations and firms to participate, and submit their qualifications and a history of past projects.

title: CDA issues tender for Sector D-12’s development work
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has released a tender of PKR 146 million to complete development work in Sector D-12, according to a press release on the CDA’s official Facebook page on April 3. The funds will be utilised to build road infrastructure and other related projects in D-12.
Read:
CDA expected to present surplus budget for
F
Y 2022-23
Reportedly, competent firms and interested parties may get the published tender from the CDA website or the headquarters of the authority in Islamabad. The tender has been issued for the road infrastructure, construction and maintenance of main and link roads, asphalt carpeting, and other development work. It should be emphasised that some regions of Islamabad have seen significant delays in development, and Sector D-12 is one of the long-stalled areas. However, development activities have been launched in all sectors due to the CDA management’s particular interest.
Read:
Islamabad launched over 50 parks in 2021: CDA
On this occasion, the CDA’s management stated that the resettlement of new sectors would further enhance the city’s beauty while also giving additional services to inhabitants in terms of uninterrupted quality of life and continuous facilities.
It is also worth noting that the CDA will present a development budget of
PKR 308 billion with a surpl
us of PKR 100 billion. The budget is the highest non-auction budget in history.

title: Korea increases EDCF grant to USD 1 bn for infrastructure development
developer: Korean government would increase Economic Development
full_text:
Islamabad: Ambassador of the Republic of Korea Suh Sangpyo, on Wednesday (April 4) said the Korean government would increase Economic Development Cooperation Fund (EDCF) loans by up to USD 1 billion, – to be offered to Pakistan over five years (2022–26), according to news sources reported.
Read:
Pakistan, South Korea signs MoU to preserve Gandhara heritage
Previously, in 2019, Pakistan and Korea signed an agreement, under which, Korea was to provide USD 500 million of EDFC loans to support Pakistan’s infrastructure development.
Under the renewed framework, the Korean government will offer another USD 500 million for the construction of infrastructure in Pakistan. In addition, the ambassador said that the governments of both countries are working on various business opportunities and development projects, including automobile, transportation, hydropower, smartphones, and confectionery production sectors. Some of the other projects highlighted by the ambassador included:
Collaboration in EDCF and IT Parks with the inauguration of the
Islamabad Technology Park in May 2021
Around 1,500 Pakistani students study in Korea in undergraduate and graduate programmes under the Global Korea Scholarship (GKS).
Self-sufficiency of virus-free potato seed multiplication and chilli production and post-harvest management technology development by Aeroponic Technique under the Korea Program on International Agriculture (KOPIA)
An MOU between the PMAS-Arid Agriculture University Rawalpindi and Chungbuk National University. The agreement would allow technical staff exchange for joint research and joint publication of research papers.
Collaboration on the Tsunami Billion Tree initiative under the Friendship Forest programme for climate change mitigation efforts in Pakistan.
Read:
Korea to provide funds for Lahore’s water treatment plant projects
The Korean companies are working on Multiple hydropower projects worth USD 4 billion. These projects include K-Water, Daewoo E&C, Korea Southeast Power Corporation (KOEN), DL E&C, Lotte E&C, Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power Corporation (KHNP), Korea Overseas Infrastructure & Urban Development Corporation (KIND), Lotte, Sambu Construction, Hyundai Eng., Doosan.

title: USAID launch safe water project for Sindh and KP districts
developer: The United States Agency for International Development
full_text:
Islamabad: The United States Agency for International Development (USAID), in collaboration with the United Nations Office for Project Services (UNOPS), has launched a safe drinking water initiative for the two backward districts of Sindh and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), news sources reported on April 1.
Read:
USAID to grant USD 200,000 to businesses, innovators under ‘Challenge Fund Grant’
The programme will benefit 70,000 individuals in Tank (KP) and Umerkot (Sindh). According to a tweet from UNOPS-Pakistan, the initiative would minimize water-borne infections by using a unique approach to increasing access to water and sanitation services in health clinics, schools, and marginalized areas of the Tank and Umerkot districts.
On the occasion, USAID Mission Director David Young said that the initiative is being lau
nched to celebrate the 75th year of Pak-USA friendship. He also said that the
USAID has helped Pakistan achieve sustainable people-oriented goals, built dams and schools, responded to humanitarian emergencies caused by floods and earthquakes, provided vaccines to people in need, and furnished tools and training to help Pakistan’s development.
Read:
DIB, PMRC sign agreement for promoting mortgaging, housing finance
It is vital to remember that Pakistan is one of the world’s most water-stressed countries, with a declining quantity of water for future generations. To address the issue, the federal and provincial governments around the country have initiated a number of water-related initiatives.

title: Punjab PDWP approves physical planning, housing projects
full_text:
Lahore: The Punjab Provincial Development Working Party (PDWP) on Tuesday (March 29) approved development projects worth PKR 41 billion for the road, physical planning & housing, secondary healthcare & medical education sectors, according to news sources.
Read:
Punjab PDWP approves PKR 1.9 bn development budget
The 71st meeting of
PDWP approved
four projects worth PKR 6.25 billion for physical planning & housing, secondary healthcare & medical education sectors. The meeting also recommended six schemes, worth PKR 35.45 billion, for the road sector to be included in the next Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP).
The following are the details of the projects cleared for inclusion in the upcoming PSDP:
Dualisation of the road from Chiniot to Pindi Bhattian Interchange, at PKR 7.95 billion
Widening and improvement of road from Mathial Chowk to Pindi Gheb City, Tehsil Jand, and Pindi Gheb, district Attock, at the cost of PKR 3.144 billion
Construction of dual carriageway from old GT Road Gujrat to Lakhanwal, at the cost of PKR 8.8 billion
Improvement and reconstruction of the road from Hafizabad to Khanqah Dogran, at the cost of PKR 1.9 billion
Dualistaion of the road from Pind Dadan Khan, Choa Saidan Shah to Chakwal, at the estimated cost of 10 billion
Construction and widening of road from Hafizabad to Alipur Chattha, at the total cost of PKR 3.03 billion
Upgradation of Thalassemia Unit and Bone Marrow Transplant Centre at the Bahawal Victoria Hospital, Bahawalpur, at the cost of PKR 1.7 billion
Read:
Punjab PDWP approves road projects in Multan, Sheikhupura
Comprehensive Water Supply Scheme for Kamalia City (revised), at the cost of PKR 455.162 million
Extension and rehabilitation of urban sewerage scheme for Gojra (revised), at the total cost of PKR 450 million
New Dhar Jawa Water Supply Scheme with New Tourist Spot of Dhirkot Spring Water Supply Scheme for Kotli Sattian and Augmentation of Water supply, drainage & sewerage system at Kahuta, Rawalpindi, at the cost of 3.5 billion

title: Punjab PDWP approves PKR 1.9 bn development budget
full_text:
Lahore: The Punjab Provincial Development Working Party (PDWP) has approved a development budget of PKR 1.986 billion for the province, news sources reported on March 26. The budget will be used to develop three schemes that include road rehabilitation and infrastructure development.
Read:
KP PDWP approves PKR 30.6 bn infrastructure development budget
Reportedly, the budget for the schemes was approved during the 70th meeting of the PDWP board. The budget has been allocated for the fiscal year (FY) 2021-22.  As per the details released, the funds will be utilised for the following:
PKR 738.513 million will be spent for the rehabilitation and carpeting of city roads (Defence Road, Shahabpura Road, Eminabad Road to Sunyarawala Pull, Raam Garha to Darbar Touheed Shah Road, Abbot Road, Railway Road, Circular Road, Jail Road, Khawaja Safdar Road, Kashmir Road, Sublime Chowk to Marala Road, Gohad Pur Road, Lari Adda Road to Bhed Pully, Imam Sahib Road and Haji Pura Road
Read:
Punjab govt establishes first overseas home in Gujranwala Division
PKR 462.337 million will be spent on the  Sewerage Scheme in Rahim Yar Khan City with a Treatment Plant and the construction of an Intermediate Pumping Station Near Niazi Colony & Installation of Force Main (2nd Revised)
PKR 785.368 million has been allocated for the Punjab Aquifer Recharge for Groundwater Management (Revised)

title: CDA launches helpline for better service delivery to citizens
full_text:
Islamabad: In a bid to provide smooth services and improve service delivery, the Capital Development Authority (CDA) has launched the ‘1819’ helpline for citizens, news sources reported. As a result, the citizens can access services related to the CDA, Excise and Taxation (E&T) and Islamabad Capital Police (ICP) under one roof.
Read:
CDA to start construction on Bhara Kahu Bypass to ease traffic burden
As per CDA, the launch of the helpline and the backend services provided by the NRCP will help increase service delivery, increase compliance, and remove red-tapism in delivering services to the citizens. Furthermore, citizens can enquire about the service and provide feedback using the helpline.
Read:
CDA launches sanitation helpline
A private cellular company will provide the technology infrastructure and performance management. Following the establishment of the helpline, citizens will be able to launch complaints and track the progress of the services. Moreover, a new facilitation centre has been established to provide land transfer, estate management, revenue, and one window operations.
The CDA helpline also provides the
facility to check the progress of property transfer applications and register complaints regarding overpriced commodities, such as groceries, through the same helpline.

title: RUDA to regularise certain housing schemes in Ravi City project
full_text:
Lahore: The Ravi Urban Development Authority (RUDA) has decided to regularise housing schemes with 500 houses or other structures already developed in Purple Zone of Ravi Riverfront Urban Development Project (RRUDP)’s Phase-1, according to a news story published on Saturday (March 19).
Read:
RUDA, CBD to offer environment-protection solution for Lahore: PM Imran
It is pertinent to note that the
Phase-1 of Ravi City project
has been divided into three zones: Brown Zone, Green Zone, and Purple Zone. In the Brown Zone, anybody can develop infrastructure according to the specifications, needs, and standards set by RUDA. The Green Zone is reserved for forestry and agricultural related activities. The Purple Zone is allotted for buildings or housing schemes developed including 1,700 small and medium industries. The CEO mentioned that all the developments in this zone will be regularised.
Read:
RUDA invites industries to register with its Industrial Zone
RUDA Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Imran Amin disclosed that the schemes located on the riverbed or flood plains will be relocated. He went on to say that the said project will consist of a media city where media houses can have new offices in the RRUDP area.

title: Plan prepared to pedestrianise Lahore’s MM Alam Road
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) is preparing plans to pedestrianise M M Alam Road in order to reduce traffic and ease public mobility, according to news published on Friday (March 18).
Read:
LDA allows commercial activities on 10 roads in city, reclassify another nine
As per the details, the government has decided to beautify and remodel some areas of M M Alam Road and Main Boulevard in Gulberg. The LDA is preparing designs for the roads in collaboration with public and private sector experts. It was disclosed that the authority is working on several proposals to transform the areas as per international standards.
Moreover, LDA plans to remove encroachments, improve the façade of buildings, enhance security, bring uniformity in signage, place benches, improve sewerage system, and install modern streetlights (LED). Under the plan, Gulberg Main Boulevard will have adequate plantation, walking, and sitting spaces. The encroachments on footpaths, service roads, and buildings setback areas will be removed.
Read:
Gulberg Elevated Expressway: Traffic plan prepared, work to start next month
Reportedly, the LDA plans to place benches in between the landscapes to prevent air pollution, which will help make the area pedestrian-friendly. The owners of buildings in these areas were also asked to help LDA in this regard. The owners were requested to maintain spaces in front of their buildings after remodeling.

title: CDA to start metro bus service trial run next month
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) will start the trial run of the metro bus service between Islamabad International Airport (IIA) and Peshawar Morr in the first week of April, news sources reported. The trial has been delayed due to the late arrival of buses from China.
Read:
Islamabad to get public transport system based on 2017’s census
Reportedly, the first shipment of the 15 buses will leave Chinese port on March 15 and reach Karachi Port in 20 days. Furthermore, it will take another four days for the buses to get clearance from customs, after which the buses will leave for Islamabad. The trial will begin in the first week of April, with the buses running a 25.6-kilometre route from
Peshawar Morr to IIA
. After completing the trial, the buses will have a fixed fare of PKR 30 per ride, with a discounted fare for women and students. It is vital to mention that the bus service will be the capital city’s first public transportation system. In the first phase, there will be 30 buses in total.
Read:
Pakistan Day Parade: Govt restricts access to certain areas of Islamabad
The National Highway Authority (NHA) was the first to design the route, and it was completed with a cost of PKR 16 billion. However, it was later acquired by CDA. The CDA will oversee metro track stations, command and control, ticketing, station administration, cleanliness, and security systems.

title: US Embassy praises CDA for swift work
developer: Pakistan has thanked the Capital Development
full_text:
Islamabad: The United States (US) embassy in Pakistan has thanked the Capital Development Authority (CDA) for acting quickly on the mission’s requests for water supply and retaining wall maintenance, news sources reported. Senior Facility Manager US Embassy Danial P. wrote a letter to the CDA Director-General (DG) Water Wing.
Read:
CDA to set up Pakistan’s first virtual zoo in Islamabad
Reportedly, the CDA Water Wing has restored water supplies to the US embassy, which was previously supplied by tankers. The CDA, on the other hand, streamlined the water provision by providing the embassy with a continuous flow of water from Khanpur and Simly dams. It was also stated that the CDA repaired the US embassy’s retaining wall, which was in poor condition. According to the report, the CDA has begun measures to provide a
permanent water supply for Sector G
in the capital, where it has restored water service to 300 residents. The authority has also established a complaint resolution unit to resolve citizens’ water concerns.
Read:
CDA restore water supply to G-7/3 other areas
According to the CDA, water supply arrangements for the capital are in the early stages as the city’s population grows. The government has announced various development initiatives to address the problem, including the construction of small dams for Rawalpindi and Islamabad.

title: KDA DG orders swift completion of infrastructure projects in Karachi
full_text:
Karachi: Karachi Development Authority (LDA) Director General (DG) Syed Muhammad Ali Shah on Sunday (March 13) instructed the concerned officials to complete the city’s ongoing infrastructure development projects as per the schedule, news sources reported.
Read:
Scheme 36 belongs to KDA: SHC rules
Reportedly, while chairing a review meeting on the city’s ongoing development projects, it was revealed that there are currently 38 development projects underway in Karachi. According to Chief Engineer KDA Syed Ali Noman, the authority has allocated sufficient funding for the ongoing development projects under the Sindh Annual Development Programme (ADP) to ensure completion on time. According to the meeting minutes, the following projects were discussed:
Construction of road in Gadap Town-Yousuf Goth
Extension of PECHS Scheme 36 Nullah
Construction in Block B of the Sindh Muslim Cooperative Society
Road construction project on Vita Chowrangi
Read:
It was also revealed that work on a variety of modest road infrastructure development and maintenance projects is ongoing. In addition, specific measures are being implemented to improve the sewage and drainage systems. Furthermore, DG Ali emphasised that road cutting practices should be discouraged by KDA team members.  He encouraged authorities to take legal action against anyone who engaged in the activities.

title: CDA to develop park in Sector D-12/2
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Monday (March 07) announced its decision to develop a new park in Sector D-12/2, news sources reported. In addition to the one large park at the D-12 Markaz, this new park will be the sixth in a series of parks to be developed in the sector.
Read:
CDA restore water supply to G-7/3 other areas
According to a CDA spokesperson, the project would cost PKR 9 million, and a tender of the project will be published in the leading newspapers soon. The park will provide inhabitants with various recreational opportunities, such as swings for children and walkways and jogging tracks for residents and visitors. In addition, the park will be fenced off and equipped with enough lighting to make it more user-friendly and safe. According to the spokesperson, three parks
are under development in Sector I-14
, one in Sector I-16. It is also worth noting that the CDA Board has approved the development of two big parks in different areas in the capital city and the installation of a Ferris Wheel.
Read:
NA passes bill to form Federal Government Properties Management Authority (FGPMA)
The Project Concept-1 (PC-1) for the two parks, in
Lake View and Bhara Kahu
, and the 180-foot-high Ferris wheel, has been prepared, awaiting final clearance from the Development Working Party (DWP) meeting.

title: CDA restore water supply to G-7/3 other areas
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has restored water supplies for the inhabitants of Sector G-7/3 after a ten-year lapse, news sources reported. The CDA has asked its water wing to restore old pipelines and water infrastructure for almost 300 homes in the area.
Read:
CDA to start uplift work in Sector E-12/4
As per the sources, the CDA decided to supply water to the residents, citing the escalating water costs from private water tankers. It was also revealed that the CDA had started a PKR 495 million water infrastructure development project in the capital city. The project started a few years ago to restore and repair water pipelines,
tube wells, and water filtration plants
for use in other areas. Moreover, under the project, the water wing has restored water lines in Sectors F-6, F-7, F-8, F-10, G-6, G-7, G-8, G-9, G-10, G-10/3, G-11, H-9, H-10, I-9, I-10, Humak Town, Rawal Dam, and other locations – under the command of the CDA board.
Read:
CDA to implement modern traffic management system on Islamabad Expressway
In addition, the authority has fixed twelve malfunctioning filtration facilities. Furthermore, in August, the federal government asked
authorities to conduct a feasibility report of small dams
for a steady water supply to the capital city residents.

title: CDA to launch metro bus trial service from Peshawar Morr to IAA
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) will launch a pilot project of the Metro Bus Service between Peshawar Morr and Islamabad International Airport (IAA) from March 15, news sources reported. The bus service will be officially launched at full capacity on March 23.
Read:
CDA to launch ‘Blue Line Bus Service’ from Soan River to Faisal Mosque
Reportedly, A six-bus fleet will initially operate from 7 am to 11 pm, charging PKR 30 per person. However, the total number of buses will be increased along with the operation hours in near future. The buses will pick up passengers from
Peshawar Morr Central Station
. The 25.6-kilometre long route will have multiple stop stations while it will be entirely run and operated by CDA. The bus service will act as an economic public transportation system between the IIA and Islamabad once it is operational. CDA will also temporarily acquire buses to run on the route as part of a stop-gap deal with the
Rawalpindi Metro Bus Authority
(MBA) until it purchases a fleet of 30 buses worth PKR 1.9 billion.
Read:
CDA approves establishment of wing to improve land acquisition process
It is important to note that the National Highway Authority (NHA) developed the project with PKR 16 billion and handed it over to the CDA in March. On the other hand, the authority is working on designing ticketing and operation systems for the bus service, and procuring a bus fleet for the route.

title: LDA shares draft of Lahore Master Plan 2050, invites suggestions/objections
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) has released the first draft of the Lahore Master Plan 2050, a post on the authority’s official social media account reported on February 23. The authority has invited the general public and citizens for suggestions and objections on the draft.
Read:
LDA invites public opinion on Lahore Master Plan 2050, seminar on Dec 1
According to reports, the LDA has requested individuals to submit their ideas and complaints about the master plan to LDA Chief Metropolitan Office, located at LDA Complex in Johar Town Lahore. Citizens may also examine the draft policy on the LDA’s official website, https://www.lda.gop.pk. Following a lengthy debate with civil society and the community to solve the city’s infrastructure problems, the
LDA has produced the first draft of the master plan
. According to the LDA, the master plan addressed public transportation, education, the environment, housing plans, cultural persistence, and industrialization in the provincial capital. Furthermore, the Master Plan 2050 tackles sustainable growth and transportation, including a bike and pedestrian lane.
Read:
Govt to unveil Lahore Master Plan on December 31
Furthermore, it was claimed that the master plan will cover other cities in the Lahore Division,
including Kasur, Sheikhupura,
Nankana, and others. The report also disclosed that the master plan was created with a 2.4 % growth rate and urban migration in mind.  It is important to note that the LDA will amend the LDA ACT-1975 and LDA master plan rule 2014 to prepare and implement Master Plan 2050.

title: Minister unveils roadmap of 7th digital census
full_text:
Islamabad: Minister for Planning, Development Asad Umar said on Tuesday (February 22) that the country’s seventh population and housing census will be conducted between September-December this year, news sources reported. The census will be Pakistan’s first digital census, allowing more transparency.
Read:
Islamabad to get public transport system based on 2017’s census
In a press conference, Asad said that the
Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS)
would share data plans with the media soon. He also said that the central government has also taken provincial governments on board for the successful census execution to ensure that the next election is held according to the latest population numerics. He pointed out that to make the process more successful, a pilot project will be launched in June to enumerate and note shortcomings and risk management.  The federal government will include the IT Ministry, National Telecom Corporation (NTC) and Natural Resources Training Group (NRTG) in the exercise. He also said that conducting a census after 15 to 18 years is not an option in today’s modern world because of rapid population dynamics changes.
Read:
Islamabad to get public transport system based on 2017’s census
As per the revealed plan, the interim census results will be completed and released by December this year, while a detailed breakdown of the resources will follow. The cabinet had previously approved the 7th census in consultation with all the provinces, following the problem with the previous census results conducted in 2017

title: LCBDA kicks-off two-month apprenticeship for fresh graduates
developer: The Lahore Central Business District Development
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Central Business District Development Authority (LCBDDA) on Monday (February 21) held a closing ceremony for the student apprenticeship programme for fresh graduates, news sources reported. A total of 36 students will receive training to improve their soft and managerial skills as part of the initiative.
Read:
Punjab demarcates areas included in LCBDA’s jurisdiction
According to reports, the initiative was well-received during the ceremony attended by Punjab Housing Minister Asad Khokhar and Special Assistant to the Chief Minister (SACM) Hassan Khawar.  the  apprenticeship programme  lead to job placement would assist in the increased employment rate among young people while also preparing them for future labour market challenges. Students will get two months of training in 12 soft skills and 10 hard skills including; interpersonal skills, team building, contingent decision making, stress management, communication skills,
artificial intelligence, project management
, and cyber security – as part of the curriculum.
Read:
LCBDA holds pre-bid session for “Lahore Prime” project
According to sources, 8,000 students from varied backgrounds applied for the project, with 450 being chosen for further interviews. Similarly, only 36 students were chosen for the two-month training programme following the last round of interviews and discussions.

title: Govt to monitor development projects through satellites, remote sensing
developer: USD 3.65 billion supported by the Asian Development
full_text:
Islamabad: The National Coordination Committee (NCC) on Monday (February 21) decided to monitor the progress of all the foreign-funded development projects (FFPs) through satellites and remote sensing, news sources reported. Under the policy, Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission’s (Suparco) will render its services to the government of Pakistan to physically monitor the progress of the project.
Read:
Minister receives briefing on ongoing 54 WB-funded projects
According to Economic Affairs Minister Omar Ayub Khan, the government has devised a three-tier approach to improve the pace with which the project is completed on schedule. Satellites will be used to physically monitor the projects, financial audits will be performed, and Gantt charts will be created to measure progress. All projects that have been declared fast track will be prioritised for financing under the financial audit process. The approach would aid in the monitoring of 34 projects in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) worth USD 3.65 billion supported by the Asian Development Bank (ADB),
European Union, World Bank
, China, France, Germany, Japan, Saudi Arabia, the United Kingdom, and the United States. In addition, the committee also discussed progress on various development projects across the country:
Read:
Islamabad to have CPEC Business & Industrial Cooperation Tower
Out of 8,000 targeted schools, 5,946 have been solarised in KP under the
ADB-funded Access to Clean Energy Investment Programme
Solarization had been completed on 53 health units, while contracts for the other 134 health units had been issued and construction was underway
Out of the total 411 micro-hydropower plants (MHPP), 287 have been completed and work is under progress on remaining.

title: RDA, CDA to collaborate to define boundaries
full_text:
Rawalpindi: Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) Chairman Tariq Mehmood Murtaza on Saturday (February 19) decided to conduct a joint survey with the Capital Development Authority (CDA) for deciding the boundaries between the two cities, news sources reported. A joint panel will be constituted to examine the boundaries of both authorities and resolve tax collection issues.
Read:
Rawalpindi DC for action against illegal housing schemes, encroachment
The commission’s recommendation was made during the RDA’s 58th governing body meeting, which was presided over by RDA Chairman Tariq Mehmood. He stated that the delimitation panel would determine which territories are under the authority of Islamabad and which are under the control of the RDA. This would improve services for inhabitants of boarding areas while increasing revenue for the authorities. It was reported that several residents now receive No Objection Certificates (NOCs) from the CDA even though they live in the RDA region. As a result, property tax collection has decreased.
Read:
CDA approves establishment of wing to improve land acquisition process
The committee also discussed the legalisation of illegal housing schemes before 1989 (RDA formation date). RDA’s
Metropolitan Planning & Traffic Engineering (MP&TE)
department members will serve on the commission. The panel will investigate the mortgage status and the extent of the schemes’ development.

title: LDA to hold balloting of plots for Avenue-1 affectees
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) on Saturday (February 19) decided to allot plots to the affectees of the LDA Avenue-1 housing project, news sources reported. The balloting of the plots will be allowed soon to compensate the file holders.
Read:
Measures in place to improve security in LDA-approved housing schemes
Reportedly, in a governing body meeting of LDA, the participants also allowed the conversion of 23-kanal residential land into a model graveyard. The management of the graveyard will be handed over to Shehr-e-Khamoshan Authority. Some of the other decisions taken during the meeting were:
Conversion of 10 roads in the city into commercial roads
Reclassification of nine roads into commercial avenues
Handing over plot numbers 50-A/1 and 50-A/2 in Rachna Block Allama Iqbal Town to Municipal Corporation Limited (MCL)
Allocation of a 10-kanal plot in Etihad Town-Raiwind Road to the Punjab Environmental Protection Department (EPD) for the building of a Model Green Building
Read:
Illegal Housing Schemes: LDA issues new regulations for advertisement
Allocation of land for the LDA workshop’s near Sherpao Bridge to the Police Department
Formation of a committee to resolve the land-related issues in Khasra number 821 in Mouza Kharak in Mustafa Town

title: CDA-DVC approves commercial plots building plan
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Monday (February 07) reviewed and approved building plans for various commercial plots in the capital city, according to news sources.
Read:
Chairman CDA inaugurates F-9 art gallery
Reportedly, the said building plans were approved by the Design Vetting Committee (DVC) of CDA. A meeting in this regard was held in CDA headquarters, which discussed eight requests for approval of building designs. The committee approved seven designs during the subject meeting.  The approved building plans include:
Plot number 21-B of sector G-10 Markaz of Islamabad
Plot number 7 of Blue Area,
G-8 / F-8
Design for the construction of a school on plot number 125 in sector H-11 was approved
The building plan of Masjid Nabavi on plot number 1 in sector G-11/4 of Islamabad was also approved
An apartment complex design was approved in sector E-8 Naval Complex
Read:
CDA to make Srinagar Highway signal-free
In another development, the CDA recently formed a committee to revise the CDA Ordinance 1960 to improve the city’s land acquisition procedure. The committee’s goal will be to eliminate litigation and make the process more open and acceptable to the public. The committee will suggest amendments to sections 2(k), 12(2)(g), and 32-A of the CDA ordinance under its mandate.

title: Punjab allows Saudi firm to invest in RUDA Industrial Zone
full_text:
Lahore: The Cabinet Committee on Legislative Business on Thursday (February 03) allowed River Ravi Urban Development Authority (RUDA) to enter into an agreement with a Saudi firm to invest in the industrial zone, news sources reported. The firm will invest in Zones A and B developed and managed by RUDA.
Read:
RUDA signs agree
m
ent to make Ravi Riverfront cashless economic zone
As reported, Punjab Minister for Law and Parliamentary Affairs Muhammad Basharat Raja convened a meeting to evaluate the situation. Previously, the administration allowed the creation of an industrial zone in Pakistan’s largest riverbank project. It would be
Pakistan’s first renewable energy industrial zone
to encourage renewable energy throughout the country. It was stated that the initiative would aid in the creation of revenue-generating employment in the country. This will also enhance environmental conservation, with a particular emphasis on pollution management. In addition, the committee approved the distribution of car licence plates to applicants via Pakistan Post. For the services, the Customs and Excise Department will enter into an agreement with Pakistan Post.
Read:
‘RUDA has sufficient land to work on Riverfront project’s phase 1’
Similarly, the meeting authorised the Punjab Aquaculture Development Corporation Act 2021, the Benazir Income Support Program (BISP) door-to-door survey, and the establishment of the departmental promotion committee (DPC) for promotion to BS-19 at the Punjab Institute of Language Arts and Culture (PILAC).

title: CDA signs MoU with RWMC for landfill site
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Rawalpindi Waste Management Company (RWMC) for a 400 kanal landfill site, news sources reported. The
MoU was signed under the Public-Private Partnership (3P)
Authority Islamabad and the RWMC on a joint venture base operation.
Read:
Islamabad to get public transport system based on 2017’s census
The proposed landfill site will be used as the city’s first solid waste management site. The site is 6 kilometres from GT Road on Mandra Chakwal Road and 55 kilometres from the city’s centre.   The landfill will be utilised in partnership with the RWMC to address the capital city’s long-standing solid waste disposal issues. According to the Minister of Planning and Development Asad Umer, the planned location will be subject to all applicable Punjab laws, rules, and regulations. Moreover, RWMC has begun the process of acquiring land for a new dumpsite.
Read:
CDA says no-objection to privatisation of Jinnah Convention Center
A 1265-kanal piece of land on Mandra Chakwal Road in Bagnial, Dera Pothi, and Sahang Tehsil Gujjar Khan District Rawalpindi has been purchased.  Furthermore, the minister instructed the relevant authorities to engage an environmental impact assessment expert for the proposed dump site.

title: CDA to launch ‘Blue Line Bus Service’ from Soan River to Faisal Mosque
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Friday (January 28) decided to launch Blue Line Bus Service on Islamabad Expressway from March 23 (Pakistan Day) onwards, news sources reported. The bus service consisting of a fleet of 10 buses will start from Soan River and end at Faisal Mosque.
Read:
CDA to acquire buses for 3 public transport routes
According to reports, the project would also feature a bus service connecting Islamabad International Airport to Peshawar Mor, which will be started on the same day. The project is part of the Islamabad mass transportation effort, for which the CDA has agreed to purchase 30 buses from China, which will come ahead of the scheduled debut date. The authority is expected to issue a tender soon for the project’s IT infrastructure and ticketing system. Moreover, it was announced that the Blue Line Bus Service will provide free travelling service for female students, which will be a significant step toward increasing female safety and security on public transit routes.
Read:
CDA approves design plans for two parking plazas in Blue Area
It was also revealed that a similar scheme with 29 buses would be
launched at a later date for three major routes
: Bhara Kahu to Faizabad, Tarnol to Railway Station to M-5 Metro Station, and Soan to Faisal Mosque. It is worth noting that the Federal Commission has agreed to launch a feasibility study for the capital’s mass transport system based on 2017 census data.

title: PM orders preparation of master plan of 80 cities
full_text:
Islamabad: Special Assistant to the Prime Minister (SAPM) on Climate Change Malik Amin Aslam on Wednesday (January 26) said that Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan has directed authorities to prepare the master plan for 80 cities across the country, according to news sources. The establishment of housing societies on agricultural land will be prohibited until the master plans are completed.
Read:
LDA to offer ‘free height’ permission to property developers
Reportedly, during a briefing given to the National Assembly committee, Aslam said that in the event of a legitimate necessity, approval from federal or provincial cabinets will be required to convert green land to brown land for residential purposes. The Punjab government has already issued a notification in this respect. Similarly, under the green stimulus project, electric buses will be operated from Islamabad Zoo to Monal.  Additionally, all brick kilns will be converted into zig-zag technology to reduce smog in big cities. He also stated that Islamabad’s master plan will be modified soon, for the first time since it was developed in the 1960s.
Read:
Master plan shared for Lahore’s Central Business District
In another development, Lahore Development Authority (LDA) Director General (DG) Ahmad Aziz Tarar said that the authority will allow multi-story buildings to be constructed on 26 roads in Lahore city. The initiative will promote the
vertical expansion of the city
while reducing unplanned housing societies. The decision was made following an assessment of the city’s commercialization efforts and monitoring. It was said that a strategy to prevent the unauthorised commercialization of important roadways is required. It was also agreed that the city needs a robust parking strategy to decrease traffic congestion.

title: ADB, Pak to conduct master study to assess gas storage infrastructure
full_text:
Islamabad: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) will provide technical assistance for a master study in Pakistan to identify and access development sites for gas storage facilities, news sources reported on January 24. The study would recommend ranking at least two underground and two over-ground gas storage facilities by December 2023.
Read:
SNGPL, SSGC shares details about major gas transmission projects
According to reports, the study will be conducted by ADB’s energy division of its Central and West Asia Department in collaboration with the ministry of energy.  The research will aid in the establishment of a legislative framework for connecting upstream, middle, and downstream infrastructure elements by December 2023. Similarly, private sector feedback will be sought for the model policy framework, which will be developed and approved by the
Cabinet Committee on Energy
by December 2023. Similarly, the project’s research will be based on the previous two technical assistance reports, which were produced in 2005 and 2019, respectively.
Read:
ADB to improve urban infrastructure in 5 KP cities, agreement signed
The study’s primary goal will be to find locations for strategic gas storage facilities and to stabilise the price market. In the long run, this will improve the
country’s energy security
.  The final analysis will focus on determining cost, mode, geology, and location closeness to transmission networks and load centres, market characteristics, ownership, and operation and maintenance, among other aspects.

title: PBS to hold 7th housing, population census
developer: According to reports, the Ministry of Planning and Development
full_text:
Islamabad: The Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) will conduct Pakistan’s 7th population and housing census this year, according to press reports on January 19. The census will be Pakistan’s first digital census, with the housing census taking place first, followed by the population census.
Read:
Lahore’s first-ever tree census begins
According to reports, the Ministry of Planning and Development has requested PKR 5 billion from the Ministry of Finance in order to complete the census utilising international standards and digital demographic methodologies.  In this respect, the Ministry of Planning has formed a
Census Advisory Committee (CAC
) comprising demographers and specialists to provide recommendations and supervise the process. It was said that the funding for the process’s commencement would be granted after the Economic Coordination Committee (ECC) granted its permission.
Read:
Pakistan to have 7th population & housing census
It is vital to note that the government has decided to update the last census, which was done in 2017. The new census was approved at the 49th meeting of the
Council of Common Interest (CCI)
, which was presided over by Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan and attended by Chief Ministers (CMs) from all four provinces. The conference also resolved to establish a permanent CCI secretariat to facilitate coordination and consensus on resource-related matters.

title: PC-1 of Gulberg Elevated Expressway approved
developer: Sardar Usman Buzdar, in a meeting of Lahore Development
full_text:
Lahore: Punjab Chief Minister (CM) Sardar Usman Buzdar, in a meeting of Lahore Development Authority (LDA), approved the PC-1 of Gulberg Elevated Expressway, from Main Gulberg to Islamabad-Lahore Motorway (M-2), according to news reports published on Thursday (January 20).
Read:
LCBDDA opens pre-
launch registrations for 7 commercial plots in Gulberg
During the meeting, the chief minister ordered the relevant departments to ascertain the financing mechanism for the elevated expressway. He further added that the project must be
completed on a priority basis
.
Moreover, the meeting attendees were briefed about Lahore Master Plan 2050. It was decided that a supervisory committee will be formed for it. CM Buzdar ordered the authorities concerned to sync the plan with the emerging needs of the locals. He added that a feasible strategy should be submitted after consultation with stakeholders.
Read:
Signal-free corridor Road linking DHA Lahore with Gulberg approved
It is important to note that CM Buzdar, earlier in January, ordered the concerned departments to start work on the elevated expressway on a priority basis. As per the details, the expressway project will ease the burden of traffic on Canal Road and Multan Road. It was mentioned that the expressway will pass over Ferozepur Road, Canal Bank Road, Jail Road, Multan Road, and Bund Road to reach Babu Sabu Interchange.

title: Galiyat opens for tourists, Home Dept bifurcates Saddar Division
full_text:
Murree: The Galiyat Development Authority has allowed tourists to visit the Galiyat region to enjoy the snowfall season, effectively resuming tourism in the region, news sources reported on January 19. The GDA and district administration allowed tourists vehicles in the region following the improvement of weather conditions.
Read:
Murree to get district status, have two parking plazas
As per the GDA spokesperson, the Meteorological  Office has forecast another spell of snowfall in Galiyat from Wednesday. The administration has decided to restrict some areas and the movement of tourists within a 25km area between Bagnotar and Dongagali over fears of landslides and avalanches. Tourists will be permitted to approach the Galiyat region through the Abbottabad-Nathiagali Road, but access to places beyond Donga Gali to Bariyan would be limited. Meanwhile, the Punjab Home Department has authorised the subdivision of
Rawalpindi’s Saddar division
into subdivisions with as many police stations in Murree as there are in Rawalpindi.
Read:
Entry ban in Murree extended, snowfall warnings for next week
Following clearance, a new divisional superintendent of police (SP) (BS-18) position would be formed in Murree to ensure the presence of 18 ranking police officers in the most frequented hill station. Similarly, three police stations would be established in Murree to maintain peace and order.

title: FWO awards contract for expansion of Islamabad Expressway
developer: As per the details shared, the Capital Development
full_text:
Islamabad: The Frontier Works Organisation (FWO) on Monday (January 17) was awarded the contract for the expansion of a 2-kilometre portion of Islamabad Expressway, from Korang Bridge to PWD Interchange, according to media reports.
Read:
CDA shares completion timelines for PWD Underpass, Korang Bridge
As per the details shared, the Capital Development Authority (CDA) called tenders under Rule 42(f) of the Public Procurement Regulatory Authority (PPRA). According to the rules, only government companies could participate in the bidding process. The FWO submitted the lowest bid of PKR 2.3 billion while the National Logistics Cell (NLC) submitted the bid of PKR 2.4 billion.
A CDA senior official stated that the authority wants the project to be completed as early as possible due to the traffic congestion and difficulties faced by motorists on daily basis.
Reportedly, the 2-kilometre long road from Korang Bridge to PWD Underpass and Railway Bridge will be constructed in 15-months. The expressway is one of the busiest roads because of the increase in the number of housing societies along its length. But, mainly because of the sudden transformation of the four-lane highway into two-lane at Korang bridge.
Read:
CDA renamed PWD Road after Dr Abdul Qadeer Khan
Presently, construction work on the widening of
Korang Bridge
is undergoing and is expected to be complete by April. The CDA is also planning to expand the remaining 7-kilometre long road from PWD to G.T. Road to address the traffic problems.

title: WAPDA to convert water supply schemes to solar power in KP
full_text:
Peshawar: The Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA) and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP)’s irrigation department on Monday (January 10) decided to convert water supply schemes onto the solar power system, news sources reported. In this regard, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed between the two entities to start the process.
Read:
First unit of Mohmand Dam to start functioning by Dec 2025: WAPDA
As per the reports, the funds for the solarisation will be provided by the
European Union’s Grant Community
Development Project, which is an international Non-Governmental Organisation (NGO) working for the development of local communities. The project will assist in reducing power outages, as well as the associated water supply delays and hindrances in various sections of the province. It was also disclosed that the initiative will assist to alleviate electricity difficulties, allowing the population to have better access to
potable and clean drinking water
. The MoU signing event was attended by the secretary of irrigation Idress Khan, the chief engineer of the central public health engineering department, Wapda, and other authorities.
Read:
ADB to improve urban infrastructure in 5 KP cities, agreement signed
It is also worth noting that the
Asian Development Bank (ADB)
has signed an MOU with KP to give USD 350 million for the development of three sewage treatment facilities, two clean water treatment facilities, and the rehabilitation of defective tube wells.

title: Seven companies pre-qualify for Sagian Road project
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) has released a list of firms that have prequalified for the Sagian Road project, news sources reported. As per the notification released a total of seven firms have qualified for the PKR 3.4 billion development project aimed at alleviating the city’s traffic congestion problem.
Read:
PC-1 for Lahore’s road infrastructure projects sent for approval
Reportedly, LDA Chief Engineer Mazhar Hussain Khan has issued the letter to the qualified firms that will be followed by the bidding process. The companies that have qualified for the initiative in the process include; Habib Construction Services, Khalid Roof Company, Saadullah Khan Brothers, KNK Private Limited,
National Logistics Company (NLC)
, Sultan Mahmood & Co., and Zoriz Engineering Company.
Read:
LDA proposes underpass at Gulshan-e-Ravi T Junction
It is important to note that the Sagian Road rehabilitation project is part of a
multi-billion rupee
road infrastructure
development project for the provincial capital, launched by the Punjab government. As per Project Concept-1 (PC-1), a road will be built from Sagian Road to Phol Mandi Chowk to Faizpur Interchange. The route is one of the busiest in the city, with commuters and heavy traffic using it to enter and exit the city.

title: LDA ordered to finalise details on city’s first electric tram project
developer: Sardar Usman Buzdar ordered the Lahore Development
full_text:
Lahore: Punjab Chief Minister (CM) Sardar Usman Buzdar ordered the Lahore Development Authority (LDA) to start work on finalising the details of city’s first electric tram project on Canal Road, according to a news story published on Monday (January 3).
Read:
Ek Moria Pull project to be separately developed: LDA
CM Buzdar was briefed on the project by LDA Director General Ahmed Aziz Tarar and Chief Engineer Israr Saeed. As per the details, LDA has submitted a plan to CM Buzdars pertaining to operating an electric tram from Thokar to Jallo.
Read:
LDA allows conversion of agricultural land for industrial use on Bedian Road
Reportedly, the tram project will have 21 smart stations constructed on the
22-kilometre long Canal Road
. It will feature an 8-feet wide track on both sides of the road. Moreover, the speed of the tram will be 25 to 30 KMPH. According to the estimates, the total cost of the project is more than PKR 21 billion.

title: ‘Gulberg’s Elevated Expressway to be launched on priority’
full_text:
Lahore: Chief Minister (CM) Sardar Usman Buzdar on Tuesday (January 4) has ordered the authorities concerned to start work on the elevated expressway from Gulberg to Islamabad-Lahore (M-2) on a priority, according to news sources.
Read:
Signal-free corridor Road linking DHA Lahore with Gulberg approved
CM Buzdar made these remarks as he chaired a review meeting for
Gulberg-M2 Expressway
in his office. Lahore Development Authority (LDA) Director General Ahmed Aziz Tarar briefed the meeting’s attendees on the recently-announced project. Adviser Dr Salman Shah, Planning & Development Chairman Muhammad Abdullah Khan Sumbal and secretaries of transport and housing departments attended this meeting.
As per the details, the elevated expressway will ease the traffic burden on Multan Road and Canal Road and help travellers reach the motorway easily. The expressway will pass over Canal Bank Road, Ferozepur Road, Jail Road, Multan Road, and Bund Road to reach Babu Sabu Interchange.
Read:
LCBDDA opens pre-launch registrations for 7 commercial plots in Gulberg
Reportedly, interchanges will be constructed on Jail Road, Canal Road, Multan Road, Ferozepur Road, and Bund Road. The Gulberg Expressway will reduce the commute time to 40 minutes only.

title: Rawalpindi’s Ammar Chowk Flyover opens to traffic
full_text:
Rawalpindi: Army Chief General Qamar Javed Bajwa on Tuesday (December 28) inaugurated the Ammar Chowk Flyover, according to news sources. The
Ammar Shaheed Chowk
extension and remodelling project was completed three days before the scheduled time.
Read:
Rawalpindi’s remodeled Ammar Chowk to open for traffic by Dec 31
As per the details, the project sustained several design changes and the construction was started in early 2021. According to the approved design, twin underpasses were constructed and a new service line was added. It also included undergrounding of High Tension (H.T) and Low Tension (L.T) cables.
Read:
Progress reviewed on Rawalpindi’s Ammar Chowk
Reportedly, the project was part of the four mega projects announced by the Punjab government to ensure the smooth flow of traffic in the cantonment city. Previously, Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) Chairman Tariq Mahmood Murtaza stated that once the Ammar Chowk project was completed, a PKR 3.8 billion two-story flyover project, in early 2022, will be started at Kutchery Chowk that will be followed by PKR 2.1 billion Defence Chowk project.

title: Punjab procures Intl’ funding for 11 projects planned in FY 2021-22

Lahore: The Punjab government Economic Affairs Division has announced receiving international assistance for eleven development projects in the province, news sources reported. A total of 26 projects were proposed to donors and international financial institutions for funding.

Pakistan, ADB finalise loan agreement for urban development projects in Punjab

World Bank suggests building new port in Balochistan to address demand

has provided assistance for the following projects:

title: CDWP refers Karachi water project to ECNEC for approval
full_text:
Islamabad: The Central Development Working Party (CDWP) on Monday (December 27) approved development projects worth PKR 191.722 billion, including Karachi’s 650 million gallons daily (MGD) water supply project K-IV, news sources reported. Other projects include the NIH safe blood transfusion project and Policy Papers (PP) related to education and the Information and Technology Sector.
Read:
Chinese firm shows interest in completing Karachi’s K-IV water supply project
According to reports, CDWP authorities have recommended the PKR 191.194 billion ‘G
reater Karachi Bulk Water Supply Scheme K-IV
650 MGD (1st Revised)’ water project to the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (Ecnec) for further consideration after deliberations and recommendations. The committee also proposed that the project’s scope be reduced by 260 MGD and cost by  PKR 126 billion before it is submitted to ECNEC, as well as the formation of a committee to address specific difficulties and concerns.
Read:
CDWP clears Rawalpindi Ring Road, Leh Expressway projects
According to the ministry of water and power, the project is intended to relieve the citizens of water crisis. Similarly, the committee approved a revised safe blood transfusion services project for Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) for PKR 528 million under the National Institute of Health (NIH).

title: LDA allows conversion of agricultural land for industrial use on Bedian Road
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) has approved the conversion of 450 kanal of agricultural land on Bedian Road to industrial land for a Chinese company looking to establish an industrial unit there, news sources reported on December 27. The special provision was made during LDA governing body meeting to approve the PKR 25 billion project in accordance with Rule 13 of the LDA Land Use Rules-2020.
Read:
CM Buzdar approved LDA-led infrastructure projects for Lahore
Reportedly, the decision was made on an application submitted in May by a Chinese corporate to grant land for the construction of an industrial unit in Mauza Pandoki, Model Town Tehsil, Lahore. The decision to grant the land for the industry was taken after deliberation over the use of land for non-hazardous industry and issuance of the No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Environment Protection Department (EPD). Similarly, the planned project was scrutinized by the
Punjab Board of Investment and Trade (PBIT)
in terms of investment. Following the clearance from the relevant authorities, the plan was presented to the LDA governing body for final approval.
Read:
LDA approved 48 land-use conversions within one week: Vice Chairman
It is important to note that the approval was given under the LDA 2020 Land-Use Rules which allow the
conversion of agricultural land to industrial
land if the proposed project is worth a minimum of PKR 5 billion to 6 billion and the land demanded for the purpose is at least 160 kanal.

title: Signal-free corridor Road linking DHA Lahore with Gulberg approved

full_text:
Lahore: The Punjab government on Wednesday (December 22) approved a signal-free corridor that will link the Defence Housing Authority (DHA) to Gulberg for flow smooth of traffic, media sources reported.
Read:
Work resumed on Lahore’s signal-free Maulana Shaukat Ali Road
As per the details, the Lahore Development Authority (
LDA
) has prepared the plan to develop a signal-free road from Gulberg’s Centre Point to Defence Mor. The project was approved by Chief Minister (CM) Sardar Usman Buzdar.
Sharing more details, it was disclosed that a one-way flyover will be developed at the Ghora Chowk Cavalry along with an underpass at Khalid Butt Chowk. Additionally, a four-lane dual carriageway with a two-way underpass will be constructed at Khalid Butt Chowk. A three-lane single-sided flyover will be constructed at Ghora Chowk from Cavalry Ground towards Defence turn.
Read:
Govt to unveil Lahore Master Plan on December 31

CM Buzdar ordered the Standing Committee on Finance to include it in Annual Development Programme (ADP). The committee has included PKR 2.80 billion for the project in the budget.

title: Govt to unveil Lahore Master Plan on December 31
full_text:
Lahore: Punjab Minister for Local Government Mian Mahmood-ur-Rashid on Wednesday (December 22) announced the unveiling of the Lahore Master Plan on December 31, 2021, news sources reported. The master plan of the city will focus on the development of sustainable urban infrastructure.
Read:
NESPAK among firms shortlisted for development of Lahore Master Plan 2050
As per the news, during a provincial assembly questions session, the minister said that the new master plan will help reduce the growing population problems and the increasing pressure on resources. This plan will also focus on the regularisation of illegal housing schemes built on either state or agricultural land. The minister also stated that the initiative will contribute to the city’s sustainability. Recently, the
Lahore Development Authority (LDA) has held seminars
to consult foreign specialists and engineers, as well as members of the general public in a bid to take their suggestions into account while planning the city’s infrastructure. According to LDA sources, the plan would focus on four areas: smart city infrastructure, urban transit, urban governance, pollution, and regularisation of urban developments.
Read:
Lahore master plan will be finalised in consultation with LCCI: LDA VC Imran
It is crucial to note that the Lahore Master Plan has been in the
works since 2019
, and the government has recommended developing master plans for all of the province’s major cities to assist them to prepare for future issues.

title: LDA handovers 122 kanals to health department for hospital project
full_text:
Lahore:  Punjab Chief Minister (CM) Sardar Usman Buzdar on Saturday (December 18) gave approval for the transfer of 122-kanal land near Kot Lakhpat to the Health Department for the construction of a 1000-bed hospital project, news sources reported. The conditional approval was given during the Lahore Development Authority’s governing body meeting.
Read:
SECP warns against investing in ‘real estate fractionalisation’ schemes
As per the report, in compliance with the directions of CM Buzdar, the LDA  Director General (DG) Ahmed Aziz Tara has notified the physical possession of the land for the construction of a Specialised Healthcare and Medical Education Department (SH&MED). The land was sold to the department for PKR 2.033 billion, which the health department plans to deposit in the LDA account by February 1, 2022. During the meeting, the chief executive also approved the tourism department’s request to extend the deadline for depositing unpaid dues for the utility site assigned in the
Abdalian Housing Scheme
. Similarly, in order to accommodate the allottees of the
LDA Avenue 1 project
, the meeting extended the deadline to deposit dues for the allotted plots in 60 days.
Read:
All new universities and hospitals in Punjab to be solarized
In addition, it was also decided to convert two plots in the Allama Iqbal Town fruit and vegetable market into a cold storage facility. CM Buzdar directed the concerned departments to expedite work on the approved and notified projects as soon as possible

title: Construction work begins on road infrastructure in Narowal District

Budget 2021-22: South Punjab gets 35% of ADP

. The following are the details about the construction work initiated:

Pakistan Railways to revive Narowal-Kartarpur railways line

title: RDA to connect Leh Expressway with I.J.P. Road, 10th Avenue
full_text:
Islamabad: The Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) seeks a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Capital Development Authority (CDA) to connect Leh Expressway with I.J.P Road and 10th Avenue, according to news published on Friday (December 10).
Read:
Islamabad’s IJP Road under construction at fast pace
As per the details, a meeting was held at CDA headquarters to review the design of the proposed overhead bridge to link Leh Expressway with 10th Avenue. The meeting was attended by National Engineering Services Pakistan (NESPAK), Zeeruk International (Pvt), CDA’s engineers, and consultants of RDA.
According to CDA officials, the proposed design was a joint effort of consultants of RDA and CDA. The design is being simplified to minimise the land acquisition requirement in the Rawalpindi area. 10th Avenue
via simple at-grade slip lanes and an overhead bridge over I.J.P road.

The RDA consultants were also asked to inform about the estimated cost of linking the expressway.  Moreover, major decisions related to the cost of land to be paid to the CDA and the issue of toll sharing will be taken up in the Central Development Working party (CDWP) and Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC).
Read:
RDA starts demarcation of land to be acquired for Leh Expressway project

title: CDA directs departments to improve city’s road infrastructure, aesthetics
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Monday (December 06) directed the road maintenance department to complete rehabilitation and renovation work by the end of the week, news sources reported. In this regard, the road department has begun work on the restoration of roadways across the capital city.
Read:
CDA to construct portion of Rawalpindi Ring Road
Work has begun in areas such as F-5
, Agha Khan Road, 7th Avenue
, G-7, G-5, F-7, Serena Chowk, and Soharwardi Road, according to the report. Patching, painting curbstones, and traffic lane marking are all part of the restoration effort. Furthermore, the CDA has directed the relevant department to work on the repair and installation of street lighting in several major markets, parking lots, and roadways. Funds have been made available in this respect. The authority has also directed that murals and cultural designs be painted on numerous bus stations and underpasses in order to promote culture and enhance the city’s aesthetics.
