Kamyab Pakistan Programme (KPP)
.
Read:
ADB predicts Pakistan’s 4% growth rate in FY22
Minister Tarin also stated that the administration has implemented changes in 14 government sectors as recommended by the Economic Advisory Committee (EAC). He stated that
reforms in the power sector
and effective collection of dues have strengthened the power industry and are likely to deliver more advantages to the entire economy. Mr Ye also informed the finance minister that ADB has approved USD 500 million for the vaccine programme of which USD 350 million have been already provided.

title: Joint Working Group formed to include IT in CPEC
full_text:
Islamabad:  China and Pakistan on Tuesday (September 21) announced the formation of a Joint Working Group (JWG) on Information Technology (IT) under the China Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), news sources reported.
Read:
Govt to put IT sector development on CPEC agenda
The said decision to establish the Joint Working Group (JWG) was made during the
10th Joint Cooperation Committee (JCC) meeting
held recently in Islamabad. The aim of the inclusion of the IT sector in the scope of CPEC was made to expand and widen the current CPEC collaboration and make it more profitable for all parties concerned.
Initially, Pakistan has prepared 10 projects for IT inclusion in CPEC. The newly-formed JWG will work on the projects related to IT transactions, ecommerce, IT infrastructure, technical collaborations & training, data centre, incubation centre and IT services. Following the approval of these projects, both sides will formally execute the projects.
Read:
Pakistan, China to collaborate on IT sector development under CPEC
The meeting which took place virtually in Islamabad was presided over by Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Asad Umar, while the Chinese side was represented by National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) Deputy Head Ning Jizhe.

title: Coastline revamp project worth USD 3.5 bn approved for Karachi
developer: Zaidi, the Karachi Coastal Comprehensive Development
full_text:
Karachi: The federal government on Saturday (September 25) announced a USD 3.5 billion plan to rebuild Karachi’s coastline as part of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), news sources reported. The decision was announced by the Joint Cooperation Committee (JCC) on CPEC, held on September 23, in Islamabad and Beijing.
Read:
Federal govt looking to develop islands off Karachi coast
According to Minister of Maritime Affairs Syed Ali Zaidi, the project would be completed entirely with direct Chinese investment, without the requirement for a loan. The proposal aims for overhauling the city with more berths for the port, a new fishing port, and a ‘majestic harbour bridge’ connecting the city to Manora islands and Sandspit beach. According to Zaidi, the Karachi Coastal Comprehensive Development Zone (KCCDZ) will cover 640 hectares or 1,581 acres on the Karachi Port Trust’s western backwaters marshes (KPT).
Read:
Bill tabled in Sindh Assembly to expand Coastal Development Authority’s jurisdiction
Furthermore, the government also intends to construct low-cost housing for 20,000 people living in adjacent fisherman colonies and slums as part of the project. In addition, the project will contain a cutting-edge fishing port with a fisheries export and processing zone. Reportedly, Prime Minister Imran Khan has lauded the development and predicted that the inclusion of Karachi’s coastal development plan in CPEC will bring the city at part with developed global port cities.

title: Punjab to implement E-tendering for transparency
full_text:
Lahore: The Punjab Housing Department on Wednesday (September 22) decided to implement an online system for tendering of government projects all over the province, news sources reported.
Read:
LDA launches online portal to receive applications, register public complaints
The decision was taken in a meeting presided over by the Provincial Minister for Housing Malik Asad Khokhar and attended by the Additional Secretary Housing Umar Farooq, Deputy Secretary Mumtaz Ahmed and PITB officials. The government will engage PITB for a centralised system to eradicate bribery culture.   According to the information shared, the proposed E-tendering system would be implemented in the Housing Department, Lahore Development Authority (LDA), Water and Sanitation Agency (WASA), and all other subordinate departments.
Read:
Lahore’s Ferozepur Road to be linked with motorway: Housing Minister
Following the system’s deployment, individuals will be able to bid for projects from the comfort of their own homes with a transparent system. A
call centre will also be developed to help consumers
with general questions.  The tender applicants will be given a unique code, and the computer will designate the qualifying firm for the respective tender award. During a press conference, the housing minister stated that only firms on the department’s approved list will be able to participate in the tendering process.

title: CDA to launch bus service, PC-1 approved
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority’s (CDA) Development Working Party (DWP) on Tuesday (September 14) approved the Islamabad Public Transport Project Concept-1 (PC-1), news sources reported. The meeting, presided over by CDA Chairman Amer Ali Ahmed authorised eight projects, including a bus service for Islamabad residents.
Read:
CDA mulls launching ‘Islamabad Bus Service’
According to the CDA spokesperson Asif Ali Raza, the PKR 873 million projects is scheduled to begin in February 2022. The proposed route for the buses includes Sohan Garden to Faisal Mosque, Bhara Kahu to Faiz Ahmed Faiz Metro Station and from Tarnol Railway Station to M5 Metro Station.
Read:
Transport route to Islamabad Airport opened; bids invited
In addition to this, funds were approved for the following projects:
PKR 193 million were approved for the construction of underpasses at the junction of Ataturk Avenue, G-5, and G-6
PKR 157 million has been approved for the widening of Jinnah Avenue and Ayub Chowk from Ataturk Avenue.
PKR 20 million is granted for a Smart City feasibility study, and it was agreed to create YouTube and FM radio channels to improve communication between the municipal authority and the people.
PKR 40 million were approved for the construction of 115 public restrooms in Islamabad
PKR 689 million has been set aside for the purchase of machinery for the modernisation of the sewage system.
Reportedly, all the projects are expected to complete in the coming six months.

title: PKR 5 billion development funds approved for KP districts
full_text:
Peshawar: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Planning and Development (P&D) department, on the directives of the Chief Minister (CM) Mahmood Khan, has approved PKR 5 billion worth of uplift projects for the seven merged districts and six sub-divisions, news sources reported.
Read:
PM receives briefing on uplift schemes, power projects underway in ex-FATA
The said uplift project includes the upgradation of streets, solarisation of bazaars, walkway renovation, sewerage projects, food streets, playing and recreational spaces, rescue stations, public toilet building, and slaughterhouse construction. All these projects are aimed at improving the economic activities and boost the local economy of the region.  According to the department’s details, CM Mehmood has approved PKR 600 million for 42
uplift projects in North Waziristan
, PKR 700 million for 140 projects in South Waziristan, PKR 260 million for Dera Ismail Khan’s Daraznada and Kohibahar sub-divisions, PKR 250 million for Tank district sub-divisions, and PKR 250 million for nine projects in Beltane sub-division.  A total of PKR 600 million has been approved for 52 projects in the Bajaur district, PKR 601 million for different uplift projects in the Orakzai district, and PKR 200 million for six bazaars in the Dara Adam Khel sub-division. Similarly, PKR 250 million has been authorised for tribal sub-division Hassan Khel’s upgradation and different development projects.
Read:
Govt to spend PKR 100bn annually on development of ex-Fata region
A sum of PKR 450 million has been granted for the launch of development projects in the bazaars of Khyber district’s Bara, Landi Kotal, and Jamrud tehsils, as well as PKR 650 million for uplift projects in Mohmand district. The provincial administration has directed the Deputy Commissioners (DC) of the respective areas to personally supervise the projects.

title: PM to inaugurate Karachi Circular Railway (KCR) this week
full_text:
Karachi: Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan is expected to inaugurate Karachi Circular Railways (KCR) on September 11, 2021, during his visit to Karachi, news sources reported.
Read:
Sindh to invest PKR 6 bn to operationalise KCR project: CM Murad
As per the KCR project details, the 43.13-kilometre-long modern circular railroad is a federally-sponsored project that will be completed in three phases. Once completed, the flagship project will serve a total of 550,000 people on a daily basis. According to sources in Railways, the project will comprise 14.95 kilometres on land while the remaining 28 kilometres of the project will be built on elevated pillars. A total of 24 stations have been included in the project.
The World Bank (WB),
the Asian Development Bank (ADB), and a
French bank
have all contributed to KCR’s funding. During his previous visit to Karachi in August, Minister for Planning, Development & Special Initiatives Asad Umer instructed the authorities to make all necessary preparations for KCR’s groundbreaking in the second week of September.
Read:
Work on KCR to start from September
According to reports, the premier – during his visit to Karachi – will also convene high-level meetings to assess progress on other federally sponsored projects, including the Karachi Green Line project, which is also a massive project aimed at improving Karachi mass transportation system and resolving traffic issues.

title: Committee formed to address Faisalabad Master plan concerns
full_text:
Faisalabad: The Faisalabad Development Authority (FDA) on Monday (August 30) formed a five-member committee to resolve difficulties preventing the approval of the Faisalabad Master Plan, news sources reported.
Read:
FDA unveils master plan for the city
The authority made the decision following a meeting with the
Faisalabad Chamber of Commerce and Industry (FCCI)
and developers of private housing schemes in Circuit House. The participants were briefed on the master plan by the private firm working on it.  To meet the city’s growing population and urban migration, the FDA has developed a Faisalabad Master Plan 2035. Concerns were expressed by FCCI members and private housing scheme representatives over the conversion of “Brown Areas” into “Green Zones” in order to boost vertical construction. The participants were also concerned by the conversion of peri-urban planning without prior notification or taking stakeholders into confidence.
Read:
FDA mulls proposals for enhancement of city’s master plan
Members of the FCCI also met with Shahbaz Gill, the prime minister’s adviser, to urge the premier’s assistance in the adoption of the master plan. In response, they were assured that a meeting with prime minister will be arranged to discuss the matter.

title: RDA to continue anti-encroachment drive against illegal constructions
full_text:
Rawalpindi: Chairman Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) Tariq Murtaza on Wednesday (August 25) directed all the departments to continue crackdown against
illegal housing constructions
and other unlawful building activities in the city, news sources reported.
Read:
Chairman RDA reviews progress of ongoing projects
He gave these directions during a performance review meeting, during which, Director Estate Management provided a thorough briefing on the RDA’s vacant land, transfer cases in RDA-owned properties, and verification and approval of residential and commercial structures.
Similarly, the Chief Engineer delivered a report on the city’s current development projects, including the
dualisation of Dr Qadeer Khan Road
from Islamabad Highway to Falcon Complex Rawalpindi and the construction of three pedestrian bridges on the Airport Road. The chairman appreciated the work on the development scheme and said that the employees must give their best and continue their work without any favour and fear.
Read:
RDA to launch housing scheme for its employees
The meeting was attended by Director Admn & Finance Asif Mehmood Janjua, Chief Engineer Aamir Rasheed, Director MP&TE Jamshaid Aftab, Director EM Saima Younus, Director LD Malik Ghazanfar, DD Engineering Azizullah, DD Finance Junaid Taj Bhatti, DD Admn Iftikhar Ahmad Janjua, DD IT Dawood Khalid, and other relevant officers.

title: Green spaces to be protected in Islamabad’s Zone III, IV
developer: The panel, chaired by Capital Development
full_text:
Islamabad: The reconstituted panel for the revision of Islamabad’s master plan met on Monday and resolved to safeguard shrinking green areas in Zones III and IV, while also working to resolve prevailing water and infrastructure issues in the federal capital, according to news sources.
Read:
Reconstit
u
ted commission to finalise Islamabad Master plan
The panel, chaired by Capital Development Authority Chairman Amir Ali, also examined Rawalpindi and Islamabad’s water concerns. The committee decided to incentivize inhabitants of the aforementioned
zones to conserve green spaces
.
The panel chose to focus greater emphasis on small dams, particularly the Chiniot Dam near Simly Dam and the Shahdara Dam. Both of these dams would supply 20 million gallons of potable water per day to Islamabad and Rawalpindi. In addition, the
commission agreed to appoint a technical consultant
for the updated master plan as soon as possible.
Read:
CDA to request land from Punjab for construction of small dam
A Greek firm developed Islamabad’s master plan in 1960, and it was meant to be amended every 20 years. However, with the exception of 43 minor modifications, the plan has not undergone a substantial revision since its inception. Previously, in 2018, the government reconstituted the 12-member panel and added three additional members to the body.

title: Reconstituted commission to finalise Islamabad Master plan
full_text:
Islamabad: The reconstituted commission for the execution and revision of the master plan of the capital city will meet on Monday (August 30) to sort out issues with the city’s infrastructure and planning, according to press reports.
Read:
CDA-DWP approves PC-II of Islamabad Master Plan (2020-40)’s Project Review
The commission will especially address Zone IV and Zone III problems. The federal government established the panel in 2018 to evaluate Islamabad’s Master Plan, which is supposed to be revised every 20 years.
However, there has been no change to the design since it was initially developed in the 1960s. Only 43 modifications have been made since then. The panel to evaluate the master plan last convened in 2019, and a
technical consulting firm was to be hired to assess the process
, but it was unable to do so for a various reasons.
Read:
Islamabad Master Plan 2040 to facilitate businessmen: CDA Chairman
According to sources familiar with the matter, the reconstituted commission plans to engage a consultant as soon as possible and complete the modification within a year. The three-member commission is meeting after a 1.5 years gap under the chairmanship of Maj Gen (Retired) Farrakh Javed, architects Murad Jamali and Sikandar Ajam. The commission will set forth important policy guidelines for the Capital Development Authority (CDA).

title: Punjab to launch 200 new development schemes
developer: Lahore, and the adoption of Lahore Development
full_text:
Lahore: Punjab Chief Minister (CM) Sardar Usman Buzdar has announced the launch of 200 new development projects across the province, news sources reported on August 24. In this respect, the chief minister has instructed Secretary of Housing Dr Zafar Nasrallah to call a meeting within three days.
Read:
Punjab releases FY 2021-22 funds for active development schemes
The proposed projects include the building of overhead bridges, underpasses, signal-free corridors in Lahore, and the adoption of Lahore Development Authority’s rules in all housing control authorities around the province in order to combat mushrooming of unlawful housing schemes. The government has planned to
develop land-use regulations
comparable to the LDA and to apply these regulations in other housing control bodies.
Read:
PDWP approves 8 development schemes for Punjab
In addition, the projects involve the building of underground water storage tanks to harvest rainwater in various parts of the province.  Director General LDA Ahmad Aziz Trar will update the Directors General (DGs) of Development Authorities and Water and Sanitation Agencies (WASAs) from Faisalabad, Multan, Gujranwala, and Rawalpindi at the forthcoming meeting held under Secretary Housing. According to sources, CM Buzdar wants all of the province’s major towns to be built in the same manner as Lahore.

title: Prequalification bids invited for Burki Road dualisation
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) has begun the process of pre-qualifying contractors for the dualisation of Burki Road and the rehabilitation of roads on both sides of the
Babu Sabu Interchange
news sources, reported. The government has invited bids for road repair around the Babu Sabu Interchange to be submitted by September 2.
Read:
PC-1 for Lahore’s road infrastructure projects sent for approval
Similarly, the pre-qualification proposals for the project to reroute Burki Road from Lahore School of Economics (LSE) to BRB are invited to be submitted by September 3. LDA has also asked firms with the requisite qualifications to submit pre-qualification proposals by September 4 for the rehabilitation of roads in New Islamia Park, Royal Park, Ranjha Road, Faisal Road, and Himayat-e-Islamia Road.
Read:
LDA to start development of Gulberg-Babu Sabu Elevated Expressway
Furthermore, the Parks and Horticulture Authority (PHA) has requested PKR 1 billion from the revenue department for the building of new parks and the maintenance of current parks. The revenue department, on the other hand, has granted PKR 500 million for PHA, and a summary has been sent to the cabinet for final approval of funds.

title: FDA mulls proposals for enhancement of city’s master plan
full_text:
Faisalabad: The Faisalabad Development Authority (FDA) convened a consultative meeting to receive public input and ideas on the
proposed Faisalabad 20-year Master Plan (2021-41)
, according to press reports. The meeting was held in the FDA committee room, where the committee proposed by FDA Director Dr Faisal Azeem accepted public proposals.
Read:
Secretary LG&CD Punjab approves formulation of master plan for 119 cities
The representative of the private business firm informed the meeting regarding the suggested master plan. Later, private firms and people provided feedback on how to improve the plan, which was accepted by the committee for additional deliberation and incorporation into the final plan, if viable.
Speaking on the occasion, FDA Chairman Chaudhry Latif Nazar stated that all available resources are being used to make the proposed 20-year master plan more comprehensive and technically sound. In this regard, the inclusion of all stakeholders in the consultation process is critical to ensuring that the plan is consistent with on-the-ground realities.
Read:
FDA is
s
ues list of sanctioned housing projects
The FDA Chairman Chaudhry Latif Nazar, Acting Additional Director/director Finance Azam Malik, and committee members attended the consultation session. Aside from that, individuals from all walks of life and businesses organisations and technical consultants attended the meeting.

title: LDA governing body approves development budget for FY 2021-22
full_text:
Lahore: Chief Minister (CM) of Punjab Usman Buzdar on Tuesday (August 17) approved the Lahore Development Authority (LDA)’s PKR 63.4 billion development budget for the fiscal year 2021-22, news sources reported. The decision was made during a meeting of the governing body, which was presided over by CM Buzdar.
Read:
Lahore
master plan will be finalised in consultation with LCCI: LDA VC Imran
Moreover, the sources also mentioned that the governing council also approved PKR 48.7 billion in amended budget projections for the fiscal year 2020-21. It has been highlighted that the approved budget is also susceptible to modifications made by the departments of planning and development, finance, and housing. A breakdown of the budget for the development and non-development programmes for the fiscal year 2021-22 includes:
PKR 9.4 billion is already available for the urban development wing (UDW), Water and Sanitation Agency (WASA) and Traffic Engineering & Planning Authority (TEPA)
PKR 22.5 billion and PKR 41.4 billion to be received from the government as non-development, annual development programme and deposit work receipts
Read:
TEPA shares details of high-rise buildings approved in Lahore
The LDA, on the other hand, is expected to spend PKR 61 billion in the fiscal year 2021-22. The authority has set aside PKR 36.6 billion for urban development projects, PKR 24 billion for the Water and Sanitation Agency (WASA), and PKR 342 million for TEPA programmes and other development and non-development initiatives.
The body has approved a six-month extension to the validity of a commission set up ‘for the rights of bona fide purchasers and the issues related to illegal housing schemes’. Moreover, PKR 500 million bridge financing for
LDA City Naya Pakistan Apartments
, amendments to LDA building and zoning regulations 2019 and a few other proposals were also approved.

title: SBP announces ‘SME Asaan Finance’ or SAAF scheme for collateral free financing
payment_plan_text: and improvement of SMEs | After three years, the refinance will be repaid by banks in 10 equal yearly instalments. | In order to support banks, the government will also provide risk coverage of 40-60% to selected banks against losses based on the loan amount. The risk cover will be: | • 60% for small loans up to PKR 4 million | • 50% for midsize loans falling between PKR 4 million and PKR 7 million | • 40% for relatively large loans between PKR 7 million and PKR 10 million.
full_text:
Karachi: The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) has introduced ‘SME Asaan Finance’ or SAAF scheme for the Small Medium Enterprises (SMEs) to get loans without collateral, a news source reported on August 16. Under the announced scheme, SMEs that were previously unable to obtain funding owing to a lack of collateral will be able to obtain a clean loan of up to PKR 10 million.
Read:
FM Qureshi invites Sri Lankan businessmen to invest in Pakistan
SBP indicated that these loans will be utilised to address SMEs’ long-term fixed capital investment and working capital credit needs. Shaukat Tarin, the Federal Minister of Finance and Revenue, stated that the move will usher in a new age of growth and
industrialization in the country.
He expressed hopes that commercial banks will also join the initiative.
‘Selected banks will get refinance from the SBP at 1 percent per annum and extend financing to SMEs at end user rate of up to 9pc p.a. which is very attractive compared to informal finance costs,” according to SBP.
Read:
PM for promotion and improvement of SMEs
After three years, the refinance will be repaid by banks in 10 equal yearly instalments.
In order to support banks, the government will also provide risk coverage of 40-60% to selected banks against losses based on the loan amount. The risk cover will be:
• 60% for small loans up to PKR 4 million
• 50% for midsize loans falling between PKR 4 million and PKR 7 million
• 40% for relatively large loans between PKR 7 million and PKR 10 million.

title: Anti-encroachment operation underway at Margalla Hills
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) and the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT)
continue anti-encroachment drive against illegal constructed
infrastructure in Margalla Hills, according to news reports shared on August 16. The directives in this regard were issued by CDA Chairman Aamer Ali Ahmed who is also the chief commissioner of the capital city.
Read:
Demarcation of Margalla Hills’ forest land demanded to avoid encroachment
The anti-encroachment drive has been underway for the last three days, the authorities demolished a number of unlawfully built structures in Gokina and Talhar areas of Margalla Hills. These include several quarters and boundary walls, according to a CDA official who monitored the anti-encroachment operation.
The drive is part of the CDA’s continuous anti-encroachment campaign to prevent illegal encroachment on Margalla Hills and against the land grabbers that are using the protected land for commercial activities.
Read:
Survey of Margalla Road begins; development work up next
According to CDA officials, moving the heavy machinery in the hilly terrain of the Margalla Hills was difficult but the operation was conducted successfully. Reportedly, the authorities also had a talk with the locals who agreed to extend their full support against the land mafia.

title: Development work on Key Faisalabad roads started
developer: April 2021, following approval from the Provincial Development
full_text:
Faisalabad: Construction work on key roads connecting the district of Faisalabad with surrounding tehsil including Samundri Road and Jhang Road has started, news sources reported. The restructuring and reconstruction of dilapidated Samundri Road has been ongoing for a month, and work on Jhang Road has also begun.
Read:
Work on Faisalabad’s SEZ underway at a rapid pace: Bajwa
Faisalabad Chamber of Commerce and Industries (FCCI) President Engr. Hafiz Ihtasham Javed expressed his delight at the start of development work. He stated that the city of Faisalabad draws thousands of textile workers who come to the city in search of work and that the development of roads would enhance the city’s infrastructure, encouraging greater industrialisation and create more job opportunities.
Read:
First phase of Allama Iqbal Industrial City Faisalabad complete
According to reports, rehabilitation work on these roads began in April 2021, following approval from the Provincial Development Working Party (PDWP). Other projects approved by the government included
construction of Satiana Road from By-Pass to Tandilianwala
at a cost of PKR 500 million, rehabilitation/improvement of roads from MC Limits up to Faisalabad Ring Road and rehabilitation of Faisalabad-Jaranwala Road and Faisalabad-Satiana Road.

title: Centre to aid Punjab to speed up the process of industrial estates’ colonisation
full_text:
Lahore: Advisor to Prime Minister on Commerce and Investment Abdul Razak Dawood on Saturday (August 7) said that the federal government will extend all possible help to Punjab for the colonisation of industrial estates, news sources reported.
Read:
Punjab SMEs Policy, establishment of small industrial estate approved
Advisor Dawood met with the Punjab Minister for Industries and Commerce Mian Aslam Iqbal to discuss the matter related to the establishment of industrial estates and an expo centre in Sialkot, an income tax refund of Punjab Industrial Estates Development and Management Company (PIEDMC)’s construction of an interchange on the motorway to link Quaid-Azam Business Park in Sheikhupura, and colonisation of industrial estates in the province.
The meeting took place in the
Punjab Board of Investment and Trade (PBIT)
office and was co-chaired by Dawood and Iqbal. The meeting members also agreed to fine those who have not yet established their industries on the allotted land within the time limit specified.
Read:
EoIs invited from investors interested in Gujrat Small Industrial estate
In addition, it was decided to establish a joint one window facility by the Federal Board of Investment (FBI) and Punjab Board of Investment (PBI) to address the grievances of the investors. Minister Aslam said that the
establishment of an expo centre
at every divisional headquarters is necessary.

title: Work on PKR 44 bn Cities Development Programme Phase 1 nearing completion
full_text:
Lahore: Punjab Secretary Local Government (LG) Noor-ul-Amin Mengal on Wednesday (August 4) said that under the PKR 44 billion Cities Development Programme Phase 1, development work in Sahiwal and Sialkot is near completion, news sources reported. He shared this information while briefing Provincial Minister for
Local Government and Community Development (LG)
Mian Mehmood-ur-Rasheed on the project’s development.
Read:
Two road projects approved for Sahiwal
According to Megal, development schemes for Sargodha, Muzaffargarh, Rahim Yar Khan, DG Khan, Bahawalpur, and Multan will be included in the project’s second phase. The meeting was also updated on the status of the Punjab Cities Program and the Punjab Intermediate
Cities Improvement Investment Program.
The secretary further informed the meeting that under the Punjab Cities Program, work on establishing municipal infrastructure is being carried out in 16 cities across the province at a cost of PKR 34 billion. Under this programme, infrastructure development and city improvement projects such as water supply, sewerage, waste management, public parks, and street lighting installation will be done. These developments will be done in accordance with international development standards.
Read:
Funds allocated for the restoration of Lahore’s historic buildings
Minister Rasheed instructed the relevant authorities to expedite and complete the development projects within the specified timeframes.

title: Alternate highway for tourists heading to Murree via Rawalpindi on cards
full_text:
Rawalpindi: In a press conference on held on Thursday (Aug 5), Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) Chairman Tariq Mehmood Murtaza said that an alternate route from Rawalpindi to Murree and other, newly establish tourist destinations will be constructed, according to news sources. The planned highway will pass through the four tehsils of Rawalpindi.
Read:
RDA Budget 2021-22 revealed
During the meeting, the chairman also mentioned that a new approval system for Private Housing Societies and Building Plans has been set up. He went on to say that over 1,600 maps of multi-storied and residential buildings were approved in the current year, making it the highest in the history of RDA.

Qadeer Khan Road

The chairman also shared details the ongoing projects:

Construction of bridges and pedestrians on old Airport Road at the cost of PKR 109.934 million.

PKR 30,250 million for land acquisition for Nullah Leh

RDA plans Miyawaki forests in Rawalpindi to curb pollution
PKR 3,630 million for remodelling of Katchri Chowk
PKR 2,220 million for remodelling of Defence Chowk

title: CDA generates almost double the expected revenue from plots auction
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Thursday (August 5) raised PKR 37.945 billion during the two-day auction of 24 commercial plots in the federal capital’s business areas, nearly double the
estimated amount of PKR 20 billion
, news sources reported.
Read:
CDA approves design plans for two parking plazas in Blue Area
As per the details, the CDA received bids of PKR 17.5 billion for 11 plots on the second day of the auction. While it received PKR 20 billion offers for 13 plots on the first day of the auction. CDA mulls launching ‘Islamabad Bus Service’

title: Communication ministry directed to expedite work on Zhob-Quetta, Thakot-Raikot road projects
full_text:
Islamabad: During a meeting of the Pak-China Relations Steering Committee on Monday, Planning Minister Asad Umar directed the Ministry of Communication to speed up work on the development of the Zhob-Quetta Road and Thakot-Raikot Road projects, according to news sources. He further directed the ministry to submit proposals to the Cabinet by next week so that the project can be moved to the next development stage.
Read:
CPEC Western route reaching fast completion: Asim Bajwa
On the occasion, the attendees were informed that the interest of local and foreign investors in the Dhabeji Special Economic Zone (SEZ) was growing and that any delay in the process to finalise a developer for the project could prove to be problematic. title: Development work to be launched soon in Central Business District of Lahore
full_text:
Lahore: Central Business District Development Authority (CBDA) Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Imran Amin said that the civil works on the 28 acres of
Central Business District
(CBD) will start by the end of August 2021, news sources reported. The required planning and development paperwork is currently being completed, following which, the authority will begin infrastructure development work that will include roads, sewers, parking places, walkways, and other civil construction.
Read:
Plan formalised to turn Walton Airport land into a business center
Moreover, the CBD will also auction 5 plots for the construction of high rise buildings on August 4 – under a 33-year extendable lease. The five plots up for sale in the first week of August have a maximum size of 18 Kanal and a minimum size of 10 Kanal.
The total area of the CBD is estimated to be around 278 acres, which is divided into two parts. Out of total land, 122 acres lie along the Ferozpur Road (starting from Kalma Chowk-Ferozepur Road to Walton Road’s originating point and some parts of Gulberg),  while the remaining 156-acre land is under the jurisdiction of Walton Airport and the Bab-e-Pakistan. Reportedly, the construction is now underway on the 28 acres of commercial land in the Walton area.
Read:
Business district to be established on Walton Airport land
During a project briefing, the chief stated that the auctioning of the building is intended to encourage vertical living in the city and avoid encroachment on green space. As per the source, the CBD will feature 120 commercial highrises and 40 to 50 vertical apartment complexes for its residential phases when completed.
Prime Minister Imran Khan launched the project
on February 26, calling it an “out-of-the-box” solution for wealth generation and the promotion of sustainable growth.

title: First phase of Allama Iqbal Industrial City Faisalabad complete
full_text:

Moreover, he said that Prime Minister Imran Khan has directed the ministries and the FIEDMC management to facilitate
foreign and domestic investors
and establish a one-window operation to expedite the work and improve delivery. Mr Kashif also said that the provision of facilities like basic infrastructure, including gas, electricity, roads and civic centres is the priority of the authorities.
Read:

The Allama Iqbal Industrial City is a 3,300-acre specialised industrial project that will feature Furniture City, Apparel Park, a modern business centre, and the country’s largest expo centre when completed. The industrial units are being assigned to export-oriented industries.

road networks, hospitals, educational institutions
, community centres, and parks in response to the city’s growing population.

title: Govt spent 101.4% of PSDP budget in FY2020-21: Asad Umar

full_text:
Islamabad: The Minister for Planning and Development Asad Umar tweeted on Tuesday (July 27) and said that the annual spending under the Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP) during the fiscal year 2020-21 has surpassed the annual target with 101.4% funds spent of the total allocated budget, news sources reported.
Read:
PSDP 2021-22: Funds earmarked for 92 hydropower, water projects
A total of PKR 659 billion has been spent on development projects across the country against the allocated amount of PKR 650 billion. Minister Umar shared the news via a microblogging platform and said that the spending is the highest since the fiscal year 2011-12 and associated the ‘exceptionally high development spending’ with Prime Minister Imran Khan’s resolve to accelerate national economic growth.
Reportedly, the PSDP spending remained low (during the first 10 months of the FY 2020-21 at around PKR 373.8 billion (57.5%) and only increased during the last two months of the financial year.
Read:
Planning ministry for prioritizing inclusion of CPEC projects in PSDP 2021-22
Previously, the federal government had allocated PKR 553 billion during the fiscal year 2019-2020, of which only PKR 540.7 billion was utilised, showing a surplus budget. During this fiscal year (FY) 2021-22, the federal government has allocated
PKR 900 billion for the PSDP
, which is the highest so far. As of now, the government has already released PKR 133.6 billion in the first 16 days of the fiscal year – which is 14.85% of the annual budget.

title: CDA to implement environmental management plan during IJP Road project
full_text:
Islamabad: Pakistan Environmental Protection Agency (Pak-EPA) on Monday ordered the Capital Development Authority (CDA) to make sure proper environmental management plan (EMP) is implemented during the rehabilitation and widening of IJP Road, according to media reports.
Read:
Construction work starts on Islamabad’s 7th Avenue Interchange, I.J.P Road
According to Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Monitoring Director Ahsan Rafi Kiani, CDA authorities were required to provide a Traffic Diversion Plan, a baseline data revived report, and the location of the camp office as the agency has acquired the
IJP Road
project. He went on to say that the information obtained must be shared in order for the EIA Report to be approved.
Furthermore, the director advised CDA staff to make the required arrangements to relocate 1,265 trees from the project site. Mr Kiani added that it is critical to investigate the survival rate of the plants transplanted previously in Islamabad before transplantation. The CDA will also plant 8,000 trees along the route, according to reports.
In addition, the director ordered CDA officials to design a working mechanism and a better location for plant operation during the project. Besides that, the director rejected the CDA’s proposal to dump waste or surplus material at the I-12 sector as it is a residential neighborhood. Instead, the Margalla Town site would be used for waste disposal.
During the meeting, CDA officials informed participants that the entire length of the road to be rehabilitated and widened is 10.2 km. Two extra lanes will be added on both sides of the road as part of this project. Furthermore, it was stated that the project would be self-financed and will be implemented in 18 months. According to PC-I, the project’s estimated cost was PKR 6.9 billion. A total amount of PKR 120 million has also been set aside for environmental protection and conservation.
In addition, two bridges and flyovers will be built, starting in Faizabad and ending at N-5. The EIA Monitoring Director Ahsan Rafi Kiani said that two camp office locations are being considered, one near Pirwadhai and the other at 9th Avenue.
Read:
CDA-DWP permits construction, upgradation of 7th Avenue interchange, IJP Road
CDA authorities released further information regarding the IJP Road project. It was reported that four pedestrian bridges will be built on IJP Road, along with drains to help reduce water accumulation during the monsoon season.

title: Three mini dams of 400 KV capacity inaugurated in KP
full_text:
Battagram: Special Assistant to the Chief Minister on Power and Energy Taj Muhammad Khan Trand, in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), launched three mini-dams in the districts of Shamlai, Trangar, and Aien, news sources reported. Read:
KMC invites agencies to beautify 106 roads in Karachi
According to Karachi’s administrator, the KMC budget has allotted additional funds for the construction of initiatives that benefit the general population. KMC, UNDP ink agreement for development of Karachi

(IESCO)
has removed the ban on new power supply connections and has requested data from the Capital Development Authority (CDA) on acquired and unacquired land, news sources reported.

Islamabad Rent Restriction Amendment Bill 2020 approved to protect tenants, landlords’ rights
The order was issued by the CDA on June 22, which corresponds to the order issued by the National Assembly secretariat on May 24. Funds allocated for development schemes in Islamabad
According to available information, Islamabad has a total area of 51,000 acres, of which 31,000 acres are part of the Margalla Hills National Park. The remaining 20,000 acres are owned by people and have witnessed a mushrooming of illegal and unlawful housing societies in the recent past.

Master Plan 2050
at Summer Palace, Lahore Fort, the news advertisement reported.

LDA holds seminar seeking stakeholders’ views on land use rules draft

title: RDA plans Miyawaki forests in Rawalpindi to curb pollution
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) has decided to plant Miyawaki forests around the city to combat climate change and the city’s growing pollution problem, press sources reported. Previously a pilot project was conducted in Rialto Park to check increasing pollution.

Moreover, the chairman expressed his resolve to complete the plantation project on a priority basis.

Sindh launches urban forest project near Clifton Beach

forest of 6000 plants in Rialto Park, Murree road.

Bajwa shares updates on Balochistan road projects launched under CPEC

Fund, PKR 2 billion for the Balochistan Enterprise Development, and PKR 2 billion for Support Fund for Persons with Disabilities

Balochistan drafts law for land allotment in Gwadar Industrial Zone

title: CM orders increased work pace on KP Cities Improvement Project
full_text:
Peshawar: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Chief Minister (CM) Mahmood Khan has directed the authorities concerned to start acquiring land to mobilise KP Cities Improvement Project (KPCIP) without delay, reported news sources. He said this while chairing a high-level meeting which was attended by Minister for Local Government Akbar Ayub, and administrative secretaries of all the concerned departments.

KP govt seeks funds to upgrade urban infrastructure in five cities

PM inaugurates Jalozai Housing Scheme in Nowshera

title: LG minister seeks increase in Sindh’s forest cover
full_text:
Karachi: Sindh Local Government Minister for Forest Syed Nasir Hussain Shah on Monday issued directives to prioritise the urban forest programme, amenity plants, and the Bahman Biodiversity Park Larkana in countering the harmful implications of climate change in the country, according to news reports.

Timely completion of Gwadar East Bay Expressway, Indus Highway Sindh ordered

:
Govt approves two road connectivity projects in Sindh

title: Separate PSDP 2021-2022 on cards for Southern Punjab
full_text:
Lahore: The Punjab government has decided to roll out a separate Public Sector Development Program (PSDP) for Southern Punjab in the upcoming fiscal year 2021-22 (FY-22), news sources reported. It was also suggested to allocate PKR 28 billion for the South Punjab public sector program in the upcoming provincial budget.
Read:
PM Khan laid foundation of the South Punjab Secretariat, launch development programs
Moreover, the federal government will allocate an additional amount of PKR 17 billion for the road sector department in addition to the provincially allocated budget. Additionally, the federal government will allocate separate funds for the southern region of the province.
According to the sources in the
Punjab revenue
department, it is suggested to allocate PKR 440 million for the irrigation and clean water schemes separately. At the same time, the federal government will give PKR 150 million for the power sector development under PSDP to South Punjab.

CM Buzdar announces PKR 13.8bn uplift package for Layyah
Additionally, the Punjab revenue department has also decided to increase the annual traffic violation challan targets on the ring road for the upcoming year. title: LDA approves two new underpasses for Lahore
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) has approved two new underpass projects – to be developed at Samanabad Chowk and Akbar Chowk – in the next fiscal year 21-22 (FY21), news sources reported. The projects are envisioned to resolve the rising traffic-related problems in the provincial capital.
In addition, the LDA engineering department has begun a feasibility assessment for the project to redesign traffic plan in the said regions. Both projects have a proposed budget of PKR 2.4 billion.
Read:
Three flyovers in Lahore to be developed on urgent basis
As per the details shared, the proposed design of the Akbar Chowk underpass involves dual underpasses on both sides, as well as the remodelling of the Maulana Shaukat Ali Road to improve traffic flow and access to the Kareem Block market. The project will reduce traffic turbulence and over 240,000 commuters will be benefited. On the other hand, the initial idea of constructing a flyover at Samanabad was rejected due to the Orange Metro line, and an underpass project was approved instead.
Recently, LDA has also started working on three more mega road infrastructure projects in Lahore, to address increasing traffic problems.

‘Ravi City Project to Generate PKR 1,000 bn Economic Activity This Year’

EPA to hold public hearings on Ravi Riverfront, Naya Pakistan Apartments

full_text:
Lahore: The Chief Minister (CM) Punjab Sardar Usman Buzdar has announced a PKR 9 billion uplift package for Bhakkar District, news sources reported. The package included 106 projects, of which the chief minister has inaugurated and laid the foundation of 102 projects.

Narowal gets PKR 5.12 bn for upgradation of roads, drain infrastructure

CDA shares completion timelines for PWD Underpass, Korang Bridge

Blue Area

:
CDA opens bids for Park Enclave III’s development contract
Further, he said that four more parking facilities in the F-8 and F10 Blue area will be constructed. It was also reported that 10% of the area of the plaza will be commercially used for generating funds for construction costs.

title: Development work on 3 road projects underway in Lahore
full_text:
Lahore: The development work on three much-anticipated road infrastructure projects; Sheranwala Gate flyover, Ghulab Devi underpass (Ferozepur Road), and Shahkam Chowk flyover (Link Canal Road) has been launched, reported a news source on May 30.
Reportedly, Director General (DG) Lahore Development Authority (LDA) Ahmad Aziz Tarar visited the construction sites of these project, accompanied by the top brass of the LDA officers including the Chief Engineer LDA Abdul Razzaq Khan, and the concerned project directors.

LDA develops traffic-relief strategies
Mr Tarar directed the Chief Engineer to complete the construction work on time and instructed that no delay in the construction progress will be tolerated.

A network of roads spanning 10 kilometres will also be part of the flyover. The project includes the building of two bridges on the Ruhi Nullah as well as the dualisation of the Defence Road. This will help solve the longstanding traffic problem of the area.
Read:
Contract for Shahkam Chowk Flyover awarded to NLC

The 1-kilometre-long Sheranwala flyover is the longest in the city and is expected to cost PKR 4.9 billion; of which PKR 2 billion is reserved for 22 Kanal land acquisition, while the remaining will be spent on the civil works. The 400-meter elevation bearing flyover is expected to handle over 121,000 vehicles daily.
Gulab Devi Underpass
Similarly, PKR 2 billion Gulab Devi Hospital underpass will resolve traffic choking issues on one of the busiest roads of the city. The
project
consultancy services are expected to cost PKR 600 million while the civil works will cost around PKR 1.4 billion. The director during his visit instructed the project director to ensure safety arrangements and traffic diversion plans.

title: ECNEC approves Sukkur-Hyderabad Motorway, other projects
full_text:
Islamabad: The Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) on Wednesday gave nod to 10 development projects worth PKR 361.5 billion including 306 km Hyderabad-Sukkur Motorway (M6), according to news sources.
While presiding over the ECNEC meeting through video link, Finance Minister Shaukat Tarin permitted the construction of the Hyderabad-Sukkur (M6) motorway. The six-lane fenced motorway project is to be executed on a Build, Operate and Transfer (BOT) basis. The estimated cost of an M-6 motorway is PKR 191.471 billion.
This project will be included in the coming federal budget and its expected completion is 30 months. Previously, the Public-Private Partnership Authority (PPPA) board proposed a 39% share or PKR 76 billion government funding. However, the public-private share has been increased to 50% respectively.
Read:
ECNEC approves major uplift projects
The PPPA directors have agreed to allocate PKR 92 billion from the budget and toll charges for constructing Hyderabad-Sukkur Motorway (M6) to make it attractive for private investors.
In addition to the M6 motorway project, ECNEC also approved the construction of the Hoshab-Awaran-Khuzdar section of the M-8 project- 168 Km section 2- Awaran Naal at the cost of PKR 32.245 billion. The National Highway Authority (NHA) will build bridges, retaining walls, toe walls, box culverts, and shoulders. The project is expected to be complete in a period of 42 months.
Moreover, ECNEC approved the dualization of the Mardan-Swabi road with PKR 13.024 billion that is expected to be completed by 2023.
For the rehabilitation of the southern, central, and eastern regions of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa PKR 28.156 billion has been approved. The restoration of the existing 274 Km highway network was also permitted and is anticipated to be completed by 2023.
Additionally, the
National Highway Authority
(NHA), the Economic Affairs Division, and Finance Division were asked to collaborate to establish a framework to raise funds for the repair and maintenance of National Highways and Motorways (NH&M).
Aside from this, the meeting approved the Gomal Zam Multipurpose project worth PKR 25.928 billion. The project will be situated on the Gomal river, South Waziristan. It will irrigate 191,139 acres of farmland and will generate 17.4MW electricity. The project falls under the authority of the Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA).
ECNEC agreed to a PKR 16.4 billion, 30MW hydropower project at Ghowari on the bank of river Shayok in Ghanche district of Gilgit Baltistan. Additionally, a 20MW hydropower plant was also approved in the Hazel district of Gilgit at the cost of PKR 12.922 billion.
Read:
Sukkur-Hyderabad Motorway (M6)’s development to start after ECNEC’s approval
In the meeting, approval was also given for the Rainee canal project that will cost PKR 20.534 billion. It will fall under the authority of WAPDA and will help in irrigating 412,400 acres in Kashmore, Ghotki, Sukkur, and Khairpur districts.

title: Survey of Margalla Road begins; development work up next
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) and Frontier Works Organisation (FWO) have jointly initiated survey of Margalla Road before formally starting construction work to widen and complete the road project, a news source reported.
The survey is expected to complete within 10 days, followed by the commencement of construction work by FWO. The joint survey is part of the project without which work can not begin, said the CDA engineer department.
Read
:
Sector I-15 uplift work reviewed by CDA

title: Inauguration of IT Park held in Islamabad

title: Secretary LG&CD Punjab approves formulation of master plan for 119 cities
full_text:
Lahore: Local Government and Community Development (LG&CD) Secretary Noorul-Amin Mengal approved the formulation of the
master plan
of 119 cities in Punjab, according to news sources. The said project is estimated to cost PKR 367 million and will be completed in two years.

Punjab approves uplift package for Gujrat

title: LDA develops traffic-relief strategies

LDA launches online appointment system

title: ‘Ravi City Project to Generate PKR 1,000 bn Economic Activity This Year’

Land notified for Ravi Riverfront Urban Development Project

title: Shahkam Flyover construction to start after Eid, alternate traffic plan formed
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) recently announced its decision to initiate the construction of the Shahkam Flyover after the upcoming Eid-ul-Fitr holidays, according to a news story published on May 4.
In this regard, the LDA has requested the traffic police to temporarily shut down the Canal Bank Road. Reportedly, the traffic police have already approved the LDA’s request to shut down the road facility for seven months.
Read:
Shahkam Chowk Flyover update: 3D Model unveiled; prequalification process initiated
In order to facilitate traffic during the construction period, an alternate traffic plan has already been finalised. As per the details available, three alternate routes have been finalised to facilitate commuters of Mohlanwal Road, Defence Road and Canal Bank Road.

In addition, the road linking Mohlanwal Road with Canal Bank Road will remain temporarily shut. Commuters heading from Bahria Town to Canal Band Road will also be required to use an alternate route.
Read:
Tender awarded for Gulab Devi underpass construction in Lahore
As per the plan, vehicles heading from Raiwind Road via Defence Road will have to use the two overhead bridges in Jaliana, while Multan Road will act as an alternate route for Mohlanwal Road.

title: Address issues hampering Ravi City’s development: PM
developer: Ravi City project is being handled by Ravi Urban Development
full_text:
Lahore: Prime Minister Imran has directed the authorities concerned to take notice of the issues hampering the establishment of Ravi City and Central Business District in Lahore, a news source reported on April 29.
The premier issued the said directives while taking a briefing in Islamabad on the developments carried out for the two projects. Ravi City project is being handled by Ravi Urban Development Authority, which was made its executing authority in September last year.
Read:
Punjab invites proposals for fair compensation to Ravi Urban Development affectees
Commenting on the venture’s importance, the PM said that Ravi City is a flagship project and its development will go a long way in creating economic prosperity in the country.
Talking about protection of green areas falling in and around the land marked for the project, PM Khan said that all such areas will be protected at all costs. He further mentioned that the steps taken by the incumbent government for the environment protection and making Pakistan clean and green, are unprecedented.

title: PM takes notice of changes made in RRR’s original route
developer: Spurred to action, the Rawalpindi Development
full_text:
Islamabad: Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan on Friday took notice of alleged changes made to the alignment of the Rawalpindi Ring Road (RRR) which has increased the project cost by PKR 25 billion and gave undue advantage to some private housing schemes, according to news sources.
Read:
740-acres of land acquired for transport hubs along Ring Road
Reportedly, PM Khan has instructed Punjab Chief Minister (CM) Sardar Usman Buzdar to investigate the matter. Spurred to action, the Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) has sealed the RRR land acquisition record and suspended the land acquisition collector till the inquiry is complete.
RDA Director General (retired) Captain Abdul Sattar Issani revealed the RRR project is being launched under the supervision of the Lahore Ring Road Authority and the Project Management Unit (PMU) was working under the divisional commissioner’s control. However, he also said that RDA had the land acquisition record and was responsible for establishment of economic zones along the Ring Road, the land records of which have now been sealed.
Reportedly, the issue was discovered when a plan was made to link the road from Rawat to the motorway and from then on to Sangjani on G T Road. An RDA official stated that after this development the project is likely to be delayed till the next year.
Read:
‘Value of land in Rawalpindi Ring Road’s economic zones inching up’
The official also revealed that nine interchanges had been planned on the road and 500 kanals have been acquired by nine housing projects for free. Moreover, five interchanges worth PKR 7 billion are to be sponsored by housing projects located near the road – which saves government funds and created a win-win situation.
Previously, the Punjab government had issued a land acquisition award for the ring road phase-I and released PKR 6.4 billion for it.  The last date for tender submission for the mega road project was April 12, which was extended by the divisional administration after the transfer of the city commissioner.

title: KMC, UNDP ink agreement for development of Karachi
full_text:
Karachi: The Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) for the infrastructural development of Karachi and overall betterment of the city. The MoU was signed by the Karachi administrator, Laeeq Ahmed and UNDP Pakistan Resident Representative Knut Ostby.
With this agreement, Karachi has become the second municipality after Istanbul to enter such an agreement with UNDP.
Read:
City Council demands urgent release of Karachi Package funds
As per the details, UNDP will work with KMC’s various departments such as Parks and Horticulture Department, for achieving targets outlined under Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth, SDG 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities, and SDG 15: Life on Land.
While development will primarily focus economic growth, urban development, environmental improvement, infrastructure development, solid waste management, health and education. Special focus is being given to addressing environmental pollution and tree plantation will be given its due importance in the city. Moreover, KMC and UNDP will cooperate for for skills development, increasing employment opportunities, and addressing the issue of urban-rural migration.
Read:
Govt to launch exclusive projects for industrial zones under Karachi package: President Alvi
Knut Osby said that the UNDP will be working in close partnership with private entities to realize the agency’s goals.

title: PM directs timely execution of Gujranwala uplift plan
full_text:
Islamabad: Prime Minister Imran Khan directed the relevant authorities to set up a timeline in regards to the Gujranwala Development Plan and deliver the execution of the project accordingly, as reported by news source published on 7
th
April.
Read:
Buzdar announces uplift projects for Gujranwala, other districts
The premier recently chaired a meeting to discuss various development projects, namely Gujranwala Development Plan, Rawalpindi Urban Regeneration and Nullah Leh Expressway, all under the umbrella of Punjab government’s Regional Development Strategy. He stressed the need for constant monitoring in the aforementioned projects and stated that the federal government would extend every bit of support to implement the strategy. Punjab Chief Minister Usman Buzdar, CM’s Advisor Salman Shah, chief secretary and other senior officers also took part in the meeting through a video link.
Read:
MoUs signed for construction of smart villas, grid station in DHA Gujranwala
The premier noted the massive potential in Gujranwala and further elaborated that the city contributed up to 13 percent in GDP, 20 percent in exports and 40 percent in remittances. Therefore, the aim is to uplift various sectors, namely knowledge and economy transfer, specialized value chain infrastructure, manual labor development, cluster support scheme, low-cost energy, communications, urban management, rural-urban market connectivity, rural development and management, and environment.
The Prime Minister was appreciative of the overall strategy and also was firm about the promotion of Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) which would contribute to the national development.

title: PTEGP invites bids for Solar Power Energy Systems
full_text:
Lahore: The International Development Association (World Bank Group) recently issued a credit to the Punjab government, according to an advert. The purpose is for the execution of The Punjab Tourism for Economic Growth Project (PTEGP) and to that effect, PTEGP is inviting sealed bids from eligible bidders to install “Solar Power Energy System” at different monument and heritage sites in Punjab, namely:
Jahangir’s Tomb, Lahore
Noor Jahan’s Tomb, Lahore
Hiran Minar, Sheikhupura
Rohtas Fort, Jhelum

Harappa Museum, Harappa

Punjab to develop 30 sites under ‘Tourism for Economic Growth’ initiative

Prospective bidders may bid for one or more lots and the evaluation of bids and award of contract will be done on a lot basis. Relevant documents can be downloaded from

. Alternatively, printed documents can be obtained directly from the office or can be couriered on request, subject to a cost of PKR 3,000.
Bids are to be delivered to the office of PMU Punjab Tourism for Economic Growth Project, 175-A, Upper Mall Scheme, between 9:00AM to 4:00PM. Each bid must be accompanied by a security of @2% of bid value for each lot issued by a scheduled bank.

Pre-bidding meeting of RRR to be held on April 5

title: Green Line BRT to be in operation by August: Asad Umar
developer: Karachi, Mr Umar asked the Sindh Infrastructure Development
full_text:
Islamabad
: Planning Minister Asad Umar on Monday directed the concerned authorities to finalize and get the much-awaited Green Line Bus Rapid Transit System (BRT) up and running by August of this year, according to a news source.
Read:
French govt to provide soft loan of PKR 12.3bn for Karachi Red Line BRT
During a recent meeting which was held in order to discuss the ongoing projects in Karachi, Mr Umar asked the Sindh Infrastructure Development Company Limited (SIDCL) to assess all the relevant activities in order to achieve the set timelines on the projects, especially with regards to the implementation of the Integrated Intelligent Transport System (IITS).
Furthermore, the minister assured that the federal government was taking every step to accelerate the BRT project in order to aid the people in terms of public transport. He also expressed that the executive was working beyond its responsibility to aid them in the transportation woes.
Read:
Turkey to fund urban transport, waste management ventures in Sindh
As per the news source, prototype buses would be ready for trial runs and commissioning by April 25. The IITS contract Package-A would be signed on March 26, Package-B on April 2 and the award of Operation and Maintenance (O&M) would be announced by May of this year.

title: French govt to provide soft loan of PKR 12.3bn for Karachi Red Line BRT
full_text:
Islamabad: The French government has announced its decision to provide a soft loan of PKR 12.3 billion for the development of the Red Line bus rapid transit (BRT) project in Karachi, a news source reported on March 18.
Read
:
Karachi Breeze Red Line buses to be powered by biogas
To this effect, French Ambassador Marc Barety and the country director of the French Agency for Development (AFD) came to terms with Economic Affairs Division Secretary Noor Ahmed for a credit finance agreement to co-finance the project, alongside the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB), Asian Development Bank (ABD) and the Green Climate Fund (GCF).
The said project, situated at the Numaish station, will connect to the Green Line and will further include the construction of a 26.6km BRT corridor in Karachi, including both the Red Line corridor and the common corridor. The Red Line services will continue on through the shared common corridor from the station till the Merewether Tower.
The soft loan demonstrates the effort made by the development agencies in order to better the livelihoods and the standard of living. The aforementioned project will be one of the very first joint ventures between AIIB and GCF on urban development, as reported by a French Embassy press release. Besides the infrastructure and construction, the project is said to be much more friendly in relation to the environment, as the bio-methane hybrid bus technology will greatly reduce CO2 emissions.
Read
:
Turkey to fund urban transport, waste management ventures in Sindh
Other salient features of the ambitious project include a better integration system for the pre-existing bus section into the new system for a seamless transition. In addition, the infrastructure will include mixed traffic lanes, bicycle lanes, proper parking, sidewalks, and a proper draining system to facilitate the climate-proofing of the infrastructure as well as the new corridor.

title: RDA to develop economic zones in all Rawalpindi tehsils
full_text:
Rawalpindi: Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) Chairman Tariq Mehmood Murtaza on Saturday announced that the authority will develop special economic zones in all tehsils of Rawalpindi district, according to news sources.
He expressed his views on the matter during a workshop organized at the authority for officers of several departments, community members and other stakeholders of twin cities. He said that the authority is making efforts to ease the congestion of Rawalpindi city by working on a mega Rawalpindi Development Plan.
Read:
‘PM Khan to perform Rawalpindi Ring Road’s groundbreaking on August 14’
Murtaza said that the creation of these economic zones is part of that mega
Rawalpindi Development Plan
, under which development work will be executed in all tehsils as per the modern urban planning strategy. He also said that the regional plan will also help control the unplanned city expansion and unnecessary urbanization.

title: CDA, RDA to sign MoU on sharing landfill site
full_text:
Islamabad:
The City Managers of Islamabad and Rawalpindi recently agreed to jointly use a new landfill site to dispose solid waste. The Capital Development Authority (CDA) and the Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) are set to sign a memorandum of understanding (MOU) in this regard, according to a statement issued by the Ministry of Planning.
The decision was taken during a meeting that took place in the presence of Minister of Planning Asad Umar. According to a news report shared in a national daily, the twin cities will now be able to mutually use a landfill site that will be developed near Chakwal.
Read:
CDA installs pickets to protect state land from encroachers
Special Assistant to Prime Minister on CDA Affairs Ali Nawaz Awan stated that “The landfill site is a chronic issue of Islamabad and today the meeting decided that both RDA and CDA will use the new landfill site to be set up in Mandra.” The land fill site will be built by the RDA and as per the MoU, both the CDA and RDA will be able to use it for proper waste disposal.
On an average, the capital city produces around 600 tons of garbage every day. Prior to this, the site that CDA planned to use was shut down due to its hazardous impact on the adjoining areas.
Read:
CDA taking steps to improve Islamabad’s water supply
The aforementioned meeting was also attended by Chief Commissioner Islamabad and CDA Chairman Amer Ali Ahmed, Commissioner Rawalpindi Mohammad Mehmood, Special Assistant to Prime Minister on CDA Affairs Ali Nawaz Awan, MNA Raja Khurram Nawaz and others.

title: Punjab govt shares details on final alignment of Rawalpindi Ring Road
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Punjab government has shared the final alignment of the Rawalpindi Ring Road (RRR) project’s 65-kilometre route — with the venture being developed under a public-private partnership model, according to a proposal shared by the Planning and Development Board’s Public-Private Partnership Cell.
Read:
Deadline for submitting RRR bidding proposals announced
The project is being developed with a central median and shoulders in three segments:
The first segment will start from N-5 to the DI Hakla six-lane dual carriageway with 3+3 lanes on both sides
The second segment will start from DI Hakla to the M-1 two plus two (2+2) rigid pavements parallel to the already existing motorway
The third segment starts from M-1 to the Sangjani six-lane dual carriageway with 3+3 lanes on both sides.
Moreover, preliminary design and technical studies have already been carried out for the segment-wise development of the RRR project, which shall be shared with the prospective bidders soon.
Read:
Commissioner reveals details on when will tenders for RRR be floated
Reportedly, the government is seeking to reduce the travel time from Radio Pakistan to Sangjani through the GT Road with the construction of the
RRR
. The project is also expected to allow long-distance travellers to skip the urban area of the city and reduce vehicle operating costs.

title: District administration imposes Section 4 for Balakot Hydropower project land acquisition
full_text:
Mansehra: The district administration has imposed Section 4 to acquire land for the
Balakot
Hydropower Project, a news source reported on March 3. The initiative will generate 300 megawatts of electricity and will cost PKR 85 billion.
Read:
KP approves funds for bridges, natural gas in Balakot, Mansehra
The Balakot Hydropower project is being executed by the Pakhtunkhwa Energy Development Organization. Deputy Commissioner Dr Qasim Ali Khan on Tuesday revealed that the administration has already fulfilled the legal formalities to acquire over 1,700 kanals of land for the project and the remaining process will be completed shortly.
Read:
KP releases funds for provision of potable water to Balakot residents
Moreover, Khan said that the project will be developed downstream of the 860-megawatt Suki Kinari Hydropower project, which is being executed under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) initiative at Kunhar River in Kaghan valley.
The delegation of the Pakhtunkhwa Energy Development Organization also visited the project site in Kaghan.

title: KP govt releases PKR 240mn for uplift schemes in Oghi tehsil
developer: Fareed, who also heads the District Development
full_text:
Mansehra: MPA Nawabzada Fareed recently stated that the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) government had disbursed PKR 240 million for two infrastructure development schemes in Oghi tehsil of Mansehra district, a news source reported on February 14.
Read
:
KP to develop 10 new tourist spots in Hazara, Malakand divisions
Fareed, who also heads the District Development Advisory Committee, stated that the provincial executive had pledged a total of PKR 440 million for the ongoing development work in the said tehsil, adding that the remaining PKR 200 million would be issued by June.

Land acquisition begins for construction of Oghi-Battal Road, Mansehra
The MPA said that the Oghi-Battal Road following its completion would generate economic and employment opportunities for the local population, which would ultimately contribute to the development of the region.

title: Funds disbursement process begins to acquire land for Rawalpindi Ring Road
developer: Mehmood said that the Rawalpindi Development
full_text:
Rawalpindi: Rawalpindi Commissioner Captain (Retd) Muhammad Mehmood has revealed that the process of disbursement of funds for Rawalpindi Ring Road (RRR) project’s land acquisition has begun, according to a news published in national dailies on February 8.

Read:
Counter established to make payments to RRR landowners
Leh Expressway is being developed under public-private partnership and once the RDA Governing Body grants an approval, it will be sent to the Public-Private Partnership Authority for review. Reportedly, Leh Express project is aimed at boosting commercial activities in the surrounding areas and significantly reduce traffic congestion in the city as this will be a signal-free zone.
Read:
Properties falling within Leh Expressway’s ROW marked; BUP acquisition cost estimates shared
During the meeting, plans for Kachehri Chowk and Defense Chowk remodelling were also reviewed. title: CDA to award contract for Margalla Road development work
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has announced its decision to resume the construction of a road link between Grand Trunk (GT) Road and Sector D, according to a news report published on January 27.

Read:
CDA shares details on bids received for roads improvement project in Sector I-14
According to reports, the authority is now finalising a new estimate and hopes to award the contract during the next month. It was also revealed that the development of the four sectors C-13, C-14, C-15 and C-16 depends on this project.
The PKR 588 million project, which includes the construction of an 8.5-kilometre-long strip for Margalla Road, was launched in 2012.

title: Funds approved for road to connect Kalam and Kumrat valleys

Zameen.com get Kalam’s Cedar Valley on board for exclusive sales & marketing services

title: LDA VC issues instructions to launch development work in housing schemes
full_text:
Lahore: Lahore Development Authority (LDA) Vice Chairman S M Imran recently issued instructions to launch development projects in three of LDA’s housing schemes: Mohlanwal Scheme, Jubilee Town and LDA Avenue-1, a news source reported.

Planning underway to construct 150,000 NPHP homes in Lahore: LDA VC
According to details, Imran had received complaints through the Citizen Portal where the allottees concerned had submitted a variety of complaints about these three housing schemes. As a result, the LDA official recently visited all three project sites.

title: CDA to set up parking plazas in capital city markets

:
Beautification of Islamabad: CDA to carpet all roads

title: PM’s aide performs Bhara Kahu Bridge groundbreaking

Islamabad: Special Assistant to the Prime Minister (SAPM) on Capital Development Authority (CDA) Affairs Ali Nawaz Awan on Friday (January 8) performed the groundbreaking for the Bhara Kahu Kayani Bridge crossing, a news source reported.

Contract awarded for design, alignment of Rawat-Bhara Kahu Bypass, Islamabad

Construction of Bhara Kahu Flyover to begin soon: SAPM CDA

title: Commissioner shares time frame for shifting bus stands to RRR

Rawalpindi: Commissioner Captain (retired) Mohammad Mehmood on Wednesday asked truck and bus stand owners to relocate their operations to the Rawalpindi Ring Road (RRR) project site; further stating that land designated for heavy duty vehicles terminals was available at cheaper rates at the RRR project site, a news source reported.

Land identificati

n for 40km of RRR’s total route complete

title: Lahore Bridge near Arfa Karim Technology Tower to be expanded

LDA to convert Qainchi Flyover, Walton Road into signal-free corridor

Three flyovers in Lahore to be developed on urgent basis

title: PDA to develop Hayatabad’s road infrastructure

LDA to convert Qainchi Flyover, Walton Road into signal-free corridor

Existing industries, settlements not to be included in Ravi Riverfront Urban project

Cost estimates for Ravi Riverfront Urban Development Project prepared

title: LDA to convert Qainchi Flyover, Walton Road into signal-free corridor

title: Existing industries, settlements not to be included in Ravi Riverfront Urban project
full_text:
Lahore: The Punjab government has decided against the proposed inclusion of existing industries and residential settlements within the land acquisition plan for the Ravi Riverfront Urban Development Project, a news source reported on December 27. However, the settlements located within the riverbed will be acquired.
Read:

Ravi Urban Development Authority (RUDA) spokesman SM Imran was speaking to the media after a meeting held with local industrialists at Mehmood Booti near the Ring Road on Saturday. The RUDA official organised the meeting on the directives of Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan who had ordered the authorities concerned to allay all concerns of the industrialists.
The industrialists were briefed about the project. According to the details revealed, PM Khan had ordered relocation for a limited number of settlements. To this effect, the RUDA spokesman stated that settlements in flood-prone areas will be acquired as they faced grave danger from river waters which continued to be released by India without warning.
The project will be a complete city spread over 120,000 acres and will be developed in three phases over 30 years. The first phase will also involve the development of a 46-kilometer-long lake by erecting 28-foot-high walls on both sides of the river besides constructing barrages at three places.
Read:
Cabinet approves PKR 5bn loan for Ravi City project land acquisition
The authorities will also establish seven water treatments in the area to treat a total of 836 cusecs of water daily which will be supplied to the lake. The lake will also serve as a reservoir and save water from being wasted. The water will then be used for irrigation. It is also expected to help improve ground water levels in Lahore.
Six million saplings will be planted within the project to make it environment friendly, while 10,000 acres of land will be dedicated for development of a forest and orchards.

title: 90% development work complete in New Malir Housing Scheme-Karachi
full_text:
Karachi: Malir Development Authority (MDA) Additional Director General (ADG) Abdul Nasir has revealed that infrastructure development in New Malir Housing Scheme has been completed by 90%, according to a news story published in national dailies on December 24.
Nasir shared this information during a media brief held in his office on Wednesday (December 23). He further revealed that the authority has also retrieved 1,200 acres of land from the land mafia during the last two months. The order in this regard came directly from Sindh Information and Local Government Minister Syed Nasir Hussain Shah.
Read:
MDA Karachi retrieves state land in Taiser Town Scheme 45

In order to retrieve the remaining land, a mega operation is underway in collaboration with law enforcement agencies. He reiterated that the operation will continue till the entire land is vacated.
Speaking about the much-anticipated launch of a new (and perhaps an affordable) housing scheme, he said that people will hear a good news soon. This news could very well be about the MDA’s much popular project Taiser Town, but the ADG didn’t give any hints on what’s coming next.

title: WB sanctions USD 300mn for disaster management, solid waste projects in Sindh
developer: To this effect, the International Development
full_text:
Islamabad: The World Bank’s Board of Executive Directors has sanctioned USD 300 million for the Sindh Resilience Project (SRP) and the Solid Waste Emergency and Efficiency Project (SWEEP), a news source reported on December 9.
Read
