China provides PKR 25mn for Karachi’s urban flooding relief measures
According to the details revealed, the funding is aimed at facilitating the Sindh government’s efforts to protect the province against natural calamities such as floods and droughts in addition to strengthening solid waste management in the provincial capital of Karachi.
To this effect, the International Development Association (IDA) has pledged USD 200 million for the Sindh Resilience Project, while the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development has expressed its intent to provide USD 100 million for the Solid Waste Emergency and Efficiency Project (SWEEP).
World Bank Country Director for Pakistan Najy Benhassine stated that protection against natural disasters and health issues was a priority for the country; adding that the disastrous impact of floods, droughts and rainfall in Sindh, as well as the huge casualty toll due to the coronavirus pandemic, required urgent investments to facilitate dialogue and coordination at both the provincial and national levels.
Read
:
WB urged to help establish two solar parks in Sindh
The Sindh Resilience Project will assist the provincial executive in tackling floods, droughts, and public health emergencies in addition to introducing improvements to disaster risk management and the province’s health sector. title: Ravi Riverfront Urban Development Project: Survey of over 15,000 acres of land completed
full_text:
Lahore: The district administration has completed the survey of over 15,000 acres of land for Ravi Riverfront Urban Development Project (RRUDP) in addition to compiling a report to this effect, a news source reported on December 8.

title: Govt approves Gwadar Smart City Master Plan
developer: Ministry of Planning and the Gwadar Development
full_text:
Islamabad: Maritime Affairs Secretary Rizwan Ahmed recently stated that the federal government had provided its approval to a draft of the Gwadar Smart City Master Plan, a news source reported on December 4.
Read:
Rapid development work underway in Gwadar Port City: Balochistan CM
He was briefing a subcommittee of the Public Accounts Committee (PAC). The session was held under the chairpersonship of Munazza Hassan to discuss and review audit observations regarding Maritimes Division.
The secretary stated that the Gwadar Port City would emerge as the new business hub for Pakistan, China and Central Asian countries including Afghanistan within the next three to four years; adding that the Gwadar Port was conducting most of the transit trade activity for Afghanistan.
He further stated that the federal government was in contact with Uzbek authorities to set up a dry port in Gwadar in a bid to facilitate all Central Asian Republics (CARs) in their trade-related endeavors. He said that Uzbekistan had expressed its intent to relocate their exports and imports to
Gwadar
as it was the nearest port city for them.
With regard to the Gwadar Smart City Master Plan, the official said that Gwadar’s population was expected to exceed the two million mark; further stating that high paid expatriate professionals would comprise 80 percent of the total population.
Ahmed said that the provision of a tax-free environment would attract investors, thereby creating employment opportunities. Additional facilities, he stated, will include high-tech industries, mega shopping malls, luxury resorts, and manmade islands.
Read:
MNA inaugurates gas supply project in Gwadar
The 75-page master plan draft has been prepared by the China Communications Construction Company in collaboration with the Ministry of Planning and the Gwadar Development Authority (GDA). The plan envisages the economic development of Gwadar with a projected GDP per capita of USD 15,000.
Moreover, it details major city developments such as international exhibition centres, multiple theme parks, luxury resorts, botanical gardens, museums. Other mega projects include 15 new power plants (to be developed at a cost of approximately USD 5 billion), desalination plants (expected to provide 700,000 m3 of fresh water on a daily basis), and a central business district.
The government anticipates Gwadar’s annual economic output to exceed the USD 30 billion mark and hopes to create 1.2 million jobs for both skilled and semi-skilled workers. Further, the city is likely to require 15,800 new homes by 2025, 47,600 by 2030, and 254,500 by 2050.

title: Punjab CM approves two more underpasses, flyover for Lahore

Authorities asked to expedite work on Gwadar road, railway network project
GDA Director General Shahzeb Khan Kakar also addressed the meeting and briefed the attendees on the implementation status of the port city’s master plan and supply of clean drinking water to the area. He informed that PKR 1 billion had been allocated for the restoration of the old Gwadar city – under the Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP) 2019-20.
He also mentioned that with these funds, the development work was underway in the region and briefed the meeting on construction of ICT Centre, Water Treatment Plant and aforementioned water supply and distribution projects.

title: Four international consortiums submit bids for Islamabad’s master plan revision
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has notified its receipt of bids from four consortiums comprising of international town planning firms for the revision of Islamabad’s master plan, according to a news report published on November 23.
Read:
CDA to spend PKR 2.7bn on rehabilitation of abandoned sewage treatment plant
As per the CDA officials, the contract for the revision of Islamabad’s
master plan
will be awarded to the lowest bidding firm following the completion of financial evaluations by the civic agency. It was also revealed that the four consortiums consisted of representatives from 11 companies. The PC-I of the project was estimated to cost PKR 600 million and will be awarded to a qualified firm with the lowest biding.
Read:
CDA directed to restore capital’s parks
The original master plan of the capital city was prepared in 1960 and was supposed to be upgraded every 20 years. To date, successive governments have introduced as many as 40 selective changes to that master plan, but without proper consultations from the town planning agencies concerned.

title: LDA to prepare proposal for Mall Road tunnel
full_text:
Lahore: Lahore Development Authority (LDA) has begun the preparation of a proposal to construct a tunnel on Mall Road in order to boost traffic flow on it – a news source reported on November 18.
Read:
Work on beautification of Mall Road begins
Mall Road is one of the busiest roads of Lahore and a number of city’s major markets including Hall Road market, Neela Gumbad bicycle market, Anarkali bazaar, Baden Road market as well as various government offices and courts are located on it. These attract a large amount of traffic particularly on weekdays.
Read:
LDA permits 400 ft building construction on Mall Road
LDA had previously been instructed by Punjab Chief Minister Sardar Usman Buzdar to work on a proposal to improve the traffic flow on Mall Road. For this purpose, LDA is now working on two ideas, one of which is the construction of the tunnel that will run from Mian Mir Bridge to Neela Gumbad Chowk and will have exit points on a number of Chowks on the road. The tunnel will go down to the depth of 40-50 feet.
The other idea involves two-way underpass at all intersections on the road.

title: Chinese envoy, Asad Umar reiterate pledge to expedite CPEC’s second phase
developer: Nong Rong, on Thursday met Minister for Planning Development
full_text:
Islamabad: The newly-appointed Chinese Ambassador to Pakistan, Nong Rong, on Thursday met Minister for Planning Development and Special Initiatives Asad Umar and the two officials vowed to expedite the work on the second phase of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), according to news sources.
Read:
CPEC Industrial Cooperation B2B Investment Conference to be held this month
The two state officials expressed a marked interest in the matters related to industrial cooperation. Other issues that were discussed involved bilateral relations and various projects being developed under the CPEC. They reiterated their resolve to work together to make the second phase of CPEC, a success.
Read:
New law to be introduced to accelerate work at CPEC projects
Moreover, the state officials expressed satisfaction on the Joint Working Groups (
JWGs
) meetings that were conducted in the recent few weeks, related to several sectors. Minister Asad Umar extended his welcome to the ambassador on his new assignments and wished him best endeavours. He iterated that the China-Pakistan relationship goes deeper than the government level cooperation as the people of two countries also share a strong sense of brotherhood.

title: Commissioner orders survey of land for Leh Expressway project
full_text:
Rawalpindi: Commissioner Rawalpindi Division Captain (retired) Muhammad Mahmood on Wednesday issued directions for the officials concerned of the Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) to survey the land required for the Leh Expressway project, according to news sources.
Read:
Foundation stone laid for bridge on Lehtrar Road
Moreover, the officials concerned tasked with devising separate estimates for the government land to be used for the project. He issued these directions while presiding over a meeting at the Commissioner Office.
Read:
Committee formed to finalise proposals for Leh Expressway project
It was highlighted that the project  will ease traffic congestion in the city, minimise environmental pollution and prevent urban flooding. The commissioner stated that the
Leh Expressway
project would include service roads and a flood protection channel. He further said that the project will support the economy as new business opportunity would be created in line with all requirements of urban life.

title: PKR 1.25 billion allocated for Bahawalpur Industrial Estate
full_text:
Lahore: Punjab Industrial Estate Development and Management Company (PIEDMC) in the latest meeting of its board of governors approved allocation of PKR 1.25 billion for Bahawalpur Industrial Estate – a news source reported on November 19. The meeting was chaired by PIEDMC Chairman Syed Nabeel Hashmi.
Read:
Five industrial estates receive SEZ status
According to details, the meeting of Board of Governors also approved a number of other major decisions for PIEDMC. These included the initiative to grant possession in the three economic zones under the management of PIEDMC so that industrial units could be established there.
Read:
Punjab to have more industrial zones
The meeting also approved special discount package for establishment of industrial units with area greater than 25 acres in Quaid-e-Azam Business Park. Moreover, the board of governors gave the greenlight to establishment of an advisory board for Quaid-e-Azam Business Park and Rahim Yar Khan Industrial Estate.

title: Design, feasibility study finalised for making Defence Chowk signal free
full_text:
Rawalpindi: In order to reduce the pressure of traffic on entrance and exit from Rawalpindi to the Grand Trunk Road (GT Road), the design and feasibility study for making Defence Chowk signal-free have been finalised – a news source reported on November 16.
Read:
Remodelling of Rawalpindi Defence Chowk approved to facilitate traffic flow
The project worth PKR 2 billion with dual lanes and underpass will allow the traffic to proceed smoothly onto the roads leading from Defence Chowk. The feasibility study was prepared by NESPAK which notes that approximately 138,414 vehicles pass from Defence Chowk each day. The intersection leads to Fauji Foundation Hospital, Al-Shafa Eye Trust, High Court and a number of housing societies due to which it is often jam packed with long lines of traffic.
Read:
RDA to prepare feasibility report on Kachehri Chowk, Defence Chowk signal-free projects
It is yet to be decided whether the project will be completed under Punjab government’s Annual Development Programme or Public Sector Development Programme. The project is also yet to be approved by Planning & Development Board. Rawalpindi Development Authority which is going to be the executing agency of the project has, however, initiated the initial work on the project.

title: DG LDA gives deadline for Abdul Sattar Edhi Underpass completion
full_text:
Lahore: Lahore Development Authority (LDA) Director General (DG) Ahmed Aziz Tarar has issued instructions for labourers working on the Abdul Sattar Edhi Underpass (also known as the Firdous Market Underpass) to complete the construction work on the project by November 19, according to the authority’s official Facebook page.
Read:
Firdous Market Underpass renamed as tribute to respected philanthropist
According to the details revealed, all members of the civic agency’s engineering staff (including the LDA chief engineer) have been instructed to remain present at the site till the project’s completion.
LDA DG Ahmed Aziz Tarar issued these orders during a visit to the
Firdous Market Underpass construction
site. He reiterated that this flagship initiative of the incumbent government would facilitate the commuters. He said that there was no justification for further delay in Abdul Sattar Edhi Underpass’s completion. He insisted on project completion at the given timeline and without compromising on the quality of construction.
Read:
LDA to prepare feasibility report on construction of overhead bridge, Circular Road underpass
Moreover, the DG LDA allowed the authority to deploy additional labour force to ensure timely completion of the project. He also stated that the horticulture work of the project should be expedited, in addition to completing asphalt laying and drain construction.

title: CDA to rehabilitate industrial sectors I-10, I-11
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has launched development work in the industrial areas of the city, according to a news source published on November 13. To this effect, the roads and other civic infrastructure of the stalled I-10 and I-11 sectors are being rehabilitated.
Read:
CDA directed to restore capital’s parks
In addition to these measures, the development authority recently also invited
technical bids
aimed at transforming the northern road located in these sectors into dual carriageways. Reportedly, the lowest bid has been identified — with the 7,200 ft long and 24 ft wide road expected to be constructed within  a pre-set timeline of six months.
Read:
CDA-DWP permits construction, upgradation of 7th Avenue interchange, IJP Road
Meanwhile, the CDA has decided to procure new machinery to expand its secondary waste collection services in the densely populated areas of Islamabad. The said decision was taken in the latest CDA board meeting that was chaired by the authority’s Chairman Amer Ali Ahmed. According to the information available, the authority will be hiring personnel to provide a clean and green environment to the city’s residents.

title: PDWP approves four uplift schemes worth PKR 4.5bn
full_text:
Lahore: The Provincial Development Working Party (PDWP) on Tuesday provided its approval to the construction of several roads and bridges at an estimated cost of PKR 4.5 billion, a news source reported on October 11.
The PDWP sanctioned these urban development schemes during its 13
th
meeting for the going year. The session was presided over by P&D Board Chairman Hamed Yaqoob Sheikh. P&D Provincial Secretary Imran Sikandar Baloch, Senior Chief (Coordination) Javed Latif, Assistant Chief (Coordination) Shahid Idrees, and other officials concerned, were all present on the occasion.
Read
:
PDWP-Punjab approves upgradation of roads in Kotli Sattian, RYK, Sheikhupura
The road projects pertain to:
Rehabilitation/widening and improvement of Bhera Bhalwal Road in District Sargodha; at a revised cost of PKR 828.258 million
Dualization of road from Amra to Sahana Lok in District Mandi Bahaud Din; at a cost of PKR 640.478 million
Dualization of Taxila to HMC Farooqia Road in Rawalpindi; at a revised cost of PKR 1,386.421 million
Further, the officials concerned sanctioned a clean drinking water scheme for UC-99, 100 and 101 in Lahore at a cost of PKR 1,655.185 million.

title: Punjab approves NPHP Ordinance 2020; forms rules to facilitate low cost housing schemes
payment_plan_text: nventory to the Punjab Housing and Town Planning Agency (PHATA). | Read: | PHATA shares NPHP Rawalpindi payment plan details | The ordinance further specifies that any developer can establish a low-cost housing scheme in the areas under the control of PHATHA, if they in turn provide 20 housing units within their own societies to the authority. This measure also comes with a guarantee that NOCs and all related-approvals will be issued to such a housing scheme on a priority basis.
full_text:
Lahore: The Punjab government recently approved the Naya Pakistan Housing Programme (NPHP) Ordinance 2020 that features a ‘historic’ relief package for developers of private housing schemes, a news source reported on November 8.
As per the details available, developers can now earmark 20 plots within their housing schemes for the development of low-cost housing units. This will provide them with immunity from having to apply for building approvals and NOC issuance. The ordinance also made it mandatory for developers of low-cost housing schemes to handover 20% of their total plot inventory to the Punjab Housing and Town Planning Agency (PHATA).
Read:
PHATA shares NPHP Rawalpindi payment plan details
The ordinance further specifies that any developer can establish a low-cost housing scheme in the areas under the control of PHATHA, if they in turn provide 20 housing units within their own societies to the authority. This measure also comes with a guarantee that NOCs and all related-approvals will be issued to such a housing scheme on a priority basis.

title: NPHA shares details on subsidies being offered on construction of low-cost houses
payment_plan_text: ow-cost housing finance | For individuals seeking to get a home loan worth PKR 1 million, the monthly instalments have been set at PKR 6,600. On loans amounting to PKR 2 million, the monthly instalment is PKR 13,199, while loans amounting to PKR 4 million and 5 million will have installments worth PKR 31,012 and PKR 38,765 respectively.
full_text:
Lahore: The Naya Pakistan Housing Authority (NPHA) has re-shared the details on the incentives and subsidies offered by the federal government (through its recent
construction industry relief package
) on the construction of low-cost housing units under the Naya Pakistan Housing Programme (NPHP), according to a news source.
The authority further claimed that the package announced by Prime Minister Imran Khan to revive the real estate industry had managed to kick start construction activities across the country.
Read:
Punjab approves development of low-cost housing projects in 10 cities
The government had previously announced a PKR 30 billion subsidy in order to supplement the market for low-cost housing projects. In this regard, the government is offering subsidies worth PKR 300,000 each to the first 100,000 people constructing low-cost houses in the country, along with a 90% concession on due taxes.
At the same time, a special loan package was released, which was aimed at facilitating the people interested in constructing a home for themselves. In this regard, the home loan markup rate on the construction of a 5-marla house is set at 5%, with a rate of 7% applicable on the development of a 10-marla unit. The loans are available for a time period ranging between 5 to 10 years.
Read:
SBP extends loan limit for low-cost housing finance
For individuals seeking to get a home loan worth PKR 1 million, the monthly instalments have been set at PKR 6,600. On loans amounting to PKR 2 million, the monthly instalment is PKR 13,199, while loans amounting to PKR 4 million and 5 million will have installments worth PKR 31,012 and PKR 38,765 respectively.

title: Process to acquire land for RRR project begins
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Board of Revenue (BOR) has initiated the land acquisition process for the Rawalpindi Ring Road (RRR) project, a news source reported on November 6. In this regard, the board has issued deadlines for receiving objections from the landowner on the rates finalised by the Punjab government.
In the initial phase, the BOR has issued notices to 20,000 landowners having properties in the marked RRR route in Tehsil Rawalpindi and Tehsil Fateh Jang. As per the report, the government has to acquire 12,950 kanals of land in these tehsils, out of which 7,725 kanals falls in the jurisdiction of the Rawalpindi tehsil.
Read:
Punjab govt to invite open bidding for RRR project
The news source revealed that the BOR has set November 16 as the deadline to receive objections on acquisition rates (notified by the board) for land in the Rawalpindi region. The landowners are required to share their objections with the Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA), which has been notified as the executive authority for the ring road project.
The RDA will start processing these case after receiving objections from the land owners. Meanwhile, the landowners from Fateh Jang have to share their objections with the Union Council Qutbal latest by November 19. The BOI has marked 5,225 kanals of land for acquisition in this tehsil.

title: LDA to prepare feasibility report on construction of overhead bridge, Circular Road underpass
developer: Sardar Usman Buzdar has directed the Lahore Development
full_text:
Lahore: Punjab Chief Minister (CM) Sardar Usman Buzdar has directed the Lahore Development Authority to prepare a feasibility report on the construction of an overhead bridge as well as an underpass on the Circular Road, according to a news report published on November 6.
The directives were issued in a meeting held to brief the CM on seven development projects planned to address infrastructure-related issues in the neglected areas of Lahore. In addition to seeking a report on the construction of these facilities, Buzdar directed the civic agency to share details on the construction of a parking plaza near these structures.
Read:
WCLA proposes five-star hotel construction on Rim Market, Circular Road Lahore
As per the LDA sources, the estimated cost of these projects is PKR 3 billion. The development authority will acquire 35 kanals of land for the construction of the flyover and the underpass. The plan further reveals that the LDA will complete construction of the dual-lane overhead bridge and underpass in eight months.

title: Punjab govt to invite open bidding for RRR project
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Punjab government has announced its decision to invite open bidding for the Rawalpindi Ring Road (RRR) project, a news source reported on October 5. According to the details revealed, the provincial executive intends to develop the initiative under a solicited project proposal.
Read
:
Cost estimates, design suggestions for RRR sought within one week
The government had communicated its decision, reached during a meeting of the Public Private Partnership Authority (PPPA)’s policy and monitoring board last month, to Rawalpindi Commissioner Captain (retired) Mohammad Mehmood and Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) Director General Ammara Khan on Tuesday (October 3).
According to reports, the RDA has been tasked with drafting a solicited project proposal for the RRR initiative within 90 days, whereas the Lahore Ring Road Authority (LRRA) will act as the executing agency under a public-private partnership (PPP) mode.
Read
:
Land acquisition for RRR industrial zone to begin soon
Moreover, the civic agency is expected to introduce commercial activities along the RRR route. To facilitate this measure, it will redefine its jurisdiction after seeking approvals from the authorities concerned.

title: Land acquisition for RRR industrial zone to begin soon
developer: December. Commenting on the occasion, Rawalpindi Development
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The authority concerned has notified an increase from the existing 2,000 acress to 10,000 acres in the land area for the industrial zone planned along the Rawalpindi Ring Road (RRR) route; with the issuance of a Section 4 notification for commencing with the land acquisition process expected soon, according to a new story published on November 2.
Preparations are already underway for the groundbreaking of the ‘game changer’ RRR project, and the event is scheduled for the last week of December. Commenting on the occasion, Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) Chairman Tariq Murtaza revealed that all hurdles impeding the development of the Rawalpindi Ring Road had been removed.
Read:
RDA bans construction activity within RRR’s 100-metre radius to facilitate town planning
Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan and Punjab Chief Minister (CM) Sardar Usman Buzdar will perform the groundbreaking. According to reports, preparation to organise a grand ceremony for the purpose are underway.
The news source also revealed that an approval has been issued to develop the industrial zone, theme park, health zone, education zone, and fruits and vegetable market with the collaboration of the Islamabad and Rawalpindi Chambers of Commerce and Industries. Further, successful negotiations were held with the National University of Medical Science for the development of an education city.
Read:
RRR land acquisition: Landowners share their demands on rates
The Punjab government has already released PKR 6 billion for the land acquisition for the circular road project. It is expected that the RDA will receive workable proposals for the establishment of a European- standard theme park along the RRR route.

title: Firdous Market Underpass renamed as tribute to respected philanthropist
full_text:
Lahore: The Punjab government has decided to rename the Firdous Market Underpass to the ‘Abdul Sattar Edhi Underpass’ as a tribute to the famous deceased philanthropist and humanitarian, according to a news source published on October 28.
Read:
Firdous Market Underpass project to include remodelling of Khalid Masjid Chowk
The Lahore Development Authority (
LDA
) has already placed the signboard with the new name on the said underpass, while a portrait of its namesake has also been installed in the area. The suggestion to rename the road infrastructure was offered by the Chief Minister Secretariat.
Read:
Addressing Firdous Market Underpass drainage issues crucial in avoiding ubran flooding in Gulberg: WASA
In related news, it was further highlighted that the progress work on the Abdul Sattar Edhi Underpass was not being executed at an ideal pace. The development of the underpass is still to be completed and the  design of the underpass’s barrel wall hasn’t yet been finalized either. The barrel road carpeting is also underway.

title: Quaid-e-Azam Monument on Islamabad Expressway to undergo renovation
developer: A meeting of the Capital Development
full_text:
Islamabad: A meeting of the Capital Development Authority’s Development Working Party (DWP) on Tuesday announced its decision to renovate the ‘Quaid-e-Azam Monument’ on the Islamabad Expressway – according to news sources.
Read:
CDA urges residents for support in keeping Islamabad clean
The site which carries the national motto ‘Unity, Faith and Discipline’, is located at the western side of the Islamabad Expressway. The steel monument also features the Quaid’s profile. It had collapsed due to heavy winds on August 13.
The meeting, held under the chair of
CDA
Chairman Amer Ali, also announced to add some enhancements to the founder’s portrait erected on the monument. The project is estimated to cost PKR 56 million and high-quality 2mm iron sheets will be used to remake the portrait. The proposed size dimensions of the portrait are 50×59 feet and a sculpture of Rohtas Fort will be added to the portrait, in addition to a fortification.
Read:
CDA to spend PKR 2.7bn on rehabilitation of abandoned sewage treatment plant
The CDA-DWP meeting also approved the following agendas:
PC-I of the grade separation facility at the intersection of 7th Avenue with the Srinagar Highway and Khayban-e-Sohrwardi
PC-II for engaging consultancy services for the alignment and feasibility study of the Eastern Bypass
PC-I for the construction of multi-purpose ground at Shakarparian Phase II
The construction of additional rooms at 22 different educational institutions of Islamabad

title: PCIC decides to remove encroachments, settlements on nullahs in Karachi
developer: Sindh Labour Minister Saeed Ghani, Planning and Development
full_text:
Karachi: The Provincial Coordination & Implementation Committee (PCIC) on Monday (October 26) announced its decision to remove encroachments and relocate settlements and commercial units set up along all nullahs in Karachi in a bid to restore the city’s drains, a news source reported.
The PCIC meeting was chaired by Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah and attended by Corps Commander Karachi Lt General Humayoon Aziz, Sindh Labour Minister Saeed Ghani, Planning and Development Chairman Mohammad Waseem, PCIC Chief Coordinator Major General Aqeel Ahmed and several other officials.
Read:
PM’s Karachi Transformation Plan: Centre commits to funding 5 infrastructure projects
The meeting members were briefed that as many as 13,441 residential and 2,948 commercial units were built on the nullahs. Out of the 13,441 houses, 5,916 are constructed on Gujjar Nullah, 4,480 on Orangi Nullah, and 1,049 on Mahmoodabad Nummah, while the Malir River is home to some 1,996 households.
According to reports, the Sindh government has notified the owners of these commercial and residential structures to vacate the area. At the same time, a
survey
by the NED University is underway to analyse the length, width and capacities of the existing 44 storm drains in the city. The study is to be completed within the next three months.
Read:
Pakistan Engineering Council to help tackle urban flooding issue in Karachi
The meeting members also decided to draft various models of human resettlements and discuss these plans during the next meeting. A rehabilitation plan is being prepared by a three-member committee comprising Karachi administrator, commissioner and local government secretary.

title: LDA shortlists firms for preparation of Lahore Master Plan 2050
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) has shortlisted three firms to develop the city’s master plan, according to a news report published on October 27. The information was shared by LDA Vice Chairman (VC) S M Imran during a meeting with a delegation of the Association of Builders and Developers (ABAD).
The meeting was attended by notable LDA officials while the ABAD delegation comprised of ABAD North Region Chairman Sheraz Munnoo. Speaking to the delegation, the LDA vice chairman said that land development authorities of other cities were adopting the building bylaws and regulations finalised by the LDA to simplify the construction procedures.
Read:
LDA to draft master plan for 49 urban settlements; shares timeline for Lahore master plan preparation
He further revealed that the civic agency was taking all necessary measures to promote construction activity in line with the vision of Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan. At the same time, related rules and bylaws are being simplified to provide ease to the public. In this regard, the approval procedures for private housing schemes are being simplified.
LDA VC Imran further stated that rules were being drafted to ensure timely completion of development projects launched under public-private partnerships.

title: LDA City launches Iqbal Sector
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) has announced launching the ‘
Iqbal Sector
‘ in its LDA City, following the successful completion of its Jinnah Sector (Phase 1), according to a news source published on October 25.
Reportedly, the new sector spans an area of 12,000 Kanals. With the land acquisition process 50% complete, the authority says that the remaining land is currently being acquired. In addition to apartments, the Iqbal sector is offering 2-Kanal, 1-Kanal, 10-Marla and 5-Marla residential plots.
Read:
Prices in LDA City estimated to nearly double in 3 years
Additionally, the project features wide roads, including 40-feet residential service roads and 200-feet wide Chenab Road – for which the tender process is underway. Moreover, the development of the 180-feet wide road leading to the society from the Ferozepur Road is also complete.
Read:
PC-1 for LDA City Naya Pakistan Apartments project approved
The LDA City is strategically situated between the Chenab Road, the Defence Road and the Lahore Ring Road to provide its residents with easy access throughout the city. The society dwellers can also enjoy a signal-free drive from the Lahore International Airport. The balloting process for Iqbal Sector’s files are expected with the Jinnah Sector’s third ballot.

title: DG sets deadline for LDA to complete, inaugurate Firdous Market Underpass
full_text:
Lahore: Lahore Development Authority (LDA) Director General (DG) Ahmad Aziz Tarar has directed the officers concerned to ensure the completion and inauguration of the
Firdous Market Underpass
by October 31, according to a news report published today (October 21).
Read
:
Commercial audit begins for LDA: Projects, income and expenses on scrutiny
While chairing a review meeting, the DG said that the project’s completion was delayed owing to the recent spell of rains; adding that the civic agency regretted any inconvenience caused.
Reportedly, the flagship project is not expected to suffer from any further delays as the project was launched to provide the people of Lahore with convenience. The DG further revealed that the work on the project has continued throughout day and night and the whole team was working very hard to get the project completed on time.
Read
:
LDA approved 48 land-use conversions within one
week: Vice Chairman
Moreover, the director general stated that the quality of work should not be compromised to complete the project by the communicated deadline and, to this effect, timely supply of the required construction materials should be ensured. He said that the contractor’s payments should be made timely – after fulfilling all the legal requirements.

title: PDWP-Punjab approves upgradation of roads in Kotli Sattian, RYK, Sheikhupura
full_text:
Lahore: The Provincial Development Working Party (PDWP)-Punjab has sanctioned five development schemes – including the widening, dualisation and improvement of road infrastructure – in Kotli Sattian, Rahim Yar Khan and Sheikhupura, according to a news story published today (October 20).
Read:
Work on road projects underway to develop Kotli Sattian on par with Murree
The approval was issued during a meeting held on Monday (October 19). Punjab Planning and Development Secretary Imran Sikandar Baloch, provincial secretaries and representatives of the related departments, members of the Planning and Development Board, and other notable officials were all present on the occasion.
The approved schemes are estimated to cost PKR 3,230 million. As per the details revealed, the PDWP also provided its approval to land acquisition for setting up sewage treatment plants in Sialkot and Sahiwal at an estimated cost of PKR 822.96 million and PKR 657.62 million, respectively.
Read:
ACs to oversee rehabilitation, beautification of major road arteries in Lahore
The three road projects approved in the PDWP meeting are:
Widening and improvement of 24.1-kilometre long Lehtrar-Kotli Kuliary Road in Tehsil Kotli Sattian, Rawalpindi at a cost of PKR 649.463 million
Dualisation of the 11.15-kilometre long Jandiala Sher Khan section of Hiran Minar Road in Sheikhupura at an expense of PKR 494.68 million
Rehabilitation, widening and improvement of Roads in Rahim Khan at a cost of PKR 605.153 million

title: CDA opens technical bids for development work in Sector I-15
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Monday notified the opening of technical bids for development works in sub-sector I-15/4. According to the details revealed, a CDA committee would evaluate the bids, followed by the opening of financial bids of qualified firms.
Read
:
CDA allocates funds for construction of grid station in Sector I-11
The development authority had previously publicized its decision to invite bids from companies registered with the Pakistan Engineering Council (PEC) in category C-2 or above. In response, a number of firms submitted their technical and financial bids.
According to the civic agency, the
development of infrastructure
(including earth works) is underway in the sub-sector I-15/3. The authority has already completed a survey of dilapidated roads and streets in said sector.
Read
:
CDA to review technical bids for initiating development work in Sector I-12
The civic agency had launched Sector I-15 two decades ago to provide affordable residential facilities to low-income citizens in the capital city. The incumbent CDA management has conveyed its intent to develop stalled sectors and to address the issues faced by the allottees of plots in said locality.

title: KP govt sanctions PKR 1.5bn for road project in Mansehra
full_text:
Mansehra: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) government has sanctioned PKR 1.5 billion for the construction of the 15-kilomtetre-long Datta-Kotkay Road in a bid to ease traffic load on the Abbottabad Road, a news source reported on October 20.
Read
:
Three road projects approved for Mansehra to promote tourism
To this effect, MPA Babar Saleem Swati stated that the provincial executive had disbursed PKR 250 million out of the total PKR 1.5 billion for land acquisition; adding that the road project was part of the government’s
Annual Development Programme (ADP)
.
He said that the new road link would reduce the travelling distance between Abbottabad and Mansehra in addition to providing the tourists from Punjab, Sindh and Balochistan an alternative route to reach the Kaghan Valley.
Read
:
KP govt seeks funds to upgrade urban infrastructure in five cities
Moreover, he that the authorities concerned had identified a chunk of land between Datta and Kotkay for the project and would issue tenders following the completion of the land acquisition process, which was expected to be carried out on a timely basis.

title: CDA to spend PKR 2.7bn on rehabilitation of abandoned sewage treatment plant
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Sunday announced its decision to spend PKR 2.7 billion on the rehabilitation of an abandoned sewage treatment plant; adding that it intended to operationalize said facility within three months, a news source reported.
Read
:
CDA issues list of services being provided through website, mobile app
CDA Chairman Amir Ali Ahmed, who conducted a surprise visit to the site, said that he had directed the formation concerned to operationalise the plant within 90 days. He further stated that the facility was expected to treat water at 25% of its capacity during the initial phase of operationalization and at 50% in the next stage.
The civic agency plans to provide eight million gallons per day (MGD) of treated water (previously provided by
Simly Dam
) for irrigation and plantation purposes. The strategy is expected to facilitate an overall increase in water supply levels to the capital city.
Read
:
CDA allocates funds for construction of grid station in Sector I-11
Ahmed said that the development authority intended to issue performance-based special allowances for officials posted at the plant. He further stated that the CDA Board would determine the amount for these individuals. He also directed the officials concerned to commence with the repair and maintenance work at the facility on an immediate basis.

title: CDA allocates funds for construction of grid station in Sector I-11
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Sunday notified the allocation of PKR 602 million for providing electricity to Sector I-11. According to the details revealed, CDA’s Mechanical-I Division will utilise said funds to construct a ‘Grid Station – Feeder Line’ in the locality.
As per the announcement, the civic agency intends to develop ‘long neglected residential sectors and uplift infrastructure in Islamabad’ as part of a comprehensive strategy. It further stated that it took a number of measures for the development of Sector I-11.
Read:
Tenders to initiate development work in CDA sectors to be issued soon
Among CDA’s going works is the construction of four box culverts in Sector I-11/2 and a storm management system in I-11 in a bid facilitate pedestrian movement and improve drainage system in the respective localities.
Moreover, it stated that the development work in Park Enclave’s phase one was set to conclude, while the work on said scheme’s second phase would commence soon; adding that work was in progress on sectors I-12, I-15 and E-12.

title: CDWP approves PKR 55.4bn New Gwadar International Airport project
full_text:
Islamabad: The Central Development Working Party (CDWP) on Monday provided its approval to the construction of the New Gwadar International Airport facility, which will be developed at a cost of PKR 55.4 billion, in addition to sanctioning reduction in the scope of a road scheme in Gwadar.
Planning Commission Deputy Chairman Jehanzeb Khan presided over the session, which reviewed the proposed upward revision in the construction cost of the airport project. According to the details revealed, the facility will be developed with government funds as well as a Chinese grant of 52 billion yuan (PKR 34 billion).
Read:
Gwadar to be linked with other cities via railway line: Bajwa
The government had originally sanctioned the project’s construction at a cost of PKR 7.5 billion in 2010. The first revision of PKR 22.5 billion was approved in 2015 and the second revision (of PKR 55.4 billion) was greenlit on Monday (October 12)
According to reports, changes to the project design resulted in the upward revision (of PKR 33 billion) of the cost (calculated in 2015). The new Gwadar airport is considered an important initiative with regard to the development of the Gwadar Port and its free zone.
The CDWP further directed the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) to review proposals pertaining to a reduction in the construction cost of Airport Security Force (ASF) and CAA buildings, which are expected to be constructed within the premises of the airport facility.
Read:
Eighty-percent development work on Gwadar East Bay Expressway completed: CPEC Chairman
The authorities concerned had previously included PKR 9.9 billion (for the construction of an ASF camp) and PKR 2.7 billion (for establishing a CAA Residential complex) in the total construction cost of the airport project, but the federal government had allocated PKR 519 million for the facility under its Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP).

title: CDA sectors to get water supply from Rawal Dam
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has planned to obtain a share of four million gallons per day (MGD) of water from the Rawal Dam to meet the growing needs of the residential sectors, according to the news source published on October 14.
Read:
Citizens urge Islamabad mayor to restore water supply in affected sectors
CDA Chairman Amer Ali Ahmed said that the authority plans to receive its approved water share from the Rawal Dam. He revealed that the department officials have even visited an abandoned water treatment plant to see about getting it fixed for getting the needed water supply. He announced that water from the dam will be made part of the water supply system of Islamabad.
Read:
Budget 2020-21: PKR 3.15bn reserved for provision of water to Islamabad, Rawalpindi
Reportedly, until 1992, the civic agency used the abandoned water treatment plant near the Polo Club on Garden Avenue to receive the ‘fixed quota’ of water for the city – but stopped after the dam was revealed to be contaminated. It was reported that the city is facing water shortage as only 65MDG of water is being provided to its residents against the total requirement of 220MGD – which is being sourced from the
Simly Dam
, the Khanpur Dam and various tube-wells.

title: Chinese firms hand over OLMT project to Punjab Mass Transit Authority
full_text:
Lahore: The China State Railway Group Co Ltd and the China North Industries have completed the development work at the Orange Line Metro Train project and handed over its control to the Punjab Mass Transit Authority, according to a news report published in national dailies on October 13. The train service is scheduled for
official launch
on October 25.
The OLMT has been developed as an early harvest project launched under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) initiative. It is the country’s first ever mass rapid urban transit train service. The construction work at the project site began in September 2015 and the launch was delayed several times owing to the potential risks to the historical buildings situated along the train’s route.
Read:
250 new job openings announced in OLMT project
The train track is 25.58 kilometres in length and features 26 stations, out of which 24 stops fall on the elevated track, which stretches to 23.8 kilometre. The underground track was laid after altering the original development plan to protect historical buildings on and around GT Road.
The project is being prepared for its official launch announced for this month. In order to make it feasible, a team of experts from the Lahore Development Authority inspected the final works and issued instruction to make certain facilities operational. The team also directed the officials concerned to clear the connected roads and footpaths of debris and leftover construction material before October 20.

title: Work revived on 10 FGHA housing projects, PM told
full_text:
Islamabad: During the weekly meeting of the National Coordination Committee (NCC) on Housing, Construction and Development on Thursday, the Ministry of Housing informed Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan that as many as 10 projects of the Federal Government Housing Authority (FGHA) had been revived recently, according to a news source published on October 8.
Read:
Bookings open for PHA-F Officer’s Residencia project in Islamabad
The PM was briefed that an accumulated 38,637 housing units would be developed at an estimated cost of PKR 120.21 billion under the aforementioned ten projects that had been stalled for the last few years.
In a similar manner, work on three residential projects falling under the auspices of the Pakistan Housing Authority (
PHA
) Foundation has also been launched — with these projects having been delayed for the last few years. Reportedly, 5,372 housing units will be developed at an estimated cost of PKR 27.86 billion under this initiative.
Furthermore, the PM was told that 26,625 housing units would be constructed at a cost of PKR 213.4 billion under the federal government’s ongoing projects. Additionally, under the new residential projects launched during 2020 and 2021, more than 25,017 and 39,955 housing units would be developed with an estimated cost of PKR 112.03 and PKR 184 billion respectively.
Read:
Housing Ministry shares two-year performance report on low-income residential initiatives
Moreover, the meeting was told that after the government had provided funds worth PKR 3 billion to the Akhuwat Foundation, work on the construction of 5,882 housing units had been initiated, while the construction work for another 4,000 units would be launched with the provision of an additional PKR 2 billion.
As per the information available, the government is expected to provide funds worth PKR 5 billion as a soft loan for the construction of housing for low-income groups through the Akhuwat Foundation.
During the meeting, the Punjab Chief Secretary also took the opportunity to apprise the session regarding the “Real-Time Construction Monitoring Dashboard” digital platform that has been created in order to monitor the ongoing construction activity in the province.

title: Plan in the works to implement ‘Islamabad the Beautiful’ initiative
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has deployed two officers at director-general’s level to resolve public complaints and ensure the implementation of ‘Islamabad the Beautiful’ initiative, according to a news source published on October 11.
Read:
CDA directorates to execute road carpeting of Islamabad Expressway, other major arteries
These two officials will answer to the authority’s member engineering and finance to ensure that the plan is implemented without any procedural delays. CDA Chairman Amer Ali Ahmed said that Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan had issued directives for the
capital city
’s restoration. He further stated that the civic agency intended to spend PKR 54 billion on the initiative.
Read:
CDA to upgrade capital’s infrastructure under new project
While talking about the recent transference of four directorates of the Metropolitan Corporation Islamabad (MCI) to the CDA, Mazhar Hussain, a spokesperson for the development authority, said that the residents of the capital city were facing several issues pertaining to the environment, roads, water, sanitation and other concern; adding that the officials deployed would resolve these complaints.

title: CDA invites proposals for flyover construction at railway lines in Sihala-Islamabad
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (
CDA
) has invited consultancy firms to submit proposals for the design and construction of a flyover at the railway lines on the Kahuta-Sihala Road in the capital, according to a post published on the authority’s official Facebook page on October 3.
Read:
CDA to upgrade capital’s infrastructure under new project
Under the project, a 400-metre-long overhead bridge and an 800-metre long approach road (400-metre-long each way) are to be constructed. The project funding would be mainly provided by the Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP), however, PKR 300 million were allocated by the federal government in the current fiscal.
Furthermore, the selected consultancy firm will also assist in “shifting of services from the vicinity in addition to keeping liaison with the Pakistan Railways for obtaining no-objection certificated (NOC)”.
Read:
CDA-hired consultant recommends upgradation of IJP Road
The construction of a flyover at the Kahuta-Sihala Road is a long-standing demand of the residents owing to the persisting traffic issues. The bridge, once completed, is expected to significantly improve the traffic flow in the area and resolve the daily commuters’ woes.

title: CDA directorates to execute road carpeting of Islamabad Expressway, other major arteries
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) administration has drafted a comprehensive plan to enhance the performance of four of its directorates and under the initial phase of the said plan, the Islamabad Expressway and other major arteries of the capital city are expected to undergo carpeting work, according to a news report published on October 9.
Read:
CDA directed to stop private societies from selling plots prior to procuring approvals
Previously, the government had transferred four directorates of the Metropolitan Corporation of Islamabad (MCI) to the CDA to ensure smooth operation of said wings and address the problems being faced by the citizens of
Islamabad
. The bodies handed over to the CDA are: Directorate of Water (Bulk Water Supply and Water and Sewerage Development), Environment Wing (Urban, Regional, Parks), Directorate of Sanitation and City Sewerage and Directorate of Engineering (MPO, Street Lights and MR&M).
Read:
CDA to launch online tax payment gateway facility
Under the said plan’s first phase, road carpeting will be executed in several housing sectors in addition to the carpeting of the Islamabad Expressway. In this regard, the authority is currently carpeting the roads in Sector I and its subsectors.
Similarly, the Environment Wing has been tasked with eliminating weeds and wild vegetation in the areas surrounding the Sri Nagar Highway, the Margalla Road, the Ninth Avenue, and the F-9 Park. Also, to improve the sanitation condition in the city, the Sanitation Directorate will now operate in two shifts.

title: SRSP launches community infrastructure schemes to rehabilitate uprooted people of Waziristan
full_text:
Peshawar: The Sarhad Rural Support Programme (
SRSP
) has launched as many as 17 community infrastructure schemes in the districts of North and South Waziristan – under the European Union (EU) funded “Aid to uprooted people in Pakistan” project, according to a news source published on October 06.
Read:
KP govt, UNDP launch vocational training programme in tribal areas
The project is being jointly funded by EU and Germany’s KfW Development Bank. The initiative aims to implement/establish six potable water supply schemes, five sanitisation, and four irrigation schemes – at a total cost of PKR 66.5 million.
Reportedly, these schemes would benefit a total of 1,800 households in selected villages. As the name of the initiative implies, all these community infrastructure schemes have been developed in areas where displaced families have recently returned.
Read:
Solar-powered water projects launched in Orakzai district
Under this programme, organised by the SRSP, the selected communities would be able to identify their infrastructural needs and implement them systematically – in the villages located in the districts of North and South Waziristan – with the technical assistance of the project team.

title: Five-year development plan for GB on cards
full_text:
Islamabad: The Planning Commission on Monday said in a statement that a ‘five-year development plan’ for the region has been deliberated with the Gilgit-Baltistan (GB) government – for the first time ever, according to news sources.
Read:
PM to announce mega-development projects for GB during his visit this month: GB governor
The said five-year development plan for
GB
involves major sectors like agriculture, infrastructure, health, tourism, education, higher education, energy and gems/precious stones. The aforementioned function – titled “Socio-Economic Development of Gilgit-Baltistan” – was jointly organised by the Ministry of Planning, Development and Special Initiatives and the Planning & Development Department of GB.
Planning Commission Deputy Chairman Dr Mohammad Jehanzeb Khan briefed the session that the central government believes that a stable and prosperous GB is vital for the country’s economic growth. He further revealed that offices of various federal agencies would soon be set up in the province.
Read:
WAPDA directed to hire GB residents for Diamer-Bhasha Dam project development
Moreover, Jehanzeb highlighted that the incumbent government has taken various steps to facilitate the public-private partnership (PPP) arrangement, in certain mega projects, to develop the province’s social sector and “mainstreaming of the vulnerable and socially excluded population”.
Meanwhile, the function asked for an infallible and realistic implementation strategy to realise the proposed plans and programmes. It was emphasised that institutional reforms would play a key role in the region’s development and the roles of each should be clearly underlined – before unveiling the five-year plan.

title: KP govt, WAPDA to announce uplift package for Mohmand district
full_text:
Peshawar: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) government and the Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA) have revealed their intent to develop an uplift package for the Mohmand tribal district, according to a news report published on October 9.
Read:
KP govt seeks funds to upgrade urban infrastructure in five cities
The said provision will include initiatives for road infrastructure, health facilities, clean drinking water and other projects of public welfare. The uplift scheme will be announced by the KP Chief Minister (CM) Mahmood Khan upon a visit to the district.
The package was announced at a meeting held between
KP
CM Khan and WAPDA Chairman Lt Gen (r) Muzzamil Hussain. The two officials discussed matters related to the under-construction Mohmand Dam. The meeting was also attended by other officials of WAPDA.
Read:
KP govt orders crackdown on illegal construction in Makhinal
The meeting was appraised about the progress status of Mohmand Dam and the CM declared the projects ‘significant’ for the socio-economic development of the tribal district.

Lahore: Lahore Development Authority (LDA) Director General (DG) Ahmed Aziz Tarar has announced the civic agency’s decision to draft a master plan for 49 urban settlements in Sheikhupura, Nankana Sahib and Kasur, according to a news report published on October 8. The
LDA
DG also revealed that a new master plan for Lahore will be prepared within the next 18 months.
Read:
LDA-approved Etihad Town reveals payment plans for residential, commercial plots
The director general of the authority made these remarks while talking to the representatives of the three consultants shortlisted for the Lahore master plan preparation. This pre-qualifying consortium includes Dar Al-Hindsa (Lebanon), Mine Heart (Singapore) and National Engineering Services Pakistan – NESPAK (Pakistan).

LDA Auction 2020: Residential, commercial plots to be auctioned in various locations of Lahore
The objectives of this master plan include environmental protection, preservation of historical heritage, equitable use of resources, promotion of economic activities, and inclusion of all sections of the population in decision making.

title: Construction work launched on Korang Bridge and PWD Underpass

Reportedly, the work on the underpass will be finalise
full_text:
Islamabad: Capital Development Authority (CDA) Member Engineering Ayaz Khan recently revealed that the much-awaited construction work on the expansion of the Korang Bridge and the PWD Underpass (located on Islamabad Expressway) had been launched on Monday (October 5), according to news sources.
Read:
CDA to launch online tax payment gateway facility
He further stated that once the two projects have been completed, they will help reduce the traffic congestion on the city’s main roads. Reportedly, the contract for the two construction projects was earlier won by a joint venture of Maqbool Associates and Calsons. The winning bid was PKR 628.5 million for the Korang Bridge and PKR 428 million for the PWD Underpass — with these amounts respectively 17% and 19% less than the estimated cost.
The funding for the two projects is expected to be provided under the Public Sector Development Programme (
PSDP
). The first instalment worth PKR 160 million has already been released by the government — with the CDA issuing a letter of commencement for the said projects on September 23.
Read:
CDA publishes notice for hiring consultant to review Islamabad Master Plan
As per the CDA officials, the responsibility of making certain that there are no revised estimates for the two projects lies with the authority management to ensure that the low bids prove beneficial. Reportedly, the work on the underpass will be finalised in seven months, while the completion of the bridge will be take up to 15 months.

title: Punjab govt assigns master plan development task for five cities
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The provincial government recently assigned the Punjab Intermediate Cities Improvement Project (PICIP) the task to develop the master plan for five major cities, which include Rawalpindi, Sahiwal, Dera Ghazi Khan, Sargodha and Multan — according to a news source published on Wednesday (October 7).
These plans will be developed by keeping in mind the infrastructural needs of the selected cities for the next 20 years. Reportedly, while the Rawalpindi Development Authority had already finalised the consultant for the development of the master plan for the city, this responsibility has now been handed over to the PICIP.
As per the information available, the PICIP is being funded by the Asian Development Bank (ADB). Previously, under the PICIP, the bank had approved funds worth USD 200 million in September 2017 for improving the delivery of urban services and infrastructure in Sialkot and Sahiwal.
For the development of the aforementioned master plans, the PICIP will ask the government departments concerned to prepare and share their proposed projects based on the projected figures for population growth over the next 20 years. The PICIP will then share its feedback on the planning and implementation of the planned development schemes based on their recommendations.

title: Park Enclave I bridge opened to traffic
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has formally opened the Park Enclave-Phase I bridge following its work completion, a news source reported on October 5. The facility has been constructed over a storm drain in the project.
Read:
CDA completes ballot process for plots in Park Enclave III
According to details, the said bridge was recently completed and tentatively marks the end of majority of the development work in the phase. The authority has taken a number of steps for the provisions of maximum modern facilities for the residents of the Park Enclave Phase I.
Read:
CDA shares details on submitting online applications for Park Enclave III residential plots
Moreover, the introduced facilities include installation of a comprehensive security system as well as completion of the housing scheme’s road network. Currently, the horticultural work is being carried out in the project. The CDA has also made payments worth PKR 602 million to the Sui Northern Gas Pipeline (SNGPL) for uninterrupted supply of gas.

title: CDA to upgrade capital’s infrastructure under new project
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Monday finalised a plan to rehabilitate parts of Islamabad under a new project worth an estimated PKR 2 billion — with this amount expected to be further supplemented if required, according to a news source published on October 6.
Read:
Contract awarded for design, alignment of Rawat-Bhara Kahu Bypass, Islamabad
The said project was finalised during a meeting chaired by CDA Chairman Amer Ali Ahmed. On the occasion, it was decided that the aforementioned uplift project would be implemented in Sector H (containing various institutions), and the residential sectors of G, F and I. The project to upgrade the capital’s infrastructure includes road carpeting, establishing pavements, executing soft landscaping, and fixing the area’s streetlights and drainage system.
Reportedly, the estimates for the individual work to be executed under the rehabilitation project are currently being mapped out. It was communicated that the tenders in this regard should be invited in October, and that the entire project is expected to be completed in three months.
Read:
CDA launches repair work on Islamabad Expressway post-torrential rain
The CDA Chairman stated that the implementation of the said project was sorely needed in Islamabad. He added that the funds generated from various
auctions
undertaken by the authority over the last few months (amounting to PKR 57 billion) would now be invested in the city’s infrastructure, starting with the aforementioned uplift project.
Furthermore, during the meeting, it was also decided that CDA’s Machinery Pool Organisation would be initiating work for the carpeting of roads in the Diplomatic Enclave on Tuesday.

title: KP govt seeks funds to upgrade urban infrastructure in five cities
developer: KP is being co-funded with the Asian Development
full_text:
Islamabad: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP government recently revealed that it had sought a USD 142 million loan grant from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) to construct, rehabilitate and revitalise core urban infrastructure of five cities of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under the ‘Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Cities Improvement Project (KPCIP)’, according to a news report published on October 5.
Read:
KP govt orders crackdown on illegal construction in Makhinal
The said initiative aims to improve access to safely-managed water, solid waste management, sanitation and green urban infrastructure spaces in Peshawar, Abbottabad,
Kohat
, Mardan, and Mingora. This is to be achieved through two-interlinked outputs; enhancement and extension of public spaces and urban infrastructure in addition to strengthening the ‘institutional capacities of urban service providers, provincial government and city government’.
Read:
KP CM orders initiation of civil works for Peshawar Revival Plan projects
This urban infrastructure project in KP is being co-funded with the Asian Development Bank (ADB) as the lead co-financer. It is expected to reduce urban pollution and prevent soil and water contamination. Under this initiative, ‘viable climate resilience measures and innovations’ will be incorporated into the detailed engineering designs.

title: CDA-hired consultant recommends upgradation of IJP Road
developer: A consultant hired by the Capital Development
full_text:
Islamabad: A consultant hired by the Capital Development Authority (CDA) has recommended that the IJ Principal (IJP) Road should be upgraded, according to a news report. The consultant stated that two additional rigid lanes and three flyovers were required to ensure smooth traffic flow.
Read:
CDA to hire consultant for IJP Road project
He presented these findings to CDA Chairman Amer Ali Ahmed, and stated that there was the need for two additional rigid lanes on either side of the road. The
CDA
issued a press release in the regard, stating that in addition to extending the existing seven box culverts on IJP Road, the development body will also construct a new box culvert. This press release also stated that the three flyovers would be built on 9
th
, 10
th
, and 11
th
Avenue, respectively.
Read:
CDA allocated funds to initiate construction work on 10th Avenue
The civic body had previously hired this consultant to conduct a feasibility study, with design and building estimates for the upgradation of this project. As per the consultant’s presentation, this project will cost approximately PKR 5.3 billion. Once this feasibility study is wrapped up, the body will launch the tender process to award the construction contracts for the project.

title: Committee formed to identify RDA City’s location along RRR route
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) has constituted a five-member committee to identify land for the location of the RDA City project — with the group expected to present its recommendations by October 15, according to a news source published on October 1.
Read:
RDA to simplify NOC procedure for builders
Reportedly, the authority has approved the establishment of RDA City on a 3,000-kanal piece of land adjoining the Rawalpindi Ring Road (RRR). This is the first-ever government residential project being developed in the city.
As per the information available, RDA City project will feature plots sized 3, 5, 7 and 10 marlas. The project is also being developed using a proper and inclusive master plan — with water, sewerage, gas and power infrastructure to be installed soon. The project is also expected to accommodate government employees of the lower basic pay scale (BPS).
Read:
RDA to invite RRR project tenders; begin land acquisition process this month
Earlier, the RDA had further approved of the decision to make the
Mouzas
falling within the vicinity of the economic zone planned along the RRR route a part of the city — with the area now coming under the jurisdiction of the development authority.

title: G-7/G-8 Underpass at Faisal Avenue to be launched
full_text:
Islamabad: Special Assistant to Prime Minister (SAPM) on Capital Development Authority (CDA) Affairs Ali Nawaz Awan inaugurated the G-7/G-8 Underpass at Faisal Avenue on Friday (Oct 2), according to a news source published on October 2.
Read:
Contract awarded for design, alignment of Rawat-Bhara Kahu Bypass, Islamabad
The G-7/G-8 Underpass at Faisal Avenue has been constructed at a cost of PKR 395 million. While the project had been slated to be completed in May, construction work had to be halted due to the coronavirus outbreak and its resulting countrywide lockdown.
The SAPM stated that this major road project had been constructed after a decade-long gap, and that now several projects — including the construction of 10th Avenue and the development of an interchange at the junction of Srinagar Avenue near Abapara and 7th Avenue — would soon be completed. He further revealed that the contract for the development of the
Rawal Dam
Interchange had already been awarded, and that work on the project would be launched in November.
Read:
Minister orders speedy completion of Islamabad IT Park project
As per Islamabad’s master plan, the CDA is expected to develop major avenues between the city’s residential sectors in order to link them through underpasses.

title: Govt considers setting up underground storage to manage growing gas needs
full_text:
Islamabad: Special Assistant to Prime Minister (SAPM) on Petroleum Division Nadeem Babar chaired a meeting on Monday to discuss setting up various underground gas storage areas to meet the country’s ever-growing requirements, a news source reported. Reportedly, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) has also proposed to help Pakistan increase its gas storage capacity.
Read:
PM orders road-map preparation to overcome gas shortage
Additionally, the meeting was briefed that European gas companies are also part of the project for installing new gas infrastructure, which would help avert the looming crisis of gas shortage in the country – for both residences and industries alike – during the upcoming winter season.
Read:
Russia eyes investing USD 1.7bn in SNGPL’s Karachi-Lahore gas pipeline project
Reportedly, the assessment report on the project will be prepared by May next year (2021) – which will decide the blueprint for the volume of the storage, modules and its security. A budget will be allocated to the project, based on the report, to immediately tackle the upcoming shortage issue in its nascence.

title: Sindh CM issues directives for early completion of BRT Orange Line infrastructure
full_text:
Karachi: Sindh Chief Minister (CM) Syed Murad Ali Shah on Tuesday (September 29) issued instructions to the transport department to complete the BRT Orange Line infrastructure on a timely basis, a news source reported.
Read:
Pakistan, ADB sign loan agreement for Karachi’s BRT project
He further directed the authorities concerned to acquire the loan grant from the Asian Development Bank (ADB) for the Red Line project and finalise the design for the Yellow Line system.
The CM was presiding over a meeting of the provincial transport department to review the progress of the development on the BRT. Minister for Transport Awais Qadir Shah was also present on the occasion. Murad said that the department should set a timeline for the inauguration of the projects.
Read:
Centre to bear Karachi Green Line BRT’s deficit; manage operations for three years
The meeting was informed that the Orange Line had been renamed as ‘BRT Abdul Sattar Edhi’. The project would feature a 3.8-kilometre-long track, four bus stations, and one terminal. The project would be completed at a cost of PKR 2.36 billion.

title: Groundbreaking of PKR 27bn Malir Expressway project scheduled for Oct
developer: Commander Lt Gen Humayun Aziz and Planning and Development
full_text:
Karachi: Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah on Monday (September 28) chaired a meeting of the newly-constituted Provincial Coordination & Implementation Committee (PCIC) during which he was informed of the Malir Expressway project’s groundbreaking in October, according to a news source.
Read:
Consortium of top businessmen to invest in mega-projects in Lahore,Karachi
Karachi Corps Commander Lt Gen Humayun Aziz and Planning and Development (P&D) Chairman Mohammad Waseem were also present at the session. The P&D Chairman gave a detailed briefing regarding various mega development projects undergoing in Karachi.
According to reports, the Malir Expressway project is being developed with a budget of PKR 27 billion and will be launched under a public-private-partnership (PPP) model.
The meeting was informed that the 27-kilometre-long Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Green Line project will be completed by June 2021. The Sindh government has also launched the 4.7-kilometre-long BRT Orange Line project, scheduled for completion by June 2021. As for the 21-kilometre-long Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Yellow Line project, it will be completed at a cost of PKR 61.44 billion.
Read:
Committee formed to oversee implementation of Karachi transformation plan
Furthermore, the meeting was informed that seven stormwater drain schemes would be launched at a cost of PKR 258.7 billion in a bid to clear the rivers and nullahs of Lyari, Malir, Gujjar, Mehmoodabad and Orangi. The DHA Karachi stormwater drainage issues were being resolved under a PKR 10 billion scheme. The stormwater drain project was communicated to be 60% complete by July 2021 and the remaining work was said to be completed by July 2020. The meeting also discussed various settlements for
compensation
of the affected people.
Other projects discussed included water supply projects in the city, solid waste management, sewerage treatment and five Combined Effluent Treatment Plants (CETPs) for industrial areas of Karachi.

title: Governing body approves LDA Building and Zoning Regulations 2020 for four districts
developer: The governing body of the Lahore Development
full_text:
Lahore: The governing body of the Lahore Development Authority (LDA) recently provided its approval to the LDA Building and Zoning Regulations 2020 for Lahore, Sheikhupura, Kasur, and Nankana Sahib, according to news sources.
Read:
LDA Auction 2020: Residential, commercial plots to be auctioned in various locations of Lahore
According to the details revealed, the LDA Building and Zoning Regulations 2020 aim to promote business, commercial and other
economic activities
in the aforementioned districts of the Lahore Division. The zones in these districts are categorized into industrial, commercial, institutional and other zones. The meeting also determined the criteria regarding plot sizes, road widths and other standards for launching new projects.
The LDA governing body meeting was held under the chair of the authority’s Vice Chairman S M Imran. The said meeting also approved the revised PC-1 amounting to PKR 49.54 billion for the phase-one of the LDA City. This sum includes PKR 9.67 billion for compulsory land acquisition.
Read:
LDA notifies its ‘area of exclusive jurisdiction’ for land-use conversions
Furthermore, the meeting decided to invite technical and financial bids for the construction of 35,000 affordable housing units under the ‘LDA City Naya Pakistan Apartments’. A committee to evaluate the responses received was also constituted in the same sitting.
The meeting also approved the proposal presented by the negotiation committee for finalizing terms with a private housing society to offer plots to the 613 affectees of LDA Avenue-I. The private housing scheme will provide 1,555 kanals of land to the authority ‘in lieu of developed plots equal to 30 per cent of its land’.

title: CDA to hire international consultant for revising Islamabad master plan
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has booked advertisements in several foreign publications in a bid to invite applications from reputable international consultant firms for the revision of Islamabad’s master plan, according to a news source published on September 29.
Read:
PM orders masterplan revisions for major cities to counteract civic issues
The process for hiring international consultant in collaboration with the planning commission was ordered by the federal cabinet in October 2019. To this effect, CDA spokesperson Mazhar Hussain said that the development authority held several sessions with the planning commission and other stakeholders and completed all requirements ahead of the consultant hiring process.
Read:
Developers Association demand CDA to prepare Blue Area Ext masterplan
Moreover, CDA officials communicated that the applicant selected will be brought in to propose solutions for several
civic issues
persisting in the capital for decades. They revealed that thousands of people had constructed homes and other structures in no-construction zones. They expressed the hope that with the help of the consultancy firm, the authority would revise the capital city’s master plan.

title: Construction of ‘Pakistan’s largest SEZ’ to begin soon in Muzaffargarh: Aslam Iqbal
developer: He also stated that the Punjab Skills Development
full_text:
Faisalabad: Punjab Minister for Industries, Commerce and Investment Mian Muhammad Aslam Iqbal has stated that the construction of the ‘largest Special Economic Zone (SEZ) in Pakistan’ would begin soon in Muzaffargarh, a news source reported on September 28. The SEZ will be established over an area of nearly 20,000 acres, he added.
Read:
Work on SEZs development and socio-economic projects under CPEC expedited: Bakhtyar
The minister was speaking to the 23
rd
Annual Meeting of Pakistan Textile Exporters Association. He said that the SEZ could be expanded up to an area of 50,000 acres as well.
He further stated that to provide full exposure to products of the exporters, the country’s ‘largest expo centre’ facility would be established on a public-private partnership (PPP) mode in Faisalabad. He added that land had been allocated for this purpose in the Faisalabad Industrial Estate.
Read:
PIEDMC to construct grid stations in Vehari, Bhalwal SEZs
He also stated that the Punjab Skills Development Authority (PSDA) had been established to provide the exporters in the country with skilled labour.

title: Work underway on preparation of Sialkot Master Plan
developer: Arrangements finalised to set up Sialkot Development
full_text:
Sialkot: Special Assistant to the Prime Minister on Youth Affairs Usman Dar on Thursday (September 24) revealed that work was underway on the preparation of a master plan for the city, a news source reported. He disclosed this information while speaking to the media; adding that the said initiative would be completed at a cost of PKR 15 billion.
Read:
Arrangements finalised to set up Sialkot Development Authority: Minister Dar
On the occasion, Mr. Dar highlighted various issues facing the city, including problems with the provision of a potable water supply, sanitation, and solid waste disposal. He stated that the provincial government was collaborating with experts from the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to come up with projects to address these issues in a sustainable manner. He added that the provincial government was also keen on improving the city’s traffic situation, provide improved recreational facilities, and to establish additional public parks.
Read:
Development projects in Sialkot to be named after top taxpayers
Additionally, Dar revealed that the Sialkot Municipal Corporation and the Sialkot Waste Company had started to receive the required machinery and vehicles to perform their tasks adequately.
