The development of the master plan is expected to help provide international-standard facilities to the city’s residents. Reportedly, the PKR 57 billion project is being financed by the ADB.

title: ‘Land acquisition along RRR route underway by private developers’
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) recently revealed that the developers of dozens of private housing schemes were actively acquiring land along the route of the Rawalpindi Ring Road (RRR) — with the developers aiming to launch residential projects on these properties in the near future, according to a news source published on September 21. The ongoing land-buying activity indicates that thousands of residential units will be constructed in the area during the coming years.
Read:
Proposals invited from private societies for construction of interchanges on RRR
Currently, the RDA is engaged with three mega infrastructural development projects, which include the RRR, the Leh Expressway, and the Rawalpindi-Islamabad Circular Railway Project. The development of these projects is expected to improve the city’s traffic situation and the socio-economic conditions of its residents. As per RDA sources, these projects are estimated to be completed in the next three years.
The authority will provide logistic and technical support to the firms engaged in conducting the development work on the aforementioned projects. Reportedly, the authority has tasked the experts working on these projects to complete the spadework by the end of 2020.
Read:
Rawalpindi Ring Road alignment finalised; details on approved route shared
Additionally, the RDA has already finalised the road alignment and route for the RRR project, and the Punjab government has also issued the requisite funds to begin the land acquisition process. The provincial government has further issued funds worth PKR 5 billion to start the initial development work on the Leh Expressway. Both these projects are expected to be inaugurated by the end of the year.
Read:
Rawalpindi Ring Road project development task handed over to LRRA
At the same time, a team of civil engineers from China are currently in the process of preparing a feasibility report and PC-1 for the Rawalpindi-Islamabad Circular Railway project. The report is expected to be finalised in the next eight months.

title: RDA to issue NOC to high-rises falling outside CAA domain
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) and other government authorities concerned will soon be empowered to issue no-objection certificates (NOC) to high rises located beyond a 15-kilometre radius of the Islamabad International Airport (IIA), according to a news source published on September 24.
Read:
RDA to simplify NOC procedure for builders
Previously, approval from the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) was required regarding the height of projects located in RDA-controlled areas near the IIA. However, as per the source, this approval process would take up to three months. In addition, developers were further required to contact the Survey of Pakistan to verify the exact location of their building in order to ensure it did not fall under the CAA’s jurisdiction.
This information came to light during a meeting between Chairman RDA Tariq Mehmood Murtaza and Federal Aviation Minister Ghulam Sarwar Khan. On the occasion, the RDA chairman directed the authorities concerned to simplify the process for the acquisition of layout plans and housing schemes’ approvals — with this move expected to be in line with Prime Minister Imran Khan’s decision to grant the construction sector the status of ‘industry’.
Read:
CDA prepares PC-1 for acquiring buses for IIA Metro Track
In turn, the aviation minister asked for a regulatory framework to be formulated that would allow for the construction of structures in already approved housing societies, without the requirement of acquiring an NOC from the CAA first. Additionally, he assured Chairman Murtaza that all requisite facilities would be provided to the construction sector for the development of new projects in RDA-controlled areas.
Separately, another online system is also expected to be created, with the involvement of the RDA, the Rawalpindi Metropolitan Corporation (RMC) and the district planning and traffic engineering departments. This facility would allow developers to verify various aspects of their projects, including building regulations, the number of high rises in the project area, and the project’s proximity to the
IIA
.

title: Punjab govt seeks full occupation of M3 Industrial Estate by year-end
full_text:
Lahore: Faisalabad Industrial Estate Development and Management Company (FIEDMC) Chairman Mian Kashif Ashfaq has revealed that the Punjab government is aiming to completely occupy M3 Industrial Estate by the year end, according to a news source published on September 24.
Read:
Punjab govt to revive industrial estate project
He revealed this information in a ceremony held to offer allotment letter of five acres of land for the Faisalabad Chamber of Commerce and Industry (FCCI) Complex in M3 Industrial Estate. He also said that FIEDMC was considering to retrieve the land from the present allottees and transfer it to those who would initiate construction immediately. These allottees will be compensated in the next phase of M3 Industrial Estate.
Read:
Development work on industrial estates in Quaidabad, Sargodha launched
Mian Kashif Ashfaq revealed that a business zone has been conceived in front of M3 – which will have a state of the art
expo centre
for regular exhibitions. He also highlighted in this industrial state a technical university and a commercial area will also be established in collaboration with Germany. A water treatment plant is also being installed to contain environmental pollution and fulfil a mandaorty condition of foreign investors.

title: Centre devices plan to avoid delays in development projects launched at provincial level
full_text:
Islamabad: The federal government has decided to avoid the unnecessary delays affecting
development projects
by transferring funds directly to the assigned account of the project director — with this initiative aimed at streamlining the said projects at the provincial level, according to a news source published on September 22.
Read:
Govt shares details of uplift schemes, development projects underway in South Punjab
Secretary Planning Development and Special Initiatives Mathar Niaz Rana revealed this information to the media after a meeting of the Senate Standing Committee on Planning, Development and Special Initiatives on Monday.
Mr Rana briefed the gathered press that the committee had made it clear to the provinces, especially Balochistan, to make an assignment account for the project director in which funds for federally-funded development projects could be transferred.
Read:
Sindh govt launches development projects to modernise Karachi’s infrastructure
He further added that it could take two to three months to procure funds under the currently-practised mechanism. Under the going procedure, the funds are first transferred to the official account no 1 of the province, then to the provincial secretary of finance, and then released to the project director — with the entire process deemed time-consuming and causes delays in development projects.

title: Directives issued to open Firdous Market Underpass for traffic
full_text:
Lahore: Lahore Development Authority (LDA) Director General Ahmed Aziz Tarar on Tuesday instructed Firdous Market Underpass Project Director Iqrar Hussain to open the under construction road project by on a partial basis by September 30, according to a news report.
The LDA DG issued the orders during a visit to the project site where he inspected the ongoing work at the structure of the underpass. Tarar also received briefing on the project’s development progress, which, according to Hussain, had achieved 90% completion status.
To help ease the traffic load on the alternate route for people heading to Gulberg, Kalma Chowk, Cavalry and Cantt., the DG asked the project director to operationalise the underpass for light traffic. Meanwhile, the contracting firm is all set to work on clearing the walkways and adjoining roads.
According to Hussain, special arrangements were made to remove the rain water accumulated around the underpass. For this purpose, 10 wells would be constructed to store the rain water while work was currently underway on the two of these facilities. In addition, another underground storage tank will be constructed in Qarshi Park to store 1.1 million gallons of rain water.

title: Diamer-Bhasha Dam: WAPDA starts hiring locals from Diamer, Gilgit-Baltistan
full_text:
Lahore: The Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA) has launched the process of recruiting locals from Diamer and Gilgit Baltistan (GB) in an effort to reduce poverty and uplift the socio-economic condition of the area; as the pace of the construction work on the Diamer-Bhasha Dam picks up, according to a news source published on September 21.
Read:
Construction work at Diamer-Bhasha Dam’s project site kicks off
The WAPDA advertised as many as 124 jobs ranging between Basic Pay Scale (BPS) 6-16 – for which only the
locals belonging to the Diamer District
and Gilgit Baltistan could apply. Previously, the authority had advertised 317 vacancies for security personnel and 179 vacancies of BPS between 14-20 – with the eligible candidates hailing from the same area be given preference.
Read:
WAPDA, GB Scouts sign MoU for Diamer Bhasha Dam project security
Moreover, PKR 78.5 billion is to be utilised for the resettlement and Confidence Building Measures (CBMs) for the socio-economic development in the area. Reportedly, 44 development schemes have been launched to enhance the region’s irrigation, water supply, health and educational infrastructure. Furthermore, the 3-megawatts (MW) Thak Hydropower Project is also near completion and would help meet the area’s power requirements.

title: CDA requests civil bodies to provide utilities in I-11
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has requested the Sui Northern Gas Pipeline Limited (SNGPL) and the Islamabad Electricity Supply Company (IESCO) to provide the necessary utilities for Sector I-11, according to a news report.
Read:
Govt housing authorities ordered to fulfill all CDA codal formalities
The higher-ups of these two organisations and the
CDA
held a meeting in this regard during which the civil body’s management asked them to provide these utilities on a priority basis. The representatives present in the meeting affirmed that this sector would get its utility connections within six months, as the due payments had already been fulfilled.
Read:
CDA signs MoU to automate property transfer, building plan approval system
As part of this project, the SNGPL would lay the pipeline and also establish door-to-door connections in Sectors I-11/1 and I-11/2. Last year, the Capital Development Authority -Development Working Party (CDA-DWP) had approved a PC-I and PC-IV worth PKR 2.7 billion for carrying out development work in Sector I-11. The next step was to deal with all the legalities and approvals involved for the actual development work.

title: Work on road projects underway to develop Kotli Sattian on par with Murree
developer: The funds approved in the Annual Development
full_text:
Rawalpindi: Rawalpindi Commissioner Captain (retired) Muhammad Mehmood on Friday (September 18) said that work on various road and infrastructure development projects was currently underway to make Kotli Sattian ‘a resort town like Murree’, a news source reported. He expressed his views on the matter during a visit to the project site.
Read:
Kotli Sattian declared tourist destination; sites to open this summer
At the moment, development work on constructing road network and other infrastructure for health, education is underway at Kotli Sattian. These projects are expected to make the area more accessible. According to reports, the Punjab government has allocated funds worth over PKR 951 million for Kotli Sattian during the fiscal year 2020-21. Some of these projects include:
Construction of 6 kilometre road linking Bostanabad with Panj Peer
Rehabilitation of the 21-kilometre long road linking Milad Chowk with Gulhara Gali
Construction of 5.75-kilometre long road linking Lower Topa with Patriata Bypass
Construction of an 8-kilometre long roa linking Sawar with Panj Peer
Expansion and rehabilitation of Chowk Pandori, Mator, Panjar, and Beor Road
Read:
Gas supply project for Murree, Kahuta, Kotli Sattian, Kallar Syedan approved
The funds approved in the Annual Development Programme (ADP) for the current fiscal year will be spent on a total of 45 uplift schemes. Availability of these facilities will make Kotli Sattian a new and popular tourist destination in Rawalpindi Division.

title: RDA to invite RRR project tenders; begin land acquisition process this month
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) has announced its decision to invite tenders for the development of the Rawalpindi Ring Road (RRR) project in the last week of September, according to a news report published on September 19. The authority will commence with the process to acquire land for the said project during the said period.
The Punjab Government has already issued funds for the acquisition of the 64-kilometre-long circular road project. As revealed in our previous report, the regional jurisdiction of the RDA had been expanded with the inclusion of 10,000 kanals of land around the Islamabad International Airport in its domain. This particular area was recently declared to be an aerotropolis and will feature several high-end developments; including 5-star hotels, a convention centre and several high-rise buildings and commercial plazas.
Read:
RDA approves to make mouzas falling in RRR economic zone part of city area
According to another news report shared on Sep 20, the ring road will also feature low-cost residential units – to be developed under the government’s Naya Pakistan Housing Programme (NPHP). For this purpose, around 6,500 acres of land will be allocated along the route. Last week, the RDA Governing Body also granted its approval for establishing its first housing project by the name of RDA City. The project’s location has not been revealed as of yet but circumstances suggest that it could also be located around the ring road.
Reportedly, the route will also feature developments giving Rawalpindi a modern facelift.
Read:
RRR to have 9 interchanges, NPHP units in surrounding areas
Prime Minister Imran Khan is expected to lay the foundation stone, marking the start of RRR project development, in December this year.

title: NESPAK among firms shortlisted for development of Lahore Master Plan 2050
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) on Saturday (September 21) announced that the authority had shortlisted three firms for the preparation of the city’s Master Plan 2050 — with the Singapore-based company Mine Heart, Lebanon-based firm Dar Al-Hindsa, and the National Engineering Services of Pakistan (NESPAK) having been selected for the purpose, a news source reported. The authority will make its final decision based on the respective technical and financial proposals submitted by the said companies.
Read:
Kasur, Nankana, Sheikhupura to be included in Lahore Master Plan
As per the LDA, the last date for the submission of the aforementioned proposals is October 19. Earlier in August, the authority had revealed that it had received seven applications in response to its Expressions of Interest (EOI) for the preparation of the Lahore Master Plan 2050. The companies that had expressed an interest in the bidding process included the Country Developers, Shahar Saaz Pvt Ltd, Pluto Planning, and Euro Consultant, along with the above-mentioned three firms.
Read:
Budzar orders completion of preparations regarding the development of Lahore Master Plan
According to sources, after the LDA’s jurisdiction was expanded to cover the entire Lahore Division via an amendment made in the LDA Act 1975 in 2013, the authority is now responsible for the city’s master planning, matters related to land use and its conversion, and for the issuance of approvals to private housing schemes located in the entire division i.e. Kasur, Nankana Sahib, Sheikhupura and Lahore.
Read:
Lahore Master Plan: PKR 750 mn drafting budget allocated
Reportedly, the authority is aiming to turn Lahore into a prosperous city through master planning. According to LDA Director General Ahmed Aziz Tarar, the new plan will be prepared for all urban and
rural areas
that are part of the Lahore Division. In addition, the master plan will include measures to protect the environment, ensure the efficient use of resources, preserve the city’s historical heritage, and promote economic activities by including all sections of the population.

title: Contract awarded for design, alignment of Rawat-Bhara Kahu Bypass, Islamabad
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Friday awarded the consultancy contract for the design, alignment and survey of the proposed southern Rawat-Bhara Kahu bypass, according to news sources.
Read:
Land audit of Islamabad’s housing schemes ordered to ascertain overselling incidents
Reportedly, an authority meeting held under CDA Chairman Amer Ali Ahmed approved the consultancy for the proposed southern Rawat-Bhara Kahu bypass — with the project to be executed by the military’s Engineer-in-Chief (E&C) Branch.
Under this contract worth PKR 10 million, the E&C branch of the
military
will be responsible for finalising the project’s alignment, design and survey over the next three months. Reportedly, the CDA gave the contract to the E&C due to its status as a government entity and its reputation for specialising in road works.
Read:
CDA, ITP & ICT directed to collaborate on fixing traffic issues in Islamabad
As per the proposed plan for the 30 to 40-kilometre-long and 600-feet wide southern bypass, the road is expected to start at Rawat, join with Murree Road near Bhara Kahu, before crossing the Defence Housing Authority (DHA), and the Nilor and Tumair locales of Zone IV and V. This project is anticipated to reduce the traffic load on several major roads in Islamabad.

title: Committee formed to oversee implementation of Karachi transformation plan
full_text:
Karachi: Sindh Chief Secretary Syed Mumtaz Ali Shah on Tuesday issued an announcement that states the formulation of a ten-member Provincial Coordination & Implementation Committee (PCIC) to oversee the implementation of the PKR 1.1 trillion special package for the city’s development, according to news sources.
Read:
PM’s Karachi Transformation Plan: Centre commits to funding 5 infrastructure projects
Reportedly, Sindh Chief Minister (CM) Syed Murad Ali Shah will be heading the committee which also has the provincial chief secretary as a member. Additionally, Sindh Planning & Development Department Board Chairman Muhammad Waseem will act as the committee’s secretary.
It was informed that the PCIC’s term of reference (TOR) includes the planning of the development projects to be implemented by the relevant provincial authorities. It will also serve as an impediment-resolving forum for coordination among the
stakeholders
involved in the implementation of the ‘Karachi transformation plan’. The committee would maintain records, ensure timely completions, make adjustments and take measures to ensure diligence and quality control for the initiative.
Read:
Govt to launch exclusive projects for industrial zones under Karachi package: President Alvi
Furthermore, the notification quoted the chief secretary as calling on all the relevant agencies and departments to immediately nominate their representatives for the PCIC, and directed the officials concerned to assist the committee as needed.

title: Ballot conducted to allot grey structures in NPHP’s Surizai Housing Scheme
developer: PKR 80 million has been allocated in the Annual Development
full_text:
Peshawar: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Chief Minister (CM) Mahmood Khan on Tuesday chaired a meeting of the Housing Department and was briefed on its overall progress; including that made towards the development of various housing schemes, according to news sources. He was informed that under the Naya Pakistan Housing Programme (NPHP), a ballot had been conducted to allot 8,000 grey structures in the Surizai Housing Scheme.
Read:
Jalozai Housing Scheme’s plot owners to get possession next year
Moreover, the meeting was informed that the civil work for the Surizai Housing Scheme will be launched within a month and will reach completion within a three-year timeframe. Regarding the recently initiated Hangu Township scheme, the chief minister was informed about the 7,500 applications received and that the project consultant has also been hired. The civil work for the
Hangu
Township Scheme has been slated to commence in January 2021.
Read:
NESPAK to consult on development of housing scheme in Surizai, Peshawar
As for the Khpal-Kor low-cost affordable housing schemes; the meeting was told that 714 plots were allotted between April 2018 and August. Moreover, it was reported that 85% of work on 144 high-rise flats of different categories have been completed – whereas PKR 80 million has been allocated in the Annual Development Programme (ADP) 2020-21 for the construction of various high-rises for the government employees in Phase-V of Hayatabad.
In response, the chief minister directed the authorities concerned to accelerate the housing initiative’s development to accommodate citizens and reduce the burden of population on major metropolises.

title: Work underway to solarise mosques in KP
full_text:
Peshawar: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister (CM) Mahmood Khan has directed the Energy and Power Department to ensure the timely completion of the ongoing solarisation work of provincial mosques and adopt ‘realistic criteria’ for their selection, according to a news source published on September 18.
Read:
Govt urged to bar mining at archaeological sites in KP
The CM made these remarks while presiding over a meeting held with the Pakhtunkhwa Energy Development Organisation to review the current progress of the project. Further, the provincial government has assured the authorities concerned that they would be provided with all the required resources for commencing with the
solarisation
of mosques.
Read:
50 MW solar power plants to be developed in KP, Sindh
Moreover, the meeting was informed that five solarized mosques – with a cost estimate of PKR 1,053.82 million – had already been constructed by the Pakhtunkhwa Energy Development Organisation; with these projects expected to save PKR 82 million in operational expenditures for the national treasury per annum.
Additionally, the session was told that over 6,500 homes, 300 mosques and non-Muslim places of worship had been solarised in different parts of the province under this scheme; with 6,000 more mosques being solarised at a total estimated cost of PKR 3,734 million. Overall, these projects would save PKR 348 annually for the national exchequer.

title: CDA all set to open Barma Bridge for traffic on Sunday
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Thursday announced its decision to open the Barma Bridge on Lehtaraar Road for commute on September 20, according to the civic agency’s official Facebook page.
Read:
CDA set to launch construction of Malal Bridge on Lehtarar Road
The construction of the Barma Bridge on Lehtaraar Road was initiated upon the directives of CDA Chairman Amer Ali Ahmed. The authority stated that it put ‘earnest efforts for completion of the construction of Barma Bridge’ to facilitate the locals ‘at the earliest’.
To ensure the timely completion of the project, technology-based real-time monitoring was established for the said project. Despite the coronavirus-induced lockdown as well as the recent record-breaking monsoon rain spells, CDA notified the project’s completion within the communicated timeframe.
Read:
CDA sends Sihala-Kohuta Road Flyover PC-1 to interior ministry for approval
Meanwhile, the CDA administration stated that it was currently working on:
Construction of
underpass at Faisal Avenue G-7/G-8
Bridge in Park Enclave-I
Construction of PWD underpass
Korang Bridge
Construction of Interchange on Rawal Dam Chowk
Development of stalled sectors I-11, I-12, I-15, E-12 and Park Enclave.

title: KP to offer home loan facility to deserving Peshawar Residencia allottees
payment_plan_text: nt’s decision to offer soft loans to the deserving Peshawar Residencia allottees for the payment of instalments or down-payment of their housing units, according to a news source published on September 17. | Read: | Govt urged to bar mining at archaeological sites in KP | Moreover, the Pakistan Housing Authority Foundation (PHAF) would provide all the required documents to facilitate these people in obtaining the soft loans. The minister said that KP is committed to giving shelter to the low-income strata at affordable rates. He said that the | housing department | is not a profit-earning enterprise and
full_text:
Peshawar: Minister for Housing Dr Amjad Ali, while chairing a meeting on the Peshawar Residencia Project (PRP) – under the Naya Pakistan Housing Scheme in Surizai – revealed the government’s decision to offer soft loans to the deserving Peshawar Residencia allottees for the payment of instalments or down-payment of their housing units, according to a news source published on September 17.
Read:
Govt urged to bar mining at archaeological sites in KP
Moreover, the Pakistan Housing Authority Foundation (PHAF) would provide all the required documents to facilitate these people in obtaining the soft loans. The minister said that KP is committed to giving shelter to the low-income strata at affordable rates. He said that the
housing department
is not a profit-earning enterprise and operates solely to help out the citizens in need. He assured that the PRP is a flagship project and would be completed at any cost.
Read:
Membership drive initiated for low-cost NPHP houses in PHA Residencia, Sorazai
Furthermore, Ali highlighted that the housing scheme offers the construction of grey structures at subsidised rates – which includes land and developmental charges. The meeting was informed that the PHAF was the PRP’s execution partner and is responsible for the land acquisition, construction of roads, boundary walls, main gate, and check posts.
Meanwhile, the provincial government would also construct a road from Zangali check post at an estimated cost of PKR 3.47 billion.

title: RDA approves establishing its first housing scheme RDA City
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Rawalpindi Development Authority’s (RDA) governing body on Wednesday approved its first housing scheme – titled ‘RDA City’ – and constituted a five-member technical committee to compile a report on its land acquisition and other project-related affairs within 15 days, according to news sources.
Read:
RDA offers 5,000 kanal-land to Chinese firm as payment for developing Leh Expressway
The new RDA housing scheme is to be designed on the patterns of Lahore’s LDA City and would span over 3,000 kanals. The governing body has also approved a short-term consultancy in a bid to prepare a feasibility study for highlighting a suitable location for the project.
Read:
RDA’s one-window centre being computerised to facilitate citizens, overseas Pakistanis
Moreover, the meeting also allowed the construction of buildings on the
RDA
-authorised commercial roads, as per the new building by-laws.
The said decisions were made in the 49th meeting of the authority’s governing body held under Chairman Tariq Mehmood Murtaza. The meeting agenda also included a plan to establish a direction for future development of the metropolis.

title: LDA holds Lahore Master Plan 2050 Consultant Selection Committee meeting
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) on Tuesday held a meeting of its Consultant Selection Committee to scrutinize the firms that had submitted their applications for developing the Lahore Master Plan 2050, according to a news source. LDA Director General Ahmed (DG) Aziz Tarar presided over the session.
Read:
Budzar orders completion of preparations regarding the development of Lahore Master Plan
As per the details shared, notable officials representing the Metropolitan Planning, City and Regional Planning, and Planning and Development Department attended the meeting. The meeting members reviewed the applications submitted by
seven firms
interested in working on the Lahore Master Plan 2050.
The master plan will give the road map for city’s infrastructure and civic needs for the next three decades. This blue print will focus on the development of urban as well rural areas of the provincial capital.
Read:
PM briefed on Lahore Master Plan 2040
According to the LDA DG, the civic agency intends to seek input of the civil society on various aspects of the master planning in a bid to preserve the city’s rich history, improve its
environment
, ensure efficient use of natural resources, and promote business activities.

title: Funds approved for rehabilitation of dilapidated road network in SITE, Karachi
full_text:
Karachi: Sindh Chief Minister (CM) Syed Murad Ali Shah on Monday approved the funds required for the rehabilitation of the dilapidated roads in the Sindh Industrial Trading Estate (SITE) Karachi, a news source reported.
Read:
Three road projects approved for Mansehra to promote tourism
The CM approved funds worth PKR 1. 37 billion for the reconstruction of roads in the SITE area during a meeting held with the SITE Association. The members of the association apprised the CM about the dilapidated condition of the roads in the area following the recent heavy rains in Karachi.
CM Shah further approved the transfer of property tax collection to SITE Limited. The authority is expected to use the locally generated funds for the development of the industrial estate. Stating that the provincial government would reconstruct all roads under the Karachi Mega Project, the CM has asked the industries department to prepare the PC-1 for the SITE roads project and submit it for approval from the Planning & Development Department.
Read:
Centre, Sindh govt to work on 6 priority areas for Karachi’s development
The CM additionally issued orders to assign the reconstruction work for the roads in SITE to the Karachi Mega Project team. He added that the development of the drainage system in the area should also be initiated under the said mega project.

title: PM to visit Gwadar next month with special package for southern Balochistan
full_text:
Quetta: Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan is set to visit Gwadar next month — and is expected to announce a special developmental package for southern Balochistan during the trip, according to a news source published on September 15.
Read:
Eighty-percent development work on Gwadar East Bay Expressway completed: CPEC Chairman
The PM had paid a visit to Quetta two days ago, where he was accompanied by Minister for Planning, Development, Reforms and Special Initiatives Asad Umar. While PM Khan had left after a short trip, the planning minister had stayed in the city in order to consult with the relevant stakeholders on the aforementioned package for southern Balochistan. As per the official sources, the said package is expected to be worth around PKR 150 billion and will encompass the newly merged tribal districts as well.
Additionally, Minister Umar and Minister for Defence Production Zubaida Jalal visited Turbat on Monday. On the occasion, the planning minster stated that the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) project would change the fate of not only Pakistan, but the entire Asian region. He added that once the
CPEC
initiative had been completed, it would bring peace and prosperity to Balochistan.
Read:
Over 80 CPEC projects anticipated to create 2.3 million jobs in Pakistan: Gwadar Pro Report
Regarding the Balochistan package, Minister Umar said that the present administration had been taking all the necessary measures to encourage development in the previously neglected province. He added that the government was also seeking to resolve the various issues faced by the people of Makran, and to provide them with the maximum employment opportunities.
Balochistan Chief Minister Jam Kamal Khan Alyani further revealed that the planning minister was visiting the Markran division in order to consult the authorities concerned regarding the special package being prepared for the province.

title: RDA offers 5,000 kanal-land to Chinese firm as payment for developing Leh Expressway
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) has offered 5,000 kanals of land to the Chinese Civil Engineering Construction Corporation (CCECC) as payment for developing the Leh Expressway, according to a news source published on September 16.
Read:
RDA’s one-window centre being computerised t
o
facilitate citizens, overseas Pakistanis
The Chinese construction firm has been made the offer to complete the
Leh
Expressway project on either build-operate-transfer (BOT) or public-private partnership (PPP) arrangement. If the firm accepts, the said land can be used for the establishment of residential or commercial structures.
Reportedly, the CCECC has asked the development authority to identify the offered land before making a final decision with regards to the acceptance of the offer.
Read:
RDA begins talks to award Rawalpindi Master Plan development contract
As per the sources, the RDA will identify the said land and a 10-member team of CCECC would then visit it to finalise their decision. Moreover, the firm has also expressed an interest to take up the project of constructing the circular railway and cementing the Leh Nullah channel in the twin cities.

title: CDA shares details on bids received for Kurang Road expansion
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has shared the details on the bids received for the planned expansion of the Kurang Road, according to a news report published today (September 16). This road stretches between Margalla Town Phases I and II – connecting the two.
Read:
CDA to start bids evaluation for Kurang Road expansion project in Margalla Town
Over 11 firms participated in the bidding process for Kurang Road, with an NIT of PKR 80.04 million. The lowest bid was PKR 48.04 million – 39% below the estimated cost – making it the winning bid.
Read:
CDA invites construction bids for South Blue Area’s service road
Moreover, the relevant authorities have been instructed to complete all legal formalities in this regard on a priority basis so that the project’s construction process can timely begin. The process would include widening the road, carrying out the electrical and mechanical work, and soft landscaping. In addition to this, the company would also be installing three culverts – all within a timeframe of six months.

title: CDA, ITP & ICT directed to collaborate on fixing traffic issues in Islamabad
full_text:
Islamabad: Islamabad Chief Commissioner Amer Ali Ahmed on Friday (September 11) directed the Capital Development Authority (CDA), the Islamabad Traffic Police (ITP), and the Islamabad Capital Territory Administration (ICTA) to work jointly to resolve the traffic concerns of the capital city, according to a news source.
The chief commissioner, who is also the CDA chairman, issued these orders while presiding over a meeting held at the CDA headquarters last week. Islamabad Police Inspector General Amir Zulfiqar Khan, Islamabad Deputy Commissioner Muhammad Hamza Shafqat and other senior officials representing the CDA, ICT and ITP were also present during the session.
Read:
CDA to install intelligent traffic-management system in Islamabad
On the occasion, the chief commissioner asked the CDA to upgrade the city’s traffic related infrastructure, including the marking of lanes and the installation of
smart traffic signals
, street signs, and street lights. In addition, the development authority was further asked to upgrade the service roads along major throughways like the Srinagar Highway and the Islamabad Highway on priority. The commissioner also told the officials concerned to conduct proper fencing work along the city’s major roads and to distinctly mark their entry and exit points.
Read:
International traffic rules to be implemented in Islamabad
In order to improve traffic flow during rush hours, the chief commissioner asked the CDA to conduct patch work on the roads that required rehabilitation. Ahmed additionally asked the ITP to chalk out a traffic plan for the Islamabad Highway in order to ensure that the ongoing construction work wouldn’t  cause commuters any trouble. He also issued directives to address issues with traffic congestion on Margalla Road.

title: RDA begins talks to award Rawalpindi Master Plan development contract
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) has initiated a round of talks with the management of Mott McDonalds to formally award the contract for the development of the Rawalpindi Master Plan 2020-40, a news source reported.
The said firm had won the contract for the development of the master plan during the prequalification round, for which the RDA had
invited
expressions of interest in April earlier this year. Reportedly, Mott McDonalds will begin working on the city’s master plan once
terms of reference
for the initiative have been finalized. The firm is then expected to submit a draft for the plan within one year of the contract being awarded.
Read:
Rawalpindi master plan redrafting to begin next month
As per the information available, the RDA has allocated funds worth PKR 600 million for the development of the master plan. In addition, the initiative is anticipated to determine the city’s future needs for the next 20 years — with all the government departments and civic agencies expected to initiate projects according to the recommendations shared in the master plan.
Read:
Master plan indispensable for business promotion: Rawalpindi DC
The city’s master plan is mainly expected to focus on the water and electricity supply infrastructure, sewerage system efficiency, construction of roads and related infrastructure including parking facilities, and development of new commercial and residential areas. Environmental protection measures will also be considered when formulating the plan.

title: RRUD: PM breaks ground for Pakistan’s second planned city in Lahore
full_text:
Lahore: Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan on Tuesday performed the ground-breaking ceremony of the Ravi Riverfront Urban Development (RRUD) Project; stating that it would be a ‘planned city’ featuring the latest provisions required by a modern metropolis, according to news sources.
Read:
DHA Lahore announces Overseas Enclave for expatriates
While addressing the inauguration ceremony at Kala Khatai – a small town on the outskirts of Lahore – the PM acceded that the project was ambitious in nature and its completion would be tricky. He said that ‘there will be many obstacles along the way but we must persevere’ and issued directions for the provincial government to execute the RRUD project with all the possible haste.
Khan, while highlighting the features of the RRUD project, said that six million trees would be planted in it. He said that the local and international investors have also evinced their interest in the mega-urban project.
Read:
PM invites overseas Pakistanis to invest in real estate projects in Lahore, Karachi
Moreover, the prime minister pointed out that over 40% of the city’s population was living in slums, being ignored for several years and facing issues like reduction in the provision of potable water as the city’s sewerage waste mixes with the river – increasing its arsenic content. Khan revealed that the government would develop the project’s basic infrastructure, while the ‘rest of the city would be raised from investments’.
Furthermore, the premier promised that there will also be affordable housing in the
new project
, alongside separate education, and Information and Technology (IT) centres. Reportedly, the RRUD project will be the second properly planned and the first ‘Green city’ of Pakistan – with high rises that would protect and preserve the environment.

title: China to use Artificial Intelligence technology for inspection of CPEC projects
full_text:
Islamabad: China has decided to use Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology for the inspection of infrastructure projects being developed under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) initiative, according to a news source published on September 15.
Read:
China, Pak sign project development agreement for Rashakai SEZ
Sources revealed that China would first use AI-powered robots for the inspection of the Matiari-Lahore Power Transmission & Transformation project. They added that as many as 20 robots would be utilized for this purpose. Reportedly, the State Grid Corporation of China (SGCC) already completed the testing of these robots last week.
According to the details available, traditional inspection techniques presented various problems like poor detection quality, high labour intensity, and low work efficiency. To overcome these issues, China decided to deploy AI technology for a comprehensive inspection of CPEC infrastructure projects.
Read:
Eighty-percent development work on Gwadar East Bay Expressway completed: CPEC Chairman
Official sources further revealed that the regular inspection of the Matiari-Lahore project would ensure that all its components were functioning normally. The project comprises of the first high-voltage direct current transmission line developed by China and Pakistan.

title: Murree-Kohala Road nears completion; inauguration expected by October end
payment_plan_text: d by the end of October, according to a news source published on Saturday (September 12). The final instalment of PKR 550 million required for project completion has also been issued. | Read: | Punjab govt approves five development projects | The Murree-Kohala Road project involved transforming the throughway into a signal-free, dual carriageway — with the venture holding strategic importance as it connects Islamabad with Muzaffarabad – Azad Jammu and Kashmir. Reportedly, the 18-kilometre road winds through the mountains to connect the two cities, and costed a total of PKR 1.32 billion to develop. | A
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Murree-Kohala Road is nearing completion — with the project expected to be inaugurated by the end of October, according to a news source published on Saturday (September 12). The final instalment of PKR 550 million required for project completion has also been issued.
Read:
Punjab govt approves five development projects
The Murree-Kohala Road project involved transforming the throughway into a signal-free, dual carriageway — with the venture holding strategic importance as it connects Islamabad with Muzaffarabad – Azad Jammu and Kashmir. Reportedly, the 18-kilometre road winds through the mountains to connect the two cities, and costed a total of PKR 1.32 billion to develop.
Additionally, modern European technology is being used for the construction of the roads in order to tackle the issue of land-sliding in the area during periods of heavy rainfall.
Read:
ECC approves development of Kohala, Azad Pattan hydropower projects
Moreover, the official date set for the completion of the project is October 30, with the venture expected to be inaugurated on the same date as well.

title: CDA to accommodate affectees of E-9, E-10, D-11, Chauntra village in H-16
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has decided to switch the land-usage arrangement of Sector H-16 from ‘institutional to residential’ in a bid to accommodate the affectees of Sectors E-9, E-10, D-11, and the Chauntra Village, according to a news report published on September 12.
Read:
CDA shares details on submitting online applications for Park Enclave III residential plots
The authority made this decision in a recently-held meeting that sanctioned the land-use change of Sector
H-16
, and forwarded the decision for the federal government’s approval – as it reserves the rights to modify the city’s masterplan.
Read:
CDA begins work to finalise alignment of south-eastern bypass linking Rawat with Bhara Kahu
At present, the Sector H-16 is meant for institutions with half of it as a buffer zone. Reportedly, in one of the sub-sectors, a public park would be developed, while a jail is being constructed in another subsector. The remaining two subsectors are where the aforementioned
affectees
will be accommodated.

title: Construction work at G-7/G-8 underpass, Park Enclave Bridge in final stages
full_text:
Islamabad: Capital Development Authority (CDA) Chairman Amer Ali Ahmed on Sunday revealed that the construction work at the G-7/G-8 underpass (on Faisal Avenue) and the Park Enclave Bridge was currently in its final stages, a news source reported.
Read:
Construction of 3 underpasses, 5 parking plazas approved for Rawalpindi
With regard to the construction of the G-7/G-8 underpass on Faisal Avenue, the CDA chairman said that only carpeting work remained underway. He added that the CDA intended to lay down the carpeting within a few days and inaugurate the project during the next 10 days. The Park Enclave Bridge and Burma Bridge were also near completion, he said.
CDA officials stated that the underpass project on Faisal Avenue faced delays due to recent rain spells in Islamabad. They added that apart from carpeting, all work was completed on the project. They explained that after completion, the underpass would allow traffic from the twin cities to move beneath its while that from G-7 and G-8 to cross using the top.
Read:
CDA shares updates on G-7 Underpass, Park Enclave & Burma Bridges
On the other hand, as a test case, CDA opened one lane on Friday for accessing Blue Area without the carpeting done yet.

title: Leh Expressway route extended to Srinagar Highway; project added to CPEC initiative
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The federal government on Friday announced its decision to extend the Leh Expressway route from the IJP Principal Road to the Srinagar Highway – and to include the project under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) initiative, a news source reported.
Read:
Leh Expressway to feature high-rise buildings for becoming ‘Rawalpindi’s new business hub’
Earlier, the Chinese Civil Engineer Construction Company (CCECC) had forwarded this recommendation for the route’s length to the authorities concerned. In a high-level meeting to discuss the project’s inclusion in CPEC, the federal executive accepted the proposal. Sources revealed that following the approval, the Capital Development Authority (CDA) would also become part of the mega project.
As per the details revealed, the Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) would construct the road from the Soan Bridge to the IJP Principal Road and the CDA would construct the section going towards the Srinagar Highway.
On the other hand, the government has also approved the addition of the New Islamabad International Airport 100-kilometre circular railway project to CPEC. According to sources, it has announced its decision to use the metro track as a circular train track. As per this decision, the authorities concerned would run 5-box trams instead of metro buses on the track.
Sources revealed that the metro bus administration would run its ‘red tram mono train’ on the track. Meanwhile, the public and private sector would run the ‘green mono tram train’ and ‘orange tram train’, respectively. They added that the government would construct an elevated circular train track from the Soan River Bridge to the Kutcheri Chowk, the Mall Road, and the Peshawar Road. The project would run on an electrical system, the sources said.
Read:
PM to soon receive briefing on Leh Expressway project, RRR launch this year: RDA Chairman
As per the details shared, the planned shift from the metro track to the circular train track would save the government significant sum of money in subsidy. Sources added that the saved money would help the metro bus administration, the government, and the private sector to run their tram services, respectively, instead of metro buses. Source:

title: Construction of 3 underpasses, 5 parking plazas approved for Rawalpindi
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The authority concerned has given its nod to the development of three underpasses and five parking plazas to address the city’s incumbent traffic issues, according to a news report shared in a national daily today (September 11). The planned underpasses are geared to make the busy roads of the metropolis ‘signal-free’ – and to ease up its heavy traffic situation.
Read
: Project consultant hired for parking plazas’ construction in Rawalpindi
According to Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) Chairman Tariq Murtaza, the development of these underpasses and parking plazas will help improve the city’s traffic system within a time frame of two to three years.
Additionally, the planned parking plazas will be developed under the private-public partnership (PPP) arrangement – in commercial areas and markets. The authority concerned will also construct an additional floor in the Fawara Chowk parking plaza to increase its parking capacity.
Read:
RDA to finalise TORs for awarding Rawalpindi Master Plan contract
As per the information shared by the news source, these plazas will be constructed in Kacheri Chowk, Bani Market, on City Saddar Road and Ghazni Road. Moreover, for the construction of these underpasses, the RDA has reportedly initiated the survey to determine the projects feasibility status. According to the RDA’s proposals, Murree Road’s entrance point, Mareer Chowk and Liaqat Bagh Chowk urgently need the development of underpasses to ease the traffic issue.

title: Funds allocated to fix faulty streetlights in Islamabad
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has allocated funds worth PKR 60 million for fixing faulty streetlights across the federal capital — a news source reported on September 11.
Read:
Govt urged to develop infrastructure in Islamabad markets
According to the details available, the city has a total of 40,000 streetlights on nearly 1,600 kilometres of the capital’s roads. However, of the total number of lights, over 17,000 are currently out of order — leaving large parts of the city in darkness at nightfall. These include the streetlights situated on major avenues, service roads, markets, parks and grounds.
As per the source, the streetlights have been slowly dying over the past decade, and the majority of non-functional lights are located within the city’s relatively older sectors, like G6, G-7, G-8, G-9, I-9 and I-10. Other major areas include parts of the Kashmir Highway from Peshawar Morr onwards, and roads leading to Pir Sohawa and Monal.
Read:
RMC to shift Rawalpindi’s streetlights to solar power
Out of the total funds allocated for the project, PKR 50 million have been allocated for the installation of requisite electrical equipment, while the remaining amount will be spent on the repairs of the streetlights. Additional funds for the project are also expected to be allocated soon.

title: PM invites overseas Pakistanis to invest in real estate projects in Lahore, Karachi
full_text:
Islamabad: Prime Minister (PM) Imran on Thursday invited overseas Pakistanis to invest in the country’s real estate projects; including the Ravi Riverfront Urban Development (RRUD) Project of Lahore and the Bundle Island Project of
Karachi
, according to news sources.
Read:
PM to officially launch Ravi Riverfront Urban Development Project on Sep 15
Khan made these remarks while chairing a meeting of the National Coordination Committee (NCC) on housing, construction and development. He said that the government will offer maximum facilities to investors contributing to the construction and real estate projects of the country.
Read:
PM appreciates growth in construction sector; orders early completion of Ravi Riverfront project
Regarding the RRUD Project of Lahore and Bundle Island Project of Karachi, the premier said that these mega infrastructural projects would prove to be the milestones in strengthening the country’s economy. He expressed contentment with the interest shown in the said projects by various builders, investors and construction firms.

title: Master plan in making to resolve potable water, sewerage issues in Multan
full_text:
Multan: Newly-appointed Commissioner Multan Javed Akhtar Mahmood has revealed that the city administration is developing a master plan to ensure the provision of potable water, proper sewerage infrastructure, and the repair and maintenance of road networks in the metropolis, according to a new source published on September 10.
Read:
Ballot date revealed for 2-marla commercial plots in DHA Multan
The commissioner said that the officials from the Planning and Development Department and Water and Sanitation Agency (WASA) have been directed to timely develop the master plan for the provincial government’s approval.
Reportedly, Mahmood has a deep-rooted association with the city and is at a grassroot-level with the issues faced by its residents. He assured of prioritising adequate resources to resolve these persistent civic issues hand-in-hand with the city’s administration.
Read:
Multan’s e-khidmat centre to be inaugurated on August 14
Moreover, he revealed that a team has been constituted to survey the city’s out-of-order water filtration plants and sewerage issues. Once the survey report is in, systematic steps will be taken to restore the water filtration plants in the first phase, he said and added that he intends to visit the
Walled City Project
– which is undergoing development work – and aims to preserve the centuries’ old heritage and culture.

title: RDA’s one-window centre being computerised to facilitate citizens, overseas Pakistanis
full_text:
Rawalpindi: Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) Chairman Tariq Mahmood Murtaza on Wednesday revealed that the authority’s one-window operation centre was being computerised to provide additional facilitation to citizens and overseas Pakistanis, according to news sources.
Read:
PM to soon receive briefing on Leh Expressway project, RRR launch this year: RDA Chairman
The chairman said that the government has issued directions for the authority to ‘leave no stone unturned’ when serving the city’s residents. He said that the initiative to computerise the one-window centre was launched a few months back and would soon start receiving online applications. The
one-widow cell
is aimed at timely expediting public issues.
Murtaza said that the authority is banning direct access to functionaries and shifting all applications to online channels. These measures are being taken to make the whole process more transparent.
Read:
RDA to develop a Miyawaki Urban Forest in Rawalpindi
Moreover, the chairman also revealed that the desilting of Nullah Leh was completed by the Water and Sanitation Agency (WASA) before the monsoon rain spells and lauded WASA for completing the work in PKR 30 million – which falls within the government-designated funds of PKR 40 million.
Meanwhile, it was also announced that a sewage treatment plant will be developed at Goraghpur, near the Adiala Jail on an area of 5,000 kanals.

title: Centre, Punjab finalise financial model for Ghazi Barotha project development
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The federal and Punjab governments have finalised the financial model for the development of the Ghazi Barotha project — with the total cost of the venture set to be divided equally among the centre and the provincial government, a news source reported on August 11. In this regard, the Punjab government has been directed to issue its share of the funds to the Capital Development Authority (CDA).
Read:
CDA to invite international tender for Ghazi Barotha initiative
The Ghazi Barotha project — which is expected to supply nearly 200 million gallons of water each day to the twin cities — is estimated to cost a total of PKR 80 billion. Water and Sanitation Agency (WASA) Managing Director Raja Shauqat Mahmood has stated that the project is being developed in order to resolve the various water issues facing Islamabad and Rawalpindi for the next hundred years.
Read:
Ghazi Barotha project’s consultant hiring process begins
Reportedly, out of the project’s total water supply, 100 million gallons per day will be provided to the Capital Development Authority, 50 million gallons per day will be provided to the Water and Sanitation Agency, and the remaining 50 million gallons will be provided to the cantonment board.

title: Rawalpindi Ring Road project development task handed over to LRRA
developer: This led to the Rawalpindi Development
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Rawalpindi Ring Road (RRR) project has once again been handed over to the Lahore Ring Road Authority (LRRA) — with the move having been approved by Punjab Chief Minister Sardar Usman Ahmed Buzdar, according to a news source published on Friday (Sep 11).
Earlier in March this year, the Punjab government had announced that the
LRRA
would be the authority in charge for the development of the RRR project. However, later in April, the LRRA was
prevented
from taking over the project, since amendments were underway in the authority’s regulations at the time. This led to the Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) becoming the executive agency for this project.
Read:
Proposals invited from private societies for construction of interchanges on RRR
Now, the project has once again been handed back to the LRRA. This essentially means that the authority will be in charge of arranging an open auction for the project’s development by inviting private investors to apply. Once the ring road’s development has been completed, the LRRA will earn a toll tax for the next 30 years, after which the project will be handed over to the RDA. As per the arrangements approved by the CM, the RDA will still be in charge of acquiring land for the project, and setting up and operating the economic zone planned along the road.
Read:
Funds approved for land acquisition of Rawalpindi Ring Road’s right-of-way
Earlier this week, RDA Chairman Tariq Mehmood Murtaza said that the provincial government had released funds worth PKR 52 million to begin the process for the acquisition of land for the RRR. As per the information shared in the press release issued by the development authority, the land acquisition process is expected to be initiated soon.

title: Low-cost hydel electricity production via Tarbela 4th ext crosses 10bn units
developer: This power generation has earned Water & Power Development
full_text:
Lahore: The Tarbela 4th Extension Hydel Power Station on Wednesday achieved another significant milestone in terms of its contribution of low-cost hydel electricity to the National Grid by crossing the 10-billion-unit generation mark, according to news sources.
Read:
Work on low-cost solar power project, other hydel projects underway in Punjab: Minister
This power generation has earned Water & Power Development Authority (WAPDA) a revenue of about PKR 75 billion. In addition, the low-cost hydel electricity project has also saved the national exchequer from spending PKR 100 billion – which would have been the cost for equal electricity generation produced through a thermal process.
Furthermore, it is also informed that the Tarbela 4th Extension Hydel Power Station has proven instrumental in meeting with the country’s electricity needs and promoting socio-economic development.
Read:
WAPDA’s electricity generation capacity via hydel power at its highest
The project is located on the Tunnel No 4 of the Tarbela Dam encompassing three generation units – with a capacity of producing 470 megawatts (MW) each. With the completion of the 4th extension, reportedly, the production capacity of the station has increased to 4,888 MW from 3,478 MW. Meanwhile, the it was also hailed as the flagship project of WAPDA by the
World Bank
(WB).

title: NA committee directs CDA to control unplanned constructions in capital
developer: Interior on Thursday directed the Capital Development
full_text:
Islamabad: The National Assembly (NA) Standing Committee on Interior on Thursday directed the Capital Development Authority (CDA) to control the unplanned constructions in Islamabad, a news source reported.
Read:
Repair work launched on Islamabad Expressway post-torrential rain
During the meeting, the committee took notice of the mess created in Islamabad due to increasing number of unplanned constructions. The committee members directed the CDA Board to take a decision on this matter soon or it would become difficult to manage the issues arising. Meanwhile, CDA Master Planning Director also briefed the meeting on a presentation regarding the revised Islamabad Master Plan.
Read:
PM for controlling Islamabad’s unplanned expansion
Last week, Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan also took notice of the unplanned expansion in Islamabad. In this regard, he ordered the CDA and the Islamabad Capital Territory Administration (ICTA) to control this expansion and transform the capital into a ‘model city’. He further directed both authorities to ensure the provision of clean drinking water, transport facilities, health centres, and educational institutions.

title: GDA prepares feasibility report for construction of 13 major roads under PPP mode
full_text:
Gujranwala: The Gujranwala Development Authority (GDA) has prepared a feasibility report for the construction of 13 major road links in all districts of the Gujranwala Division, according to a news report published on September 9. These roads are to be constructed under the private-public partnership (PPP) arrangement.
As per the details, the construction cost of these roads are estimated at PKR 49.79 billion and would be developed in Sialkot, Narowal, Gujranwala, Gujrat, Hafizabad, and Mandi Bahuddin.
Read:
Gujranwala city to be linked with motorway: Buzdar
Following are the details on these road projects and the estimated funds required for their development:
Dualisation of Gujranwala-Hafizabad Road at an estimated cost of PKR 18.14 billion
Dualisation of Fareed Town Road, Pasroor Road, and Sialkot Road linking Lahore-Sialkot Motorway (M11) at an estimated cost of PKR 1.76 billion
Construction of road linking Awan Chowk Bypass and Khanqah Dogran with Lahore-Islamabad Motorway (M2) at an estimated cost of PKR 3.88 billion
Construction of a 16 kilometre-long dual carriageway linking Aimanabad Road with M11 at an estimated cost of PKR 3.9 billion
Construction of the road link between Alipur Chowk and Alipur Chatha at an estimated cost of PKR 2.15 billion
Expansion and rehabilitation of Kharian-Dinga Road in Gujrat at an estimated cost of PKR 2.5 billion
Construction of the road linking Mandi Bahuddin with Head Jago at an estimated cost of PKR 3.92 billion
Construction of the road connecting Kot Hara with Pindi Bhattiyan at an estimated cost of PKR 5 billion
Construction of road linking Wazirabad with Sialkot Road at an estimated cost of PKR 1.8 billion
Dualisation of the road connecting Sialkot with Pasroor at an estimated cost of PKR 1.63 billion
Rehabilitation of Muridke-Narowal road at an estimated cost of PKR 6.42 billion
Construction and rehabilitation of road linking Shakargarh with Narowal at an estimated cost of PKR 5 billion

title: PM to soon receive briefing on Leh Expressway project, RRR launch this year: RDA Chairman
full_text:
Rawalpindi: Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) Chairman Tariq Mahmood Murtaza on Wednesday revealed that both the Leh Expressway project and the Rawalpindi Ring Road (RRR) launch were scheduled to be held during the ongoing year, according to news sources.
Read:
Punjab approves Rawalpindi Ring Road project development under PPP mode
He further added that Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan would receive a presentation on the Nullah Leh Expressway project within a few days for making decisions regarding the project’s final developmental model.
The chairman revealed that all the planning and development of the RRR project is complete, and the launching ceremony will be performed by either PM Khan or CM Buzdar in November or December of this year. He said that the Punjab government has released PKR 6.5 billion to RDA for the RRR’s land acquisition.
Read:
Leh Expressway to feature high-rise buildings for becoming ‘Rawalpindi’s new business hub’
Moreover, the authority’s chairman also informed that special industrial, medical, recreational, educational, residential and aerotropolis zones would be established alongside the RRR project to decongest the city. Regarding the
Leh Expressway
, Murtaza expressed hope that the project will resolve the city’s traffic woes.

title: CDA launches repair work on Islamabad Expressway post-torrential rain
full_text:
Islamabad: In the wake of recent monsoon rain spells, the Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Tuesday launched repair work on the Islamabad Expressway, a news source reported. The authority’s administration directed the MPO Directorate to carry out the repair, maintenance, and patch work on the road.
Read:
CDA mulls leasing petrol-pump sites on Islamabad Expressway, Kashmir Highway
According to the details shared, the Islamabad Expressway is one of the major arteries in the city – a sole way for the residents of various housing schemes to reach the main city. Sources added that the section of the expressway from Gulberg Interchange to GT Road at Rawat was in poor condition and caused troubles for daily commuters.
In this regard, the CDA administration instructed the MPO Directorate to start the repair and maintenance work on the expressway as well other roads in the city. So far, the directorate has carried out work on the Islamabad Expressway, the Kashmir Highway, the Faizabad Interchange, the IJP Road from Golra Mor to Saidpur Road, 9
th
Avenue Junction with IJP Road, Nazim-ud-Din Road Sector F-8, Service Road Sector I-10, Ibn-e-Sina Road Sector G-11, Constitution Avenue, and more areas.
Read:
PC-1 for construction of PWD Underpass, Korang Bridge on Islamabad Expressway approved
The administration has also directed other CDA formations to facilitate MPO Directorate to prevent any delays in work. Additionally, it has instructed the Finance Wing to ensure the availability of all funds required.

title: PM’s Karachi Transformation Plan: Centre commits to funding 5 infrastructure projects
developer: In this regard, the Ministry of Planning, Development
full_text:
Karachi: The federal government on Tuesday pledged to provide funds for the development of five mega projects under the ‘PM’s Karachi Transformation Plan’ recently announced for the city, a news source reported. In this regard, the Ministry of Planning, Development, & Special Initiatives shared the details of the plan devised for the development of Karachi’s infrastructure.
Read:
Sindh appoints new Karachi administrator, deputy administrators for 6 districts
Under the PM’s Karachi Transformation Plan, the federal government has committed to providing finances for the following initiatives:
Karachi Circular Railway (KCR)
Greater Karachi Water Supply Project (K-IV)
Greenline BRT
Railway Freight Corridor
Rehabilitation of rivers,
nullahs
, and storm water drains, along with resettlement of affected people
As per the detailed revealed, the total cost of these projects amounts to PKR 736 billion out of which the centre has committed to providing an estimated PKR 611 billion. Meanwhile, the provincial government is expected to provide PKR 375 billion.
In a related development, the federal government has announced its decision to request the Supreme Court (SC) to allow the partial utilisation of the Bahria Town Settlement Fund.
Due to railways being a federal subject, along with SC’s directions on the project, the federal government is now duty-bound to execute the KCR project. Therefore, the centre will have the responsibility of bearing the financial cost of this initiative.
Read:
Centre, Sindh to solve Karachi’s problems with PM’s PKR 1.1 trillion relief package
Sources said that the centre sought to work together with the Sindh government for the development of Karachi. They added that the details of federal and provincial responsibilities were shared to remove ambiguities.
Minister for Planning & Development Asad Umar has directed the officials concerned to prepare time-bound action plans for the implementation of their respective projects. He also instructed them to seek approvals or NOCs from the provincial government where required.

title: CM directs LDA to repair broken roads, footpaths in Lahore
developer: Sardar Usman Buzdar has directed the Lahore Development
full_text:
Lahore: Chief Minister (CM) Sardar Usman Buzdar has directed the Lahore Development Authority (LDA) to initiate work to repair the city’s roads and footpaths, and to ensure the beautification of the provincial capital — a news source reported. The project is expected to be completed within a period of two months.
Read:
LDA approves Defence Road rehabilitation project
According to the details available, the CM assigned four major tasks to the LDA. These included the repair and patchwork of roads, repair of footpaths (including the task of changing curb stones where required), lane marking on the roads, and the beautification of underpasses.
The work on these tasks is expected to begin later this month — with all the projects estimated to be completed within two months. The CM has also issued instructions to the officials concerned to submit a comprehensive report once all the tasks have been completed.
Read:
LDA shares details on measures taken to facilitate private developers, housing schemes
In order to comply with the CM’s directives, the Lahore Metropolitan Corporation has already prepared a list of major roads and avenues that require repair and beautification.

title: CDA’s PC-1 for operations, management of Metro Bus Service gets a nod
developer: The Ministry of Interior Departmental Development
full_text:
Islamabad: The Ministry of Interior Departmental Development Working Party (DDWP) on Monday approved the PC-I prepared by the Capital Development Authority (CDA) for the management, operations and maintenance of the Metro Bus Service, according to a news source published today (September 8).
Read:
CDA gains financial stability; starts returning loan to govt
The Metro Bus Service will cover a route stretching from the Islamabad International Airport (IIA) and the Peshawar Mor. Under the PKR 1.9 billion-worth PC-I, the CDA will
procure 30 buses
and will supervise their operations. As per sources, the matter of the ‘funding arrangements’ for the services is decidedly referred to the federal cabinet.
Read:
PM orders CDA, ICTA to control Islamabad’s unplanned expansion
Moreover, the meeting was informed that the 25.6 kilometre-long metro track – being currently developed by the National Highways Authority (NHA) – is near completion. The project is worth PKR 16 billion and will soon be transferred to the CDA. Meanwhile, the development authority is exploring options to ensure swift initiation of the bus service operations.

title: PDA ordered to fix civic issues in Regi Model Town, Hayatabad
developer: Taimur Khan Jhagra on Monday directed the Peshawar Development
full_text:
Peshawar: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Minister for Health and Finance Taimur Khan Jhagra on Monday directed the Peshawar Development Authority (PDA) to immediately address and fix the civic issues faced by the residents of Regi Model Town and Hayatabad, a news source reported. The minister issued these orders while presiding over a meeting held at the PDA office.
Read:
PHC halts NOC issuance for new housing projects in Peshawar
As per reports, the meeting was attended by senior officials representing the PDA, among others from related departments, and residents of the two societies. The meeting was told that the residents of Hayatabad demanded for the development of a community centre in each of the society’s phases and also demanded establishing of more Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) terminals.
Addressing the meeting members, Jhagra asked the departments concerned to find an alternative route for heavy traffic passing through Hayatabad and issued directives to solve the sewerage system problems in the Regi Model Town area.
Read:
PDA directorate gets hold of land to develop Regi Model Town sports complex
Furthermore, the minister also took notice of the inactive water filtration plants in Hayatabad and asked the officials concerned to fix the existing plants and install additional ones to allow uninterrupted supply of potable water to the residents.

title: Section 4 imposition ordered to acquire land for Gujrat’s Samman-Dinga Road project
full_text:
Gujrat: City Deputy Commissioner (DC) Saif Anwar Jappa on Monday direct the assistant commissioner (AC) to immediately impose ‘Section 4’ of the Land Acquisition Act in order to expedite the land acquisition process for the dualisation of the Samman-Dinga Road, a news source reported. Jappa issued the directives while chairing a meeting.
Read:
Funds required for completion of Shahbazpur Bridge linking Gujrat, Sialkot
As per reports, the project is estimated to cost around PKR 7.7 billion, out of which the federal government has allocated PKR 1 billion in the ongoing fiscal year – out of this however, PKR 500 million will be spent on the required land’s acquisition. As per the estimates, over 750 kanal of land will be acquired for the dualisation of the said road.
Additionally, the deputy commissioner also directed the project’s executing authority to procure the required no objection certificates (NOCs) from the Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA), National Highways Authority (NHA), Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Ltd (SNGPL) and other departments to remove their installations along the route, so as to timely initiate the development work.
Read:
Flyover proposed over Gujrat railway track
The road-dualisation project also includes construction of a flyover from River Chenab to the entrance of Gujrat and another at the Upper Jhelum Canal.

title: Blue World City invites Turkish businessmen for investment
developer: Nazir, Project Director Arshad Awan and Business Development
full_text:
Islamabad: The Blue World City management has completed its scheduled meetings in Istanbul and has moved on to Tavşanlı, a town and district of the Kütahya Province — with the delegation geared to meet with the representatives of the Tavşanlı Chamber of Commerce and Industry on this location and invite the Turkish business community to invest in the project, according to a new source published on September 6.
Read:
Blue World City set for official launch
The Blue World City (BWC) delegation included Senior Manager Saad Nazir, Project Director Arshad Awan and Business Development Consultant Kamal Asaaf. During their meeting with Chamber President Davut Efe and Foreign Relations Manager Hasan Hüseyin Çakmak, the management revealed that they intended to complete their residential project by 2022.
Read:
Blue World Group launches low-cost Awami Residential Complexes in Lahore, Rawalpindi
Saad Nazir addressed the Turkish companies and investors on the occasion, and advocated that the BWC was a ‘serious and big investment’ and pledged that a  large chunk of land had also been reserved exclusively for interested Turkish brands.
Previously, the residential scheme had made the headlines by signing
Engin Altan Düzyatan
— the actor who portrays historic hero Ertuğrul Gazi in the televised series “Diriliş Ertuğrul” — as the project’s official brand ambassador.

title: Citi Housing Multan completes development work in Phase I, invites members to receive plot possession
full_text:
Multan: The administration of the Citi Housing Multan Phase-I recently announced the completion of the society’s development work — with the management further having requested the individuals concerned to receive possession of their allotted plots and get them registered, according to a news source published on September 6.
Read:
Citi Housing Multan project officially launched, booking process initiated
The project administration has further notified the developers and members that construction on these plots can now be launched. The
management
additionally disclosed that it had also established a design wing for their esteemed members, which could be utilized in order to obtain layout plans for their respective constructions without incurring any extra costs.
Read:
Citi Housing launches ‘Exclusive Overseas Eiffel Tower Block’
Citi Housing is a successful residential scheme, with projects in Multan,
Gujranwala
, Sialkot, Jhelum, and Faisalabad. Their latest Multan project had officially been launched in June, and is located on Bosan Road in Lutfabad — with the venture having already been approved by the Multan Development Authority (MDA). For more information or details, interested parties can contact (061)111-555-551 or visit the website: https://www.citihousing.pk/

title: Funds approved to lay gas-supply infrastructure in Park Enclave-I
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) administration has approved PKR 96 million for the installation of gas-supply infrastructure in Park Enclave-I, according to a news source published on September 7.
Read:
CDA shares ballot date for Park Enclave Phase III residential plots
The said amount is expected to be paid to the Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited (SNGPL) in a few days — with the process to
install the gas-supply infrastructure
expected to be launched in Park Enclave-I soon after. Under this project, the gas company will install an external gas connection network and also provide a door-to-door internal gas conduction network.
Previously, the SNGPL had issued a demand notice worth PKR 243.397 million for the gas provided to the aforementioned residential scheme. However, upon the CDA’s insistence, the gas supply company later decided to issue a revised and reduced cost notice to Park Enclave-I.
Read:
CDA shares updates on G-7 Underpass, Park Enclave & Burma Bridges
The project’s development is almost near completion and it is a result of the CDA’s commitment to transform
Park Enclave-I
into a “model, modern, dynamic and futuristic housing project in Islamabad”.
Meanwhile, the CDA has also invited applications for plot allotments in Park Enclave–III to be submitted before September 17.

title: DHA Lahore reveals its ‘new offer’; shares important details
payment_plan_text: ails regarding its new offer pertaining to the sale of residential and commercial plots on a 3-year payment plan — with a DHA Lahore open ballot to be held on October 26 for this purpose, according to the authority’s official Facebook page. | Read: | DHA Lahore initiates development work in Sector-IV, Phase-XI (Rahbar) | This recent announcement follows the authority’s previous teasers regarding the aforementioned offer — with its decision being in line with Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan’s policy for the housing sector. | Interested parties have been invited to apply for the open ballot between Septe
full_text:
