Lahore: The Defence Housing Authority (DHA) Lahore on Sunday (September 6) unveiled the details regarding its new offer pertaining to the sale of residential and commercial plots on a 3-year payment plan — with a DHA Lahore open ballot to be held on October 26 for this purpose, according to the authority’s official Facebook page.
Read:
DHA Lahore initiates development work in Sector-IV, Phase-XI (Rahbar)
This recent announcement follows the authority’s previous teasers regarding the aforementioned offer — with its decision being in line with Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan’s policy for the housing sector.
Interested parties have been invited to apply for the open ballot between September 16 and October 5. The sizes of residential plots on offer are 2-kanal, 1-kanal, 10-marla, 7-marla and 5-marla. Similarly, the commercial plots on offer are 80-marla, 40-marla, 16-marla, 8-marla, 4-marla and 2-marla in size.
Read:
DHA Bahawalpur to sign MOU with 3 companies for provision of project facilities
Moreover, DHA Lahore has also announced a relaxation in the bylaws for commercial construction on these plots. The developers will be able to enjoy the following special incentives:
Height
relaxation
Additional Parking Space
Improved floor area ratio (FAR)
Priority on DHA procedures and processes
4-5% rebate on lump-sum payment
No drawing submission fee
Furthermore, DHA Lahore has announced new commercial areas, entertainment facilities and educational institutes in order to offer better amenities for its residents. Reportedly, the details of phases, sizes, prices, registration fee and instalment fee will be posted on DHA’s official website (www.dhalahore.org) by September 16.
The residential scheme had previously launched developed plots in established phases in February 2016 and October 2019 as well — with the authority receiving a great public response at the time.

title: PM orders CDA, ICTA to control Islamabad’s unplanned expansion
developer: Imran Khan on Thursday ordered the Capital Development
full_text:
Islamabad: Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan on Thursday ordered the Capital Development Authority (CDA) and the Islamabad Capital Territory Administration (ICTA) to control the city’s unplanned expansion, a news source reported. He further directed the authorities to transform Islamabad into a ‘model city’ with the provision of all basic amenities.
Read:
Punjab Highway Patrol to launch One-District-One-Road project in Rawalpindi
The PM ordered CDA and ICTA to provide facilities like clean drinking water, transport for locals as well as residents of adjoining areas, health centres, and educational institutions. Chairing a meeting on development projects in the city, PM Khan said that Islamabad’s population had experienced a significant increase over past two decades and that there was a need to control the city’s unplanned expansion.
He further directed the civic agency to resolve matters arising from the urban sprawl in the capital city. He highlighted that the protection of green areas was a priority for the government. He further asked the officials concerned to ensure the removal of encroachments from the city.
Read:
ICT Administration issues flood advisory for Islamabad
The PM also reviewed the progress of work on the Metro Bus Service extension project from Peshawar Mor to Islamabad International Airport (IIA). The meeting provided its approval to the establishment of a Mass Transit Authority (MTA) to oversee the matters concerned with the project. PM Khan further ordered to accelerate the work on Ghazi Barotha project to overcome water shortage in Islamabad.

title: Authorities urged to complete KCR Phase-III soon
full_text:
Islamabad: Minister for Planning, Development, Reforms and Special Initiatives Asad Umar on Thursday has urged all the concerned authorities to take all possible steps to ensure fast-track completion of the Karachi Circular Railway (KCR) Phase-III, according to news sources.
Read:
KCR gets PKR 10.5bn for rehabilitation on like of ML-1 project
The minister gave instructions in this regard while chairing a KCR project review meeting. Minister Umar directed Pakistan Railways (PR) to formulate a public-private partnership for KCR Phase-III. The meeting decided that legalities will soon be completed to initiate the development work on KCR Phase-III within the current financial year (FY) 2020-21.
To this effect, the Public-Private Partnership Authority (PPPA) is asked to offer the necessary cooperation and assistance to the Railway Ministry.
Read:
Repair work on KCR stations, tracks and gates begin
Moreover, the meeting was informed that the KCR construction will be completed within three years, by the middle of 2023. It was also revealed that the Ministry of Railways has kept Sindh government in constant loop and
development work
on underpasses at several locations is expected to start soon.

title: Islamabad Ring Road project to start in 2021-Q1
developer: Federal Minister for Planning and Development
full_text:
Islamabad: The Islamabad Ring Road project development is expected to begin during the first quarter of 2021, a news source reported on Friday (Sep 4). Without quoting its source, the report further states that the official approval in this regard has already been sanctioned.
The story additionally claims that Federal Minister for Planning and Development Asad Umar has agreed to allocate development funds for the ring road project under the federal Annual Development Programme for the current fiscal year.
Read:
PKR 50bn allocated for Islamabad Ring Road in FY 2020-21: Minister Sarwar
The Islamabad Ring Road project was proposed last year when the related developments for the Rawalpindi Ring Road initiative were being completed. While both the ring roads are meant to provide an alternate traffic route for the twin cities of Islamabad and Rawalpindi, the executive agency for overseeing the Islamabad Ring Road project development has yet to be finalised.
This particular ring road highway stretch will be more than 50 kilometers in length with its starting point set at Sangjani; the point where the Rawalpindi Ring Road also terminates. After looping in Islamabad along the Margalla Avenue and heading all the way to the Express Highway, the road will end at the starting point of Rawalpindi Ring Road at the site of the Radio Pakistan Building in Rawat (on GT Road) – and is set to be developed on the pattern followed by the motorways.
Read:
Funds approved for land acquisition of Rawalpindi Ring Road’s right-of-way
The news source further stated that the ground breaking for the Rawalpindi Ring Road project is expected to be performed in November this year; while that for the Islamabad Ring Road would be held in March 2021.
Both these projects will be developed by bringing private partners on board, who will be allowed to operate toll plazas on the two roads for a certain period of time in exchange for their services.

title: Consultant for NPHP project in Sorazai-Peshawar finalised
developer: Department had sought approval from Planning and Development
full_text:
Peshawar: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Minister for Housing Dr Amjad Ali was briefed on Thursday (Sept 3) that the consultant for the development of the Naya Pakistan Housing Project (NPHP) in Sarozai, Peshawar had been finalised, a news source reported. This information was shared during the monthly review meeting held to discuss various projects overseen under the KP Housing Department.
Presiding over the session, Dr Ali directed the officials concerned to complete the development work of high rise apartments for government employees in Hayatabad Phase 5 within the stipulated time frame. He further ordered for the ground breaking ceremony of flat units in the Civil Quarters to be held within three weeks.
Read:
KP CM orders early start to CPEC City Nowshera’s development work
The minister was informed that construction work was in full swing at the Jalozai Housing Scheme project site – and that it would be completed by year end. The project would see to the addition of 2,500 kanals of land in its third phase, said the briefing officer.
The meeting was further intimated that for the construction of the NPHP Housing Scheme-Saruzaimain’s main entrance, boundary wall and check posts, the Housing Department had sought approval from Planning and Development Working Party.
Read:
Jalozai Housing Scheme’s plot owners to get possession next year
Commenting on the latest update received on the establishment of Satellite Towns in Swat, Khyber District, Bajaur, and Waziristan, the minister directed the authorities concerned to complete the land identification process and feasibility studies for these projects. In response, Dr Ali was informed that the department had identified land for developing the said initiatives in Peshawar, Swat, Kohat, Abbottabad, Kohat, Mardan, Lakki Marwat, D.I Khan, Malakand, Tank, and Khyber District.

title: PM to officially launch Ravi Riverfront Urban Development Project on Sep 15
full_text:
Lahore: Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan, during a visit to Lahore on Tuesday, received a progress briefing on the
Ravi
Riverfront Urban Development (RRUD) Project — with the premier, later, deciding to officially launch the venture on September 15, according to news sources.
Read:
Punjab to set up shelter homes in rented buildings in Lahore
This proposed launch event will follow the previous soft launch that had been performed by PM Khan on August 7.
During a meeting held on his visit to Lahore, the PM directed Chief Minister Sardar Usman Buzdar to supervise the RRUD project on a daily basis and to ‘keep him in the loop’. He also directed the officials concerned to ensure that international standards were maintained in both the project’s construction, and the measures taken to protect the environment. He further stressed that this venture would not only help recharge Lahore’s aquifer and ensure drinkable water supply; but also provide a boost to the country’s construction sector.
Read:
RUDA invites EOI for Ravi River Development City design, development
In addition, the premier maintained that the project had already caught the attention of many local and foreign investors.

title: KP Culture & Tourism Authority invites bids for leasing camping pods sites
full_text:
Peshawar: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Culture & Tourism Authority (KP-C&TA) has invited bids for the lease and operationalization of nine government camping pod sites for a duration of 10 years — with the initiative falling under the auspices of the ‘The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Govt Rest Houses and Tourism Properties (Development, Management and Regularization) Act 2020’, according to a post published on the authority’s official Facebook page on September 2.
Read:
300 vacancies approved for KP Tourism Police force
These camping pods are being leased out on an ‘AS IS WHERE IS’ basis to various reputed firms and private corporations that wish to operate and make these camping pods available to the general public — under the conditions highlighted in the bidding documents.
Reportedly, the eligible firms are required to be registered on the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR)’s Active Taxpayers List, and to be in possession of a Security Exchange Commission Pakistan (SECP) certification where applicable. The bidding for the government camping pods is expected to be conducted through the Single Stage-Two Envelope procedure.
Read:
KP tourism body reviews proposal for setting up Kalam Development Authority
Additionally, interested firms have been requested to submit complete bidding documents to the
KP
-C&TA Director General’s office before 02:30 pm on September 24. The authority’s subcommittee shall open the technical bids on the same day, in the presence of bidders that choose to attend the proceedings at 3 pm in the Tourism Department’s Conference Hall.
The bidding documents can be obtained through the director general’s office, or from the following websites till September 24 (for a non-refundable fee of PKR 5,000): www.kptourism.com and www.kpra.gov.pk

title: CDA begins work to finalise alignment of south-eastern bypass linking Rawat with Bhara Kahu
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has initiated work to finalise the alignment of the proposed south-eastern bypass between Bhara Kahu and
Rawat
, according to a news story published on September 3.
For this particular project, the military’s Engineer-in-Chief branch is cooperating with the CDA to finalise the design and alignment of the bypass.
Read:
CDA announces dates for 2nd auction of commercial plots
As per the details available, the CDA was given a presentation by the military’s Engineer-in-Chief branch on Monday to propose the final alignment of the road. The CDA official termed this meeting an initial presentation — with the finer details of the project yet to be determined.
Read:
CDA to announce pending ‘Built-Up Property’ award for 7 sectors
The 40-kilometre-long and 600 ft wide bypass road is expected to start at Rawat, and will be linked to the Murree Road near Bhara Kahu. It will also cross through the Defense Housing Authority (DHA)’s developments in Nilor and Tumair.
Once the south-eastern bypass project has been completed, it is expected to significantly alleviate the traffic burden on the Murree Road, Kashmir Highway and other thoroughfares in the area. The Zone-IV and V — the location for numerous housing projects of the city — will also use the road in order to reduce congestion on the capital city’s roads.

title: CDA announces dates for 2nd auction of commercial plots
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) administration has made arrangements to hold another auction of commercial plots located in various developed sectors of the city from September 21 to 23 — with the initiative falling in line with the government’s policy to promote the country’s construction sector, according to a news source published on September 2.
Read:
CDA to announce pending ‘Built-Up Property’ award for 7 sectors
This second auction of commercial plots by the CDA is expected to be held within three months of the first successful auction. Previously, 12 commercial plots worth PKR 17.4 billion were auctioned off in the city’s
New Blue Area
— with the final sum collected beyond the authority’s original estimations.
The proposed auctions are aimed at further cementing the investors’ confidence in the investment-friendly policies recently introduced by the CDA and the federal government.
Read:
CDA invites construction bids for South Blue Area’s service road
The auction is expected to encompass plots from the New Blue Area, the Diplomatic Enclave, F-10 Markaz, G-10 Markaz, I-8 Markaz, Industrial Triangle Kahuta, and various Class-III shopping centres in Sectors G-9/1, G-9/2, G-10/3, G-11/4 and I-11/4. The types of plots presented at the planned auction will be suitable for setting up industrial units, agricultural farms, apartment structures, and shopping malls.
The
CDA
has also formed a committee — headed by Member Finance — to preside over the auction proceedings. In addition, the brochures for the said auction are available at the One Window Operation Directorate and designated branches of various banks.

Multan: The Defence Housing Authority (DHA) Multan management recently announced September 4 as the deadline for the submission of applications for 2-marla commercial plots in sectors M, Q, R, U and H — according to a post published on the society’s official Facebook page on September 2.
Read:
DHA Lahore initiates development work in Sector-IV, Phase-XI (Rahbar)
The deadline for submission of application forms for commercial plots is set to expire in the coming two days. Moreover, the management has issued the following payment structure for the purchase of 2-marla commercial plots in sectors M, Q, R, U and H:

Possession announced for Sector Q – DHA Multan

application forms
could be downloaded online, from the housing society’s website: www.dhamultan.org. In addition, payments can be made through a bank transfer or debit/credit card.

title: CDA invites construction bids for South Blue Area’s service road
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has invited sealed bids for the construction of South Blue Area’s service road (from 9th Avenue to F-10 roundabout), according to a news report published on August 29.
Read:
New Blue Area’s bids for 12 commercial plots approved
Only firms licensed by the Pakistan Engineering Council (PEC), having valid registration certificate in Category C-3, and above with specialisation project codes CE-01 & CE-02, can send in their bids. The forms can be obtained with a PKR 5,000 fee from the office of Deputy Director Roads-II, located at the Old Naval Headquarter, Sector G-6 of the capital by September 15.
Moreover, the bids will be received until 11:30 AM on September 16 and will be opened at 12-noon. The NIT cost of the project has been estimated at PKR 243,912,368, while the earnest money amount has been fixed at PKR 4,878,000.
Read:
CDA sets up dedicated desk for New Blue Area plot owners
Furthermore, the earnest money will have to be deposited in favour of Deputy Director Roads-II from a local scheduled bank of Pakistan and must be attached with the application. If no call deposit is submitted with the bid, the tender will not be entertained and the cash/cheque will not be accepted either.

title: RWP Commissioner orders survey to identify, raze encroachments along Soan River
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The divisional administration has decided to execute a survey to ascertain the illegal constructions along the Soan River – recently unearthed during the heavy rains that damaged some houses, according to a news source published on August 29.
Read:
Funds approved for land acquisition of Rawalpindi Ring Road’s right-of-way
Rawalpindi Commissioner (retired) Captain Mohammad Mehmood visited the area along the Soan River to inspect the damages caused by the flood-situation in and adjacent to the Sharoon Colony. Many unauthorised structures were discovered on the river banks during this visit.
The commissioner directed the district revenue department to conduct a survey to identify the illegal construction along the river, so as to an action plan could be formulated to eliminate the said encroachments and also to avoid the flooding situation in the future.
Read:
Project consultant hired for parking plazas in Rawalpindi
Over 100 houses were affected by the rising water levels in the Soan River, as it entered the Sharoon Colony on Thursday. The affected residents were transferred to safer places by Rescue 1122 officials.
Moreover, the
commissioner
was told that the Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) has written to the housing societies along the Soan River about their revenue limits. However, no response was received from them. Mehmood said that under the law, no construction was permissible along the river banks and its right of way – which is only reserved for the agriculture purposes.

title: Karachi Rain: CM Sindh orders survey to assess damages for repair, compensation
developer: Saturday issued instructions to the Planning and Development
full_text:
Karachi: Sindh Chief Minister (CM) Syed Murad Ali Shah on Saturday issued instructions to the Planning and Development (P&D) Department and the revenue boards to conduct a survey in the metropolis to assess the infrastructural damage to houses and crops so that the rehabilitation work can be initiated and compensation for the damages can be paid, according to news sources.
Read:
Torrential Rains: Hub Dam fills to capacity after 13 years
Meanwhile, the CM issued PKR 5 million to the deputy commissioners of Karachi, Mirpur Khas and Hyderabad divisions to drain rainwater and tackle similar issues. He made these decisions while presiding over a meeting to review the post-rainfall situation in all the districts of the province. Also, he stated that after the next rain spell, the repair work on damaged road network would be initiated.
Read:
NDMA to initiate desilting of Karachi’s storm drains
Moreover, the CM further directed the finance secretary to release the funds to deputy commissioners for
rainwater
disposal. He was appraised that the K-Electric had restored 1,730 feeders out of 1,900 total feeders in the city and that the KE is not restoring power in areas where the rainwater remains stagnant.

title: Govt housing authorities ordered to fulfill all CDA codal formalities
full_text:
Islamabad: Federal Ombudsman Syed Tahir Shahbaz on Saturday chaired a meeting to review the progress of various government housing sectors in the city and issued directions to the Federal Government Employees Housing Authority (FGEHA) and the Pakistan Housing Authority (PHA) to ensure implementation of all codal formalities prescribed by the Capital Development Authority (CDA), according to news sources.
Read:
CDA prepares PC-1 for acquiring buses for IIA Metro Track
Shahbaz expressed concern over the low-quality construction work, unnecessary delays and difficulties in completion of government housing projects in the capital. He requested all departments concerned to ensure standardised construction work and provision of development facilities in these government-owned housing projects. He directed
FGEHA
to form committees of allottees in all government sectors to eliminate construction and maintenance issues, and resolve all the complaints – if any.
Moreover, Tahir also issued directions for the FGEHA, the CDA and the PHA to offer healthcare facilities in these new sectors. The ombudsman also directed the chairman of CDA to hand over plot possession to allottees in the Park Enclave I & II.
Read:
CDA holds 2-day session with builders, developers to promote construction
As per the details, PHA Managing Director (MD) Tariq Rasheed informed the meeting members that out of 588 flats in Kuri Road Project, 272 have been handed over to the allottees. The possession of remaining apartments will be handed over in October, after the apartments are completed by September 15. The meeting was also informed that the required no-objection certificates (NOCs) from all departments concerned had been obtained for all PHA housing projects.
Additionally, the director general of FGEHA briefed the meeting that the plan of Green Enclave I & II (at Bara Kahu) is completed. He also added that the development work on Green Enclave I will be completed by April 2023 and over 6,000 plots have been created in Green Enclave II.

title: Punjab govt to set up 13 Special Economic Zones
full_text:
Lahore: The Punjab government plans to set up 13 Special Economic Zones (SEZs) in the province, a news source reported on August 30. Chief Minister (CM) Usman Buzdar revealed the information during a meeting with Ambassador of United Arab Emirates (UAE) to Pakistan Hamad Obaid Ibrahim Salem Al-Zabi.
Read:
CPEC industrial cooperation MoU to be elevated for SEZs development
During the meeting, the Punjab CM revealed that it was the first time in the history of the country that a provincial government was going to set up 13 SEZs. He added that the Punjab government would also ensure the provision of special facilities with regard to investment in these SEZs. He highlighted that similar facilities would be available for the Ravi River Urban Development Project.
The UAE envoy and Buzdar deliberated upon matters of mutual interest, along with promotion of bilateral relations and cooperation in different fields. Both officials discussed sectors including housing, trade, industry, and business to boost cooperation between the two countries.
Read:
UAE expresses investment interest in Pakistan’s seaport projects
Al Zabi extended his appreciation to the Punjab government for its effective strategy in dealing with the coronavirus pandemic. He added that the UAE wanted to enhance cooperation with the provincial government within different sectors.

title: CDA prepares PC-1 for acquiring buses for IIA Metro Track
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Friday revealed that it had prepared the PC-1 for acquiring 30 buses for running on the Islamabad International Airport (IIA) Metro Track, a news source reported. As per details, the PC-1 also covers the establishment of a ticketing and command & control centre for the bus service between Peshawar Mor and IIA.
Read:
Rawalpindi Administration approves two new public transport routes to IIA
Following the directions of the federal government, CDA Chairman Amer Ali Ahmed held a meeting for discussing options to start the bus service along the IIA Metro Track. The officials concerned informed the meeting that the PC-1 worth PKR 1.9 billion had been forwarded to the interior ministry for approval. They added that after receiving the approval, it would take at least six to eight months to launch the metro service to the airport.
The officials said that as an alternative solution, CDA would acquire the services of private bus operators or the Punjab Metro Bus Authority to run some buses along the route while the process of procuring buses and setting up ticketing system was underway. The meeting decided that the relevant officials would work on the two proposals and the next meeting would take the final decision in this regard.
Read:
Traders demand MCI merger with CDA
According to details revealed, the National Highway Authority is currently working on construction of the IIA Metro Track. The CDA chairman has directed officials to complete all arrangements so the civic body could begin operating buses within three days of NHA handing over the control of the track. Officials also briefed the meeting that CDA was working on a proposal to reduce the volume of the subsidy for the metro route.

title: Torrential Rains: Hub Dam fills to capacity after 13 years
developer: As per the officials of Water & Power Development
full_text:
Karachi: The Hub Dam on Thursday (Aug 27) was filled to its maximum capacity for the first time since 2007, owing to the recent influx of torrential rains in Balochistan and Sindh, according to news sources.
Read:
Addressing Firdous Market Underpass drainage issues crucial in avoiding ubran flooding in Gulberg: WASA
The rainwater stored in the Hub Dam can now ensure a smooth supply of drinking water to the metropolis of Karachi for the next three years. The water level in the dam has increased up to 340 ft – and has begun to outflow from the spillways into the sea from near Mubarak Village.
In the last three days, the catchment area of
Hub
Dam – which stretches up to the mountain range in Balochistan – has risen up to more than 9 feet.
Read:
NDMA to initiate desilting of Karachi’s storm drains
As per the officials of Water & Power Development Authority (WAPDA), more rainwater relays from the catchment area are reaching up to the dam. Officials of the Hub Dam Management Agency, WAPDA and irrigation department have been present on site in case of any emergency situation. The settlements below the dam have also been evacuated as a safety measure. Moreover, it is reported that over 30 feet of water have been filled into the dam after the recent rains.

title: WAPDA’s electricity generation capacity via hydel power at its highest
full_text:
Lahore: The Water & Power Development Authority (WAPDA) on Thursday announced that its hydel power electricity generation capacity had reached its highest mark, a news source reported. Officials revealed that the power generation capacity crossed 8,500 megawatts (MWs) for the first time in Pakistan.
Read:
WAPDA hands over Murunj Dam’s feasibility study contract to NESPAK
According to sources, the last time WAPDA crossed its record hydel power electricity generation was in September 2019 with 8,474MWs. They added that this new high was a result of increased reservoir level at Tarbela and Mangla dams, more water outflows as per indent by the Indus River System Authority (IRSA), and effective operations at the hydel power stations owned by WAPDA.
Read:
KP expedites construction in seven hydel power projects
Official sources also stated that the installed capacity of WAPDA hydel power stations had increased to 9,389MWs. They added that this was possible due to the phased completion of three mega hydropower projects. The officials revealed that these projects included Neelum Jhelum, Golen Gol, and the Tarbela 4
th
Extension project.

title: Ammar Shaheed Chowk remodeling project handed over to Chaklala Cantonment Board
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Punjab Cabinet has granted its approval to the transfer of Ammar Shaheed Chowk remodeling project to the Chaklala Cantonment Board (CCB), according to a news report published August 28.
The project was to be previously managed by the Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA). As per the new arrangements, the RDA will now transfer the funds allocated for the project to the Chaklala Cantonment Board.
Read:
Haq seeks briefing on Rawalpindi’s Ammar Shaheed Chowk Tunnel
According to previous news reports, the Punjab government had reserved funds worth PKR 754 million for the remodeling of Ammar Shaheed Chowk in its Annual Development Programme 2020-21. The project is deemed vital for getting rid of existing traffic issues in the city.
Due to undisclosed reasons, the government had dropped the project from its Annual Development Programme 2019-20. Given the importance of the project, the RDA requested the provincial government in February this year to
handover
the project to the Chaklala Cantonment Board as the Ammar Shaheed Chowk is located in its
jurisdiction
.
Read:
RDA sends revised PC-I for Ammar Chowk to cabinet
Sources also claim that project design has also been finalised.

title: KP utilises all funds allocated under ADP 2019-20
full_text:
Peshawar: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) government has utilised all the funds allocated under its Annual Development Programme (ADP) for Fiscal Year (FY) 2019-2020, according to a news report. This includes all the funds allocated towards developing the merged tribal areas.
Read:
KP CM directs to include tribal development projects in new ADP
KP Chief Minister (CM) Mahmood Khan revealed this information during a high-level meeting he chaired to review the projects listed under the
ADP
. The members of this meeting learned that over 99% of the funds had been spent, and none of the allocated amounts had lapsed.
The meeting also reviewed the performance of various departments in this regard. The Agriculture Development ranked the highest, with a score of 86, while the Local Government and Public Health Engineering departments ranked second and third, respectively.
Read:
Road projects in KP receive nearly half of allocated ADP funds
Additionally, it was also disclosed that 249 development projects had been listed under the ADP for the settled districts and 88 projects for the merged tribal areas. In addition, 122 projects in these areas had been placed under the Accelerated Implementation Programme (AIP). Over PKR 55 million had been spent for projects in these tribal areas, meaning that 100% of the allocated funds had been utilised.

title: KP govt approves 21 uplift schemes for tribal districts
full_text:
Peshawar: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) government has approved 21 uplift schemes aimed at developing the province’s tribal districts, according to a news report. These projects will develop both the settled and newly-merged districts at a cost of around PKR 19.97 billion.
Read:
PKR 49bn allocated for development schemes in KP’s tribal districts
The sectors covered under the initiative will include healthcare, education, and administrative services; along with the upgradation of relief and rehabilitation facilities. The allocated funds will be used to improve these sectors in the tribal districts.
The KP Provincial Development Working Party (
PDWP
) discussed these projects at a meeting held on Wednesday, which was chaired by Additional Chief Secretary Shakeel Qadir Khan.
Read:
PM receives briefing on uplift schemes, power projects underway in ex-FATA
The session attendees discussed a total of 24 projects related to agriculture, health, water, relief and rehabilitation, revenue, urban development, multisectoral development,
auqaf
, home, and forestry. Three of these projects were referred to their relevant departments for rationalisation, while the rest were approved. Some have been nominated under the Accelerated Implementation Programme (AIP) and are set to be prioritised during the development phases.

title: LDA holds seminar seeking stakeholders’ views on land use rules draft
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) on Thursday arranged a seminar for stakeholders asking them to submit their input of recommendations and objections retrieved from the general public regarding the draft of the Land Use Regulations formulated under the previously notified Land Use Rules Act, 2020, according to news sources.
Read:
LDA approves Defence Road rehabilitation project
The seminar was attended by a large variety of people including town planners, housing scheme developers, architectures, businessmen, journalists and lawyers. During the seminar, attendees voiced their concerns and gave suggestions on the draft of the
Land Use
Regulations.
LDA Chief Town Planner Tariq Mahmood, in his address, assured the public that their input shall be given due deliberation and that their recommendations and objections will be presented before the authority’s governing body for approvals.
Read:
LDA conducts survey in Sabzazar Scheme to determine illegal property occupation
He further expressed the resolve of the LDA to implement the policy regarding commercialisation in a systematic and planned manner, as to avoid causing a burden on the present infrastructure. The LDA director general has already issued instructions for the department officials to give due consideration to the opinions and suggestion posed by the stakeholders so that additional job opportunities and business endeavours could be generated.

title: DHA Lahore initiates development work in Sector-IV, Phase-XI (Rahbar)
amenities: Linked with Ring Road | Commercial Area | Parks and Green Belt
full_text:
Lahore: The management of the Defence Housing Authority (DHA) Lahore has announced the initiation of development work in Sector IV, Phase XI (Rahbar), according to a post published on society’s official Facebook page on August 28.
Read:
DHA Lahore cautions people to get affidavits verified
The salient features of the project include:
Linked with Ring Road
Commercial Area
Parks and Green Belt
Community Club
Hospital
Educational Institutes
Underground Electrification
Read:
DHA Lahore office offers ‘Executive Services’ to its premium clients
Earlier, the DHA Lahore also reopened the Defence Public Library with enhanced facilities including more books, e-lab, dedicated section for seniors, cafeteria and a kids’ section. Also, the
DHA Lahore
has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the famous eatery chain ‘McDonalds’ to open several branches in various chains.
Moreover, the society’s management has also issued a cautionary warning to potential buyers requesting them to get their affidavits verified by the DHA Lahore Land Branch office to avoid becoming victim to any fraudulent schemes.

title: PM orders speedy approval process for pending construction projects
full_text:
Islamabad: Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan on Thursday issued directives for all the provincial chief secretaries to fast track the approval-process of the pending applications related to the construction and the housing sector, according to news sources.
Read:
Pakistan’s current account balance registers surplus: PM
The premier made these remarks while chairing the weekly meeting of the National Coordination Committee (NCC) for Housing, Construction and Development. He said that the development of the construction sector is key to stability and growth of the national economy.
Capital Development Authority (
CDA
) Chairman Amer Ali Ahmed briefed the prime minister regarding various developments in the construction sector – including the incentives being offered for various sectors in the capital city. The PM was also briefed about new projects in Park Enclave III, Blue Area, the progress in the auction of commercial plots and the CDA’s complete automation initiative. He was told that the fee for the floor area ration has been reduced by 55% and facilities of mortgage and insurance has been simplified.
Read:
CDA holds 2-day session with builders, developers to promote construction
Moreover, the authority’s chairman said that since June, 429 out of 578 applications for residential and commercial projects have been approved. The provincial chief secretaries also appraised the meeting regarding the number of applications received and their approval status.

title: KP revenue generation via hydropower projects increases by 100% in FY2019-20: report
full_text:
Peshawar: A progress review meeting of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Energy and Power Department – chaired by Chief Minister (CM) Mahmood Khan – was told that the Pakhtunkhwa Energy Development Organisation had doubled its revenue generation through hydropower projects in the last two years, according to a news report published on August 27.
Read:
PM praises KPRA for increasing revenue during pandemic
The meeting was further informed that during the fiscal year 2018-19, the organisation generated revenue worth of PKR 1,571.14 million, whereas in the following year, a revenue of PKR 3,458 million was generated through various hydropower projects in the province.
The meeting was also told that new hydropower projects including 17 MegaWatts (MW) Ranolia Hydropower project, 2.60 MW Machai Hydropower Project and the 36.6 MW Dral Khwar Hydropower Project in Swat were completed in last two years. These three projects were developed at a cost of PKR 14 billion and are likely to generate PKR 2 billion annual revenue for KP.
Read:
KP govt to extend health insurance to all residents
Furthermore, the KP Transmission & Grid Company is all set up and ready to become operational. The meeting was told that a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model has been launched to fast track implementation of the hydropower projects. The CM directed the officials to ensure timely completion of these ongoing
hydropower projects
so that the public can avail the benefits without further delay.

title: Development work on phase I of Balochistan’s Kachhi Canal project nears completion
full_text:
Quetta: Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA) Chairman Lt Gen (retired) Muzammil Hussain on Monday said that the development work on the first phase of the Kachhi Canal and its extension was near completion, according to news sources.
Read:
Balochistan to get 40% share of gas revenue from Sui field
The WAPDA chairman revealed this information while in a meeting with Balochistan Chief Minister (CM) Jam Kamal Khan Alyani. He said that the documentation for the Nolang Dam has been completed and the tenders for the project will soon be floated. He said that the project can store millions of acres feet of rainwater and floodwater – which could be utilised for power generation and agriculture in the province.
Read:
CM Balochistan calls for environment-friendly reforms in the construction sector
The chief minister further said that the completion of the Kachhi Canal project will boost the provincial economy and create employment opportunities. He also remarked that millions of acres of land can be brought under cultivation with the development and construction of
water reservoirs
. Alyani went as far as to say that ‘Balochistan could meet the food requirement of the entire country’.

title: LDA approves Defence Road rehabilitation project
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) recently approved a new rehabilitation project for the Defence Road and the Shahkam Chowk Flyover — a news source reported. The project will now be completed in two phases over a period of two fiscal years — with the old pre-qualification bids having been cancelled as well.
Read:
LDA finalises designs for Shahkam Chowk Flyover, Defence Road expansion projects
According to the details available, the new project has also been approved by LDA Chief Engineer Habib-ul-Haq Randhawa. According to the initial estimates, the project is expected to cost PKR 3.4 billion, out of which PKR 2.48 billion is dedicated for the rehabilitation of the Shahkam Flyover, while PKR 1.24 billion will be allocated for work to be conducted on improving the Defence Road.
Read:
Punjab Budget 2020-21: Funds earmarked for Shahkam Chowk Flyover development
The work on the flyover is expected to be completed by the end of this fiscal year, while work on the Defence Road is estimated to be completed by sometime next year. After cancelling the prequalification bids, the LDA has now invited separate bids for both projects once again, as adequate budgetary allocations could not be assigned to the project under the Budget 2020-21.

title: NDMA to begin cleaning nullahs in Karachi from next month
full_text:
Islamabad: Federal Minister for Planning & Development Asad Umar on Wednesday stated that the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) would begin cleaning the riverbeds and
nullahs
in Karachi from September onward, a news source reported.
Read:
Govt urged to allow NDMA, FWO rebuild infrastructure in Karachi
Umar took to Twitter stating that NDMA would finish cleaning the
nullahs
in Karachi in one year. He added that he would approve soon approve the plan, which would solve the problem of the city becoming submerged in water during heavy rains. The minister highlighted that Karachi was the largest tax-paying city of the country and deserved better than the issues it was currently facing.
Read:
SWEEP: Survey of nullahs being carried in Karachi
Recently, the federal and Sindh governments had also formed a joint committee that would work on six significant issues for developing Karachi. These included work on the sewerage system, solid waste disposal, roads infrastructure, removal of encroachments, water, and transport. The committee consists of six members, who would ensure the timely completing of all ongoing development projects of the city within these categories.

title: CDA holds 2-day session with builders, developers to promote construction
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Monday organised a two-day session for local developers, builders and representatives of private housing societies in a bid to promote construction activity in the capital city, according to news sources.
Read:
CDA completes ballot process for 437 deleted plots in Sector I-12
The session was held in the backdrop of Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan’s special package for housing and construction sector and was attended by the representatives of the private housing societies and Association of Builders and Developers (ABAD).
The said session discussed all the pressing issues faced by both the industries. The representatives of builders and developer association presented their concerns and mulled over various solutions. The most pressing problems involved timely-approvals of building plans, traffic assessment, environmental concerns, building bylaws, graveyard levy charges, Sector E-II projects, layout plans and insurance policies — and were discussed at length.
Read:
CDA reduces charges on construction of additional storeys in all markets
The authority responded to these issues by highlighting that the Design Vetting Committee (
DVC
) is meeting on a regular basis to approve the building designs. The officials said it has timely concluded all its obligations with the investors whose legal requirements were met with.
Moreover, the meeting was also informed that another auction of commercial plots – with special incentives – is going to be held later in September by the CDA. Officials revealed that they are establishing a separate new directorate to provide speedy solution to the prevailing issues pestering the business community.
Finally, both sides reaffirmed their resolve to positively contribute towards the prime minister’s scheme for housing and the construction industry.

title: Govt to establish authority for development of barren islands
full_text:
Islamabad: The government on Monday announced its decision to establish an authority for the development of barren islands located within the territorial waters of Pakistan, a news source reported. According to the Ministry of Maritime Affairs, the executive would set up the Pakistan Islands Development Authority (PIDA) to facilitate the measure.
Read:
PM directs Maritime Affairs Ministry to complete Gwadar Port projects on priority
The Maritime Affairs Ministry revealed that it would propose the Pakistan Islands Development Authority Act 2020 to facilitate the establishment of PIDA. The tasks of the authority will include development of barren islands in the territorial waters of Pakistan, along with undertaking residential and infrastructure projects in these islands. Sources revealed that these initiatives would help revive over 50 allied industries as well as generating large-scaled skilled employment opportunities.
Read:
Mangroves plantation campaign conducted in Sindh’s coastal areas
The government aims to curb the erosion of the islands caused by natural calamities. Once the projects begin, the government may replicate these for the coastal development of Karachi city. According to the details revealed, the federal government has provided an in-principle approval to the proposal submitted by the Maritime Affairs Ministry.

title: Punjab approves development of low-cost housing projects in 10 cities
developer: Punjab Minister for Housing and Urban Development
full_text:
Lahore: The Punjab government recently approved the development of low-cost housing projects in 10 cities — with development work to be carried out as a joint venture with private investors, developers and builders, according to a news story shared in local dailies today. The initiative comes as part of Prime Minister Imran Khan’s Naya Pakistan Housing Programme (NPHP).
Read:
Construction of low-cost houses, apartments to start in Oct: Shibli
As per the details shared by Punjab Minister for Housing and Urban Development Mian Mehmood-ur-Rasheed, several builders, developers and investors had approached the Punjab Housing and Town Planning Agency (PHATA) with regards to the development of low cost housing projects in the province. Responding to these requests, the provincial government decided to initiate the process to collaborate with private entities in order to provide low-cost housing units and plots in Rawalpindi, Lahore, Faisalabad, Lodhran, Sialkot, Hazru, Chistian, Chinot, Patoki and Kharian.
Read:
SBP extends loan limit for low-cost housing finance
Minister Rasheed further revealed that PHATA was carrying out the related processes to scrutinise the applications submitted by the developers and investors interested in developing NPHP projects. The government is keen on approving these applications on a priority basis so as to initiate the development work on 169 low-cost housing projects across the province as soon as possible.
Read:
Budget 2020-21: Major relief proposed for low-cost housing sector
According to the details available, the government will provide 39,000 low-cost plots in Lahore and Faisalabad for the development of affordable housing projects, on an area measuring 20,531 acres. Sources also claim that these schemes will feature 175,000 residential plots — with 44,927 plots measuring 3 marlas in size and 38,662 plots measuring 5 marlas in size.

During the proceedings, the authority will allocate plot numbers against residential plot spaces measuring 25×50 sq ft, 35×70 sq ft, 40×80 sq ft, and 50×90 sq ft; with the event scheduled to be held at the Jinnah Convention Centre in the capital.
Read:
CDA invites bids for Park Enclave-II’s infrastructural development
The last date to submit an application form to book a plot in Park Enclave III is September 17. The application forms and project brochures are available at the designated branches of the Askari Bank, Muslim Commercial Bank, United Bank Limited, and Habib Bank Limited. They can also be procured from the CDA One-Window Operation Directorate, located at Khayaban-e-Suharwardy, Sector G-7/4 – Islamabad.

CDA to launch Park Enclave-II Extension project

are available on a 10% down payment of the total price, while the remaining dues will have to be cleared in 18 monthly instalments. The CDA has further mentioned that the last instalment is to be paid at the time of possession. As mentioned in our

CDA shares updates on G-7 Underpass, Park Enclave & Burma Bridges

CDA to elevate Park Enclave-I as state-of-the-art model project

CDA gains possession of additional 140 kanals in Park Enclave II
