title: CDA shares updates on G-7 Underpass, Park Enclave & Burma Bridges
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Sunday notified that the Sector G-7 and G-8 underpass on Faisal Avenue, the Park Enclave Bridge and the Burma Bridge were all nearing completion and would likely be opened for public use within a few days, according to a news source.
Read:
Construction of Bhara Kahu Flyover to begin soon: SAPM CDA
CDA Spokesperson Mazhar Hussain said that the underpass on Faisal Avenue only requires the final finishing touches and highlighted that the project is being completed below the bidding cost – which was already lower than the estimate.
He said that the completion of the G-7 and G-8 underpass was expected in May, but the construction work was halted owing to the anti-COVID-19 lockdown ensued by the coronavirus outbreak in the country.
Read:
CDA to initiate infrastructure, housing projects in Islamabad
As for the
Park Enclave
Bridge, the CDA spokesperson said that the project only needs a few more engineering interjections and is being completed within the bidding cost. The Burma Bridge on Lehtrar Road is also near completion and is being launched earlier than expected – with cost savings.
Furthermore, the authority is all set to launch work on mega projects including the expansion of Korang Bridge, the PWD underpass, and an interchange on the Rawal Dam Chowk.

title: Construction of Bhara Kahu Flyover to begin soon: SAPM CDA
full_text:
Islamabad: Special Assistant to Prime Minister (SAPM) on Capital Development Authority Ali Nawaz Awan has announced that the construction work for the Bhara Kahu flyover would begin soon, a news source reported on August 21.
Read:
Bhara Kahu Bypass construction kicks off in August
He stated that, in a meeting held with the National Highway Authority (NHA) officials, the matter of opening the 17-mile U-turn on the Bhara Kahu Road was discussed and its timeline as well. The meeting also discussed the matter of installing a pedestrian bridge in Malpur, Islamabad.
Moreover, the meeting was briefed about the stages at which each of these projects currently stood and the SAPM was assured that all of these projects would be soon launched.
Read:
Bhara Kahu Housing Scheme to be launched next month
The meeting was also attended by NHA Chairman Captain (retd) Sikandar Qayyum, other high officials of the NHA and officials from the Public-Private Partnership Authority (PPPA) as well.

title: RUDA invites EOI for Ravi River Development City design, development
full_text:
Lahore: The Ravi Urban Development Authority (RUDA) has invited expressions of interest (EOIs) from well-reputed developers and consortium firms for ‘state-of-the-art’ designing and development of the Ravi River Development City initiative – part of the Ravi Riverfront Urban Development (RRUD) Project, according to a news source published on August 21.
Read:
Ravi Riverfront project to be developed in 3 phases
With this latest development, the RUDA has launched work to initiate the phase-wise development of the RRUD. As per the details, in the first phase of the project, some 3-10 thousand acres of land will be divided into several zones.
Moreover, the provincial government aims to revive the lost heritage and glory of the once-mighty river in Lahore. The
RRUD
Project aims to control pollution in the areas surrounding the river and treating the water inflowing in the river to make the atmosphere eco-friendly. The project plans to develop a modern smart city to counter the issues being created by the ever-increasing population of Lahore.
Read:
Punjab Cabinet approves establishment of Ravi Urban Development Authority
Under this initiative, thousands of low-cost housing units will also be developed in the Ravi River Development City – under Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan’s Naya Pakistan Housing Programme (NPHP).

title: CDA to initiate infrastructure, housing projects in Islamabad
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Monday announced to initiate a number of infrastructure and housing projects in the city, a news source reported. To this effect, the authority has commenced with the construction of three pedestrian bridges at different locations of the capital city.
Read:
CDA-DWP approves PC-II of Islamabad Master Plan (2020-40)’s Project Review
CDA has also begun the civil work for the construction of these pedestrian bridges. The authority is constructing these crossings on the Kashmir Highway near Weekly Bazaar, Jinnah Avenue at Mehran Gate F-9 Park opposite to Sector G-9/2, and Faisal Avenue G-7/2/G-8 near PIMS Hospital.
According to the details revealed, the total construction cost of these bridges would be PKR 135 million. The aim of these Islamabad infrastructure projects is to curb accidents and maintain a smooth flow of traffic in the city. CDA has almost completed the construction and installation of another pedestrian bridge at the Constitution Avenue.
Read:
Plantation drive to grow Islamabad’s first fruit garden launched
Sources revealed that the construction of the bridges was part of CDA’s comprehensive strategy for uplifting the infrastructure and developing neglected residential sectors in the capital.

title: Islamabad-Rawalpindi Circular Railway Track: Chinese team initiates survey
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The 8-member team representing the Chinese Civil Engineering Construction Corporation (CCECC) has initiated the survey for laying the 100-kilometre-long Islamabad/Rawalpindi Circular Railway Track along the Leh Expressway, according to a news report published on August 20. The team carried out the survey work under strict security surveillance.
Read:
Leh Expressway: Demarcation for route alignment completed
As per news sources, the team visited the following sites; Rialto Chowk, Soan River, Ammar Shaheed Chowk, Saddar Road, New Katarian, and Gawalmandi Chowk. According to the project’s focal person Mir Atiq-ur-Rehman, the team has been conducted a detailed survey of the various sites where the track is to be laid.
Reportedly, the Chinese experts have also initiated the work to prepare the project’s feasibility study. The feasibility study report is expected to be shared with the concerned authority in the next 6 months. As revealed earlier, the Circular Railway Track is among the projects being constructed under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) developments.
Read:
RDA to identify land for sewage plant under Leh Expressway project
The railway track will be laid along the Nullah Leh, all the way from Islamabad Secretariat to Islamabad International Airport. Sources also revealed that after conducting the survey, team members had a meeting with the Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) Chairman Tariq Murtaza to discuss the various aspects of the project development.

title: LDA notifies amended land-use rules, others
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) has notified the implementation of ‘Land Use Rules 2020’ by making amendments in the existing Building and Zoning Rules and Private Housing Schemes Rules framework, a news source reported on August 19.
Read:
LDA issues checklist for property buyers to avoid real estate frauds
After the implementation of these improved rules, the issue of commercialisation of frozen road will be resolved. To this effect, a new committee has been constituted for the frozen roads under the supervision of
LDA
Director General Zahid Akthar Zaman.
Moreover, the amended rules reveal that the process to obtain approval for marquee structures is also chalked out to facilitate the businesses. In addition, the amended rules have also allowed the establishment of petrol pumps in the LDA-controlled areas.
Read:
LDA approves plans for 576 new structures, alterations to 162 existing ones
Other amendments include an exemption to non-profit organisations (NGOs) from presenting their bank transaction records of the past three years. Also, the authority has approved the establishment of a special development zone for property owners who own land sizing between 24 kanals and 200 kanals.
Furthermore, LDA Vice Chairman S M Imran said that the authority has established a committee to facilitate the citizens in following these amended rules – so as to avoid any ambiguity or unlawful developments.

title: Centre, Sindh govt to work on 6 priority areas for Karachi’s development
full_text:
Islamabad: The federal and Sindh governments on Wednesday formed a joint committee to work on six priority areas for the development of Karachi, a news source reported. According to the details available, the six-member committee will ensure the early completion of all the ongoing long-standing development projects in the city.
Read:
Kidney Hill Park reopens in Karachi
Minister for Planning & Development Asad Umar stated that the committee would work on priority areas, including water, transport, sewerage system, solid waste disposal, roads infrastructure, and removal of encroachments. In this regard, he added that the authorities concerned had either already designed the requisite projects or initiated new ones for development of Karachi in these particular areas.
Read:
People’s Square inaugurated in Karachi
The meeting between the centre and the provincial government decided upon the removal of all impediments pertaining to projects like the KCR, KIV, and S3 with mutual consultations. Additionally, Umar revealed that the final project list would be shortlisted within two weeks, along with a decision regarding the division of responsibilities for each venture between the federal and Sindh governments.

title: CDA-DWP approves PC-II of Islamabad Master Plan (2020-40)’s Project Review
full_text:
Islamabad: In its 48
th
meeting held on August 17, the Capital Development Authority’s Development Working Party (CDA-DWP) approved the PC-II for the Islamabad Master Plan 2020-40’s Project Review, according to a press release issued by the development authority.
Read:
CDA to establish PMU to oversee revision in Islamabad master plan
Reportedly, the meeting was held to further build up momentum for development activity in the city. The session was presided over by CDA Chairman Amir Ali Ahmed, and representatives of the Ministry of Planning, the Ministry of Interior, and the Ministry Finance were also in attendance, along with officials from other relevant government departments.
The CDA has recently started work on a record number of development projects in the city, including the construction of road interchanges, bridges, establishment of wetlands, and initiation of development work in stalled residential sectors.
Read:
CDA to construct 5 interchanges in FY 21 under Islamabad Master Plan
In addition to approving the PC-II for the Islamabad Master Plan Project Review, the meeting also approved the PC-I for development work in Sector D-12 and for the construction of a bridge on Kiyani Road. Furthermore, the CDA-DWP approved a PC-II for the engagement of consultancy services for a feasibility study and detailed designs for the development of parking plazas that have been planned for various locations across the city.

title: Leh Circular Railway: Chinese team arrives in Rawalpindi to conduct project’s feasibility study
developer: An official of the Rawalpindi Development
full_text:
Rawalpindi: Representatives of a Chinese company on Monday arrived in the city to conduct the feasibility study for laying down the Nullah Leh Circular Railway track, a news source reported. According to the details revealed, the federal and provincial governments, along with the China Civil Engineering Construction Company (CCECC), have announced their decision to begin the feasibility study of the circular track – planned to run along the Nullah Leh Expressway project.
Read:
Leh Expressway: Demarcation for route alignment completed
Sources stated that the company would conduct the study on the cost of the Nullah Leh Circular Railway track project. The Chinese experts would undertake the preliminary study on the project’s feasibility – including technical, legal, and financial assessments – along with its commercial viability.
Read:
MoU signed with Chinese firm to conduct feasibility study of Leh Expressway
An official of the Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) revealed that currently two proposals were under consideration for commencing with the Nullah Leh Expressway project development. One proposal featured land allocation for a sewage treatment plant in Adiala to a private land development company to earn money in return for investment in the project under private-public partnership, he said. He added that the second proposal pertained to covering Nullah Leh from New Kattarian to Soan River near the LHC Rawalpindi Bench for the commencement of commercial activities and letting a private investor earn money from these.

title: Contract awarded for construction of culverts in Sector I-11/2
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) recently awarded a contract in response to the lowest bid of PKR 94.12 million it received for the development of box culverts in Sector I-11/2 – planned to drain high volumes of water, according to a news source published on August 13.
Read:
CDA-DWP to review Islamabad Master Plan (2020-40) PC-II next weeek
The authority has issued an official statement in this regard and revealed that it had
invited bids
for the project – with an estimated cost of PKR 137.42 million for the construction of four box culverts.
During the bidding process, as many as 17 firms expressed interest to undertake the project; however, the tender was granted to the firm that presented a bid of PKR 94.12 million – which is 31.6% lower than the initial estimate.
Read:
CDA to initiate work on development of Malal Bridge
These four box culverts in Sector I-11/2 will drain high volumes of water and handle a higher flow rate as compared to pipes. Moreover, these culverts will accommodate vehicular and pedestrian movement.

title: LDA approves plans for 576 new structures, alterations to 162 existing ones
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) on Wednesday announced that it had issued building plan approvals for 576 new structures in the city, a news source reported. It further notified alteration approvals to the building plans for 162 existing structures.
Read:
SBCA introduces pre-approved residential building plans
Sources revealed that the LDA issued these building plan approvals within the past three months. They added that the authority had also provided completion certificates to 59 new buildings in Lahore during the same period.
LDA Vice Chairman Sheikh Muhammad Imran met with Honorary Consul of the Republic of Belarus Walid Mushtaq. He informed the honorary consul that the authority had simplified the process of sanctioning approvals for private housing schemes in Lahore. He added that that a scheme could now obtain an LDA approval within 30 days.
Read:
Metro Bus service resumed in Lahore, twin cities
During the meeting, the two officials discussed the development of Lahore and other matters of mutual interest. They also reviewed the prospects of benefiting from Belarus’s experience in town planning.

title: CDA-DWP to review Islamabad Master Plan (2020-40) PC-II next week
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has announced that the 48th meeting of the CDA-Development Working Party (DWP) is to be held on August 17; with its proceedings anticipated to further the program for the development of the city, according to a post published on the authority’s official Facebook page on August 11.
Read:
CDA to initiate work on development of Malal Bridge
The said CDA-DWP meeting is to be held under the chair of CDA Chairman Amer Ali Ahmed. The meeting agenda includes various PC-I and PC-II of development schemes in the capital. This 48th
CDA-DWP
meeting will also review the revised PC-II of Project Review of Master Plan of Islamabad (2020-40).
Other projects on the agenda include PC-I of Sector D-12’s Development Work, PC-I for Project Construction of Bridge at Rd-2800 Kiyani Road (between Bara Kahu and Quaid-e-Azam University) and PC-II for ‘Engagement of Consultancy Services for Feasibility Study and Detailed Engineering Design of parking plazas’ at various locations of the capital.
Read:
CDA sets up self-accountability system to prevent fraudulent plot allotments
The said meeting is to be attended by the representatives of the Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Planning, Ministry of Interior and other relative officials.

title: CDA opens bids for Indus River Water project consultancy contract
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Friday opened financial bids to hire a consultant for a project related to the ‘conduction of water from the Indus river to Islamabad and Rawalpindi’, and for the preparation of a wastewater master plan for the capital city, according to news sources. So far, the lowest bid received for the project amounts to PKR 843 million from a joint venture.
Read:
CDA to initiate work on development of Malal Bridge
Previously, the authority had flouted an international tender to get proposals for the hiring of a consultant. In response to the advertised tender, five firms submitted their technical and financial proposals. These bids were evaluated by the committee that shortlisted three firms that qualified on a technical basis.
Read:
CDA to hire consultants for development projects in Islamabad
The project of Conduction of Water from Indus River System at Terbela Dam was initiated in 2004-05 to develop a perennial source of potable water for the twin cities. And despite being approved by the Council of Common Interest (CCI) back in 2016, the project remained stalled. As a result, an acute shortage of drinkable
water
in the twin cities has been observed as the local population grows with time.

title: Neelum-Jehlum Plant contributes milestone units to national grid
full_text:
Lahore: The Neelum-Jehlum Hydropower Plant — which has a production capacity of 969 MW — on Sunday recorded a landmark contribution of over 10 billion units to the national grid, according to a news sources.
Read:
Work on Koto Hydropower Project to resume this week
In addition, the  generation of over 10 billion units to the national grid has earned revenues of up to PKR 120 billion for the project. This revelation was made by a spokesperson of the Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA), who took the opportunity to laud this news. He further stated that as the project was being efficiently operated, it was not only meeting the design generation targets, but was exceeding the annual rated generation targets as well.
Read:
PKR 177.5 bn allocated for water sector & hydropower projects under PSDP 2020-21
During the last fiscal year (FY2019-20), the plant succeeded in generating 4,843 million power units, against its target of 4,660 million units — despite various coronavirus-related complications.
The Neelum-Jehlum Hydropower Plant has four generating units with a capacity of 242.25 MW (each).  The first unit of the project commenced its operations in April 2018, and attainted its
maximum generation
capacity of 969MW by August 14, 2018 (with commissioning of all four units).

title: CDA to initiate work on development of Malal Bridge
full_text:
Islamabad: The construction of the Malal Bridge on Lehtarar Road is likely to be initiated soon, after the financial bids for the project were recently opened by the Capital Development Authority (CDA), according to a news source published on August 11.
Read:
CDA to launch Park Enclave-II Extension project
Earlier, the CDA had invited bids from construction firms through a notice in various national newspapers. The project’s NIT was PKR 100.818 million and the lowest bid received amounted to PKR 70 million — which is 22% below the estimated cost of the project.
Read:
CDA board approves establishment of 2 new directorates
In the short tenure of the incumbent CDA administration, this is the second infrastructural project to be developed on Lehtarar road — the first being the construction of the Burma bridge, which is nearing completion. This bridge project also encompasses the construction of a 700-metre-long dual road.
Previously, the Lehtarar Road had been dualised in 2008. However, due to a lack of the Malal Bridge and Burma Bridge, the road kept on experiencing traffic congestion issues. Now, the
authority
has reassured locals that the development of the Malal Bridge project would be completed within a year’s time.

title: Rawalpindi Ring Road project PC-1 for land acquisition approved
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Punjab Planning and Development Department has approved the PC-I – worth PKR 6.7 billion – for the Rawalpindi Ring Road (RRR) project’s land acquisition effort, according to a news source published on August 8.
Read:
RDA authorised as executive agency for development of RRR project
Reportedly, the land acquisition was approved for the project’s Package–I. The total cost of the project is PKR 52 billion and is said to take over two years to complete. However, it is revealed that the work on the
land acquisition
– 14,600 kanals to be acquired in 27 villages – will initiate after Muharram.
Commissioner Rawalpindi Captain (retired) Mohammad Mehmood said that the land acquisition will soon be initiated under the Section 6, Land Revenue Act. The project will start from Radio Pakistan, Rawat at Grand Trunk (GT) Road to ‘motorway from Islamabad to Lahore near the New Airport’.
Read:
Proposals invited from private societies for construction of interchanges on RRR
Moreover, he said that the project will also link the Islamabad Margalla Road (via Sangjani) with the speed limit set at 120 kilometres per hour for the six-lane road. The commissioner opined that the ring road will facilitate the transportation sector and ease the traffic woes in the area. He added that the local and regional economic activities – like hospitals, colleges and new housing schemes – will be launched as part of this project.

title: Ghazi-Barotha water supply project gets consultant
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Sunday announced that it had selected a consultant for the Ghazi-Barotha water supply project for Islamabad and Rawalpindi, a news source reported.
Read:
WASA prepares plan for 5 mn gallon daily water supply to Rawalpindi
CDA officials revealed that the lowest bidder was selected for this mega project of obtaining water from Indus River to the twin cities. They further announced the development authority’s decision to commence with the land acquisition process for the project.
According to the details revealed, CDA proceeded ahead with the Ghazi-Barotha water supply project as per the instructions of the federal government. To hire consultancy services for the project, the authority invited proposals from both national and international companies. A committee selected the lowest bidder following the evaluation of the bids submitted.
Read:
Budget 2020-21: PKR 3.15bn reserved for provision of water to Islamabad, Rawalpindi
The hired company will provide its consultancy services to develop a perennial source of potable water supply for Islamabad and Rawalpindi. The twin cities have faced serious water shortage issues for some time now.

title: PKR 5 trillion Ravi Urban Development Project launched near Lahore
full_text:
Lahore: Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan on Friday laid the foundation stone for the Ravi River Urban Development Project — with the venture reported to be developed at a cost of PKR 5 trillion, according to news sources.
Read:
Punjab Cabinet approves establishment of Ravi Urban Development Authority
The premier deemed this project vital to save the historical city of Lahore from the environmental damages caused by its unplanned settlements. It is further aimed at reviving the ‘lost glory of Lahore’, which is struggling to cope with serious issues like pollution, water shortages and sewerage disposal.
Read:
LDA directed to prepare grounds for establishing Ravi Urban Development Authority
The PM stated that the Ravi Urban Development Project would help develop the drying river into a perennial freshwater source, with high-quality waterfront urban development. The modern
city
is also expected to provide all the requisite facilities to its residents — with forest cover encompassing six million trees to be developed in the area as well.
Moreover, Khan said that the project would be the country’s second-largest such initiative, and that it would provide employment to millions of people.

title: LDA to install two additional rainwater harvesting systems
full_text:
Lahore: Following the completion of the rainwater harvesting project on Lawrence Road, the Lahore Development Authority (LDA) has announced its decision to install two additional rainwater harvesting systems in the city, a news source reported on August 7. The authority has approved the two new projects – having a collective capacity of 2.7 million gallons of water – at a cost of PKR 240 million.
Read:
Govt to expand underground rainwater storage project to other cities of Punjab
LDA will install the two rainwater harvesting systems at Bismillah Park in Tajpura and outside Sheeranwala Gate on Circular Road, respectively. The first one will have capacity of 1.2 million gallons of water, and the second system will have a storage capacity of 1.5 million gallons.
Read:
WASA constructs large tank to channel, store Lahore’s rainwater stock
Sources have revealed that the authority plans to launch eight more such project in different parts of Lahore. Meanwhile, LDA’s governing body has also approved the plantation of trees at 24 reserved spots in its housing schemes for controlling air pollution in the city. In this regard, the authority allocated PKR 150 million in its annual budget.

title: RDA plans to uplift Raja Baazar, surrounding areas
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) has announced launching a campaign to restore the Raja Bazaar and its surroundings to uplift the lifestyle of its residents, improve the traffic flow and highlight the cultural and tourism potential of the place, according to a post published on the authority’s Facebook page on August 6.
Read:
WASA prepares plan for 5 mn gallon daily water supply to Rawalpindi
To this effect, a meeting was held at the RDA office which was attended by Director General (DG) Walled City Lahore Authority (WCLA) Kamran Lashari, among other RDA officials.
Read:
Project consultant hired for parking plazas in Rawalpindi
RDA Chairman Tariq Mahmood Murtaza addressed the meeting and said that with the suggestions of WCLA director general, the authority will work to promote tourism activities and highlight the importance of cultural heritage in the historic city. He said that research work and development plans to ease
traffic flow
and restoration of dilapidated roads will soon be worked out.

title: RDA launches construction on three pedestrian bridges
full_text:
Rawalpindi: Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) Chairman Tariq Mehmood Murtaza recently announced that the authority has launched construction work on three pedestrian bridges at different points in the city to maintain traffic flow, according to a news source published on August 4.
Read:
RDA invites RFPs for Fawara Chowk parking plaza extension
As per the RDA Spokesperson, these three pedestrian bridges are being developed at Gulzar-i-Quaid on Airport Road, Nur Khan Air Base Chowk, and Shah Khalid Colony in Rawalpindi. This walkways project has been initiated as result of the local residents’ demand for safer road crossings.
Read:
RDA inaugurates one-window operation center to facilitate people amid pandemic
Previously, the Pakistan Air Force Base Commander had been asked to issue a no-objection certificate for the construction of pedestrian bridges on
Airport Road
. The Punjab government had also earmarked PKR 110 million in the budget of (fiscal year) FY2019-20 for this purpose. Now, the bridges are being developed to facilitate foot traffic and avoid undue accidents.

title: Bodies formed to expedite development of Gwadar Port, other projects
full_text:
Islamabad: Federal Minister for Planning & Development Asad Umar on Wednesday formed two special bodies for the preparation of a programme to expedite the development of Gwadar Port and other projects in Balochistan, a news source reported.
Read
:
Punjab mulls setting up industrial zone along border with Balochistan
Chairing a meeting on development work in Balochistan, the minister announced to form the two special committees. He highlighted that during the ongoing fiscal year, the federal and provincial government would spend a sum of PKR 200 billion on the development of the province.
Umar revealed that Deputy Chairman Planning Commission Dr Jehanzeb Khan would chair one committee, and Maritime Affairs Minister Ali Zaidi and Commerce Advisor Razak Dawood would co-chair the second one.
The Dr Jehanzeb Khan-led committee would make a plan for improving service delivery in areas of water resources, agriculture, tourism, roads, infrastructure, and energy. The co-chaired committee would devise a plan for the development of Gwadar Port.
Read
:
Gwadar Eastbay Expressway slated for completion by April 2021
The planning minister stressed on the development of southern Balochistan as per the directives of Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan. He assured the provincial government that his ministry would release the funds require for the development projects. He added that any plan for the province’s uplift would reach finalisation with prior consultation of all the stakeholders.

title: CDA board approves establishment of 2 new directorates
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) approved on Wednesday the establishment of two new directorates to further facilitate the construction sector (in line with Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan’s vision to promote low-risk sectors), according to news sources.
Read:
CDA waives off 5% bank guarantee to facilitate developers
The CDA Board took this decision at a meeting held at its headquarters in Islamabad. As per reports, one of the new directorates is being set up for processing building plans – aimed to fast track the construction sector. This newly-approved ‘Directorate of Building Control – III’ will regulate the increasing developments in rural areas and enforce
building bylaws
in Zone 3, Zone 4 and Sector E-11.
Initially, two building directorates existed in Islamabad. The Directorate of Building Control-I regularises the commercial and residential buildings in sectoral areas, while the Directorate of Building Control-II regulates the developments in E-11 and authorised housing schemes.
Read:
CDA to elevate Park Enclave-I as state-of-the-art model project
Meanwhile, the civic authority has also (in principle) approved the Directorate of Urban Infrastructure Development – which will operate in coordination with the relevant directorates of the Metropolitan Corporation Islamabad (MCI).
The authority’s official statement also said that the request of private building owners is to be denied and they have to comply with the new building regulations and pay their dues as required.
In addition, the CDA board also subjected the policy for bus stations to the approval of Islamabad Transport Authority. It has also decided to provide ‘insurance guarantee or mortgage of the scalable area in place of bank guarantee’.

title: Foundation stone ceremony of Ravi Riverfront project expected today
developer: Punjab Cabinet approves establishment of Ravi Urban Development
full_text:
Lahore: Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan is expected to lay the foundation stone of the Ravi Riverfront project during his visit to the city today (Friday), a news source reported. The project comprises the construction of a new urban city along River Ravi.
Read:
Punjab Cabinet approves establishment of Ravi Urban Development Authority
With regard to the development of the Ravi Riverfront project, the Punjab government is all set to revive an old urban development project. According to the details revealed, the area spans across hundreds of acres and the project would feature residential and commercial zones, along with a central business district.
The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) has sought to acquire 99,000 acres of land to develop the project. As per sources, the authority has already started work on the project following the instruction of the PM.
Read:
Ravi Riverfront Development (RRUD) project: 99,000 acres to be acquired
During his visit to the city, PM Khan would also conduct meetings with Punjab Chief Minister (CM) Usman Buzdar and Governor Chaudhry Muhammad Sarwar.

title: CDA begins massive anti-encroachment drive
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Wednesday announced its decision to launch a massive anti-encroachment drive in the city, a news source reported. As per the details revealed, the drive is set to begin today (Thursday).
Read:
CDA to fence Park Enclave II to prevent encroachments
During the CDA anti-encroachment drive, the officials concerned would remove constructions beyond the plot lines. These encroachments include obstructions on roads, streets, and pedestrian pathways, barbed wires and fences found around buildings, car or parking sheds, security apparatus, animals and birdcages, lawns and gardens, and electric generators. The CDA officials would also target illegally occupied state land in front of commercial buildings and industrial complexes, high-rises, government, residential, institutional, and government residences within the sectorial areas of Islamabad.
Read:
ICT, CDA remove encroachments from Sabzi Mandi as part of social distancing measures
The ICT Administration, Islamabad police, MCI, and other formations concerned would participate in this campaign. Previously, CDA had warned the general public multiple times against encroaching footpaths roads, green belts, and state land in the capital. The authority had stated that it would take strict action against those found to be violators. To remove these encroachments, CDA has now initiated this massive campaign across the city.

title: ECNEC approves upgradation project of ML-1 track, others
full_text:
Islamabad: The Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) on Wednesday approved a project to upgrade the Mainline-1 (ML-1) railway track – with an estimated cost of PKR 1.137 trillion, according to news sources.
Read:
ECNEC approves Sukkar-Hyderabad Motorway, three other projects
The meeting, held under the chair of Adviser to Prime Minister on Finance and Revenue Abdul Hafeez Shailk, also approved three other development projects that are estimated to cost an accumulative PKR 114 billion.
The upgradation project for the Pakistan Railways’ existing 2,655-kilometre-long track of
ML-1
and development of a dry port near Havelian was greenlit at a rationalised cost of USD 6.807 billion. The expenditure will be shared by both the governments of China and Pakistan.
The Chinese banks will provide 90% of the cost in form of long-term loan – the conditions for which are yet to be finalised. The remaining 10% will be provided by the Pakistani government.
Moreover, of the total amount, 59% (PKR 672 billion) amount will be spent on local material, workforce and equipment – while machinery of USD 2.7 billion will be imported.
Read:
ECNEC approves USD 330mn project to improve Punjab’s HDI ranking
The project will be executed in three phases and the loan amount for each is to be separately contracted. With the ML-1 upgrade the speed of passenger trains shall increase from 65-100 kilometres per hour to 165 kilometres per hour, and the line capacity shall increase from 34 to 137/171 trains per day (each way). A project steering committee will also be set up for the effective implementation of the said development.
Furthermore, a restructuring plan for the Pakistan Railways has been approved by Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan, under which new firms will be carved out. For a cost of PKR 11.074 billion, the ECNEC has also approved the Pakistan Single-Window Project – to be funded by the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR).
Additionally, the committee approved the change in cost-bearing ratios of Asian Development Bank (ADB) and its financing partners for the ‘construction of BRT Red Line Project in Karachi’ at a cost of PKR 78.384 billion – including a Foreign Exchange Component (FEC) of PKR 66.378 billion.

title: CDA to hire consultants for development projects in Islamabad
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Wednesday stated that it would hire consultants for two development projects in the city, a news source reported. Officials revealed that these projects included the construction of parking plazas and cleaning the nullah along with building rainwater facilities in the capital city.
Read:
British Airways to resume flight operations for Islamabad this month
With regard to these development projects in Islamabad, the CDA management has established a special unit called the ‘Urban Infrastructure Directorate’. The purpose of the unit is to liaison with the Metropolitan Corporation Islamabad (MCI) and other organisations concerned, the CDA officials said.
Official sources revealed that there was a significant need for developing parking plazas in the city. They added that the consultant hired would be responsible for preparing a financial model for the projects as well as fulfilling other requirements within three months of employment.
Read:
Leh Expressway to feature 100-km-long ‘Islamabad-Rawalpindi Circular Railway’ line
Similarly, the CDA would also engage a consultant for the improvement of rainwater facilities in Islamabad. According to details revealed, rainwater in the city was going to waste but these facilities would help recharge the groundwater and use it for horticulture purposes.

title: Need for improved measures to support SMEs stressed
full_text:
Islamabad: Punjab Board of Investment and Trade (PBIT) Director Projects and Policy Sohail Qadri has suggested that institutes like the Punjab Small Industries Corporation (PSIC) and the Small and Medium Enterprise Development Authority (SMEDA) should join forces to mitigate the economic impact of the coronavirus on Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs), according to a news source published on August 4.
Read:
SCCI seeks practical steps for development of small industries
Qadri made this proposal while speaking at an online consultative dialogue on ‘Better business regulation for the SME sector in Punjab Province’ – organised by Sustainable Development Policy Institute (SDPI).
He informed that PBIT was aiming to create a platform to boost SME’s capacity building services and assist them in the exploration of the global market. He also observed that the needs of SMEs should be prioritised in the relevant policies to encourage more clusters of small-sized businesses.
Read:
SBP asked to provide easy loans to small businesses
SDPI Joint Executive Director Vaqar Ahmed said that it was ‘need of the hour’ for Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) to ease laws for
SMEs
and startups across the country. He said that the existing laws have no room for idle liquidity in the economy to diversify into investing in innovative firms.
Moreover, Vaqar also revealed that expatriates complain of lack of credible venture capital and policy framework in this regard. He called for SECP to revise existing facilities and regulatory framework, as it is due for an evaluation and upgrade.

title: DG LDA for fast-track development of Firdous Market Underpass
full_text:
Lahore: Lahore Development Authority (LDA) Director General (DG) Ahmed Aziz Tarar has issued instructions to expedite the development work on the Firdous Market Underpass for its completion by the first week of September, according to a post published on the authority’s Facebook page on August 3.
Read:
Governing body approves budget for LDA, WASA & TEPA
Tarar has also permitted the recruitment of additional labour to complete the project on time and has directed the concerned officials to ensure the provisions required. These instructions were issued while the DG and Member Governing Body LDA Engineer Amir Riaz Qureshi were visiting the development site of Firdous Market Underpass.
The visiting officials were informed that the development work on the project is over 60% complete. They were told that presently the shuttering work is being executed and that Water and Sanitation Agency (
WASA
) has installed a new sewerage line for the underpass.
Read:
Budzar orders completion of preparations regarding the development of Lahore Master Plan
Moreover, the authorities were briefed that the project is aiming to be completed by September 5. They were told that the underpass will accommodate over 91,000 vehicles on a daily basis and save millions in additional fuel expense.

title: Kashmir Highway relabelled as ‘Srinagar Highway’ to express solidarity with IOK
full_text:
Islamabad: The authorities concerned on Monday retitled the capital’s prominent ‘Kashmir Highway’ road artery as ‘Srinagar Highway’ in a bid to express solidarity with the residents of Indian-Occupied Kashmir (IOK) ahead of the Youm-e-Istehsal on Wednesday (August 5), according to news sources.
Read:
CDA mulls leasing petrol-pump sites on Islamabad Expressway, Kashmir Highway
Reportedly, the direction boards located on the Zero Point, Faizabad, Dhokari Chowk, Golra Chowk and Express Highway are modified to replace the Kashmir Highway as Srinagar Highway – which is to be inaugurated on August 5. Moreover, the development work on the project is almost complete. Previously, in January,
four new interchanges
– under the Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP) – were added to covert the road into a signal-free passageway.
Read:
CDA to build flyovers at Kashmir Highway, other venues
Foreign Minister Shah Mahmood Qureshi described several activities planned for the day in a media briefing and said that a one-minute silence will be observed at 10am on the day, after baring of sirens.

title: Over 130 development schemes completed under PSDP 2019-20
full_text:
Islamabad: The federal government on Friday announced that it had completed more than 130 development schemes under the Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP) 2019-20, a news source reported. It further stated the relevant departments used about 80% of the allocated funds for completing 132 development projects.
Read:
Govt sets aside PKR 650 bn for development projects under PSDP 2020-21
To this effect, Federal Minister for Planning Asad Umar said that the utilisation of development funds was higher within the last two years. In this regard, a list of completed development schemes under PSDP 2019-20 was forwarded to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).
The list highlighted the completion of major projects in different parts of the country. These included the 6-lane highway from Kala Shah Kaku to Lahore Ring Road, Faisalabad-Khanewal (M-4) Motorway, KKH Phase-II Havalian-Thakot, Lahore-Multan Motorway (M-3 section), Sukkur-Multan section of Peshawar-Karachi motorway project, and several others.
Read:
Govt shares details on funds released under PSDP during FY2019-20
Official sources also highlighted that due to the global COVID-19 situation, some projects did face delays, but the departments concerned would the working on these soon.

title: Budzar orders completion of preparations regarding the development of Lahore Master Plan
developer: Wednesday to review matters regarding the Lahore Development
full_text:
Lahore: Punjab Chief Minister (CM) Sardar Usman Buzdar chaired a meeting on Wednesday to review matters regarding the Lahore Development Authority (LDA) and ordered the early completion of Lahore’s master plan preparations, according to news sources.
Read:
PC-1 for LDA City Naya Pakistan Apartments project approved
The CM maintained that through the ‘holistic reforms in LDA’ more projects are being initiated to facilitate the people living in the provincial metropolis. To this effect, he stated that the authority’s apartment project will ensure a roof over the low-income segments of the society. Additionally, the was informed that the construction of high-rise buildings has also been permitted in Lahore.
Read:
CM Buzdar inspects Khanki Barrage uplift arrangements
Furthermore, the meeting was briefed that the LDA has been made a public-friendly institute that provides amenities to people on their doorstep.
Buzdar
asked for the strategic recommendations to be presented after the LDA’s jurisdiction is re-evaluated.

title: KP to launch Apna Rozgar Scheme, housing scheme for minorities
developer: He said that the PC-1 of the Annual Development
full_text:
Peshawar: The Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) has announced its decision to launch an ‘Apna Rozgar Scheme’ and a housing project in all divisions of the province for religious minorities, according to a news source published on July 29.
Read:
Jalozai Housing Scheme in final stages of development: KP Minister
The scheme will benefit both the women and youth in the province by providing them with livelihood opportunities. The information was revealed by the Special Assistant to the Chief Minister for Minority Affairs Wazirzda Kalash to the former members of the Peshawar district council from minorities.
The chief minister’s aide said in its initial phase the housing projects will be introduced in Mardan, Hazara, Kohat and Peshawar divisions. Meanwhile, the Apna
Rozgar
Scheme would be introduced for the minorities throughout the province, including the tribal districts. To this effect, PKR 50 million has been allocated for the settled districts and PKR 100 million have been allocated for the tribal districts, he added.
Read:
KP CM orders housing department to launch CPEC City Nowshehra
Kalash said that the government is taking concrete steps for the prosperity and development of the minority segments. He said that the PC-1 of the Annual Development Programme (ADP) schemes for minorities would be prepared and approved by September 2021.

title: PHE Secretary issues instructions to ensure steady supply of water to Gwadar
developer: The meeting was informed that the Gwadar Development
full_text:
Gwadar: Public Health Engineering Secretary Saleh Muhammad Baloch on Tuesday directed the authorities concerned to ensure a steady supply of potable water to Gwadar — a news source reported. Baloch issued these instructions while chairing a meeting to assess the situation of potable water in the city and address any issues related to the matter.
Read:
Gwadar International Airport’s construction work enters second phase
A number of other high officials of the local and provincial government also attended the meeting. Addressing the session, the Secretary further instructed the relevant officials to ensure that Jiwani is also ensured a consistent supply of potable water.
Read:
Gwadar breakwater project to be approved soon: CM Balochistan
The meeting was informed that the Gwadar Development Authority is constructing a 68-kilometre-long water supply line between Gwadar and the Sood Dam, at a cost of PKR 3.8 billion. After the project has been completed, the supply of water from the dam to the city will begin and help significantly address any water issues in the area.

title: LDA empowers town planning wing’s operational authority
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) has proceeded to empower its Directors Town Planning Wing by abolishing its recovery and commercialisation wings; in a bid to streamline the enforcement of its building/commercialisation rules and process the recoveries of various fees, according to a news source published on July 20.
Read:
PC-1 for LDA City Naya Pakistan Apartments project approved
The LDA’s Town Planning Wing has expanded its operations to oversee the matters of approval of building plans, building control, commercialisation, recovery of dues and sealing of illegal commercial use of property. This decision was taken by LDA’s newly appointed Director General (
DG
) Ahmed Aziz Tarrar, who stressed for the director of each wing to enforce rules within his/her jurisdiction.
Read:
High Court bars LDA from commercialising plots in WCHS
To this effect, an official document has redefined powers of Director Town Planning. It stated that different functions of several directorates were overlapping and consequently affecting performance – which is why these reforms were being introduced.
Additionally, the budget target of the (Fiscal Year) FY2020-21 has also been revised upward – from PKR 2.1 billion to PKR 3.1 billion.

title: Uplift schemes of over PKR 1,200mn to be executed in Attock
full_text:
Attock: The District Development Committee (DDC) on Sunday revealed that the Punjab government would execute uplift schemes worth over PKR 1,200 million in the district during financial year (FY) 2020-21, a news source reported. According to details, the provincial government plans to execute 87 uplift schemes in Attock with a sum of PKR 1,277.565 million.
Read:
Groundbreaking held for Hazro, Attock’s low-cost NPHP project
Deputy Commissioner Ali Anan Qamar chaired the DDC meeting while several other officials concerned were also in attendance.
The members of the meeting stated that PKR 302.299 million had been allocated for the execution of five different schemes pertaining to the construction of buildings. They added that there was an allocation of PKR 1695.191 million for 23 public health projects, along with PKR 339.041 million for six different sports facilities in various towns of Attock.
Read:
Govt to generate PKR 100bn via privatisation of state-owned entities in FY2020-21
Meanwhile, PKR 5952 million has been reserved for 25 projects related to the construction of highway roads and 2757.105 million for the execution of four schemes for improving the irrigation system in the district.

title: Consultation underway to finalise Faisalabad Master Plan 2040
full_text:
Faisalabad: Faisalabad Development Authority (FDA) Director General (DG) Muhammad Sohail Khawaja has revealed that consultation with stakeholders is currently underway to finalise the city’s Master Plan 2020-40, a news source reported on Wednesday (July 22). The DG also mentioned that the development authority had collected the data on the city’s future requirements to address its incumbent shortage of civic facilities.
Read:
Speaking to the officials working on the formation of the master plan for the next 20 years, Khawaja said that the plan will pave way for introducing organised and sustainable development projects to modernise the industrial city.
‘Being the third largest city of Pakistan, Faisalabad needs a strong basis for modern and reliable developments in order to meet its growth targets, and for this purpose, the Master Plan 2040 will provide the required foundation,’ he highlighted.
Read:
Under the said plan, the authorities intend to make Faisalabad a ‘city for all’. In this regard, special focus will be laid on making it ‘greener’, central industrial city will have all the required facilities to provide a dependable civic infrastructure and employment opportunities for everyone. The director general further added that the master plan will assist in the planned industrialisation growth, along with the establishment of special economic zones (SEZs).

title: Construction of Ratodero-Gwadar Motorway M-8’s Hoshab-Khuzdar section to begin soon
developer: PKR 4 billion for the project in the Public Sector Development
full_text:
Islamabad: The National Highway Authority (NHA) on Sunday announced its decision to commence with the construction of the Hoshab-Khuzdar section of the Ratodero-Gwadar Motorway M-8 soon, a news source reported.
Read:
Work on M-8 to resume on ‘top’ priority: CPEC Chairman
NHA officials revealed that the authority intended to begin construction work on the Hoshab-Awaran-Khuzdar section. They stated that the federal government had allocated PKR 4 billion for the project in the Public Sector Development Programme 2020-21. They added that NHA would complete the construction within a time frame of 42 months.
An official of the NHA said that the Executive Committee of National Economic Council (ECNEC) had recently provided its approval to the construction of this significant section of the Ratodero-Gwadar Motorway M-8.
According to details shared, the Central Development Working Party (CDWP) has recommended the project to ECNEC at a rationalised cost of PKR 25.8 billion – excluding the foreign exchange component by deleting the security cost worth PKE 207.4 million.
Read:
NHA to upgrade Shikarpur-Rajunpur section of Indus Highway N-55
On the other hand, the Balochistan government has agreed upon the provision of security and transfer of ownership of the existing track from Hoshab to Awaran to NHA free of charge.

title: Leh Expressway to feature 100-km-long ‘Islamabad-Rawalpindi Circular Railway’ line
developer: Punjab government and the Capital Development
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The authorities concerned on Sunday revealed that the Leh Expressway would feature a 100km-long Islamabad-Rawalpindi Circular Railway line, a news source reported. To this effect, the Punjab government and the Capital Development Authority (CDA) recently signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with a Chinese construction company.
Read:
Railway track part of Leh Expressway project: RDA chairman
The Islamabad-Rawalpindi Circular Railway line would fall between the twin cities and the New Islamabad Airport. Based on Clean and Green initiative, the project would not use petrol or diesel, and run completely on electricity instead. The track would run beside the Leh Expressway and all the industrial units and localities would connect to it.
Officials stated that the services would be quite affordable and the route would be from Saddar to Pak Secretariat and end at the airport. It will feature mini stations on all significant points along this route.
Read:
Leh Expressway design contract awarded to NESPAK
Project Focal Person Mir Atiq ur Rehman revealed that the feasibility study for the track was underway and would reach completion by February 28, 2021. He added that following the study’s completion, they would forward the project to Working Group JCC – with possibility of inclusion in CPEC. He said that construction work would also begin next year.

title: RDA invites RFPs for Fawara Chowk parking plaza extension
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) has invited requests for proposals (RFPs) for the ‘hiring of a transaction advisor’ for the construction of two additional storeys on top of its parking plaza in Fawara Chowk – on a public-private partnership (PPP) basis, according to a new source published on July 26.
Read:
RDA shares list of approved housing schemes in Rawalpindi
The request for proposals is invited from renowned, dynamic and experienced consulting firms or joint ventures – under the Punjab Procurement Rules 2014 (PPRA). The hired firm is required to offer transactions and technical advisory services for legal, financial and technical project aspects – which is to be constructed on a PPP mode.
Read:
RDA auctions off parking stands in Raja Bazaar
Moreover, the interested firms can obtain/purchase set of RFPs (on request) from the office of Deputy Director (Engineering) for a fee of PKR 2,500. However, the proposals for parking plaza extension should be completed and submitted on or before August 18.
Previously, the civic authority had floated tender for the construction of additional floors and announced that the PKR 10.33 million contract for the
parking plaza
extension will be awarded for two years on a time-sharing basis.

title: PC-1 approved for construction of Rawalpindi Ring Road project
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Punjab government on Sunday provided its approval to the PC-1 for the construction of the Rawalpindi Ring Road project, a news source reported. The provincial executive approved the PC-1 for the 51-km-long route connecting Radio Pakistan Building on GT Road with the CPEC Route of the project under phase 1 at a cost of PKR 1,300 million.
Read:
RDA authorised as executive agency for development of RRR project
According to details, the Punjab government would provide funds for land acquisition, build-up property, and transfer of services. Meanwhile, the authorities concerned would complete the Rawalpindi Ring Road project on a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) mode.
Read:
Proposals invited from private societies for construction of interchanges on RRR
The Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) would play the role of the project’s executing agency. On the other hand, the Project Management Unit (PMU) established for the construction would work under the supervision of Project Director and Rawalpindi Commissioner Captain (retired) Muhammad Mahmood. Sources revealed that the project would collectively feature nine interchanges as well as separate tracks from small and heavy vehicles.

title: DWP approves 19 uplift projects for KP
full_text:
Peshawar: The Provincial Development Working Party (PDWP) approved 19 uplift projects on Thursday for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) with worth a total of PKR 26.66 billion, according to news sources. These projects are related to agriculture, forestry, elementary & secondary education Department (E&SE), health, multi-sectoral development, urban development, relief & rehabilitation, auqaf, Board of Revenue, road infrastructure, water, and power.
Read:
CDWP sanctions 7 projects, submits 2 for ECNEC’s approval
The first session of PDWP meeting was presided over by Additional Chief Secretary Shakeel Qadir Khan and mulled over 30 uplift projects –approved 19 and recommended 3 projects for Central Development Working Party (
CDWP
). The meeting deferred 8 projects.
Some of the approved projects are Merged Areas Integrated Development Forestry Project, Mini Zoo at Kanju Township in Swat and execution of feasibility study/establishment of the University of Engineering and Technology (UET) in Swat.
Read:
PDWP approves 29 development projects in KP
The projects approved for multi-sector development includes clearance of unresolved liabilities of contractors, arbitration awards, compensation to the affectees and payment of amounts as decreed by the court.
Furthermore, the meeting also approved the contribution to the Prime Minister’s National Agriculture Emergency Programme (with focus on merged districts) – under the Accelerated Implementation Programme (2020-21).

title: Khanpur Dam authorities retrieve illegally occupied land
full_text:
Haripur: The Khanpur Dam authorities on Wednesday reclaimed area spanning to 150 kanals from an illegal occupant, according to the news sources.
Read:
Authorities open Khanpur Dam spillways for second time in one week
Water & Power Development Authority (WAPDA) Sub-divisional Officer at Khanpur Dam Mohammad Bashir said the reclaiming of the land was conducted following the Supreme Court’s (SC) verdict. He revealed that the land on the left bank of Khanpur reservoir was illegally occupied by an individual since 2007, constructed a farmhouse and refused to vacate despite issuance of repeated notices.
Read:
Monsoon rains fill Simly, Khanpur, Rawal Dams
The apex court presided over the case and after listening to the arguments from both the sides, the verdict was given in favour of the
Khanpur dam
authorities. The dam authorities on Wednesday razed the grey structure of the farmhouse built on the reacquired land.

title: Faisalabad Master Plan (2020-40) scheduled for implementation next year
full_text:
Faisalabad: Faisalabad Development Authority (FDA) Director General (DG) Muhammad Suhail Khawaja on Wednesday revealed that the city’s Master Plan (2020-2040) is all set for implementation next year – after the authority gives it some final touches (expected within a timeframe of six weeks), according to news sources.
Read:
FDA to propose Techno Park, Faisalabad Ring Road, other projects to Punjab govt
Khawaja revealed this after meeting with the consultants working on the preparation of the city’s masterplan. He said that necessary data and the requirements for additional development had been collected, and consultation with the stakeholders will be soon be initiated to finalise the comprehensive plan.
The director general further said that
Faisalabad
, being the third largest city of Pakistan, requires a sustainable and strong management system to reach advanced development and the masterplan is aimed at providing the foundation for this development. He revealed that Faisalabad’s masterplan is labelled ‘city for all’, under which the socioeconomic opportunities and employment generation has attained special attention.
Read:
WASA, PHA, FWMC, MCF team up to make Faisalabad green, improve civic facilities
Moreover, he said that the masterplan will involve strategies for development of commercial, industrial, economic, agricultural sectors. He also said that the creation of roads network, energy, transportation, waste management, sanitation, landscaping and other infrastructure will be developed by devising rules for the use of land.
Furthermore, the city’s plan will encompass zoning facilities to promote the business community for the multi-dimensional development of many sectors.

title: PM chairs NCC meeting on construction sector, issues major directives
full_text:
Islamabad: Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan has directed the chief secretaries of all the provinces to submit a roadmap for introducing ‘one-window facility’ and online approvals of ‘permits, fee payments and parallel working of all departments related to the housing sector’ within a week, according to a news source published on July 24.
Read:
Efforts underway to acquire land for construction of Pakistan House in Makkah, Madina: Qadri
Khan was chairing a meeting of the National Coordination Committee (NCC) on Housing, Construction and Development. He directed for the completion of the government’s approvals like no-objection certificate (NOCs) and others, within the communicated time frame. He warned that the officials found negligent in their duties or causing unnecessary hurdles will be strictly dealt with.
Read:
Registration deadline set for developers looking to avail construction industry amnesty scheme
While addressing the meeting, the premier said that the government is resolved to offer ease and provide facilitation to a maximum number of people who are availing the incentive package formulated for the construction sector. He called for the utilisation of Information Technology tools in all levels of the construction sector – to make it swift and easier.
Regarding the mortgage facility for low-cost houses’ construction, Khan directed the State Bank of Pakistan (
SBP
) and the Ministry of Finance and Revenue to finalise the process to offer a subsidy to banks.

title: PDA directorate gets hold of land to develop Regi Model Town sports complex
full_text:
Peshawar: The Peshawar Development Authority (PDA) has handed over 350 kanals of land to its Land Directorate for the development of a sports complex in Regi Model Town, a news source reported today (July 23). In doing so, the authority acted upon the instructions issued by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Chief Minister (CM) Mehmood Khan to this effect.
Read:
Regi Model Town: Jirga formed to address land disputes
Earlier in June, the chief minister had directed all the concerned departments to finalise the plan on provision of civic amenities in Regi Model Town within 10 days, which included provision of electricity, gas, healthcare, recreational, and educational facilities. Responding to the CM’s directives, the departments and officials concerned sped up the process to address these issues.
Read:
PDA to provide utility services to Regi Model Town on urgent basis
The latest development in this regard is that the PDA Land Directorate got hold of the 350-kanal land for development of the sports directorate in Regi Model Town. Sources also claim that an official notification of land allocation for this facility has been issued. Not to mention that the chief minister had also issued directives in the past to provide modern sports facilities to the residents of Peshawar.

title: Govt to include 8 new infrastructure projects into CPEC
full_text:
Islamabad: The federal government is looking to include eight new infrastructure projects in the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) framework 2020-22, according to a news report published on July 21. The projects will be presented before the 10th meeting of the Joint Coordination Committee on CPEC later this year.
Read:
Bidding process for CPEC western route in progress: Bajwa
The projects to be included are:
Greater Peshawar Mass Transit Project
82-kilometre Swat Expressway Phase-II
Karachi Port Development Project
105-kilometre Thar-Chor Railway Line
22-kilometre Hub-Karachi Railway Line
Keti Bandar Port Development Project
182-kilometre Karachi-Quetta-Chaman Motorway
Optical Fibre Phase II
Read:
Iran, China trade to strengthen CPEC, Gwadar: Mushahid
The infrastructure projects that have already been completed, approved or are being constructed under CPEC include:
Sukkar-Multan (M-5) Motorway
Sukkar-Hyderabad (M-6) Motorway
Hakla-Dera Ismail Khan section
Zhob-Dera Ismail Khan segment
Zhob-Quetta section
Orange Line Metro Train in Lahore
Havelian-Thakot highway projects

title: DHA Quetta to award tender for construction of ‘DHA Expressway’ soon
payment_plan_text: shared in several national dailies today (July 22). | Read: | DHA Quetta announces deadline for second down payment | The bids were opened in the presence of all the firms who had participated in the tendering process. While the news report referenced does not make any mention of the company that has been awarded the contract, it does reveal that the construction work at the site of the DHA Expressway is scheduled to start after Eid-ul-Azha (which further indicates that the project contract is to be awarded soon). | Read: | DHA Quetta floats tender for construction of Expressway, road network in 4 sect
full_text:
Quetta: The Defence Housing Authority (DHA)-Quetta has opened the bids submitted by contracting firms interested in pursuing the construction of ‘DHA Expressway’ proect – and is, apparently, close to awarding the contract for the project’s development, according to a news report shared in several national dailies today (July 22).
Read:
DHA Quetta announces deadline for second down payment
The bids were opened in the presence of all the firms who had participated in the tendering process. While the news report referenced does not make any mention of the company that has been awarded the contract, it does reveal that the construction work at the site of the DHA Expressway is scheduled to start after Eid-ul-Azha (which further indicates that the project contract is to be awarded soon).
Read:
DHA Quetta floats tender for construction of Expressway, road network in 4 sectors
The news report also details that the construction work at the entrance gate of DHA Quetta would also resume after the said festivity.
Earlier on July 4, DHA Quetta revealed via its Facebook page that, following the initiation of development work at the society’s main entrance, the authority would commence with the Stage-I development work in its Phase I residential sectors; for which it intends to complete the required land transfer process as soon as possible.
Read:
DHA Quetta resumes file verification operations in all offices; shares SOPs
According to the post, the last date for the completion of the land transfer process has been set for July 31. Additionally, any files issued against the property transferred after this date would not be accommodated under the sectors developed under Stage-I.

title: RDA mulls allocating treatment plant’s land to private real estate developer
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) is considering a proposal to allocate 5,500 kanals of land near Adiala Village, earmarked for the development of a sewerage treatment plant, to a private real estate developer in exchange for financial assistance required for the
construction of the Leh Expressway project
, a news source reported.
Read:
Leh Expressway land demarcation completed; ban imposed on property sales
It is pertinent to mention here that the Punjab government in the past turned down the RDA’s request for using the aforementioned land for developing a private housing scheme, instead of setting up the treatment plant. This particular project was planned to channel Rawalpindi’s sewerage water to the Leh Nullah, where it was to be treated and later used for agricultural purposes.
Sources claim that since the land for the development of this public project was acquired at the government rate back in 2006, using it for the development of a housing scheme might make the original landowners seek the court’s intervention in getting payment for the land at market rate. Based on this, it is unlikely that the provincial government will allow the RDA to hand over this land to a private housing scheme, claim the sources.
Read:
RDA to finalise TORs for awarding Rawalpindi Master Plan contract
As per the information available, the RDA hasn’t been able to find an investor to develop the Leh Expressway project. It now wishes to allocate the sewerage treatment plant land to a private company that can finance the project. At the same time, the provincial government also lacks the funds required to complete the project on its own, and intends to complete the project with the help of private partners.
Sources also claim that the Leh Expressway’s PC-1 will be presented before the Public Private Partnership Authority after Eid-ul-Azha.
Read:
Leh Expressway’s feasibility report sent to PPPPA
According to Rawalpindi Commissioner Mohammad Mehmood, ‘legal assistance has been sought from the Punjab Law Department in order to vacant the said land in Adiala Village for development of a housing scheme’.

title: LDA DG visits entertainment park site in Johar Town, issues instructions
full_text:
Lahore: Lahore Development Authority (LDA) Director General (DG) Ahmad Aziz Tarar on Saturday directed the authorities concerned to devise a plan for the establishment of a world-class ‘Entertainment Park’ in the Johar Town area, according to news sources.
Read:
LDA approves Finance & Trade Center-Johar Town development work
Tarar issued these directions during a visit to the site of the entertainment park in Johar Town. He was briefed by Project Director Abdul Razzak Chohan regarding the project’s development so far. The director general was informed that the park will span over an area of 140 kanals and will require a construction budget of PKR 330 million.
Read:
LDA shares new bids submission deadline for Johar Town theme park project
The project director revealed that the development authority has finalised an international-standard entertainment park and has pre-qualified contractors and engineering firms for the project’s execution. Chohan further said that the tenders will soon be floated.
Read:
LDA begins digitisation of land records in Gulberg, Johar Town, other areas
Meanwhile, he mentioned that the park will include a gym, a jogging track, tennis court, basketball court, and a mini-golf club among other amenities for outdoor games.

title: Tender process for Quetta Master Plan to be completed this month
full_text:
Islamabad: The Balochistan government on Sunday announced that the authorities concerned were scheduled to complete the tender process for the Quetta Master Plan this month, a news source reported. To this effect, a meeting was recently held where the Urban Planning & Development Secretary revealed that the tendering process for hiring the consultant for revising the plan would reach completion by the end of July.
Read:
Balochistan CM orders early implementation of Quetta Master Plan
The meeting discussed the concerns pertaining to the construction of commercial buildings in the residential areas of Quetta. To resolve this issue, the officials concerned decided to amend the relevant rules and regulations of the Metropolitan Corporation Quetta and the Quetta Development Authority.
The session attendees also reached the decision of banning the transfer of residential plots for commercial use in the city. Additionally, it also banded the new constrictions on roads under development as part of the Quetta Package.
Read:
Govt bans construction of plazas on residential plots in Quetta
Reportedly, the Local Government (LG) secretary will head a committee to formulate the rules and regulations for constructing commercial buildings and land zoning of new roads. Meanwhile, the meeting also took notice of the constriction of commercial buildings and plazas in the city violating building codes. The agencies concerned received directives on taking strict action against such buildings.

title: Firdous Market Underpass: Project development completed by 50%
full_text:
Lahore: Lahore Development Authority (LDA) Director General (DG) Ahmed Aziz Tarar paid a visit to the construction site of Firdous Market Underpass on Friday (July 17), where LDA Chief Engineer Habib-ul-Haq Randhawa briefed him regarding the project work at the underpass, which has been completed by 50%, a news source reported.
Read:
Firdous Market Underpass construction: Alternate traffic plan shared
According to Randhawa, piling work on 770 out of a total of 880 piles has been completed, while the rest of the work will be completed in another week. At the same time, theconstruction of the 350-kilometre long retaining wall has also been completed. In addition to that, the Water and Sanitation Authority (WASA) has also completed the work to lay an 18-inch-wide sewerage line
Read:
LDA shares update on development of Firdous Market Underpass
As per the details shared by the LDA Chief Engineering, the following tasks at the Firdous Market Underass construction site are underway:
Digging work at the entry points of the underpass
Demolition of the old drain lines
Relocation of gas supply lines
Read:
Firdous Market Underpass project will be completed in 90 days: LDA VC
After receiving the briefing, the LDA DG directed the project director Iqrar Hussain to take all measures necessary for the timely completion of the project. He also instructed the director to place a proper rain drainage system in order to ensure that the project faces no lags.
