full_text:
Multan: The Defence Housing Authority (DHA) Multan has issued guidelines for sales and purchase of plots to avoid any malpractices and facilitate the members, according to a notification published on the society’s Facebook page today (July 20).
Read:
DHA Multan introduces android mobile application
What are the dos and don’ts of sale and purchase of plots in DHA Multan?
Following are the dos and don’ts of sale and purchase of plots in DHA Multan:
It is pertinent to make the deal through authorised DHA property dealers/real estate agents. The details of these authorised agents are available at the society’s official website
The buyers or sellers should always be present for the property transaction and must abide by the written agreements
Prior to signing the transfer document in front of the Transfer and Record Branch of
DHA
Multan, people should verify the authenticity of the demand draft/pay order
The interest parties should verify the price offered from the market, by inquiring with other dealers
Before making the deal, the mode of payment and schedule should be finalised in writing
Before making the deal, the commission of the dealer should be decided
The sellers must hold the original allotment letter and computerised national identity card (CNIC) at the time and date of the deal. The copies of these documents should be crossed before handing over to the dealer
To confirm the amount on demand draft/cheque, the sellers should contact the relevant bank. If feasible, the buyer and seller should meet before the transfer of the plot.
Read:
DHA Quetta announces deadline for second down payment
The rights should not be given to the dealer for finalisation of sale and purchase of plots
Any paper or affidavit (prepared by the realtor) should not be signed without reading
Do not sign the ‘Biana’ affidavit before finalising terms and conditions of the sale/purchase of the plot
Do not hand over the right to the purchaser for plot sale on Biana/affidavit before plot transfer
Never give up your exact plot number in DHA
Multan
while getting an assessment from the market
You can get more details or address your queries at +92-61-111-111-189 or visit www.dhamultan.org

title: Buzdar approves construction of South Punjab Secretariat, GORs
full_text:
Bahawalpur: Punjab Chief Minister (CM) Sardar Usman Buzdar has approved the summary of the construction of the South Punjab Secretariat, as well as several Government Officers’ Residences (GORs) in Bahawalpur and Multan, for a sum of PKR 4 billion – which is to be allocated under the current fiscal year’s Annual Development Programme (ADP), according to a news source published on July 19.
Read:
Punjab mulls setting up industrial zone along border with Balochistan
The said summary was submitted for approval by Principal Secretary Iftikhar Ali Sahoo. According to the chief minister’s approval, the construction will be executed under the Infrastructure Development Authority of Punjab (IDAP).
The summary’s contents establish that the South Punjab secretariats were planned to be set up in both Bahawalpur and Multan with fully operational departments of planning and development (P&D), finance, police, education, health, irrigation, communication and works, local government, housing, agriculture. Moreover, special directorates and regional offices will be established under the department – each headed by a secretary.
Read:
New infrastructure development projects in Punjab to be completed under PPPPA
The summary highlighted that all the attached departments needed offices for functioning and also requires residential accommodations for the officers. Consequently, for the construction of
secretariat
in Bahawalpur and Multan, suitable locations have been identified and land will be transferred soon.

title: New Blue Area auction concludes on a high note for CDA
full_text:
Islamabad: On the third (and final) day of the auction of commercial plots in the New Blue Area held on Friday (July 17), the Capital Development Authority (CDA) reported on the conclusion of ‘successful proceedings’, according to news sources.
Read:
CDA to offer possession of Park Enclave plots soon
The CDA’s auction accepted record highest offers that amounted to PKR 17.04 billion for the 12 commercial plots in phase two of Blue Area. The board of the civic authority will accord the final approval to the highest bids.
Read:
CDA to offer possession of Park Enclave plots soon
After the auction of
eight commercial plots
for an accumulated PKR 12.76 billion, another four plots were auctioned for PKR 4.25 billion on the last day. CDA Chairman Amer Ali Ahmed expressed gratitude to the investors for their interest and confidence in the government and the authority. He assured the winning bidders that a one-window facility will be offered to facilitate their projects in minimal time. He highlighted that the auction generated more capital than that expected by the authority – more than the sum generated in the whole fiscal year.

title: ECNEC approves Sukkar-Hyderabad Motorway, three other projects
developer: According to Federal Minister for Planning and Development
full_text:
Islamabad: The Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) on Thursday (July 15) provided its approval to the construction of four mega projects including the Sukkar Hyderabad Motorway, a news source reported.
Read:
Baba Ala Dhand Dheri (Chakdara) Interchange on Swat Motorway opens to traffic
The approved projects include the following:
Construction of Swat Expressway’s Chahdara-Fatehpur Section
Development of Sukkur Hyderabad Motorway
Construction of Ratodero Gwadar Motorway M-8’s Hoshab-Awaran-Khuzdar Section
Development of road project linking Khyber Agency and Khyber Pass Economic Corridor
Read:
ECNEC approves Gwadar Eastbay Expressway, Karachi BRT, & other projects
The development cost of the above-mentioned projects is estimated to be PKR 289 billion. According to Federal Minister for Planning and Development Asad Umar, PKR 24 billion has already been spent on
acquiring land
for Sukkur-Hyderabad Motorway, where the land acquisition process is near completion.
Speaking about Ratodero Gwadar Motorway M-8, the minister said that the construction of Hoshab-Awaran-Khuzdar Section will improve road connectivity in Balochistan. ‘The section will play an important role in providing connectivity to the future trade between central parts of the country and Gwadar,’ he said.
Read:
Work on Peshawar-DI Khan Motorway, other mega projects to begin soon
Sharing details on Chahdara-Fatehpur Section of
Swat Expressway
, the minister said that the road will run between Chakdara, Saidu-Sharif/Mingora, Matta, Khawazakhela to reach Fatehpur. This section of the expressway will help harness tourism potential of the region. ‘The Khyber Pass Economic Corridor extension project will National Highway N-55 with Peshawar-Torkham Motorway and further link it with Chimkani and Jhagra’, revealed Umar.

title: POL discovers oil and gas reserves in Kohat
developer: POL tested hydrocarbons discovered in its Development
full_text:
Peshawar: The Pakistan Oilfields Limited (POL) – the country’s leading oil and gas production and exploration firm – on Tuesday discovered oil and gas reserves in the
Kohat
region of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), according to news sources.
Read:
Oil and gas reserves discovered in upper Punjab: Pakistan Oilfields Limited
In its filing to the bourse, the POL has informed that hydrocarbons have been discovered in an exploratory well ‘Mamikhel South-01’ – which was drilled and is undergoing a testing phase.
Read:
PPL discovers hydrocarbon reserves in Kalat
After the discovery of oil and gas reserves in the Kohat, the Drill Stem Test (DST) was conducted at the well to test the Lockhart and Hangu formations; the well has tested for over 3,240 barrels of condensate, 16.12 MMSCF of gas and 48 barrels of water each day. Earlier in March, the POL tested hydrocarbons discovered in its Development Well Pindori-10, which is located in Rawalpindi.

title: PCAA shares construction updates on Gwadar International Airport, other projects
full_text:
Islamabad: The Pakistan Civil Aviation Authority (PCAA) on Monday shared construction updates on the Gwadar International Airport and other projects being developed in the country, a news source reported. According to details revealed, the authority is currently implementing nine projects and has seven more in the pipeline for making improvements to aviation services in the country.
Read:
Work underway on USD 230 mn Gwadar Int. Airport project: Bajwa
Sources revealed that among the ongoing projects, PCAA was executing the construction of the new green field Gwadar International Airport. It is also working on the provision of night-landing facility at the airport. Meanwhile, the upcoming projects include expansion of Quetta, Lahore, and Faisalabad airports, along with the following:
Land acquisition for Mansehra Airport in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
Establishment of Air Traffic Management System at Islamabad Airport
New radar at Islamabad Airport
Replacement of passenger boarding bridges & upgrading other facilities at Karachi Airport
Read:
Balochistan, FGEHA sign MoU for housing schemes in Quetta and Gwadar
For the financial year 2020-21, the federal government has provided funds worth over PKR 1,300 million for executing 15 aviation sector projects under the Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP) 2020-21.

title: KP expedites construction in seven hydel power projects
full_text:
Peshawar: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) government on Tuesday said that it had expedited construction work on seven hydel power projects in the province, a news source reported. According to details revealed, the provincial executive plans to complete work on these projects by the end of this year.
Read:
Funds allocated to supply electricity to villages around Chitral
The Pakhtunkhwa Energy Development Organisation stated that the said seven projects were under construction in the following districts:
Swat
Shangla
Lower Dir
Mansehra
Chitral
Kurram
Officials revealed that these hydel power projects would generate more than 400 megawatts (MWs) of electricity in the province. They added that the projects would also assist in bringing thousands of acres of barren land under cultivation in the respective districts.
Read:
KP govt to complete 672 mini hydroelectric power projects in FY2020-21
In March, the KP government had announced that it would construct 672 mini hydroelectric power projects during the financial year 2020-21. Officials had revealed that the provincial government had also identified the sites for constructing these projects.

title: LDA sets up more counters at one-window cell to ‘trigger’ construction activity
full_text:
Lahore: In following through with Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan’s vision of encouraging the growth of the local construction sector, the Lahore Development Authority (LDA) has established two additional counters at its one-window cell facility to further stoke the city’s developmental run, according to a news source published on July 14.
Read:
LDA directed to meet timelines specified for layout approvals, NOC issuance
The newly-established counters have been operationalised to facilitate the increasing number of applicant’s visits – which have reached from 160 to 200 per day. These visitors are reported to be complying with the government-sanctioned standard operating procedures (SOPs) for coronavirus prevention.
As for now, over 140 applicants can submit their applications at the LDA’s one window cell at Johar Town Office, while 40 applicants can submit their applications for various works at the
LDA
Avenue One office.
Read:
Foundation stone for Lahore Ring Road SL-III project laid: CM Buzdar
Moreover, LDA Director General (DG) Ahmad Aziz Tararb visited the E-Khidmat Markaz at Arfa Kareem Software Park and spoke with the management for closer coordination between the two organisations – in a bid to effectively implement the Prime Minister’s package for the construction industry.

title: Faisalabad SEZs near M-4 to be connected with M-3 via ‘Super Expressway’
full_text:
Faisalabad: The Faisalabad Industrial Estate Development and Management Company’s (FIEDMC) special economic zones (SEZs) located near the Faisalabad-Multan Motorway (M-4) are to be connected with the Faisalabad-Pindi Bhatian Motorway (M-3) through a ‘Super Expressway’ — a news source reported on July 17. This highway stretch will be constructed by the Frontier Works Organization (FWO).
Read:
Faisalabad SEZ to have an expo centre: FIEDMC
Providing further details of the project, FIEDMC Chairman Mian Kashif Ashfaq stated that it would be a 4-lane, 80-kilometre-long road and that it is expected to cost PKR 10 billion. Additionally, the venture will be developed on a Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) basis.
Read:
Faisalabad SEZ to include furniture city
Furthermore, the chairman revealed that the double carriageway road would connect the Sahianwala Interchange with the Jaranwala Interchange. He expected that this would benefit all the special economic zones established in the area, and that the industries would flourish as a result. Moreover, he hoped that it would also benefit the nearly 300,000 locals living in the area.

title: Locals appeal to PM to restart Rawalpindi-Sihala-Kahuta Road dualisation project
full_text:
Rawalpindi: Union council members of Sihala and Kahuta have appealed to Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan to restart the dualisation initiative of the Rawalpindi-Sihala-Kahuta Road through a July 17 publication carried in a local daily.
Read:
WB to fund rehabilitation of 100-year-old road track in Murree, Kotli Sattian
According to the details available, the dualisation project had been approved by the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council back in March 2018. The project had been awarded under the title of “Dualisation of Rawalpindi-Sihala-Kahutr Road” by the National Highway Authority in April 2018.
However, no progress has been made on the project in the two years since — with the venture facing trouble in obtaining relevant approvals from the Planning & Development Ministry. According to the publication, this delay has caused the cost of the project to rise.
Read:
Rawalpindi Ring Road route to feature new city development; project approved
The locals have appealed to the PM to take notice and help relaunch the stalled project, as it is expected to be highly beneficial for the residents of the area.

title: New Blue Area: 2nd day of auction gets tremendous response
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Thursday conducted the second episode of the New Blue Area auction and again received a ‘tremendous response’ from the attending investors, according to news sources.
Read:
CDA webinar held to promote upcoming New Blue Area plots auction
In the two days, of the three-day auction of the commercial plots in New Blue Area of Islamabad, the auction committee has accumulated PKR 12.79 billion so far and has accepted highest bids for eight commercial plots. These plots are large and are located in a prime location of the federal capital.
Read:
‘New Blue Area’ to fetch PKR 15 bn investment; amount to be spent on Islamabad road projects
The CDA committee followed up the auction of four plots PKR
7.25 billion
on day one, with okaying highest bids for another four plots for PKR 5.54 billion. A total of 17 commercial plots are being offered to the developers in the three-day auction.
CDA Chairman Amer Ali Ahmed said that the great response by the investors is a testament to their confidence in the authority and the Government of Pakistan.

title: CM breaks ground for Jalozai Economic Zone
developer: According to reports, the KP Economic Zones Development
full_text:
Peshawar: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister (CM) Mahmood Khan on Wednesday launched the development work on the Jalozai Economic Zone located within the Nowshera district by officiating its ground-breaking ceremony, according to news sources.
Read:
Jalozai Housing Scheme in final stages of development: KP Minister
According to reports, the KP Economic Zones Development and Management Company (EZDMC) is developing the Jalozai Economic Zone over 257 acres of land. The project is likely to generate 5,000 direct and indirect jobs, and is expected to attract an investment of worth PKR 6 billion.
The chief minister called the occasion a ‘historic event which will mark the beginning of the rapid industrialisation in the province’. Given its strategic location, the project will be a game-changer, he added. Khan further planted a sapling on the site to launch the tree plantation campaign under the Clean and Green Pakistan initiative.
EZDMC Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Javed Khattak told the CM that the company is expediting efforts for industrialisation, aimed at the development of a sustainable agro-based industrial ecosystem in the southern part of the province. He also revealed that the company plans to capitalise on the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) route.
Read:
KP to have 4 new economic zones
The official statement issued regarding the
Jalozai Economic Zone
said that the project will accommodate Pakistan hunting and sporting arms cluster. Furthermore, it stated that construction, food processing, pharmaceutical, marble and granite, food packaging and furniture industries will also benefit from the project.
It said that for the provision of all required utilities to the zone, the EZDMC is working on an agreement with the Provincial Housing Authority (PHA) for the supply of 5 to 10 MW electricity from the nearby 132 KV grid station’s 11 KV feeder – planned for the adjoining housing society. Moreover, it was also revealed the EZMDC has subsidised the plots’ process to promote industrialisation.

title: New Blue Area Auction – Day 1: CDA shares details on bids received; generates PKR 7.32 billion
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Wednesday notified the accrual of PKR 7.32 billion realised through the auction of four commercial plots located within the New Blue Area, according to news sources.
This was the first day of the three-day auction. A CDA official expressed gratitude and said that the authority expected to generate PKR 7 billion in three days, which the highest bidders at the
auction
committee made possible on day 1.
Read:
CDA to offer possession of Park Enclave plots soon
According to the auction details, the highest bid of PKR 894.7 million was received for plot number one (spanning over 672.22 sq yds) – at a rate of PKR 1.33 million per sq yd. Meanwhile, plot number 4 measuring 2,000 sq yds secured the highest offer of PKR 2.11 billion at a rate of PKR 10.5 million per sq yd.
Similarly, the plot number 8 (spanning over 672.22 sq yds) was auctioned for the highest bid of PKR 857.7 million, and plot number 9 (spanning over 2,500 sq yds) was auctioned for the highest bid of PKR 3.37 billion.
Read:
CDA approves building plans for 7 real estate projects in capital
Furthermore, the plot number 10 (measuring 3,333.33 sq yds) received the highest bid of PKr 3.18 – but remained to be approved by the auction committee.
The said committee is headed by the CDA Finance Member, with Planning and Design Member, Deputy Financial Adviser among other officials.

title: DHA Peshawar offers incentives on construction of houses
full_text:
Peshawar: The Defence Housing Authority (DHA) Peshawar has announced its decision to offer incentives to plot owners who plan to start living in DHA Peshawar or initiate construction of their houses before June 30, 2021, according to authority’s official Facebook page.
The efforts are geared towards promoting construction activity in the real estate sector in line with Prime Minister Imran Khan’s vision. Moreover, construction of houses and increasing population in
DHA
Peshawar is expected to make the society more attractive for both end users and investors.
Read:
DHA Peshawar extends forms submission deadline for commercial plots
As per the DHA Peshawar official Facebook page, the authority will offer free-of-cost 6kW solar power systems to those who will move to their newly constructed houses in the society before June 30, 2021. At the same time, those who will start construction of their houses before the above-mentioned date will get ‘solar-powered bore’ to draw underground water for domestic and construction-related use.
At the moment, the developer is busy completing development work in society’s Sector C. Development work in Sector A and B has already reached completion and, according to another Facebook post shared earlier on June 29, construction of several houses is underway.
Read:
DHA Peshawar invites EOI for electrification work
Not to mention that DHA Peshawar is the only gated housing society in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) being developed under KP Assembly Legislation Act i.e. DHAP Act 2009.
For more updates from DHA Peshawar, stay tuned to Zameen News.

title: Govt bans construction of plazas on residential plots in Quetta
full_text:
Quetta: The Government of Balochistan on Monday expressed its concern over the ongoing practice of building commercial structures on residential plots in the city; calling for an all-out ban on the issue with immediate effect, according to news sources. This decision was taken during a meeting chaired by Chief Minister (CM) Jam Kamal Khan Alyani.
Read:
Construction work at Sariab Road, Quetta to start this month: Balochistan CM
The meeting also decided to formulate the legislation to amend the rules and regulations of the Quetta Development Authority (QDA) and Quetta Metropolitan Corporation (QMC) for banning the construction of commercial structures in the city’s residential areas.
Read:
Balochistan, FGEHA sign MoU for housing schemes in Quetta and Gwadar
Additionally, the meeting mulled the Quetta city’s master plan and 30 other towns in the province. The secretary of Urban Planning and Development told the meeting members that the hiring of consultant services for the master plan will be completed by the month’s end.
The meeting also banned the construction work on new roads being developed under the
Quetta
package that includes Sariab Road, Joint Road, Sabzal Road, Prince Road and Nawa Killi, Patel Road.

title: Rawalpindi Ring Road route to feature new city development; project approved
developer: While speaking to media, Rawalpindi Development
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Government of Punjab has approved the establishment of a new city near Rawat, along the Rawalpindi Ring Road’s (RRR) route, according to a news source published on July 12. The planned development will fall under the Rawalpindi District’s jurisdiction and will span an area of 6,000 acres.
Sources claim that the authorities concerned have acquired the land for this project. The city will be featuring various amenities and other facilities planned along the route of the RRR will also be in close proximity of the said project.
Read:
RDA shares list of approved housing schemes in Rawalpindi
While speaking to media, Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) Chairman Tariq Murtaza said that the new city will be developed according to the master plan and the foundation stone for the project will be laid in 2020 as preparations are already underway.
As per the details, the new city will feature an underground electrification system, its own dedicated water supply arrangement – along with underground and overhead water tanks. It will be located close to the fruits and vegetable markets already planned along the
RRR route
.
Read:
Property transaction volumes register spike in Rawalpindi
In addition to the above-mentioned facilities, the project will feature a 500-bed hospital, educational institutes and a theme park.
For more details on the project, stay tuned to Zameen News.

title: Construction of parking plaza planned for Murree
full_text:
Lahore: The Punjab government on Friday announced its decision to build a parking plaza in Murree, a news source reported. As per details revealed, this parking plaza would have host approximately 4,000 vehicles on a daily basis.
Read:
Police check posts set up to stop tourists from entering Murree
Punjab Housing & Urban Development Minister Mian Mehmood-ur-Rasheed shared the information on construction of the parking plaza during a meeting of the Murree Improvement Trust. Several senior officials and members of the trust attended the meeting.
During the meeting, the minister also took notice of the encroachments creating traffic problems in the area. He directed the officials concerned to take strict measures for removing these encroachments and pave the way for smooth traffic flow. He added that these measures were necessary for maintaining the beauty of the hill station.
Read:
RDA delays Fawara Chowk Car Parking Plaza auction due to COVID-19 spread
Rasheed also extended his appreciation to Trust members for their efforts in starting development schemes in
Murree
. To this effect, he directed the officials concerned to ensure the completion of these schemes on a timely basis. He also highlighted that the matters related to the Trust were being dealt with in a transparent manner.

title: Railway track part of Leh Expressway project: RDA chairman
full_text:
Islamabad: Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) Chairman Tariq Saleem on Monday informed Railways Minister Sheikh Rashid that the Circular Railway Track was part of the Leh Expressway project, a news source reported.
Read:
Leh Expressway’s feasibility report sent to PPPPA
Rashid chaired a high-level briefing for reviewing the progress on the said project. He stated that its early completion would permanently resolve the flooding issue in Rawalpindi.
During the meeting, Rashid directed the officials concerned to complete the preparations so that the Leh Expressway project could be completed on a timely basis. In response, the officials stated that they would soon have a mechanism ready for constructing the expressway. They added that departments concerned would spend PKR 60 billion on completing this project.
Read:
Railway track planned for coal transportation at Port Qasim
According to details revealed during the meeting, the project would feature construction of roads along the 16-km-long embankments of Nullah Leh. The federal and provincial governments would collaborate to complete the project on a Built-Operate-Transfer (BOT) basis.

title: ICCI asked to submit proposals for SEZ development in Islamabad
full_text:
Islamabad: The Ministry of Planning & Development on Friday asked the Islamabad Chamber of Commerce & Industry (ICCI) to submit proposals for the development of the proposed Special Economic Zone (SEZ) in the capital city, a news source reported. According to details, this SEZ would be part of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) initiative.
Read:
Federal government taking active steps to launch Islamabad and Karachi SEZs
To this effect, an ICCI delegation met with Planning & Development Secretary Mathar Niaz Rana. The delegation discussed various proposals for the promotion of industrialisation in the region. Rana informed the delegation that the ICCI could play a major role by encouraging investors from the private sector to utilise opportunities for business partnerships in CPEC projects.
Rana stated that for the planned SEZ development in Islamabad under CPEC, ICCI should submit its proposal so that the minister could prepare the right policy in this regard. He added that Islamabad needed sector-specific industrial clusters to facilitate local and foreign investors.
Read:
BoI launches SEZs Information Portal, two other online portals
In response, ICCI President Muhammad Ahmed Waheed stated that the planning ministry should play its role in the materialization of the said project to boost industrial activities and create new jobs in the capital city.

title: CM approves RUDA for development of Dubai-like new city near Lahore
full_text:
Lahore: Punjab Chief Minister (CM) Sardar Usman Ahmed Khan Buzdar, on Friday (July 10) provided his approval to the formation of the River Urban Development Authority (RUDA), according to a news source. The authority will be responsible for managing the establishment of a modern, Dubai-like new city along the banks of River Ravi in the north of Lahore.
Read:
RUDA to prepare master plan for new city settlement along River Ravi
The Punjab government will soon promulgate the ordinance for establishment of RUDA while the CM will be the authority’s chairman. The main task of RUBA will be geared towards establishing the new city along the bank of River Ravi. In order to keep the city safe from flood waters, the provincial government will construct three barrages on the river and develop a big lake to meet the water needs of the new city.
Read:
PM directs LDA to take measures for boosting construction activity
RUDA will also work for the rehabilitation of the dying river and turn it into a freshwater body. This will help make the new project a sustainable development. For this purpose, RUDA will also install waste water treatment plants along the river.
Here are some details on the project:
The city will be modelled after Dubai
It will span over an area of 100,000 acres
The project is expected to fetch investment worth PKR 5 trillion from the private sector
The city will feature high-rise commercial, residential and mixed-use buildings
Establishment of the city will help solve several major issues such as the shortage of water, pollution and traffic congestion in Lahore

title: Authorities gear up for launch of Karachi Circular Railway project
developer: The representative of the Sindh Planning and Development
full_text:
Karachi: The city administration has decided to make arragements for the launch of the 44-kilometre-long Karachi Circular Railway (KCR) project – as per the directives of the Supreme Court (
SC
) – in coordination with the Pakistan Railways (PR) and other stakeholders, according to a news report published today (July 13).
Read:
Pakistan Railways to float tenders for rehabilitation of KCR project
The commissioner house issued a press statement on Sunday revealing that a meeting regarding the KCR project was held under the chairmanship of Karachi Commissioner Iftikhar Shallwani at his office to review the project’s progress. The revealed that the meeting made various decisions to remove the hurdles hindering the KCR’s launch.
The meeting ordered for the development work on a 14-kilometre track – to be laid between the city and Orangi Town – and the railway stations, along the route, to be completed within two months.
Read:
KCR to be made fully functional by July 30
Pakistan Railways Divisional Superintendent Arshad Salam Khattak explained to the participants regarding the steps being taken to revive the project. The meeting discussed the issue of the replacement of the sewerage infrastructure at Urdu Bazar (towards Depo Station). The Karachi Water and Sewerage Board (KWSB) was tasked with this initiative.
The representative of the Sindh Planning and Development Department (P&D) briefed the participants about the fencing work along both sides of the route, saying that it will be initiated next week.

title: Chief Secretary visits E-Khidmet Centre to review services for construction sector
developer: He issued directions for Planning & Development
full_text:
Lahore: Punjab Chief Secretary Jawwad Rafique Malik on Saturday reviewed the E-Khidmat Centre established at the Arfa Software Technology Park — with the center featuring 32 new facilities recently introduced to facilitate the construction sector, according to news sources.
Read:
LDA, PITB sign agreement for online map-approval system
The chief secretary inspected various sections of the E-Khidmet Centre and made inquiries from the customers regarding the quality of services. One citizen expressed surprise at the fact that his residential building design was approved within 10 days – without him having to visit the office.
The chief secretary urged the customers to reveal their insights about the improvement of the facilities. He issued directions for Planning & Development Chairman Hamed Yaqoob Sheikh to devise a comprehensive strategy for expanding the scope of the services provided by the E-Khidmet Centre.
Read:
Bids invited for OLMT project operations, maintenance
He expressed an interest in expanding the services in districts through the manual procedure under the
one-window
operation. He added that all these improvements and automated services are being introduced to facilitate the construction sector and simplify the procedure for approvals to bring convenience to the people.

title: PC-1 for New Islamabad Airport’s Metro Bus service prepared
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Sunday revealed that it recently prepared the PC-1 for the operationalization of Metro Bus Services for the New Islamabad International Airport, a news source reported. According to details, the Metro Bus System would run from Peshawar Morr to the airport.
Read:
CDA to run Islamabad Metro Bus Service
According to details, the project’s PC-1 includes fleet acquisition, security surveillance & AFC system acquisition, IT, and construction of allied infrastructure such as command & control centre. The PC-1 also includes the preliminary cost estimation of the project.
While preparing the PC-1 for the airport’s Metro Bus Service, CDA has also included the operations of 30 new air-conditioned buses – preferably electric – that will run on the said route according to a fixed time schedule.
Initially, CDA will act as the executing agency for the project but following the establishment of the Capital Mass Transit Authority, the project will undergo a transfer.
Meanwhile, CDA officials will submit the PC-1 to the federal government for final approval and to secure the release of the required funds.
Read:
Work underway on USD 230 mn Gwadar Int. Airport project: Bajwa
The New Islamabad Airport’s Metro Bus Service will feature a 25.60km-long signal-free corridor from Peshawar Morr to the airport. The corridor will have eight median stations. The National Highway Authority (NHA) would manage the construction of the project.

title: Rawalpindi Ring Road project alignment gets RDA’s approval
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA)’s governing body on Friday provided its approval to the Rawalpindi Ring Road (RRR) project alignment, a news source reported. The decision was announced during the 48
th
meeting of the governing body – chaired by RDA Chairman Tariq Mehmood Murtaza.
Read:
Alignment of RRR project finalised
According to details revealed, the RRR route would begin from Radio Pakistan Rawat N-5 and end at Sangjani N-5. The project also includes the construction of special economic zones (SEZs) along the RRR route.
Apart from approving Rawalpindi Ring Road project alignment, the governing body also sanctioned the Amendment in Regulation 2.5 (A) VI of the Building & Zoning Regulations 2020 pertaining to apartment buildings and auction of lease rights of RDA Properties Regulation 2020.
Read:
Section 4 notification for RRR land acquisition finalised
The director general (DG) of the development authority also presented the budget for the fiscal year 2020-21. Out of the budget worth over PKR 3,500 million, RDA has allocated more than PKR 2,300 million for development works. On the other hand, the RDA chairman expressed his commitment to leaving no stone unturned for serving the public of Rawalpindi.

title: CM Buzdar inspects Khanki Barrage uplift arrangements
developer: Chenab River. With the help of the Asian Development
full_text:
Gujranwala: Chief Minister (CM) of Punjab Usman Buzdar on Tuesday visited the Khanki Barrage to inspect its uplift arrangements, according to a news report. The aim of this trip was to ensure the barrage’s readiness to mitigate the expected negative impact of the upcoming flooding season.
For this purpose, he instructed all relevant line departments to remain alert and meticulously monitor the water levels in the Indus, Jhelum, and Chenab Rivers. The CM also revealed that he would visit and inspect other headworks as well.
Read:
Concerns raised about water wastage in barrages
During the visit, the irrigation secretary told the CM that the authorities had constructed a 27-kilometers (KM)-long road from Wazirabad to the Khanki Barrage. In addition, he informed Buzdar about setting up a vocational center and a recreational park in the area. The secretary also briefed the CM about the water situation of various rivers in the region.
Read:
Census demanded on Sindh Barrage to save delta from destruction
The Khanki
Barrage
was originally constructed in 1892, and lies on the Chenab River. With the help of the Asian Development Bank (ADB), the project has been upgraded and a new barrage has been built there at a cost of PKR 300 million and PKR 21 billion. This will guarantee a flow of 11,500 cusecs in the Lower Chenab Canal throughout the year, and with a constant supply of water to 2,825 water channels along the 4,689-KM-long irrigation system. This means that it will irrigate over 3,301 million acres in Gujranwala, Toba Tek Singh, Hafizabad, Faisalabad, Chiniot, Jhang, Nankana Sahib, and Sheikhupura.

title: Govt shares details on Balochistan’s ‘priority’ road project developments for 2020-21
full_text:
Islamabad: The federal government on Wednesday shared details regarding the Balochistan’s road upgradation and expansion projects to be developed on priority during (Fiscal Year) FY2020-21, a news source reported. Official sources have revealed that the government is prioritising the upgradation and expansion work of the province’s nationalised road infrastructure.
Read:
Balochistan completes Phase 1 of Hanglaj Mandir Link Road project in Lasbela
According to the details available, the government aims to bring Balochistan at par with the developed areas of the country with these projects. In order to achieve this target of developing Balochistan’s road projects, the government has allocated significant funds in the Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP) 2020-21.
The road projects in the province that have received fund allocations under PSDP are as follows:
Zhob to Kuchlak Road
106-km-long two-lane highway from Basima to Khuzdar
Construction of black-top roads from Yakmach to Kharan via Dostain-Wadh-Khurmagai
Qila Saifullah Loralai Waigum Rudd of N-70
Zhob-Mughal Kot section of N-50
Widening & strengthening of Rakhi Gajj-Bewata section of N-70
Construction of Dera Murad Jamali Bypass
Construction of Hoshab-Awaran Section of M-8
Construction of Ziarat Mor-Kech-Harnai Road
Construction of Harnai-Sanjavi Road
Read:
Quetta’s road rehabilitation projects to be completed within 1 year
The government has also made allocations for the dualisation and improvement of the exiting section of N-50 from York to Zhob via Sago. This project will also include the construction of the Zhob Bypass.

title: CDA shares details on bids received for roads improvement project in Sector I-14
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA), in a bid to revive and develop the stalled sectors in the capital city, recently opened several bidding documents submitted for a road infrastructure project in Sector I-14, according to an official statement issued on July 7.
Read:
Umar directs CDA to share report on Islamabad’s water supply system
As per the official notification, the Notice Inviting Tender (NIT) cost of the project was PKR 8.126 million. However, the lowest bid that was submitted to the CDA amounted to PKR 4.656 million – which is 47.4% below the estimated NIT cost.
Under this road infrastructure improvement project, the repair and rehabilitation work of the damaged street and roads’ portions in Sector I-14 will be carried out. The initiative is another part of the CDA’s strategy to develop and uplift the
long-neglected sectors
and infrastructural projects in the capital.
Read:
CDA webinar held to promote upcoming New Blue Area plots auction
Previously in January, the CDA management approved PKR 210.552 million for the provision of gas in the remaining areas of Sector I-14. Additionally, the authority’s Development Working Party (CDA-DWP) in its 45
th
meeting held in October last year approved the PC-I of worth PKR 3112.162 million for the said sector’s development.

title: Centre committed to complete Karachi’s development projects: Umar
full_text:
Islamabad: The Minister for Planning Development and Special Initiatives Asad Umar has stated that the centre is committed to completing all of Karachi’s development projects – a news source reported today (July 10). Umar stated this in a meeting with the Governor Sindh Imran Ismail.
Read:
PM orders expediting Karachi developmental projects
The two officials discussed various matters relating to the Public Sector Development Programme in Sindh. The minister also pledged to complete all projects under Prime Minister’s Karachi mega-projectwithout any delays.
He further said that the central government is awaiting the Sindh government’s response on the K-IV project and that the federal government will provide its share of funds and will expedite the project.
Read:
Centre releases funds for Karachi development projects
The role of Sindh Infrastructure Development Company (SIDCL) also came under discussion. The governor stated that all the projects managed by the company are progressing at a steady pace and will be completed on schedule.

title: Construction work at Sariab Road, Quetta to start this month: Balochistan CM
full_text:
Quetta: Balochistan Chief Minister (CM) Jam Kamal Khan Alyani on Wednesday (July 8) announced that the construction work on the Sariab Road would start during the next 15 days; with work already underway on the development of a 5,000 kilometres long road network in the province, according to a news source.
Read:
Balochistan’s 1,500 heritage sites to be connected with road network
The CM shared this information with the media during his visit to inspect the pace of ongoing development work at various projects, including the Nawa Killi Bypass, Urak Road, and Airport Road; as well as to monitor the beautification initiative geared to uplift Quetta’s outlook.
Speaking on the occasion, the CM stressed the need for the timely utilisation of the development funds allocated by the federal government under Public Sector Development Programme; directing the authorities concerned to share a monthly review report on their expenditure. He further ordered the officials to increase coordination among the departments concerned to complete the development work of ongoing schemes.
Read:
Development work underway on Balochistan’s Kashmore-Suhbatpur Highway
Alyani additionally warned the officials that unnecessary delays in the completion of the development schemes would not be tolerated; cautioning of legal penalties in any instances of tardiness. He revealed that the Balochistan government had already suspended a number of executive engineers and sub-divisional officers on accounts of negligence.

title: Gulpur Hydropower Project begins contributing to national grid
full_text:
Lahore: NESPAK Managing Director (MD) Dr Tahir Masood on Wednesday stated that the Gulpur Hydropower Project had started contributing electricity to the national grid, a news source reported. He added that after obtaining the due certification for commercial operation, the project had commenced with adding cheap electricity to the network.
Read:
ECC approves development of Kohala, Azad Pattan hydropower projects
According to the details available, the Gulpur Hydropower Project is a run-of-the-river hydroelectric generation plant. It is located on the Poonch River, which is a major tributary of the Jhelum River near Gulpur in the Kotli District of Azad Kashmir. The project received its financing from the Korea Axim Bank, the International Finance Corporation (IFC), the Asian Development Bank (ADB), the Islamic Development Bank, and the ECO Bank. Additionally, NESPAK provided the consultancy services and technical support required for the completion of the project.
Read:
CPEC Update: Suki Kinari Hydropower project to become functional by 2022 end
Sources revealed that the project was developed as part of the federal government’s Policy for Power Generation Projects 2002, as adopted by Azad Jammu & Kashmir (AJK) at a cost of PKR 52 billion. They added that the plant has the capacity to generate an average annual energy of 102 Megawatts (MWs).

title: Construction work on OLMT-Package II stations reviewed
full_text:
Lahore: Lahore Development Authority (LDA) Director General (DG) Ahmed Aziz Tarar on Thursday visited the stations developed under the Orange Line Metro Train (OLMT) project-Package II on Multan Road, a news source reported. During his visit to the project site, the LDA DG reviewed the ongoing construction work.
Read:
OLMT test-run completed successfully, project launch after lockdown
An LDA spokesperson revealed that Project Director Akbar Hussain briefed the DG on the development work on the OLMT project-Package II stations. Tarar also visited the stations in Chauburji/Awan Town. He further inspected the rehabilitation work, following the electrical and mechanical works at these stations, executed by the Chinese contractor CR Norenko.
Chief Engineer Habib-ul-Haq Randhawa apprised the DG regarding the situation of the work being conducted along the OLMT route. He revealed that officers concerned had completed 95% of the work on the ‘eight grade works’ on the OLMT route from Dera Gujran to Ali Town. He added that 95% of the construction work on the route had also reached completion.
Read:
LDA staff to expedite work pace at OLMT, Shahkam Chowk, LDA City other projects
During his visit, Tarar directed the project contractor to complete the ongoing development work on the station building at the earliest, before the beginning of the train operations. He added that this way the public would have access to a complete transport package.

title: KP to complete two hydropower projects by December 2020
developer: MW. Meanwhile, the Pakhtunkhwa Energy Development
full_text:
Peshawar: The Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) plans on completing two hydropower projects – with a combined generation capacity of 60 megawatts (MW) – by December of this year (2020), according to a news source published on July 8.
Read:
ECC approves development of Kohala, Azad Pattan hydropower projects
The details of the hydropower projects, currently under development, in the province are as follows:
10.2MW hydropower project at Jabori in Mansehra
11.8MW hydropower project at Shangla
84MW hydropower project at Gorkan Mittaltan in Swat
40.8MW hydropower project at Koto in Lower Dir
69MW Lavi project in Chitral
300MW hydropower project in Balakot
10.56MW hydropower project at Chapri Charkhel in Kurram district
Read:
PKR 177.5 bn allocated for water sector & hydropower projects under PSDP 2020-21
Out of these seven power generation projects, two will be completed by the end of this year and add 60 MW to the grid. As per the officials, some 84% of the development work on transmission lines has already been completed.
Moreover, the authorities are hiring a consultant for the Chapri Charkhel Hydro Project. The KP power division has also identified four corridors near Dir, Chitral,
Swat,
Mansehra and Kohistan for overcoming the shortfall in electricity production.
The Swat corridor has a total generation capacity of 1,100MW. Meanwhile, the Pakhtunkhwa Energy Development Organisation (PEDO) has already completed a feasibility study for Swat-Mittaltan transmission line – with 84MW power generation capacity.

title: CDA approves building plans for 7 real estate projects in capital
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) Design Vetting Committee (DVC) on Thursday approved the design proposals for seven building developments that fall in line with the government’s efforts to revive economic and construction activity within the capital, according to news sources.
Read:
CDA committee formed to review restoration of cancelled properties
The CDA-DVC meeting was held at the authority’s headquarters and was chaired by a member of CDA Planning and Design. A total of 12 design proposals were on the agenda, seven of which were approved and four designs were rejected due to some shortcomings. The remaining proposal was subjected to non-consideration since the applicant failed to make an appearance.
Read:
CDA board declines suggestion to allocate land for nursery development
The approved designs include proposals for the Pakistan Institute of Development Economics Sector H-11/2, hotels and residential apartments in Islamabad. The
CDA-DVC
has approved design proposals of 16 projects for the capital city – within the past one and a half month. These projects are expected to promote business and investment opportunities in the capital.

title: CDA committee formed to review restoration of cancelled properties
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) Board on Thursday allowed the formation of a committee to scrutinise a proposal concerned with the restoration of cancelled properties – before considering its summary for approval, according to news sources.
Read:
CDA’s letter of acceptance issued for three major projects
A CDA board meeting was held at the headquarters, with CDA Chairman Amer Ali Ahmed in the chair. As per the Restoration Policy 2014, the board is required to restore the properties that have been cancelled for the terms and conditions’ breach of their allotment letters. However, the east wing expressed its wish to amend the policy and delegate the power to a committee or a member. In response, the board permitted for the constitution of a committee instead.
Read:
CDA launches road infrastructure rehabilitation work in Farash Town
Moreover, the board also approved the new dates of the
auction
of 24 commercial plots – to be held this month. In addition, the board also approved the revised budget estimates summary for the fiscal year 2020-21. The board then approved a summary regarding Kashmir Highway’s alignment (from Golra Moor to Grand Trunk (GT Road)) and subjected it to the environmental impact assessment before execution.

title: Umar directs CDA to share report on Islamabad’s water supply system
full_text:
Islamabad: The Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Asad Umar has directed the Capital Development Authority (CDA) to draft a comprehensive report reviewing the rehabilitation, operation and maintenance facets of Islamabad’s water supply system – a news source reported.
Read:
CDA given deadline to revise Islamabad Master Plan, water supply projects
The minister was chairing a review meeting on water supply projects to Islamabad and Rawalpindi from Khanpur Dam. The meeting was briefed on various measures taken to resolve the issues of water supply to the twin cities of Islamabad and Rawalpindi.
Special Assistant to Prime Minister (SAPM) on CDA Affairs Ali Nawaz Awan informed the minister that steps have been taken to enhance the water supply to the twin cities through Khanpur Dam. He also revealed that work is being done for an interdepartmental agreement to facilitate regular maintenance of water channels that run through the territories of Punjab and Islamabad Capital Territory.
Read:
Govt to ensure equitable water supply distribution, completion of ongoing projects in Islamabad
Additionally, the meeting was also informed that CDA is in the process of hiring consultants for its water supply project from Ghazi Barotha.

title: Issuance of notification detailing incentives announced for construction industry urged
developer: Waheed revealed that the Capital Development
full_text:
Islamabad: Islamabad Chamber of Commerce and Industry (ICCI) President Muhammad Ahmed Waheed has called for the departments concerned in Islamabad to issue a notification regarding the implementation of Prime Minister Imran Khan’s incentive package for the construction industry, according to a news source published on July 9.
Read:
Punjab issues notification specifying processing time for housing, construction sectors
Reportedly, the package was aimed at providing a boost to economic activity and investments in the country. The ICCI president stated that it has been three months since the announcement of the said package, yet the lack of an official notification was hindering its proper implementation.  He said that the Punjab government had issued its notification and timelines for the construction sector, and he urged the federal government to do the same at the earliest.
Read:
Govt will protect agricultural land while giving boost to construction sector: CM Mehmood
Additionally, president Waheed revealed that the Capital Development Authority (CDA) Board had approved the industrial building bylaws as well, but the official notification was yet to be issued on the matter. He said that these delays were affecting both industrial growth and the CDA’s revenue generation capacity. He highlighted that the business community was also facing issues in receiving lease renewals from the CDA. He asked for the CDA to issue all the relevant notifications and streamline the lease renewal procedure in order to promote business and economic growth.
Moreover, Mr Waheed said that the materialisation of the Naya Pakistan Housing Programme (NPHP) for low-income segments of the society was important. He further called for Prime Minister Imran Khan to issue directions for the proper implementation of the
construction industry package
.

title: CDA webinar held to promote upcoming New Blue Area plots auction
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Wednesday organised a webinar aimed at getting foreign parties interested in the upcoming auction of commercial plots in the New Blue Area of the city, according to news sources.
Read:
Gulberg Greens Farm Housing Scheme gets CDA NOC
The civic authority plans to auction off 24 plots located in the New Blue Area (the portion of Blue Area adjoining Sector G-9 on the southern side of Jinnah Avenue) this month. This
auction
is part of an incentivised package released under the vision of Prime Minister Imran Khan. The said area has been tailor constructed to attract maximum investment.
The webinar speakers included Chairman Naya Pakistan Housing Authority (NPHA) Lieutenant General (Retired) Anwar Ali Haider, Special Assistant to the Prime Minister (SAPM) for Overseas Pakistanis Syed Zulkfiqar Bukhari, Chairman CDA Amir Ali Ahmed, Member Planning CDA Dr Shahid Mehmood, Town Planning Expert Dr Tariq Habib Malik, and Director Building Control CDA Muhammad Fasil Naeem.
Read:
PKR 50bn allocated for Islamabad Ring Road in FY 2020-21: Minister Sarwar
SAPM Bukhari took the opportunity to state that the location of a project mattered most in the real estate sector, and that the New Blue Area project fulfilled this requirement. He went on to urge expatriate Pakistanis to invest in the project, and said that a dedicated cell had been created to grant approvals — with no delays in this regard to be tolerated. The SAPM further said that the project would enhance business activities in the city and help increase the value of commercial properties.
Other speakers also highlighted the project’s importance and features. Chairman CDA revealed that special building bylaws had been prepared for the project in order to offer more architectural freedom; ensuring that there was a separation between each plot.
Moreover, Dr Shahid Mehmood said that the project allowed for multiple uses for the construction of structures. In addition, he said that plots were between 672 to 10,000 square yards in size in order to provide a variety of options for potential investors.

title: Climate Change Ministry to help provinces mitigate adverse impact of increased construction
full_text:
Islamabad: The Ministry of Climate Change has announced its decision to assist the provinces in introducing alterations in town planning and building systems to control and mitigate the adverse impacts of increased construction and climate change, according to a news source published today (July 9).
Read:
Recreational facilities planned along Clifton Beach pose environmental threat: Experts
To this effect, a draft of recommendations has been formulated in line with the National Climate Change Policy. As per the policy, the provinces will be asked to install wastewater treatment plants as a fundamental part of all sewerage schemes. The recommendations also included separate collection, disposal and reusing recyclables, composite and bio-degradable waste, preferably at the source.
The draft proposal highlighted the need for updated town planning design principles for minimal carbon footprints. Also, it stresses the need for designing zero-emission buildings through renewable energy to utilise the potential of the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM).
Read:
EPA takes up task to purify Islamabad’s environment, water
Furthermore, other issues discussed by the proposal included curbing rural-to-urban migration, infrastructural development and provision of supportive facilities in small agriculture-based towns and periphery urban areas. It stated that a proper land-use planning should encourage vertical planning.
The draft stated that
hazard mapping
and zoning of the area should be made mandatory (prior to the launch of construction work), and if required, the reconstruction in the aftermath of natural disasters should be made climate-resilient.
Additionally, it said that the water heaters based on solar power should be run in residential areas (as per requirement) and large industries should be established in designated areas.
It is proposed for the corporate sector to establish a Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) fund for fuelling the efforts aimed at controlling the carbon footprint.

title: Punjab Cabinet approves establishment of Ravi Urban Development Authority
full_text:
Lahore: The Punjab Cabinet on Wednesday granted approval for the establishment of the Ravi Urban Development Authority (RUDA), a news source reported.
Read:
RUDA to prepare master plan for new city settlement along River Ravi
The RUDA will be responsible to perform various tasks and manage several matters regarding the area falling in vicinity of River Ravi. However, the authority’s most crucial responsibility will be to develop a new city on the bank of the said river. Reportedly, the concerned department has already identified
99,000 acres
of land for the said project, while
section 4 notification
to begin the land acquisition process has also been issued.
Read:
PM orders development of 12 cities along River Ravi
In addition to developing a new city, the RUDA will also be responsible for managing traffic in the area, work on making the river water usable, and take
measures
to stop the river from being contaminated. Furthermore, the authority will work on improving the overall ambience and environment of the area by developing and taking care of the green belts.

title: RDA authorised as executive agency for development of RRR project
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Punjab Private-Public Partnership Authority (PPPPA) has approved to reassign the executive agency role to the Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) for the development of the Rawalpindi Ring Road (RRR) project, according to a news source. The formal decision in this regard was taken in a meeting held yesterday (July 7) with Punjab Chief Minister Sardar Usman Ahmed Khan Buzdar in the chair.
Read:
Proposals invited from private societies for construction of interchanges on RRR
Earlier in March this year, the Punjab Government decided to hand over the RRR project to the Lahore Ring Road Authority (LRRA). For this purpose, the LRRA had set up a project management unit at the Commissioner’s Office and asked the RDA to hand over all documents related to the RRR project.
Later in April, the Punjab government
suspended
the LRRA from taking charge of the ring road project; stating that the decision was based on the amendments that were underway at that time in the LRRA Act.
Read:
RRR, LRR SL-III, 6 other projects to be completed under PPP model during FY2020-21
With RDA once again becoming the project’s executive agency, it is expected that positive developments will take place with regard to the formation of RRR’s PC-I. During the meeting held to formally approve the decision, Punjab CM was briefed that Section 4 notification for land acquisition has already been issued, while issuance of other related notification is still awaited.
Read:
RRR work plan approved; preparation for project launch in full swing
The meeting was also informed that the land acquisition process for RRR project had slowed down due to its transfer to the LRRA.

title: Kacheri Chowk Remodeling project’s feasibility study contract awarded: RDA
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) has awarded the contract for conducting the feasibility study for the planned Kacheri Chowk Remodelling project to the National Engineering Services of Pakistan (NESPAK), a news source reported. The said development was officiated on July 7.
Read:
Remodelling of Rawalpindi Defence Chowk approved to facilitate traffic flow
As per the details available, the RDA made its decision based on the fact that the NESPAK had submitted the lowest bid for the project at PKR 8.5 million. It is pertinent to mention here that the authority had reserved PKR 15 million for conducting the project’s feasibility study.
Read:
Rawalpindi Kutcheri Chowk to be made signal-free; RDA directed to hire project consultant
Reportedly, the feasibility study will help the authorities determine if the construction of underpasses at the said
chowk
will be more feasible than developing flyovers. Determining the most suitable project design will ensure fixing the long standing traffic congestion issues in the city.

title: Proposals invited from private societies for construction of interchanges on RRR
developer: According to sources within the Rawalpindi Development
full_text:
Rawalpindi: Rawalpindi Commissioner Captain (R) Mohammad Mehmood on Friday (July 3) formally sought proposals from the developers of private housing schemes for the construction of interchanges along the Rawalpindi Ring Road (RRR) route, a news source reported.
The purpose of the initiative is to arrange for some financial help for the Government of Punjab to address the traffic issues in the city by providing the required infrastructure facilities. Furthermore, the participation of the private housing schemes’ developers is also expected to increase economic activities in the neighbourhood.
Read:
PKR 50bn allocated for Islamabad Ring Road in FY 2020-21: Minister Sarwar
According to sources within the Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA), the provincial government had decided to return the RRR project’s execution responsibility to the RDA due to resentment expressed by some private firms being engaged for the project. The government had previously announced to handover the project to the Lahore Ring Road Authority (LRRA). Sources also claim that a formal notification in this regard will also be soon issued.
In order to initiate the related developments for the said project’s execution, the Land Revenue Department is currently surveying the area to identify land owned by the provincial government and the private owners.
Read:
Stakeholders invited to benefit from ‘land-use’ plan drafted for developments along RRR route
While presiding over a meeting held to discuss the project, the commissioner said that the project will be developed in
partnership with the private sector
, where the provincial government will manage PKR 8 to 9 billion of the project’s total expense. This amount is in addition to the funds allocated for the purpose of land acquisition.
The commissioner further revealed that all the homework – to help timely launch of the project’s development work – would be completed by the end of this month. Detailing on the project route, he said that the RRR will start on N-5 (GT Road) near Radio Pakistan Building and will end at Sangjani, while passing through Islamabad-Peshawar Motorway M-1 and Lahore-Islamabad Motorway M-2. From Sangjani onwards, it will then merge into the Islamabad Ring Road at Margalla Road.
Read:
RRR: Identification of private lands ordered to compensate owners
The road will have a maximum speed limit of 120 kilometres per hour for cars, allowing motorists to reach Rawat from Tarnol in 1 hour and 14 minutes. The speed limit set for trucks and heavy vehicles is 50 kilometres per hours.

title: CDA opens bids for laying storm drain systems in I-11/1, I-11/2
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has opened bids for laying a storm drainage system in Sectors I-11/1 and I-11/2; with the lowest bid received – so far – being of PKR 61.08 million, a news source reported earlier today (July 6). The said figure is 24.26% lower than the estimated cost of the project.
Read:
CDA to complete balance work on dualization of Service Road in I-10, I-11
According to the details available, the total NIT cost of the project was estimated to be PKR 80.645 million. The use of best practices and the competitive nature of the bidding process meant that the final bid was considerably lower than the estimated cost. The drainage system will now be installed at a cost of PKR 61.08 million.
Read:
CDA floats tender for construction of culverts in I-11/2
The CDA has reinitiated development work in Sector I-11 in order to complete the construction and development work in the area that has been stalled for decades. As a result, the process to install a proper drain water system in order to get rid of storm water from the streets and roads of the sectors will finally be completed.

Multan: The Defence Housing Authority (DHA) Multan management on Wednesday made public announcement of the details of the development charges (and possible discounts) mentioned in allottees’ information/allocation letters, according to the society’s official Facebook page.
Read:
DHA Multan initiates construction of Villas Shopping Mall
The DHA Multan has announced that the development charges will be applicable as follows:
For ballot plot holders and OL/Cash file holders in Sectors M, Q, R, U, H, A and V, the
development charges
will be payable from September 30 – in eight equal instalments that span over two years.

10% rebate on lump-sum payment of development charges till December 31, and 5% rebate on lump-sum payment of development charges till June 30.
