DHA Multan resumes development work
To this effect, the DHA Multan will be sending a formal communication to the concerned members with development charges details and payment schedules.
Recently, the society announced possession in
Sector M
in June and has announced that the developmental work in the other six sectors (Q, R, U, H, A & V) are in full swing.

title: District admins approve 37 small projects for Shangla
full_text:
Shangla: The Shangla district development advisory committee (DDAC) on Wednesday approved 37 small development projects worth PKR 67 million — with the initiative falling under the auspices of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Community-Driven Local Development (CDLD) programme, according to news sources.
Read:
KP govt to connect Malam Jabba with Shangla to boost tourism; project plan approved
The projects were approved in a meeting held at Deputy Commissioner Imran Hussain Ranjha’s office — with the officials and heads of all departments concerned also in attendance. The approved uplift projects for Shangla included schemes related to the development of water supply systems and street pavements. It also included the construction of protective walls, roads, government schools, and an RCC bridge in the area.
Read:
Tree plantation campaign of over 4.5mn saplings launched in Shangla
Reportedly, around 20 projects were approved for the Alpuri
tehsil
, 15 for the Puran tehsil, and two for the Chakisar tehsil.
Meanwhile, the district administration on Wednesday banned cattle transportation from
Shangla
to other districts for three months, under Section 144. The ban was imposed due to public complaints about transportation of sacrificial animals, and the increase in their prices.

title: Land acquisition begins for construction of Oghi-Battal Road, Mansehra
full_text:
Mansehra: The Revenue Department on Thursday launched a land acquisition drive for the development of the Oghi-Battal Road project — with the venture estimated to cost PKR 220 million, according to news sources.
Read:
Saudi Arabia allocates PKR 2.5 bn for gravity flow water project In Mansehra
Member Provincial Assembly (MPA) and District Development Advisory Committee (DDAC) Nawabzada Fareed revealed the project particulars in a media briefing in Oghi. He said that this mega road project had been approved by Chief Minister Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Mahmood Khan and that work on the venture had already been launched. He also took the opportunity to assure that the KP government had also launched additional
road infrastructure projects
in other parts of the province as well.
Read:
NHA clears Sathan Gali Road in Mansehra for traffic
MPA Fareed appealed to the people to extend their cooperation to the Works and Communications Department in clearing their land for the construction of the Oghi-Battal Road in order to ensure the timely completion of the project. He further disclosed that development work on the estimated PKR 40 million worth Gandar Pari Road project had also been launched last month.

title: Leh Expressway’s feasibility report sent to PPPPA
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) has submitted the Leh Expressway feasibility report to the Punjab Public Private Project Authority (PPPPA) for approval, according to a news source published today (July 3). Even though the expressway project had been proposed 12 years ago, its
feasibility report
was prepared only a short time ago.
Read:
Leh Expressway land demarcation completed; ban imposed on property sales
The Leh Expressway project has been delayed in the past due to one reason or another. Lately, the government has expressed a keen interest in developing the project — with the venture aimed at fixing the city’s flooding issue at Nullah Leh and to address the traffic congestion problems in the area.
In order to make the project development feasible, the authority concerned now plans to construct the Leh Expressway under the
private-public partnership mode
. This will also help reduce development costs. The PPPPA will be in charge of carefully scrutinizing the feasibility report to assess if the project is viable.
Read:
Leh Expressway to be made part of CPEC developments
The findings based on this scrutiny will be shared with Punjab Chief Minister Sardar Usman Buzdar, who will take the final decision regarding the execution of the project.

title: KP CM directs for Cities Improvement Project by year end
full_text:
Peshawar: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Chief Minister (CM) Mahmood Khan recently directed the officials concerned to ensure that the groundbreaking for the Cities Improvement Project (CIP) was completed by the end of this year, news sources reported earlier today (July 3).
Read:
KP CM directs uplift measure for housing, construction sectors
As per an official handout, the said directives were given in a meeting chaired by the CM regarding the progress made on the project so far. The KP government is planning to launch a mega scheme aimed at improving and strengthening the municipal infrastructures/services in its
five major cities
; Peshawar, Abbottabad, Mardan, Kohat, and Swat.
Read:
KP to establish ‘Rescue 1122’ service in all merged district tehsils
According to the information available, the CIP project is being launched with monetary assistance from the Asian Development Bank (ADB). Under the Cities Improvement Project, several municipality uplift schemes will be executed in the selected cities to enhance their municipal infrastructure and enhance departmental capabilities.
CM Mahmood Khan instructed the officials concerned to finish the detailed engineering designs for all the CIP sub–projects in order for practical work to be initiated at the earliest opportunity.

title: PM Khan lays foundation stones for interchanges, other developments in capital
full_text:
Islamabad: Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan on Thursday performed the ground-breaking for the Rawal Dam Chowk Interchange, PWD Interchange, the Korang Bridge (at the Islamabad Expressway), and various development works at Sector I-15, according to news sources.
Read:
Govt to set up Gemstone City in Islamabad to promote foreign investment
The PM launched these projects through a video link while chairing a meeting on the ongoing development projects in the capital city. On the occasion, he also received a briefing on the estimated cost of these uplift projects, as well as their estimated completion timelines.
Previously,
PM Khan
had been informed that the Rawal Dam Chowk Interchange would be completed by utilizing the resources of the Capital Development Authority (CDA) — with the initiative to be part of its Traffic Management Solution.
Read:
Smart lockdown imposed in a number of Islamabad sectors
The timeline for the construction of the PWD Underpass and the Korang Bridge will be span over 7 and 15 months respectively. The CDA will execute these projects by utilizing funds from the Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP).
During the meeting, PM Khan also directed the authorities concerned to ensure that the green areas of the Federal Capital were protected while the aforementioned projects are being developed.

title: LDA invites EOI for preparation of Lahore Master Plan 2050
full_text:
Lahore: The Lahore Development Authority has invited expressions of interest (EOI) from reputable and experienced local and international firms for the preparation of the Lahore Master Plan 2050, according to a news report published today (July 3).
Read:
PM Khan directs WASA, Lahore to start work on water treatment plant projects
As per the publication, the chosen firm will be responsible for providing the following services:
Forming a profile of the Lahore region
Preparing inception report
Formulating a strategic development plan
Laying out regional plan and master plans for urban settlements
Implementing framework and guidelines
Monitoring and evaluating the framework
Preparing communication and consultation plan
Read:
MCL approves mega commercial, industrial projects in Lahore
The interested firms with relevant experience in master planning are required to submit their applications within 30 days from the publication of the advertisement. The EOI documents for the Master Plan for Lahore Region (MPLR) – 2050 are available for download at www.lda.gop.pk and www.ppra.punjab.gov.pk.
Read:
LRRA, NLC sign construction agreement for Lahore Ring Road-Southern Loop III
In case of any queries, the applicants can reach the LDA Chief Metropolitan Plan (CMP) via email at mplr2050@gmail.com or contact the CMP office by visiting the LDA office: 467-D/II, Khayaban-e-Firdousi, M.A Johar Town, Lahore. Phone: +92-42-9926-2332.

title: CDA’s letter of acceptance issued for three major projects
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Wednesday issued a letter of acceptance for three major projects in the capital city, a news source reported. The civic body issued the letter to a Karachi-based construction company that had recently won contracts for Rawal Dam Interchange, Korang Bridge expansion, and PWD Underpass.
Read:
PM to inaugurate three infrastructure projects in Islamabad
Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan is expected to inaugurate all three Islamabad developments today via online correspondence.
According to details revealed, the Rawal Dam Interchange would be constructed on the junction of Murree Road and Park Road – also known as the Rawal Dam Chowk. CDA will execute the project with its own funding. Meanwhile, the PWD Underpass construction and Korang Bridge expansion will take place on the Islamabad Expressway.
Read:
Budget 2020-21: Funds earmarked for several mega projects in Islamabad
CDA officials stated that once these three development projects reach completion, they expect to prevent traffic congestion in their vicinities. CDA spokesperson Mazhar Hussain also confirmed the issuance of bid acceptance letter for all three developments to the successful bidder.

title: Funds allocated for road projects in Malakand, Hazara
full_text:
Peshawar: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) government on Monday allocated funds for several road projects in order to promote tourism in Malakand and Hazara divisions, a news source reported. To this effect, the provincial government has announced its decision to spend PKR 4,400 million on the repairs and construction work on different roads in the two divisions.
Read:
KP tourism body reviews proposal for setting up Kalam Development Authority
According to details, the KP government aims to revive tourism in the province in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic. For this purpose, the provincial government has allocated significant amount of funds in the financial budget 2020-21. This amount includes funds for repairing and constructing the communication infrastructure for tourist destinations in Malakand and Hazara.
On the other hand, the KP government has allocated PKR 3,000 million for developing tourist sites in Tirah Valley of Khyber, Parachinar in Kurrum, Samona in Orakzai, North Waziristan, and South Waziristan. Meanwhile, the federal government has directed the provincial government to prepare the master plans of five feasibility studies for the development of tourism resorts at Kohi Suleman in Dera Ismail (DI) Khan, Chapri Parachinar in Kurrum, Sheikh Badin, and Takhat Bhai in Mardan districts.
Read:
KP tourism development attracts Sweden’s interest
Sources said that KP government was going to prepare these master plans on the pattern of Integrated Tourism Zones. They added that camping huts had been established in the remote scenic areas of the province for addressing the residential problems faced by domestic and foreign tourists.

title: Developers of private housing schemes directed to install water treatment plants
full_text:
Rawalpindi: Commissioner Muhammad Mehmood has directed the developers of private housing schemes in all four districts of the city to install water treatment plants in their projects, a news source reported. The commissioner issued this instruction while presiding a meeting of the Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA)’s officials on Tuesday.
Read:
Excise Rawalpindi gears up to bring recently constructed properties under tax net
The commissioner further ordered that developers of private housing schemes to install a proper sewerage system in their respective projects. For facilitating these measures, he directed the RDA officials to finalise SOPs to ensure the implementation of the Commissioner Office’s directives.
Commissioner Mehmood further warned the officials that no negligence will be tolerated with developers using delaying tactics to install water treatment plants and lay proper and sustainable sewerage lines in accordance to the future needs of the societies’ residents.
Read:
RDA shares list of approved housing schemes in Rawalpindi
A few days ago, the commissioner
warned
the owners of private housing schemes against carrying out development prior to procuring an NOC from the RDA. He also mentioned that the government is making complete efforts to promote activity in the construction industry to create jobs and facilitate investors.

title: Govt keen on providing gas countrywide by year-end: Zulfi Bukhari
full_text:
Lahore: Special Assistant to the Prime Minister (SAPM) on Overseas Pakistanis & Human Resource Development (HRD) Zulfi Bukhari on Saturday revealed that the government was keen on ensuring countrywide gas provision by the end of the going year, a new source reported.
Read:
SC orders SSGC to ensure gas supply to areas near extraction fields
The SAPM expressed these remarks on countrywide gas provision after attending the ground-breaking ceremony of gas supply to Dhok Loharan. Managing Director Sui Northern Gas Pipeline (SNGPL) was also present on this occasion.
Read:
Work on Kohat gas supply project initiated
During his visit to various areas of Attock City, he ordered the Sui Gas Managing Director to ensure gas supply in these areas on a priority basis. He also the official concerned to resolve public issues regarding the installation of gas meters. Bukhari revealed that the government would soon provide gas connections to the villages of Jand Tehsil situated within a 5km radius of Dakhni Oil Field. He added that the installation of gas meters in Chhapri Village would begin next week, which would benefit hundreds of families residing within the area.

title: Ammar Chowk Remodelling: Local admin mulls transferring project to RCB
developer: Ammar Chowk Remodelling project from the Rawalpindi Development
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The local administration is considering transferring control of the Ammar Chowk Remodelling project from the Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) to the Rawalpindi Cantonment Board (RCB) — a news source reported.
Read:
RDA sends revised PC-I for Ammar Chowk to cabinet
The PKR 785 million project is aimed at remodelling and expanding the city’s Ammar Chowk. Now, the authorities concerned are set to hold a meeting over the possibility of transferring control of the venture from the RDA to the RCB. However, the Punjab government is looking to transfer funds for the project to the RCB via the RDA for administrative reasons, which is causing undue complications. As it stands, the project has been allocated PKR 150 million during the current fiscal year.
According to RDA officials, the project needs to be transferred to the RCB for security concerns that need to be handled by the cantonment board.
Read:
Remodelling of Ammar Chowk to begin next month
The project had been launched previously as well, but had been dropped at a later date. However, this fiscal year it has been included in the Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP) and funds have been allotted for its completion.

full_text:
Karachi: The Karachi Metropolitan Corporation’s (KMC) current city council on Monday passed the last annual budget of its tenure — worth PKR 24.84 billion — for (Fiscal Year) FY2020-21, according to news sources.
In this budget, no new taxes are introduced and the KMC city council meeting was held and approved in the council hall of the Old KMC building on MA Jinnah Road, under the chair of Karachi Mayor Wasim Akhtar. The budget was characteristically surplus.
Read:
KMC defers rent payments in 43 markets; introduces four-month instalment plan
According to the budget document, the municipal administration’s total estimated budget is PKR 24.845 billion and the current receipts in the budget are PKR 20.67 billion, whereas the capital receipts are PKR 1.66 billion. The city council allocated PKR 2.5 billion to the Annual Development Programme (ADP) and PKR 15.57 billion as establishment expenditures.
Additionally, PKR 200.96 million were allocated for repair and maintenance, and estimations for development works are PKR 4.38 billion.
Read:
Operation against hazardous structures underway in KDA, SBCA & KMC-administered areas
The
mayor
said that PKR 680 million are earmarked for the repair and maintenance of the city’s infrastructure. The Special Development Project and Nehr-i-Khayyam will receive PKR 120 million each. PKR 100 million has been earmarked for the Kidney Hill Park. For the uplift of the Shahabuddin Market Parking Plaza, PKR 300 million is allocated; and PKR 100 million (each) is allocated for the uplift/lightening of major city arteries and various parks.
For the cleanliness of drains, the council has allocated PKR 100 million. PKR 75 million is earmarked for maintenance of underpasses, flyovers, and bridges. The sum of PKR 75 million was earmarked for the uplift of landfill sites, construction of a fire station and Zulfikarabad Oil Tankers Parking Terminal’s phase II.
Furthermore, the KMC allocated PKR 52 million to fund the development initiatives at the zoos and the Safari Park, while PKR 50 million has been allocated for the purchase of various birds and animals.

title: WAPDA, GB Scouts sign MoU for Diamer Bhasha Dam project security
full_text:
Lahore: The Water & Power Development Authority (WAPDA) and the Gilgit Baltistan (GB) Scouts on Monday signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for Diamer Bhasha Dam project security, a news source reported.
Read:
Work on Diamer Bhasha Dam continuing well despite pandemic: Vawda
Under the agreement, GB Scouts would raise a GB Scouts Wing for the purpose of Diamer Bhasha Dam project security. According to sources, the new security wing is a significant step towards the implementation of the dam project. They added that due to the remote area chosen for the project’s construction, it was important to have adequate security measures available for its smooth and timely completion.
Moreover, the GB Scouts Security Wing would provide a secure and safe working environment at the project site. The scouts would utilise their professional capabilities for placing an effective security mechanism within the area.
Read:
Construction machinery reaches Diamer Bhasha Dam site: Vawda
The Diamer Bhasha Dam is under construction on River Indus and scheduled for completion in 2028-29.

title: RRR: Authorities mull constructing interchanges with help from private societies
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The authorities concerned are considering the construction of two new interchanges on the Rawalpindi Ring Road (RRR) route through collaborations with private housing scheme developers, a news source reported.
The proposal was shared in a meeting held yesterday (June 28) to discuss various aspects of the planned project. Rawalpindi Commissioner Capt (R) Muhammad Mehmood presided over the session.
Read:
RRR: Identification of private lands ordered to compensate owners
The suggestion to bring the developers of private housing societies on board for the
construction of interchanges
along major road avenues in the city was first shared by the Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) earlier this month. According to sources within the authority, the purpose of this collaboration is to reduce the traffic load on city roads, and to help finance the requisite infrastructural developments.
As per the details available, the proposed interchanges will be developed at the ring road’s starting point near Radio Pakistan Building on GT Road, and at the ending point on Sanjani Interchange on the Lahore-Islamabad Motorway M-2.
Read:
RRR, LRR SL-III, 6 other projects to be completed under PPP model during FY2020-21
Reportedly, Punjab Chief Minister Sardar Usman Buzdar will give the final approval for the construction of these interchanges under the private-public partnership model.

title: PM to inaugurate three infrastructure projects in Islamabad
full_text:
Islamabad: Officials of the Capital Development Authority (CDA) have said that Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan is expected to perform the groundbreaking for three road infrastructure projects in the capital city on June 30, a news source reported.
Read:
Govt to set up Gemstone City in Islamabad to promote foreign investment
Khan issued instructions for early completion of the projects that include Rawal Dam Interchange, Korang Bridge and the
PWD Underpass
on Islamabad Expressway. The construction of the PWD underpass will render the Express Highway of the capital to be a signal-free corridor. The contract for these projects in Islamabad was awarded to the joint venture of Maqbool Associates and Calson.
CDA Planning and Engineering Member Shahid Mehmood said that the joint venture would also see to the legal and other formalities, upon the projects’ completion. He also that the extension of the Rawal Dam Interchange was needed to ease the congestion on Park and Murree Roads.
Read:
PC-1 approved to initiate development work in I-12, Rawal Chowk
Reportedly, the joint venture of Maqbool Associates and Calson won the contract by bidding 11%, 17% and 19% for the Rawal Dam Interchange, Korang Bridge and PWD Underpass, respectively.
Meanwhile, the development authority is currently working to complete the underpass connecting Sector G-7 and Sector G-8 on Faisal Avenue.

title: CDA launches road infrastructure rehabilitation work in Farash Town
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has initiated road infrastructure rehabilitation work in the Farash Model Urban Shelter Project, according to a news report published on Sunday (June 28).
Read:
Four ration warehouses to provide food essentials to needy in Islamabad
The project will be the first uplift scheme in the area after two years. As per the official CDA administration’s statement, the authority is working on an inclusive approach that involves the development of all residential areas in the capital city. Moreover, the developmental work will not discriminate between residents based on their income.
The statement read that the rehabilitation project in Farash Model Urban Shelter Project, is being conducted in continuation of the authority’s strategy to improve the facilities in the city’s low-cost housing projects.
Read:
CDA to receive complete possession of Jedah Town in 1 week
In the first phase, the rehabilitation of roads one, two, three and four will be executed. To this effect, Triple Surface Treatment of the said streets will be carried out and a drainage system will be provided in
Farash Town
. The contractors have launched the preliminary work. The authority also aims to provide streetlights, sewerage system and other missing amenities in the area.

title: Punjab for affordable housing project with WB’s assistance
full_text:
Islamabad: The Government of Punjab has proposed the establishment of an affordable housing project along with requesting the World Bank’s (WB) support for the formulation of a comprehensive provincial housing strategy and policy to facilitate housing for low-income groups, according to a news report published today (June 29).
Read:
Punjab govt prepares for soft launch of Quaid-e-Azam Business Park
The project cost is estimated at USD 350 million, out of which USD 300 million will be provided by the WB’s International Development Association (IDA). The WB will evaluate the proposal after the COVID-19 pandemic situation is stabilised.
Read:
Punjab Budget 2020-21: PKR 7.5bn earmarked for development in Multan
Moreover, the housing project will also address the demand-supply conundrums of the housing value chain. The said solutions will be replicated in other provinces after successful implementation. The project proposal suggests that to provide affordable
housing in Punjab
, a long-term and multi-pronged approach is required. It will cover access to land with basic infrastructure, construction, building and planning regulations, and end-user finance.
Additionally, the proposal suggests the government to switch from acting as a ‘housing provider’ to a ‘market enabler’. This development will incentivise the private sector to support affordable housing value-chain segments.

title: FDA approves WASA’s three-year business model
developer: The governing body of the Faisalabad Development
full_text:
Faisalabad: The governing body of the Faisalabad Development Authority (
FDA
) on Thursday approved a three-year business model for the Water and Sanitation Agency (WASA) – developed under the directions of the Resource Mobilisation Committee, according to news sources.
Read:
FDA sets timelines to issue approvals for boosting construction activity
Now, the WASA model will be tabled before the Standing Cabinet Committee on Finance and Development for final approval.
The managing director (MD) of WASA briefed the meeting attendees on salient features of the new WASA business model. He revealed that the department is making every effort to provide the best possible services for the citizens, despite the financial constraints. He also revealed that WASA is updating its revenue system and taking measures to improve the revenue recovery rate to boost departmental mechanisms.
Read:
WASA operations, streetlights in Punjab to go solar
The meeting also approved the tariff revision after much deliberation. Furthermore, the meeting participants stressed the need for detection of illegal water supply and sewerage connections and demanded an evolved and transparent system.

title: Dedicated desk established at MDA office for construction-related matters
full_text:
Multan: Multan Development Authority (MDA) Director General (DG) Agha Muhammad Ali Abbas on Sunday inaugurated a dedicated desk facility for the construction sector-related inquiries at the MDA office, according to a news report published on June 21.
Read:
MDA to lease out plots, auction commercial land
The said facility is set up at the
one-window cell
in the MDA office and will facilitate people to obtain complete property certification, private housing societies’ map approvals and land conversions.
Reportedly, this dedicated desk at MDA is aimed to promote Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan’s vision to promote the construction industry. As per the fixed new time frame for this dedicated desk, citizens will be able to get complete property certificates within a month. Similarly, applications related to conversion or commercialisation of domestic properties will be resolved in 45 days and layout plans of private housing societies’ will be approved within 60 days.
Read:
MDA serves notices to developers of 162 unapproved housing schemes
Speaking to the inaugural assemblage, the authority’s director general issued directions for the strict adherence to the government-sanctioned standard operating procedures (SOPs) to prevent the coronavirus spread.

title: Three mega road projects awarded to Zero Point Interchange builders
full_text:
Islamabad:A Karachi-based construction company that developed the Zero Point Interchange was recently awarded the contracts for three mega road projects in the federal capital, according to a news report.
On Thursday, the Capital Development Authority (CDA) had opened bids for the construction of the Korang Bridge, the PWD Underpass on Islamabad Expressway, and the Rawal Dam Interchange. A joint venture between Maqbool Associates and Calson won the contracts for all three projects as they had submitted the lowest bids.
Read:
Minister orders speedy completion of Islamabad IT Park project
These details were shared by member planning and engineering Dr Shahid Mahmood, who added that these projects would be officially awarded to the selected developers once all legal proceedings and formalities had been concluded. The joint venture presented bids worth PKR 1.17 billion (11% lower than the estimate) for the Rawal Dam Interchange, PKR 628.5 million (17% lower than the estimate) for the Korang Bridge, and PKR 420 million (19% lower than the estimate) for the PWD Underpass. All three projects have been deemed important to reduce traffic congestion on the major arteries of Islamabad.
Read:
Budget 2020-21: Funds earmarked for several mega projects in Islamabad
The CDA will execute the Rawal Dam Interchange project through its own funding, while the other two
projects
will be executed through the Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP).

title: Punjab Budget 2020-21: PKR 7.5bn earmarked for development in Multan
developer: A number of schemes proposed under the Multan Development
full_text:
Multan: The Punjab government has earmarked funds worth PKR 7.5 billion for establishing the proposed development projects in the Multan division in its Budget 2020-21 — a news source reported. These funds will be spent on nearly 340 ongoing development schemes in the division; while an additional PKR 220 million have been allocated for new projects in the city.
Read:
Multan DC orders completion of development schemes by June 30
A number of schemes proposed under the Multan Development Package by Commissioner Multan Division Shan-ul-Haq have also been included in the budget. In addition, the provincial government has given special attention to the various ongoing health schemes in the division.
Read:
Multan admin directed to implement CJP orders regarding infrastructural developments
Reportedly, PKR 100 million have been dedicated for the development of shelter homes, while PKR 50 million have been earmarked for the agriculture sector. Moreover, PKR 1 billion have been allocated for the construction of the 500-bed Nishtar Hospital; PKR 350 million have been allocated for the Nishter Pharmacy and Store Block; PKR 150 million have been earmarked for a project to extend the Chaudhry Pervaiz Ilahi Institute of Cardiology; and PKR 150 million have been allocated for the DHQ Hospital.

title: RDA inaugurates one-window operation center to facilitate people amid pandemic
full_text:
Rawalpindi: Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) Chairman Tariq Mehmood Murtaza and RDA Director General (DG) Ammara Khan on Wednesday officially inaugurated the One-Window Operation Center (OWOC) by laying its foundation stone, according to news sources. The ceremony was held at the authority’s office, where the facility’s
computerisation
effort was also initiated.
Read:
RDA shares list of approved housing schemes in Rawalpindi
Reportedly, the OWOC will do online processing of the property-related matters to make them efficient and hassle-free. The authority’s chairman addressed the ceremony and lauded the digital measure.
Read:
RDA sets timeline for issuance of NOC, building plans’ approvals
Moreover, the one-window facility is said to become operational in three months and will begin receiving online applications for further processing. The facility will not only enable the locals but also expatriates to submit their applications. With being accessible through the RDA’s official website, applicant can enter their window number to see their application status or any authority objections, if applicable.

title: CDA commences with installation of traffic signals along Ataturk Avenue
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Sunday began installing traffic signals along the Ataturk Avenue, a news source reported. The civic body initiated the process of installing the signals from Khyaban-e-Soharwardi to Nazim-ud-Din Road.
Read:
CDA chairman reviews progress of Ataturk Avenue project
Previously, CDA had floated tenders for the task of installing traffic signals along the avenue. During the process, traffic signals would be installed at six locations. These include junction of the avenue with Khyaban-e-Soharwardi, NADRA Chowk, junction of the avenue with Jinnah Avenue, and junction of the avenue with Fazal-e-Haq Road. The project of installing traffic signals along the road project is part of CDA’s initiative to implement smart signals in the capital city.
Read:
Ataturk Avenue wearing course work starts today
According to details, the dualisation work on the avenue had stared in 2017. Once the dualisation process reaches completion, it would help resolve the issue of congestion along this road. Last year in November, CDA had begun the work of laying down the wearing course on the road.

title: NHA awards contract for e-bidding system development

full_text:
Islamabad: The Executive Board of the National Highway Authority (NHA) has awarded the contract for the development and implementation of an e-bidding system at PKR 132.47 million to M/s Tejari Pakistan Pvt Ltd, according to news sources.
Read:
Work underway on road projects in less developed areas of KP: NHA
The board made this decision in its recently held meeting, where the NHA Chairman was also authorised to constitute a three-member technical committee for supervision of the development process. The committee will present its findings to the board in three months’ time. Furthermore, the board has also asked for the reports on progress status of previous information technology (IT) projects.
Read:
NHA opens motels on Multan-Sukkur Motorway
Additionally, the NHA Executive Board has recommended the “PC-I for construction of 4-lane flyover at Bhara Kahu (N-75) project” at a cost of PKR 7.608 billion for the Central Development Working Party (CDWP)’s approval. Similarly, on condition of a 100% mutation of Right of Way (

) by the provincial government in NHA’s name (with no subsequent cancellation of mutation); the board has also recommended federalisation of the following roads:

Neela Dullah Interchange (M-2) – Mangwal Road – as extension of M-2 (strategic road).

title: Zarghoon Housing Scheme Quetta gets electricity supply
full_text:
Quetta: The Quetta Development Authority (QDA)’s Zarghoon Housing Scheme finally achieved electrification on Tuesday (June 23), a news source reported. The society’s residents had long been demanding for the basic facility.
Zarghoon Housing Scheme was launched in 2011, and the plot allottees completed their payments to receive property possession in 2017. While the QDA completed work on setting up the society
grid station
in 2019, it took almost a year to initiate electricity supply.
Read:
BHC issues stay order against Zarghoon Housing Scheme expansion agreement
With the electricity supply mechanism up and running, the QDA is now expected to begin work on the installation of streetlights. At the same time, work is still pending on laying a gas supply line, finishing the sewerage system, and installing a security system in the society.
Zarghoon Housing Scheme Welfare Association President Abdullah Kakar expressed his pleasure regarding the news that the society was finally getting an electricity supply, and further thanked the Quetta Electric Supply Company for allowing the development of a 32-KV grid station in the housing scheme.
Read:
NAB compensates victims of fake housing scheme in Quetta
He added that his association expected that the QDA would be addressing the other concerns raised by the residents soon; allowing Zarghoon Housing Scheme to become a popular place to live in Quetta.

title: CDA re-invites bids for infrastructural development in I-15/4
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has re-invited bids from contractors for  infrastructural development in Sector I-15/4, according to a publication shared in national newspapers on June 25. It issued a tender notice for this purpose earlier on May 23.
Read:
Strategy formation in place to fix delays in CDA sectors
According to the latest advertisement, the bid documents will be available for purchase at the CDA Office in Melody, G-6, Islamabad on July 15 by 12 AM. The bids can be submitted by July 23, not later than 11:30 AM. As per the CDA’s rules, the bidding firms have to have their Pakistan Engineering Council License 2020.
The development authority has lately resumed development work in the sectors that have been stalled from the last several decades. In this regard, the CDA is handling various related tasks in several sectors including E-12, I-12,
I-14
and I-15.
Read:
Cadastral survey planned to verify BUP claims in stalled CDA sectors
At the same time, several other CDA sectors and projects await similar developments. These include i-14, G-15, I-17, H-16, F-13, F14, E-13, D-13, C-15 and C-16.

title: Work on Diamer Bhasha Dam continuing well despite pandemic: Vawda
full_text:
Lahore: Federal Minister for Water Resources Muhammad Faisal Vawda on Wednesday revealed that work on the Diamer Bhasha Dam project was progressing well despite the ongoing pandemic situation, a news source reported.
Read:
Construction machinery reaches Diamer Bhasha Dam site: Vawda
Vawda presided over a meeting held at the Water & Power Development Authority (WAPDA) House to review the implementation plan for the Diamer Bhasha Dam Mega Hydel Project. He issued orders to the project authorities, contractors, and consultants to adhere to the timelines planned for the venture.
During the meeting, WAPDA Chairman Muzammil Hussain revealed that following the contract signing, the contractors and machinery had been mobilized at the project site. He added that construction on the main dam would start soon.
Read:
ECNEC approves land acquisition, resettlement plan for Diamer Bhasha Dam
Hussain assured the meeting that WAPDA was committed to completing the project within the specified timeframe. According to the details available, once completed, the Diamer Bhasha Dam would provide water for agriculture and low-cost hydel electricity — leading to economic development, along with mitigation of floods in Pakistan.

title: Housing societies near Tarnol area identified for polluting Sanday Mar Dam
full_text:
Islamabad: The Sanday Mar Dam, located in the federal capital territory, has been identified for its role in consistently polluting Sectors E-16 and E-17, and the Tarnol area – causing serious agricultural and fishing hurdles, according to news sources.
Read:
Govt releases funds for construction of Chehan Dam; project completion likely in next FY
As per reports, the drainage of untreated wastewater in the natural stream of Sanday Mar Dam has turned into a major environmental disaster and a health hazard.
The executive engineer of
Small Dams Division
Islamabad of the Small Dams Organisation, Irrigation Department, Punjab has written letters to the two cooperative housing societies located in the said sectors and to the chairman of the Capital Development Authority (CDA); urging them to stop the practice and save natural resources. The letters further directed for serious measures to preserve the natural creek and streams to avoid strict actions.
Read:
Dadhocha dam to be completed in three years: Chairman RDA
An official revealed that since the CDA approved these housing societies under conditions that the societies must have their own sewerage treatment plants. The water of the dam issued for land irrigation and fisheries and untreated water’s seepages into the Sanday Mar Dam has also affected the underground drinkable water sources of the adjoining areas.

title: RDA suggests housing schemes to construct interchanges on major road
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) has proposed allowing the developers of private housing schemes located in its controlled areas to construct interchanges on major roads leading to the respective societies, according to news sources.
Read:
RDA shares list of approved housing schemes in Rawalpindi
In this regard, the authority has, reportedly, held meetings with developers of five housing schemes. RDA Chairman Tariq Murtaza, without naming the developers, said that these societies’ representatives have been suggested to construct interchanges on major road avenues passing close to their projects at their own cost. The sources claim that the developers have sought time to think over the proposal and conduct a feasibility study to ascertain its various aspects.
Read:
RDA sets timeline for issuance of NOC, building plans’ approvals
By allowing the construction of these interchanges, the RDA expects to reduce traffic load on the connected road network. This, at the same time, will also provide faster and easier access to the residents of these societies. In addition, this will also help reduce the financial load on the government  to develop the needed infrastructure facilities.

title: Work underway on road projects in less developed areas of KP: NHA
developer: Sarai Gambila to Kohat under the Public Sector Development
full_text:
Peshawar: The National Highway Authority (NHA) on Monday stated that it was working on several road infrastructure projects in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), many of which were set to be constructed in the less developed areas of the province, a news source reported. An NHA official revealed that once completed, these projects would provide opportunities for earning livelihood to the people of adjacent areas.
Read:
Murad shares important details on ongoing NHA projects, CPEC Western Route
According to details provided by the NHA official, that KP government had allocated PKR 6,500 million for the dualisation and upgradation of a section of the Indus Highway. He added that the provincial government had allocated and released funds for the said section from Sarai Gambila to Kohat under the Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP) 2020-21.
The official revealed that the KP government had also earmarked and released over PKR 1,110 million for the Lowari Tunnel and its access roads. He added that it allocated and released another PKR 2,500 million for the 32km long Peshawar Northern Bypass.
Read:
NHA invites bids for dualisation of Zhob-Quetta section on N-50
According to the official, NHA was also working on the following road infrastructure projects in KP:
Thakot-Havelian Motorway
Upgrading of Yarik-Sagu section of N-50
Dualisation & improvement of Old Bannu Road
Rehabilitation of national highway network damaged by flash floods of 2010

title: CDA to complete balance work on dualization of Service Road in I-10, I-11
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has launched the process to complete balance work on the dualization of Service Road (North) that runs between Sector I-10 and I-11, according to news sources.
Read:
CDA allocated funds to initiate construction work on 10th Avenue
The estimated cost for the completion of balance work is PKR 34,847,796 and the authority has issued tenders in this regard. After the completion of all the codal formalities, the development work will start. The dualization of the said road has remained pending for some time. The development work on the service road was launched in 2011 and was to be completed by the next year.
Read:
CDA approves funds for development of PWD Underpass, Korang Bridge, other projects
The incumbent
CDA
administration is following a comprehensive strategy to complete the development work on such stalled sectors and projects. The dualization of this road will help facilitate incoming traffic  from  Kashmir Highway, 9th Avenue and other adjacent highways (including I J Principal Road). Furthermore, the road enhancement will particularly facilitate the transportation of the industrial raw materials from and to the industrial units established in Sectors I-9 and I-10/3.

title: No plot transfers without scrutiny committee’s approval: CDA
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (
CDA
) has issued another letter to halt plot transfers without the scrutiny committee’s approval, according to news sources. It took this step to prevent new cases of fraudulent plot allotment.
Read:
CDA to auction New Blue Area commercial plots in July
The scrutiny committee was constituted by Land Director Shafi Marwat to ensure that plots are allotted based on genuine and authentic documentation and in a transparent manner.
Reportedly, many prime plot allotments in Sectors D-13, E-13 ad I-12, up until March, were conducted through fraudulent practices like backdating and fake signatures. One CDA Security Directorate also highlighted fraudulent and
backdated allotments
of more than 300 plots last year. A formal inquiry was then launched to verify the matter.
Read:
CDA approves budget outlay of PKR 49bn for FY 2020-21
Meanwhile, the CDA team is also surveying layout plans and physical sites of cooperative housing societies to examine the ground situation of public and amenity plots. Out of 15 such societies, a survey of seven has been conducted so far.

title: Punjab govt prepares for soft launch of Quaid-e-Azam Business Park
full_text:
Lahore: The Punjab government on Monday notified that it was making preparations for a soft launch of the Quaid-e-Azam Business Park, a news source reported. According to details revealed, Minster for Industries Mian Aslam Iqbal is leading the said initiative and the Punjab Industrial Estate Development and Management Company (PIEDMC) is overseeing the project’s development.
Read:
Quaid-e-Azam Business Park to have its own grid station
During a recent high-level meeting, PIEDMC Chairman Nabeel Hashmi shared the business plan for the Quaid-e-Azam Business Park. Sources have also revealed that had it not been for the pandemic, Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan would have inaugurated the project in March. Now, the provincial government is committed to kick starting the business activity in Punjab with the project being part of that initiative.
Read:
Booking underway for industrial plots in Quaid-e-Azam Business Park, Sheikhupura
On the other hand, the Punjab government also plans to develop a state-of-the-art IT Park in Lahore. The said project would improve the competitiveness of the service industry. It would also help take the advantage of the exchange rate depreciation leading to greater exports of IT products and services.

title: EPA takes up task to purify Islamabad’s environment, water
full_text:
Islamabad: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) recently announced its decision to purify Islamabad’s environment and water, a news source reported. In the regard, EPA will set up environment cleansing and water purification units in the city.
Read:
Smart lockdown imposed in a number of Islamabad sectors
The EPA expects to complete the project within three years and carry it out solely itself. The department’s chairing lady Farzana Altaf stated that the environment-cleansing unit would mitigate the effects of harm caused by chemicals in the atmosphere. She added that similarly the water purification unit would regulate the cleansing of water.
Read:
TORs devised for Islamabad’s environmental protection
On the other hand, the government has not launched any new scheme for the environmental sector in the new financial year. It allocated PKR 5 billion for the six ongoing climate related projects under the Public Sector Development Project (PSDP). The government would spend PKR 4.9 billion on Tsunami Tree Project and PKR 100 million on other initiatives.

title: Firdous Market Underpass project will be completed in 90 days: LDA VC
full_text:
Lahore: Lahore Development Authority (LDA) Vice Chairman (VC) SM Imran has said that the construction work on the Firdous Market Underpass will be completed in 90 days, according to a news source. He shared the information while speaking to media after visiting the project site.
Read:
During the visit, LDA Chief Engineer Habib-ul-Haq Randhawa briefed the VC on project development and land acquisition status. National Engineering Services officials and representatives of project contractor, Maqbool Associates, also attended the briefing session.
The VC further said that feasibility study will be conducted soon for making signal-free corridors and development of underpass and flyover at busy roads and intersection of Lahore including Barkat Market, Karee Block, Akbar Chowk, near Jinnah Hosipital and Shahdara.
Read:
Sharing details on Firdous Market Underpass project, VC Imran said that once the underpass completes, the LDA will construct a pedestrian bridge on Jam-e-Shirin Road. The two-lane Firdous Market Underpass will be 540 metres in length and it will facilitate approximately 100,000 vehicles on a daily basis. The project will help ease traffic flow on Centre Point, MM Alam Road, and Cavalry Ground.

full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Monday announced its decision to auction commercial plots in the New Blue Area between July 15-17 – under Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan’s stated ‘Naya Pakistan’ vision, according to news sources. These commercial plots are located in the Central Business District and their sizes range from 600 sq ft to 10,000 sq ft.
Read:
CDA allocated funds to initiate construction work on 10th Avenue
The
auction was delayed
due to the outbreak of the coronavirus in Pakistan. CDA Director Public Relations Mazhar Hussain revealed that the auction will be held at Jinnah Convention Centre – under the slogan of ‘Blue Area, New Vision’ to provide a unique opportunity for businesses and investors to become a part of the newly-developed business hub of Islamabad.
Moreover, the CDA will offer special incentives to the prospective bidders which include a dedicated team tasked with facilitation of investors through every step. Additionally, the investors will be given 30 days of bid acceptance letter for payment of the first instalment of 25%. The investors will be given a building plan approval facility after the first instalment and they can start construction on full payment.
Read:
CDA approves budget outlay of PKR 49bn for FY 2020-21
Investors who pay the full amount in advance will receive a 10% discount and the advance income tax will be collected on pro-rata basis. For plots less than 1000 sq yds, 100% coverage will be offered while 70-75% coverage is offered for the plots spanning over 1000 sq yds. Each plot shall have all-round circulation strip. The plots come with ample parking space and application of reformed building bylaws.
The income generated from this auction will be utilised to fund development projects in Islamabad. Further details of the auction are available on the
CDA
’s website. Additionally, details and brochures are available at the authority’s One-Window Directorate and designated branches of the Muslim Commercial Bank (MCB), Askari Bank, Habib Bank Limited (HBL) and Bank of Punjab (BoP).

title: KP Budget 2020-21: Fund reserved for infrastructural development in selected cities
full_text:
Peshawar: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Finance Minister Taimur Saleem Jhagra on Friday announced the provincial government’s decision to allocate PKR 5 billion for infrastructural development in a number of cities during (Fiscal Year) FY2020-21 — a news source reported.
Read:
KP govt announces property, trade, other tax concessions for FY2020-21
During a budget speech, minister Jhagra stated that with the assistance of the European Union, the government would be spending PKR 3.9 billion on the development of infrastructure and other services in selected cities across the province.
He revealed that PKR 1.8 billion had been dedicated for the construction of the northern sector of the Warsak Road to Nasir Bagh. Similarly, nearly PKR 550 million is expected to be spent on the development of the provincial capital, under the Peshawar Development Program. Meanwhile, an additional PKR 300 million will be used to improve and rehabilitate amenities and services in the province’s rural areas.
Read:
Foundation stone laid for Char-Elum Road construction in Buner, KP
Finally, the minister said that land fill sites will be constructed in Mansehra, Chitral, Upper Dir and Swat. He added that a number of markets would also be established in some tehsils of the province through this initiative.

title: Pakistan, ADB sign loan agreement for Karachi’s BRT project
full_text:
Islamabad: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) on Saturday inked two loan agreements with the Government of Pakistan – amounting to USD 359 million – for funding the bus rapid transit (BRT) project in Karachi and enhancing the quality of the Sindh secondary education system, according to news sources.
Read:
ADB approves USD 235 mn for Karachi BRT project
Economic Affairs Secretary Noor Ahmed and ADB Country Director for Pakistan Xiaohong Yang signed the agreements on behalf of their respective associations. Under the agreement, the ADB will provide USD 235 million loan for the 26.6-kilometre-long BRT Red Line corridor.
Additionally, the Green Climate Fund will also provide USD 37.2 million as a loan and USD 11.8 million as a grant for the same project. The project features innovate energy and climate-resilient characteristics to enhance Karachi’s mass transport system. The Karachi’s
BRT
project also aims to ease congestion, improve commuting and add to the quality of life for the citizens. Presently, the project is undergoing the procurement of civil works and services to timely expedite its implementation.
Read:
Peshawar BRT services to become operational soon
Furthermore, the second loan agreement – of worth USD 75 million – was signed for the Sindh Secondary Education Improvement project and would be financed through the ADB’s Concessional Ordinary Capital Resources that offers low-interest rates.

Quetta: The management of the Defense Housing Authority (DHA) Smart City Phase I has issued a reminder for its members to submit their first down payment before the communicated deadline expires – which is tomorrow (June 23), according to the society’s official Facebook page. Those failing to do so may be at risk of losing their plots.
Read:
DHA Multan announces possessions in Sector M
The development of the society’s infrastructure is currently underway on an expedited basis. The society has also issued tenders for the construction of DHA Quetta Smart City Expressway that waves around the sectors A, B, C and D.
The initial
deadline
for payment of first down payment was April 14, which was then extended to May 30 to facilitate the people amid government-imposed coronavirus lockdown. The project has also announced a reduction in the first down payment – from 10% to 8% – for residential plots and for farmhouses, it was reduced to 16% from 20%.
Read:
DHA Quetta floats tender for construction of Expressway, road network in 4 sectors
For additional details including downloading the payment voucher, members can log onto https://ballotapp.dhaquetta.org/my/resister/. Payments can be made nationwide at any branch of Askari Bank Limited.

full_text:
Karachi: The Bahria Town management has announced opening the bookings for its latest, low-cost, ‘Bahira Greens’ housing project, according to the developer’s official Facebook page. The booking forms can be downloaded from the society’s official website and can be submitted (along with bank draft/cash) at any Bahria Town office or nationwide branches of the United Bank Limited (UBL) and Allied Bank Limited.
Read:
Bahria administration denounces online portals for illegally adopting company IPRs
The project is claimed to be the country’s largest low-cost housing project with a limited number of residential plots spanning 75 sq yds (15’x40’). The permissible structure encompasses ground plus two floors with four bedrooms. The booking fee is PKR 295,000 and the total amount is PKR 1,675,000. The possession will be given in 3 years and payments can be made in 16 quarterly instalments spreading over 4 years (PKR 86,250 each).
Furthermore, the processing fees for the application is PKR 5,000 – non-refundable. For preferences like corner plot, boulevard location and park facing – the investors will have to pay an additional 10% (each). The development charges, maintenance and service charges are not included in the mentioned prices.
Read:
Bahria Town Karachi bans entry of visitors, non-residents
People can also avail home financing services for the construction of houses.
Bahria Greens
includes an overseas block – created especially for expatriates. The developmental work on the project is currently being conducted at a rapid pace. However, the investors will have to construct their houses in line with the designs communicated by the society management. The plots’ location is allocated temporarily and will be finalised after demarcation.
Buyers will have to pay all the registration charges, sales agreements and transfer fees as required. In case of cancellation, after the plot allotment, the allottee will have to surrender the investments already made. Investors will have to comply with all the allotment, possession, ownership, construction and transfer bylaws administrated by the society administration or any other relevant authority.

title: PM directs LDA to take measures for boosting construction activity
developer: Imran Khan has directed the Lahore Development
full_text:
Lahore: Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan has directed the Lahore Development Authority (LDA) to take measures for boosting the workings of the local construction/infrastructures industry and improving public services delivery within the city, according to news sources.
Read:
LDA governing body approves amendments in Private Housing Schemes Rules 2014
Khan issued these directives while in a meeting with the LDA Vice Chairman S M Imran. In addition, the prime minister asked the VC to ensure expedition of the development work underway to launch the
River Ravi
Urban Development (RRUD) project. He said that the hurdles hindering the initiation of water level rising and wastewater treatment project to be removed promptly. The PM opined that the LDA should take effective steps to conserve water for the coming generations.
Read:
LDA urged to take action against illegal buildings, colonies near Lahore airport
Earlier, the vice chairman briefed the premiere about the progress of the River Ravi Urban Development (RRUD) project, LDA’s one window operation and land-use rules, among other things. He requested Khan to spare 700 kanals of forest land along the Ravi River for the establishment of forests and urged him to direct the National Highways Authority (NHA) to construct overhead bridges across the said river.

title: PC-I approved for Multan’s Madni Chowk flyover
full_text:
Multan: The Multan Development Authority (MDA), in its 82
nd
Governing Body meeting held on July 17, approved the project concept (PC)-I for development of the Madni Chowk Flyover, according to a news source. The PKR 600 million project was approved by the MDA earlier in October 2019.
Read:
Multan DC orders completion of development schemes by June 30
The session, chaired by MDA Vice Chairman Mumtaz Ahmed Qureshi, also approved the selling of plots reserved for disposal stations under the auction framework; and was attended by Punjab Chief Minister’s Spokesperson Sabeen Gul Khan, Member Punjab Assembly Malik Muhammad Saleem, and several notable MDA officials.
Read:
MDA body approves new housing scheme for Multan
In addition to the above mentioned projects, the MDA also sanctioned the business plan for the Water and Sanitation Authority (WASA)’s water supply and sewerage initiatives. Further, the attendees decided that WASA would recover bills from the housing schemes that still await MDA approval.

title: Development projects for Karak, Hangu, Kohat included in ADP 2020-21
developer: Karak, Hangu, and Kohat districts in the Annual Development
full_text:
Peshawar: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Chief Minister (CM) Mahmood Khan on Thursday announced the inclusion of development projects for Karak, Hangu, and Kohat districts in the Annual Development Programme (ADP) 2020-21, a news source reported.
Read:
PDWP approves 29 development projects in KP
During a meeting with Member National Assembly (MNA) Shahid Khattak, the KP CM stated that there would be two new projects of clean drinking water included in the
ADP 2020-21
for Karak. He added that the provision of clean drinking water to the people of the district was among the top priorities of the provincial government.
CM Khan said that the KP government has allocated PKR 1.3 billion for Karak, PKR 1 billion for Hangu, and PKR 550 million for Kohat for the purpose of various development projects in these districts.
Read:
Development budget to remain unaffected by coronavirus outbreak: KP CM
The CM highlighted that during the first phase, the amount allocated for Kohat division would be utilised under oil and gas royalty to help resolve the problems faced by the people.

title: Govt releases funds for construction of Chehan Dam; project completion likely in next FY
developer: This was informed to the Rawalpindi Development
full_text:
Rawalpindi: The Punjab government has released all the funds required for the construction work of the Chehan Dam and water pond; which is expected to be started next year, according to news sources.
Read:
Punjab CM issues directive for construction of small dams, reservoirs
This was informed to the Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) and Water and Sanitation Agency (WASA) Chairman Tariq Mehmood Murtaza, RDA Director General (DG) Amara Khan and WASA Managing Director (MD) Raja Shaukat – when they visited the Chehan Dam site.
Additionally, the Small Dams Organisation Executive Engineer Umair Khan informed them that the dam’s construction work will be completed in the next fiscal year. He stated that the dam pond is ready and spillways are being constructed.
Read:
13 small dams approved for Rawalpindi Division
Moreover, the funds granted by the provincial government will be utilised for
land acquisition
for laying the main water supply line, filtration plant, ground storage and overhead tanks, among other project-components.
Presently, the design work of the project is underway, while the construction work will be launched in the next year. After the project completion, six union councils (UCs) of the district will be supplied with 6 million gallons of drinking water per day.

title: KP to form UDA to monitor efficiency of existing development authorities
developer: Monday announced establishing the Urban Areas Development
full_text:
Peshawar: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) government on Monday announced establishing the Urban Areas Development Authority (UDA) – through an ordinance – to oversee the existing nine development authorities (and their performance) operational within the province, according to news sources.
Read:
KP approves Land Acquisition Rules 2020, formation of GDA Board of Authority
The UDA will ensure improvement in the provision of basic amenities to the public. A statement in this regard was issued by Chief Minister’s Special Assistant on Local Government, Elections and Rural Development Kamran Bangash, stating that the provision of these amenities was the government’s utmost priority. He said that the UDA will upscale the performance of the local government and the development authorities in Bannu, Kohat, Karak, Mardan,
Galiyat
, Swabi, Swat and Peshawar – which are reportedly paralysed.
Read:
KP tourism body reviews proposal for setting up Kalam Development Authority
Bangash said that the new authority will empower the existing development authorities to improve revenue generation and decision making. He also said that under the new authority, these authorities will come up with plans for affordable housing societies.

title: PM Khan directs WASA, Lahore to start work on water treatment plant projects
developer: Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, the France Development
full_text:
Lahore: Prime Minister (PM) Imran Khan recently directed the Water and Sanitation Authority (WASA), Lahore to immediately initiate the development work for setting up waste water treatment plants within the city, according to a news source.
Read:
WASA to lay tunnel sewer system in Lahore
Reportedly, WASA Vice Chairman S.M Imran had briefed the PM on the planned projects during his visit to Lahore on June 13. After receiving the briefing, the PM directed the vice chairman to start work on the proposed projects immediately. title: Budget 2020-21: Punjab allocates PKR 337 bn to Annual Development Programme

Budget 2020-21: Relief measures announced for real estate, construction sectors

title: LDA urged to take action against illegal buildings, colonies near Lahore airport

full_text:
Lahore: The Allama Iqbal International Airport management on Sunday issued a warning to the Lahore Development Authority (LDA), the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA), and other departments concerned regarding the construction of high rises, colonies and illegal developments near the airport landing area; seeing as the practice can lead to unfortunate collision incidents, according to news sources.

, city commissioner and director general of LDA in separate letters. He urged the

Govt decides to lift ban on construction of high-rises near airports

title: Govt sets aside PKR 650 bn for development projects under PSDP 2020-21
full_text:
Islamabad: The government has set PKR 650 billion – including foreign assistance worth PKR 72.5 billion – for development projects under the Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP) 2020-21, according to news sources.
This budget highlights the importance of public investment to create employment opportunities, revive the economy and alleviate poverty in the aftermath of coronavirus pandemic that has put the economic wheel to a halt.
Read:
Govt shares details on funds released under PSDP during FY2019-20
This year’s PSDP focuses on completion of existing projects, provision of funds to cover foreign-funded projects and to support initiatives under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC). Moreover,
PSDP FY 2020-21
seeks to innovate financing modes to reduce burden on the national economy and to address the needs of the less developed areas to promote regional balanced development.
To mitigate the COVID-19 impact, a special programme will be launched to a tune of PKR 70 billion – with a focus on education, Upgradation of existing health services, sewerage, solid waste management, and clean drinking water provision.
Read:
PKR 177.5 bn allocated for water sector & hydropower projects under PSDP 2020-21
An amount of PKR 179 billion has been allocated to meet minimum requirements for CPEC and other priority projects of communication and transport sector. In PSDP 2020-21, special interventions have been made for less developed areas of Balochistan, merged districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Gilgit-Baltistan.
For the power and water sector projects, funds of worth PKR 80 billion and 70 billion have been earmarked. An amount of PKR 12 billion has been allocated for food security and agriculture. The climate change ministry is to receive PKR 5 billion with special focus on the first phase of ‘Ten Billion Tree Tsunami Programme’. Furthermore, the government has earmarked PKR 24 billion for special programmes, with a special focus on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG).

title: EOI invited for construction of low-cost NPHP apartments in LDA City

For the remaining directorates of the authority, including Human Resource and Finance, the PM’s office has directed the concerned officials to bring them under the control of the Metropolitan Corporation Islamabad (MCI). Japanese companies willing to invest in Pakistan Railways: Envoy
The meeting reviewed the restructuring process and its members were told that private companies would be operating 15 passenger trains. CPEC Authority chairman shuns rumours about shelving ML-1 project

title: CDA completes Wetland Wastewater Management Project Phase-I
full_text:
Islamabad: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Monday notified the completion of the construction work for Phase-I of the Wetland Wastewater Management Project, according to news sources. The civic agency has handed over the project – situated in Muslim Colony between Bari Iman (Noorpur Shahan) and the Diplomatic Enclave –to the Sanitation Directorate for maintenance and management.
Read:
CDA to run Islamabad Metro Bus Service
CDA Chairman and Islamabad Chief Commissioner Amer Ali Ahmed said that the project was launched upon the directives of the Supreme Court (SC). He said that the authority chose three sites for the wetlands’ construction – which will aid in controlling the deteriorating environmental conditions and restore the natural charm of this brook running down the Margalla Hills.
Read:
Sindh to rehabilitate degraded wetlands
Amer said that the first ‘Wetlands environmental intervention’ project – spread over less than an acre – has been completed at a cost of PKR 1.5 million and produced highly encouraging results. He added that the water quality has improved considerably and with the construction of two more wetlands, more betterment will be seen. The chairman revealed that another wetland is being constricted on the opposite side of the Muslim Colony and the third one is under-construction in Bani Gala – to prevent the contamination of
Rawal Lake
.
He said that given the cost feasibility and encouraging results, such wetlands will be constructed on all natural brooks and streams running from Margalla Hills and joining Nullah Leh.

title: Construction of dams to enhance hydel generation capacity to 30,000MW
full_text:
Islamabad: The Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA) has formulated an elaborate plan to enhance the hydel generation capacity to 30,000 megawatts (MW), in addition to increasing water storage capacity through the development of dams, according to news sources.
Read:
ECNEC approves funds for small dams in Balochistan, BRTS, other projects
The plan envisages steps to increase the hydel generation capacity from 9,406 megawatts (MW) to 14,000MW by 2025 and 30,000MW by the year 2030 through Dasu Hydropower phase I & II,
Mohmand Dam
, Diamer Basha Dam, and the project of 5th extension to Tarbela dam.
As per the official sources, the construction work is already underway on Mohmand and Diamer Basha dams. These dams will help store additional water for both irrigation and generating cheap hydel generation. Reportedly, the Mohmand dam project will be completed by the end of 2024.
Read:
Mohmand, Diamer Bhasha Dams ideal for int. investment: Wapda Chairman
Moreover, the sources revealed that constriction of the Diamer Basha, Mohmand, Kurram Tangi, Sindh Barrage, Naulong, Chiniot, Murunj and Hingol and other projects will ensure 100% increase in the storage capacity by 2030 – which currently stands at 13 Million Acre Feet (MAF).
